  a part whose leaves are not consecutive among the leaves of the process's driver, and a slice that is not the last step. A whole read
  goes through `read_obj`'s callers as before and the per-activation copy of #630 is filled by one `SigGather`.
- **(Superseded by "IR optimiser round 14": every part is a scatter again.) A part is driven leaf by leaf when another drive of the process may override it** (`Fx::overridden_signals`: two targets of one
  signal in the process whose field paths are the same or one below the other, such as `port_req(i) <= a; if c then port_req(i).stb <= b`).
  The drive-deleting pass (`opt/drives.rs`, #667) drops the first of two drives on the paths where the second follows, which it can for
  single-leaf `Drive`s and not inside a `SigScatter` (its targets are known only at run time). Measured on `neorv32_single_min`
  (`port_req(i)`, a default and an override in a loop over five ports): as one scatter +5.9 percent instructions over the leaf-by-leaf code
  with the pass (more assignments: the default of the selected port is done as well), as leaf-by-leaf code -0.9 percent against the
  commit before. A whole record (no step) keeps the scatter as in the first step (#677). Corpus: `composite/sigrec_arrays` (the same
  signals driven again and again: the leaf-by-leaf code), `sigrec_arrays_scatter` (one drive of each part: the scatter), `sigrec_arrays_nested`,
  `sigrec_arrays_kinds` (every kind of leaf in the elements) and `sigrec_arrays_null` (arrays of records without an element).
- **Length check** (LRM 10.5.2.1): a record value driven onto a record signal has the signal's length in every array field; the check
  is `Fx::check_desc` in `drive_record`, ahead of the scatter and of the per-leaf code (it used to be only the outer dimensions of an
  array). A mismatch is the length error `value length N does not match <object> length M` with the name the reference simulators use for a record: the
  object a value is (`variable W`), else `target`; for an array it stays the target. Before the check a value of other field lengths in
  the same plane block was driven silently (`0101UUUU`); corpus tests `composite/sigrec_length_error`, `_part`, `_waves` (several waveform
  elements: the per-leaf code). The signal parameter case reads `parameter V` where the reference simulators say `constant V`.
- **Measured, not done**: drives with several waveform elements (0 of 515 drive sites over ten designs), signal parameters (9 sites;
  `osvvm_axi4_random` has one in 12.7 percent of the executed ops of its statements, about 1 percent of its instructions, which an
  elaboration three times that size hides), a per-leaf event stamp to skip the leaves a gather finds unchanged (the kernel's share is
  `assign_code_fast`/`commit_code` and does not depend on the instructions), a plane block for the `n` instances of a logic scalar leaf
  (`ponytail:` in `gather.rs`: one assignment per instance), and the single-field reads, which are one `SigVal` and one read each.
  The census (executed IR ops per statement and the share of the ops of the statements that still read or drive a record signal leaf
  by leaf): `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` 7.7 percent (`stage_r`, an array of records), `neorv32_single_min` 10.4 percent (`port_req(i)`),
  `grlib_leon3mp` 0.4 percent, the other designs below 0.1 percent.

## Window generator: no pass pipeline or forced compile changes the run; what is left is the accessor chain (#493, #679, #680, 2026-10-24)

Measurements in docs/STATUS.md "Window generator against sim1: where the time is now". Decisions (none changes code):

- **No `licm` or `gvn` in the lean pipeline.** Whole program under `--tier=llvm` with `YAVS_LLVM_PIPELINE`: lean 222.0 G instructions, with
  `loop-mssa(licm)` 226.4 G, with `gvn` and `licm` 225.5 G. The loop-invariant object look-ups of the codec loops are not hoisted because the
  calls and slow-path exits of the loop body may change the object table. A hoist needs the generator to know which instructions keep the
  table (`keeps_objects`), as a known object across a loop, not a general pass.
- **Compile policy facts for #680 and #673** (the policy is not changed here): forcing the 15 refused or interpreted functions leaves a warm run
  where it was; in a cold run the compile thread is 13 to 14 G instructions of the 55 to 70 G cold overhead and the rest is code that is not
  compiled yet, so lower compile cost per LLVM instruction (70 000 LLVM instructions after the passes in 45 timed compiles, a flat profile) helps the second
  half only through the latency.
- **The remaining distance to sim1 is the pointer-table and codec chain of the test runner**: 36 percent of the instructions of a warm run are
  75 M `get`, 40 M `set` and 13 M each of `length`, `unsafe_push`, `unsafe_pop` (call counts of #493), `get` at about 285 instructions per call. The four object look-ups and three dope tests of one `get` are the design of generational handles and bounds
  checked descriptors; the flat heap view (#655) and larger inlining (#493) were tried and lost. The option left is the one on #493 (native
  implementation of the test runner's pointer tables and queue), which is the maintainer's to decide.

## llvm: code in one arena of huge pages, entry dispatch as a tree, the hot edge falls through (yavs-llvm, #679, 2026-10-24)

- **Decision: on Linux x86_64 all compiled code lives in one contiguous region and is backed by huge pages** (`arena.rs`). ORC's
  default linker (JITLink) maps each module wherever the kernel puts it, in 4 KiB pages, and its allocator cannot be replaced through
  the C API; the object layer is now RuntimeDyld with our own section allocator (`LLVMOrcCreateRTDyldObjectLinkingLayerWithMCJITMemoryManagerLikeCallbacks`).
  Code sections are bump allocated in compile order (the hot functions of a run are next to each other) in a 2 MiB-aligned 1 GiB
  reservation that is read-write-execute (nothing to finalise, no instruction cache to flush on x86), data sections in a second zone of
  the same reservation (code and data within 2 GiB). A 2 MiB chunk is asked to be a transparent huge page (`MADV_HUGEPAGE`, then
  `MADV_COLLAPSE`) once it holds 256 KiB, so a small run keeps small pages and a big one has two or three iTLB entries for its code; a
  collapse that fails is tried again at twice the fill. It replaces `huge_code` (the whole-program module only) where it applies. Every
  other target, a failed reservation and `YAVS_LLVM_ARENA=0` keep LLJIT's default linker; `YAVS_LLVM_HUGE=0` keeps the arena without huge
  pages. Memory of dropped JITs stays in the arena (a `ponytail:` in the code). Test: `crates/yavs-llvm/tests/arena.rs`.
- **Decision: the entry switch of frame-mode code is a tree** (`Gen::entry_dispatch`): range compares on the sorted entry pcs with
  `switch` leaves of at most four cases. The unoptimised code generator (`Fast`, every function of 1 000 IR instructions or more) lowers a
  `switch` to a chain of `mov; sub; je; jmp` per case, and a process is entered at one of its resume pcs at every resume: 31 percent of the
  instructions executed inside the compiled `iu:comb` copy of the LEON3 design (1 357 entries) were that chain. Heat-mode L1i misses of
  `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` fell by a quarter with it.
- **Decision: `Gen::cond_br` with `likely` branches on the negation of a condition that is not a compare**, so the rare edge is the
  `jcc` and the hot path falls through. For `br (a & b), hot, cold` the code generator emits `jne hot; jmp cold` with `hot` the next
  block: a taken branch over a jump at every such guard (a bounds check of every memory access). Compares keep their form (the code
  generator fuses them and inverts the predicate itself). The 5 478 `jcc`-over-`jmp` pairs in the LEON3 `comb` copy are 1 879 now;
  branch misses fall 10 to 25 percent, instructions rise 0.1 to 0.4 percent (the `xor`).
- **Measured, not built (machine function splitting):** a made-up profile summary and an entry count per function make LLVM
  (`-enable-split-machine-functions -mfs-count-threshold`) put the blocks its branch weights call rare into a second section, and the
  arena can send a repeated section name to a cold zone. The hot part of the 24 000-instruction `comb` copy was 1.1 MB instead of
  3.7 MB, but L1i misses rose by a fifth (neorv32 47 to 60 M, reader 64 to 74 M, writer 127 to 144 M, heat mode) and cycles did not
  move: the rare edges are taken more often than 1:2000, and each trip lands in a far section. Not kept. The cold blocks of the
  slow paths already sit at the end of their function (`Cur::cold`), about a tenth of the code. `zext(trunc x)` for the 32-bit masks
  (a 2-byte `mov` instead of a 10-byte `movabs` and an `and`) was tried and dropped: instcombine turns it back into the mask.
- **What the machine code of a large process is made of** (LEON3 `comb` copy, 23 641 IR instructions, 3.7 MB, 158 bytes per IR
  instruction, `Fast`): 20.6 percent reloads from stack slots, 7.6 spills, 7.3 loads and 4.0 stores through pointers, 12.6 immediates
  (40 000 `movabs`: 20 000 are the callee address of a `callq *%rax`, 10 000 a 32-bit mask), 2.4 register copies, 45.5 everything else;
  the frame is 110 KB (one slot per value). (The small code model and the spills: next section.)
## llvm: small code model, calls through the GOT, blocks in execution order, narrow masks (yavs-llvm, #679, 2026-10-24)

- **Decision: with the code arena the code is generated for the small code model with position independent code** (`jit.rs` `model`;
  the arena is the precondition: code, stubs and data are within 2 GiB of each other). A call of a runtime callback is `call [rip+got]`
  (6 bytes) where it was `movabs rax, imm64; call rax` (12), globals and tables are RIP-relative. The callbacks are declared
  `nonlazybind` (`Gen::effects`, `Gen::declare`): without it the linker makes a PLT stub per callback and object and every call pays a
  second jump (measured: the stubs cost what the shorter call saves, cycles level). Without the arena (other targets,
  `YAVS_LLVM_ARENA=0`) and with `YAVS_LLVM_CODEMODEL=large` the JIT default is kept. The model is part of the key of the object cache
  (`target_id`). A section that does not fit the arena is a hard stop in the small model (`arena.rs` `overflow`: a 32-bit displacement
  to memory outside the arena would link to wrong code and the release linker does not check), where the large model maps it apart.
- **Decision: the blocks of a function are put in execution order before the cold ones go last** (`lower.rs` `layout`: from each block
  on to its likelier successor, by branch weights, else the earliest). Blocks were laid out in the order they were created, which puts
  the join block of a slow path before the fast path that leads to it: the unoptimised code generator emits blocks in layout order, so
  every guarded instruction cost `jne slow; jmp go` and a `jmp join` at the end of the fast path. The `jmp`s of the LEON3 `comb` copy
  fall from 39 937 to 24 616 (the rest are the cold paths' way back).
- **Decision: the low half of a load is a 4-byte load** (`jit.rs` `narrow_masks`, after the passes, unoptimised code generation only):
  `and (load i64 p), 0xffffffff` becomes `zext (load i32 p)`, a 2-instruction saving where the mask is a 10-byte `movabs` and an `and`
  (3 000 of the 26 000 `movabs` of the `comb` copy; the small model took 12 400, the callee addresses and constant addresses). It runs after the passes because a narrower load blocks the forwarding of a
  store to the same bytes (early-cse), which made the first version (at generation time) worse in the places where the stored value was
  a constant.
- **Measured, not kept:** the address of an access (`gep` of the base and the checked offset) made before the guard instead of after it,
  so that one value instead of two crosses the branch: 0.4 percent more code, cycles level or worse (the reloads of the three function
  arguments, the frame views, are a third of the stack traffic and a new block reloads them again, which this does not touch).
  Other optimiser pipelines on the same IR (`early-cse<memssa>`, a second round, `gvn`): code size level or larger.
- **Where the instructions of a large process go now** (LEON3 `comb` copy, 20 122 IR instructions, `Fast`): 448 257 machine
  instructions, 30 percent of them stack accesses (spills and reloads); a third of those are the reloads of the function's three
  arguments (the frame views) at the start of every block, 10.5 percent of all instructions. Registers cannot be reserved for them (the
  x86 target has no reserved-register switch) and the fast register allocator reloads what is live across a block at each block. **The
  deferred register stores (`regs.rs` `Live`, the suspect of #679) are not the source** for this process: they are off for a function
  whose liveness matrix is over `MAX_WORDS`, so every register is stored to the frame; where they are on (`exec_comb` of neorv32,
  4 531 IR instructions) they save: 29 248 stack accesses and 90 901 instructions against 33 308 and 95 577 with them off
  (`YAVS_NODEFER`, a temporary switch, not kept). Raising the cap made the 20 000-instruction process read outside a heap object (#710, see "llvm: a stepped definition is read back from the frame").
  The spills that are left are values of the guards themselves (a checked offset, an address) that cross the branch of each guard, one
  new block per guard: the levers left are fewer blocks per IR instruction (guards that share a slow path, redundant bounds checks of the
  temporary area: the same `len` and constant bounds are tested instruction after instruction) or a block-local allocator that keeps the
  three views in registers.

## IR optimiser round 13: repeated drives of one driver are done once (yavs-ir `opt/drives.rs`, #667, 2026-10-24)

Decision (landed): **a process's zero-delay drive that a later zero-delay drive of the same elements deletes is delayed down the control
flow and dropped on the paths that drive again** (partial dead code elimination, `opt/drives.rs`, after the walk and the loop motion of
processes and before `memo`; processes only, off under a debugger, `YAVS_NO_DRIVES=1` turns it off, a switch of the fingerprint). The
LRM reading (10.5.2.2): a new transaction deletes the transactions of its driver at or after its time, so with both drives at delay zero
and the second reached in the same activation the first never reaches the update phase, whatever the modes (transport, inertial) and
whatever pulse-rejection limit the second has (it only deletes more). Hence:

- **What is dropped and copied.** The drive and the instructions that build its waveform (the allocated block, the stores and copies into
  it, the temporaries and constants only they read; none of them can fail) move as a unit. A drive is a candidate when its waveform is one
  element whose first word is a stored constant 0, it has no `reject`, and its target is a `SigVal` of a constant length and an offset
  that is a constant or a register defined once (a loop over the elements of a signal array has its offsets in such registers: the
  second drive of an iteration uses the same register). Registers defined once that the unit reads stay where they are. Two drives are
  the same when instance signal, offset (the same constant or the same register) and length are, **without the driver slot**: a record
  assigned whole and then by field gets two slots of one kernel driver.
- **Where the copies go.** The blocks in which the drive is still delayed are found like a topological order (a block joins when every
  predecessor joined and passes the drive on, so cycles and joins entered by an undelayed path never join); a block that ends with the drive
  delayed into a block that did not join gets a copy at its end (a `CondBr` edge is split by a new block, a `Case` cannot be split, so
  its arms all take the drive or the copy goes in front of the `Case`). The copy goes before the first instruction that can see or change
  the driver's transactions: a drive onto elements that may overlap (different instance signals, or constant disjoint ranges, are passed),
  `DriveSlot`, `SigScatter` (a whole record driven by one instruction, #677: a barrier in the first version, a footprint of its own since round 14), `Disconnect`, `Force`, `Release`, `Driving`, `DrivingValue`, a call of a procedure, a protected method, an indirect or
  foreign call; before a wait it goes in front of the wait's `Stmt` (`static_wait` wants the marker first). Reports and function calls do not
  matter. At most six copies per drive, and the drive must be dropped on at least one path, so code never grows for nothing. Each path
  still does the drive exactly once or not at all, and never later than the instruction that could tell.
- **What stays.** Drives with a delay, a `reject` limit, several waveform elements, a target of a dynamic offset not held in a register
  defined once, a drive after which the same block drives other elements through a shared waveform block, a drive whose statement reads
  memory (a variable, a loaded value). A default followed by an override after a join (`if a then ..; end if; if b then x <= ..`) is
  a mixed join: the drive is done on the path that did not skip it (tail duplication would be needed).
- **Cost.** The pass runs on a process only when two drives of it have the same static target, over blocks that are cut into per-block
  event lists (drives, barriers) so that a drive costs one walk over the blocks it is still delayed in: about +0.1 G host instructions in
  start-up of `neorv32_dual_full` (4.5 G for 1 us of simulated time), none of it per activation.

Host instructions (`perf stat` `instructions:u`, `--threads 1`, bench builds, warm world, deterministic), main at da793761 before / after, G:

| design | interp | llvm |
|---|---|---|
| `neorv32_single_min` | 44.85 / 42.76 (-4.7 %) | 61.35 / 59.14 (-3.6 %) |
| `neorv32_dual_full` | 29.94 / 29.61 (-1.1 %) | 50.59 / 50.77 (+0.4 %) |
| `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` | 91.54 / 90.37 (-1.3 %) | 92.21 / 92.25 (0.0 %) |
| `fletcher_bufferreader` | 36.48 / 36.37 (-0.3 %) | 38.07 / 38.04 (-0.1 %) |
| `sc5_fifo_repack`, `sc5_timestamp`, `poc_stat_histogram` | 0.0 % | 0.0 % |
| `poc_cache_cpu` | 15.10 / 15.01 (-0.6 %) | 16.85 / 16.81 (-0.2 %) |
| `vai_window_gen_interlock` | 495.21 / 495.22 (0.0 %) | 236.45 / 236.43 (0.0 %) |
| `poc_arith_addw` | 235.89 / 235.89 (0.0 %) | 224.18 / 224.16 (0.0 %) |
| `grlib_leon3mp` | 891.98 / 892.53 (+0.1 %) | |

(`--tier=llvm` of `neorv32_dual_full`: the 0.4 percent is in the tier's compile and run mix, the interpreter does 1.1 percent less.)

Why less than the 2 to 4 percent #667 estimated: the 17 percent repeated drives it counted were by driver, not by element. In
`neorv32_single_min` 5.6 M of the 5.7 M repeats are one process (the bus gateway's `request`, a loop over five ports with ten field
drives each, enabled ports drive twice) and this pass removes them; `counter_increment` drives the elements of one vector driver one by
one (not repeats, the kernel's marks cannot tell), `exec_comb` keeps the repeats behind joins. After the pass 4.8 M of 16 M scalar
drives of `neorv32_single_min` still count as repeats by the kernel's marks, almost all of them element-wise drives of one vector driver.
The kernel side (a pending-drive merge, option 2 of #667) was not touched: a repeat there already costs one push.

## IR optimiser round 14: record defaults (yavs-ir `opt/drives.rs`, yavs-lower, #667, #677, 2026-10-24)

Decision (landed): **the drive-deleting pass sees `SigScatter`, and every record part is a scatter again.**

- **Footprints.** A drive is written as `Fp::D(key)` (instance signal, offset, length: as before); a scatter as `Fp::S(leaf signals of its
  table (sorted), part)` where the part is `None` (the whole value, so every element of every leaf signal) or the pair of registers
  `(first, outer)` of the outermost array, each a constant or a register defined once. `covers` says what a later zero-delay write
  deletes: a drive the same key; a scatter without a part every drive of one of its leaf signals; a scatter with a part (or without) a
  scatter of the same or fewer leaf signals and the same part (equal constants or equal registers). A drive never covers a scatter (the
  length of a leaf signal is not known to the pass). `apart` says what certainly shares no element (other signals, or constant disjoint
  ranges of one): such a write is no barrier, any other overlap that is not a kill is one. Before, every scatter was a barrier.
- **A scatter is a unit that may be delayed** like a drive: its delay is the constant 0 and it has no rejection limit, its source and
  descriptor are addresses of the constant pool (`AddrOf` of a constant: the memory cannot change before a copy), its operands (delay,
  part) are registers defined once; it builds nothing, so the unit is the instruction alone. A copy gets an operand list of its own at
  the end of `Func::operands`. A default that reads a signal or a variable (`r <= other` as the default) is not delayed: it is the
  later write, the kill, that does not need to move, and the default stays.
- **Why the lowering change.** With the scatter dropped where an override follows, a record part needs no leaf-by-leaf code: `Fx::overridden_signals`
  and the `overridden` field are gone, and `port_req(i) <= term; if en then port_req(i) <= req_i; port_req(i).stb <= ..` is two scatters
  and a drive, the first dropped on the enabled path. The gain comes from the lowering change, not from the pass alone: instructions,
  bench builds, `--tier=interp --threads 1`, G, `neorv32_single_min` main at a4afa75d 38.05, new pass with the leaf-by-leaf restriction kept
  38.06 (nothing changes: the parts that matter are leaf drives there), new pass without it 37.38 (-1.8 %); `grlib_leon3mp` 670.5, 670.3,
  661.9 (-1.3 %); the other designs within noise (`docs/STATUS.md`).
- **Not done, measured or argued.** (a) A field drive after a scatter (`port_req(i).stb`) deletes one leaf of the scatter before it. Masking
  that leaf (a skip bit in the table or a mask operand, no new table: the pass cannot add constants) would split the pack run the
  scatter writes in one assignment (`write_leaf` joins adjacent leaves of one driver) into two, so it is argued to cost more than the one
  leaf transaction it saves; not built and not measured. (b) Repeats behind a join (tail duplication): a static probe over `neorv32_single_min` (each of the 1.9 k attempts of the pass)
  found a kill behind a join that some path enters without the drive in 33 attempts. The pass relies on registers defined once; a
  duplicated tail defines them twice, so everything up to the point where the paths meet again would have to be renamed as a whole.
  Not cheap, not done; no dynamic weight was measured. (c) Two parts picked by registers that hold the same value but are
  computed twice (`q(sel) <= a; if c then q(sel) <= b`) are not the same part until value numbering shares the registers.

## Specialised copies start after the declarative part (yavs-ir `opt.rs` `drop_declarations`, #678, 2026-10-24)

Decision (landed): **the optimised copy of a process for one instance (`Program::copy_of`) jumps from its entry straight to the
body; the blocks of the declarative part are one jump to themselves.** A copy takes over only between two activations of the shared
code (`Machine::specialise`: the process waits at its one wait statement in its root frame, the variables are in their slots, the
registers are the copy's own), so the declarative part never runs in it, and the optimiser's walk skips it anyway (`Opt::pass`:
blocks before `Func::body` are not walked). For a process of records with generic bounds it was the largest part of the copy: the
descriptors and initial values of the variables (the LEON3 integer unit's `comb`: 34 164 lines of IR dump in the copy, 24 486 without;
`spec_copy_ir` of 72 copies at 20 us of the LEON3 run 143 387 to 120 115, 16 percent; `neorv32_dual_full` 39 013 to 38 262).
Registers a frame starts with (defined once by a constant or an address) that the body reads keep their definition, moved to the
entry block, since the frame template is built from the definitions. No instruction counts of the interpreter change (`docs/STATUS.md`): the gain is code the tiers need not compile and the predecoder need not scan, and a copy under the memo's 6000
instructions.

What this does **not** do (#678 stays open): the 1 127 `LayoutOf` and 1 570 `Field` that remain in the copy of the LEON3 `comb` are
in the body. They read the descriptors of the process variables (`registers`, records with array fields whose bounds are generics)
through frame slots the declarative part filled, so the walk knows nothing of their contents, and the instance data being frozen
does not help. Folding them needs the declarative part evaluated for the instance: the frame slots it writes once and the body never
writes (the descriptors) as constant facts at the body entry and after each suspension, and a layout of a record type from a
descriptor whose words are known (`Ty::layout` takes the bytes). The interpreter's per-type layout memo and the `FieldOf` fusion
already make a `LayoutOf` plus `Field` cheap, so the gain is mostly in the compiled code (the address checks).

## Idle skip, round 4: concurrent conditional assignments, conditions of generics (yavs-sem, yavs-elab, #521, #678, 2026-10-24)

Round 2 and 3 gave the pure processes the idle skip, with the conditions their reads are under, but `t <= a when c else b;` (a
concurrent conditional assignment, a process with the sensitivity list of every signal of every arm) was left out, and a condition
of generics (`... when TRACE_PORT_EN else ...`, `... and NAP_EN else '0'`, as the CPU designs write them for features a configuration
leaves out) was no literal. `neorv32_single_min` woke those on every event of the signals their dead arms read (`cpu_trace`, `i_addr_i`
of every PMP region) and assigned the constant again.

- **`Db::pure_cond_reads`**: the reads of a concurrent conditional assignment (not guarded or postponed, delay default or `transport`,
  no `after`, every waveform a value, the expressions of the pure shapes of round 2). A waveform is read under its own condition and the
  negation of the earlier conditions that are one literal, a condition under those negations; the target's indices unconditionally.
  A condition the walk cannot express adds no literal (a weaker condition only makes the read count more often).
- **Conditions of constants** (`Db::const_cond`): a boolean expression of constants and generics declared outside the process (entity,
  architecture, block, generate, package), predefined operators only, with at least one name in it, is a literal (`GuardLit` with `pos`
  `GUARD_CONST`, `sig` the expression, `eq` whether it must be true). The elaborator evaluates it for the instance (`Walker::idle_parts`,
  `Model::eval`, as `if generate` does): a conjunction with a literal that is false never holds and goes, a true literal drops out of
  its conjunction, and a read with no conjunction left is no read, so an event on a signal only a dead arm reads arms nothing. A value
  that cannot be worked out leaves the literal in place (weaker).
- **`and` in a condition**: the literals of the parts that are literals are necessary for the condition to be true, so the body or arm
  is read only under them (`cond_lits(c, false)`); the negation for the later arms still needs the exact form (`cond_lits(c, true)`,
  one literal), since `not (a and b)` is not `not a`. This also lets `if sig_a = sig_b and GENERIC then` carry the generic.
- **Why it is the same run**: as in round 3, an activation does what the last one did when every signal the last one read, under the
  conditions it read it, is unchanged; a constant does not change, so an arm it rules out is never read. `YAVS_IDLE_SKIP=check`
  runs the activations the kernel would skip and fails when one assigns something else: `perf.rs` `idle_skip_changes_nothing` with the
  new `idle_when` (off, on, check equal; 586 of 2715 activations skipped), `tests/corpus/delta/idle_when.vhd` (blessed from the
  reference simulator), and the real-world designs `neorv32_single_min`, `neorv32_dual_full`, `poc_cache_cpu`, `fletcher_bufferreader`
  and `sc5_fifo_repack` in check mode print what main prints.
- **Not covered**: selected assignments (`with s select`), simple concurrent assignments (every read is unconditional), an
  assignment inside a generate whose condition is not a constant of the instance, conditions through a user function. `resize(INIT,
  q'length)` in PoC's `ffdre` (the other item of the hand-off) is a per-call computation inside a subprogram, not a read: it needs the
  call's constant arguments to reach the callee (#701).
- **Measured**: see "IR optimiser round 13" in `docs/STATUS.md`.



## Native ieee calls: one-word operands read and written in place (yavs-interp `ieee.rs`, `exec.rs`, yavs-lib `closure.rs`, #691, 2026-10-24)

- **Decision: `ieee::small` (the one-word view of an array operand of 1 to 64 elements without a metavalue) returns `Option`, not
  `R<Option>`, and reads the fat pair, the descriptor and the first plane block with `words` (three bounds-checked reads of the
  common spaces, temporary memory tested before the jump table, `Machine::mem_temp_first`). `None` for anything unusual (unreadable
  address, longer array, metavalue, a missing argument): the general path then reads the operand again and words the error, so the
  fast path has no error plumbing and no `Fault` in its return value.** `put_small` writes the 72 bytes of the result (fat pair,
  descriptor, one plane block) with one append to temporary memory (`Machine::temp_words`: the addresses follow from the start of
  the block) instead of `temp_alloc` (zero fill), two address additions and a `wr` through `obj_mut`. Results and warnings are
  unchanged (`ieee_native.rs` differential tests); the interpreter's op sequence and the work counters are unchanged.
- Per call, stepped instructions of `a + b` on two 9-element `unsigned` (`poc_arith_addw`, interpreter): `ieee::add` with its two
  operand reads, `fat_dim` and the result write 537 to 177; `to_integer` of one operand about 200 to 109. The rest of a native call
  is outside the function: about 60 instructions of `Op::CallIeee` (argument cells, function lookup, result and flag handling) and, on
  the compiled tier, about 190 of the callback layer (`yavs_rt_native`, `native_frame`) per call.
- **#691: `closure()` keeps a `HashSet` next to the ordered `Vec` of files (discovered, done) and of the files on the DFS stack
  (cycle check only when the file is on the stack).** The output order is unchanged. `olo_axi_master_full` at time 0 (interp, steady
  state): 623.4 M to 605.8 M instructions (-2.8 %).
- Not done, with the reason: (1) `std_match` and `to_hstring` as natives: none of the measured designs (`uvvm_util_rand`,
  `osvvm_axis_random`, `sc5_fifo_repack`) spends time in them, their time is in the libraries' own VHDL string code and `textio`
  natives. (2) The operand convention (a fat pair in temporary memory built by `NewDope` + `NewPair` from the `AllocReadVec` /
  `AllocCat` result: `NewPair` and `NewDope` are 10 percent of the ops of `poc_arith_addw`): a native taking data address and
  bounds in registers would save those ops and the two dependent reads in the native; that is an IR change (#697). The callback layer of the compiled tier is #698.

## Kernel round 20: a lean wide bus is finished in one pass; whole-word entries; what a skip of unchanged plane entries costs (yavs-kernel, #519, 2026-10-24)

Source of the numbers: `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` (512-bit buses through ~35 signals that each change about once a clock), bench
builds, `perf stat` on core 13, minimum of 5 alternating runs; instruction counts are exact, cycles are those of a host at load 20 to 30.

- **Where the kernel time of a wide bus went.** Counters (a temporary build, not kept): 34 M plane words change over the run
  (43 per delta cycle), 80% of them on a lean signal that keeps no codes and no activity stamps (`lean`, `codes` empty, `inactive`).
  `finish_pend` finished each of them through `finish_word` and `update_word`: ~250 instructions a changed word, of which the real
  work (xor, two blends, the block's event record) is ~40. The rest was per-word dispatch on flags that do not change within a bus
  (`lean`, `watched`, `fine`, `codes.is_empty()`), three `SmallVec` derefs and `Option` bounds checks per word, a sort check of the
  pending words, and a `cover` per word.
- **Decision:** `Signal::finish_words_lean` finishes every pending word of such a signal in one loop (slices taken once, flags tested
  once, the words in pending order unless a waiter of a part needs the runs in element order, one `cover` for the whole bus when
  only whole-signal waiters exist; the runs of a part-waited bus are noted per word as before). The cover of the words is the hull
  and the run counts add up, so `changed`, `nruns` (the `events` counter) and the wake-ups are those of the per-word path. A plane
  word entry (element 64k, 64 elements) in `commit_planes_run` is stored and marked whole, without the shift and mask paths.
  Test: `delta_paths::a_lean_wide_bus_wakes_and_changes_like_one_with_full_history` (changes, wake-ups of whole-bus, inner and
  block-crossing waiters, at 1 and 4 threads, against a bus that keeps every element's history).
- **Result:** writer 83.8 G to 77.1 G instructions (-8.2%), 30.1 G to 28.6 G cycles (-4.9%); the rest of the realbench set is
  unchanged in instructions (geometric mean 0.99, only the wide-vector tests move). `lean` stays an elaboration decision (round 18).
- **Measured and not taken: skipping a plane entry that holds the value already** (as `commit_code` does for one element, #420):
  at commit time 37% of the writer's plane entries (21 M of 58 M) and 49% of the reader's find the driving and effective value equal
  (`skip_ok` signals). Skipping them costs a block compare on every entry and saves little, because the `m == 0` path of
  `update_word` was already cheap (~35 instructions): writer +0.8% instructions, reader -1.6%, cycles level. Not kept.
- **Measured, not changed:** 6 M of the writer's 58 M plane entries repeat an entry of the same driver within one batch (10%; a
  default and its override): removing them at commit is worth ~0.7%; at the source that is #667 (IR optimiser).
- **Remaining kernel cost of a bus** (writer, per delta cycle of 100 K instructions): `finish_words_lean` 7.8%, `commit_planes_run` 4.0%,
  `finish_direct` 3.1%, `cycle` 3.0%, `assign_wide_fast` 2.7%, `commit_out` 2.7%, `Buf::write_to` 2.5%, `canonical_changed` 1.8% (a
  bus with a waiter on a part keeps a run list: ~8 runs a word with random data, sorted, merged and scanned by the waiters three
  times a cycle; ~4% of the writer in all). Exact run lists could only be replaced by a split of the signal at the waiters'
  boundaries (nexus splitting in the reference simulator), a larger change that also touches ports and observers: not started.
- **Measured and not taken (whole-picture round, same designs):** fat LTO with one codegen unit (writer +0.6% instructions, cycles
  level, reader level), `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3` (writer -2.8% instructions and 1 to 2% cycles, reader level or +5% cycles: not
  shippable to generic hosts, not a clear win; superseded for the x86_64 release archives by "x86-64-v3 baseline" below), `--threads 2/4/8` (6.5 s to 7.6/8.3/8.3 s), a single-pass `canonical_changed` and an
  aligned `Buf::write_to` (0.0% instructions each). Neither design compiles anything under `--tier=auto`; the layers of the
  interpreter side (dispatch 24 to 33%, record layout and copies 15 to 16%) and the shares of the kernel are in `docs/STATUS.md`
  "Fletcher writer and reader against the reference simulator".


## Kernel round 21: a wide bus with a waiter on a part lists its changes per cell; the split of a leaf at the waiters' boundaries is not built (yavs-kernel, #519, 2026-10-24)

Task (user, 2026-10-24): split signals that have a waiter on a part into kernel signals along the union of the boundaries that waiters,
drivers and port maps use (`NetGraph::loc`), so each piece is waited on whole and the `fine` run lists go away. Source of the numbers:
`fletcher_bufferwriter_512`, `tools/build-bench.sh --features llvm` builds, `perf stat` on core 13 at a load of 20 to 40, minimum of 6
alternating runs after the compilation cache of each binary was warm (the first two runs of a new binary still pay cache work: read
instruction counts from the third on).

- **What the design does.** Five wide signals get `fine` in the writer: three of 578 elements (a stream word of one flag bit, 512 data bits, a
  64-bit strobe and one more bit, cut at 1, 513 and 577, waited on by three concurrent statements each) and two of 74 elements (cut at 64 and 73). Every one
  is driven whole (`0+578`, `0+74`) by one process (a `CopyProcess` of a stream slice, or the interpreted `reg_proc` of the FIFO); no
  port edge and no idle read touches them. So the pieces would each have a whole-signal waiter, but the driver writes all pieces and
  the other readers read the bus whole.
- **Decision: the split is not built.** A leaf is stored in exactly one kernel signal in every layer: `LeafLoc` is one signal and a
  base, `kref`/`kpart`/`kelem` return one signal, `InstSig` is `{signal, ty, off}`, `ProcDriver` names one `DriverId`, the compiled
  tier's `TierSig` is the same, and waves, VHPI, DAP and coverage resolve an object through those (69 call sites outside the
  tests). Packs (#686) only join leaves into a signal, the opposite direction. A split turns each whole-bus drive, read, wait and
  `'event` in the interpreter and in compiled code into a loop over pieces, in exchange for at most the `fine` cost below, and moves
  the small pieces off the lean no-codes path of the bus. Not worth the risk to
  waves, ports, force and resolution for a bound of 5%.
- **The bound.** A temporary kernel build that noted the hull of the changed elements of a word (inexact: 0.14% more wake-ups) in
  place of its runs: 62.08 G to 58.62 G instructions (-5.6%), 25.9 G to 24.4 G cycles. That is the most any removal of the run lists
  can give on this design, and a split cannot reach it (it adds the drives and reads above).
- **Decision: cells (`Signal::cuts`, `Signal::watch_part`, `note_cells`, `Config::cells`, `YAVS_CELLS=off`).** The kernel keeps the
  signal whole but registers the offsets where a waited range (or an idle reader's range) starts or ends. They cut the signal into
  cells; every waited range is a union of cells. A word update that changes more than two runs notes the hull of its changed elements
  once per cell it changes (`note_cells`: a binary search over the few cuts, one note when the word holds none), and a waiter wakes
  when a note overlaps its range, which is exactly when an element of one of its cells changed. Exactness: a note lies in one cell and
  a cell with a change gets a note, so overlap with a union of cells means the cell changed. Notes of one cycle may overlap the exact
  runs another path noted (a release or deposit and plane entries), which the wake scan (`Waiters::take_woken`: sorted, disjoint runs)
  cannot take, so a signal with cuts joins overlapping runs once a cycle (`canonical_changed` now joins runs that overlap, not only
  those that touch; the first version of the new test failed there). The `events` counter keeps counting runs per word. Signals of
  64 elements or fewer, and every signal once an observer wants value changes (waves, coverage, VHPI, DAP: `Observer::wants_value_changes`),
  keep the exact runs (`Signal::cuts` cleared, never filled). Lean events (round 18) are independent: they decide what history a
  block keeps, cells decide what `changed` lists.
- **Tests:** `delta_paths::a_wide_bus_wakes_the_same_per_cell_as_per_run` (five waiters including a one-element one at a block edge and
  one across all blocks, direct and resolved buses, lean and not, forces and deposits, 1 and 4 threads, against `cells: false`, with
  and without a value-change observer); difftest 520/520 on interp, llvm and auto at 1 and 4 threads; the OSVVM and UVVM suites give
  the same results as before (UVVM 131 passed 6 skipped, OSVVM identical); an FST of the writer is byte-identical with and without
  `YAVS_CELLS=off`.
- **Result** (bench builds, core 13): writer 61.47 G to 58.74 G instructions (0.956), 35.4 G to 33.5 G cycles (0.946); reader 22.63 G
  to 22.67 G (1.002), cycles level. The update path of a resolved bus with few runs per word keeps its runs (the cutoff of two runs):
  without it the reader paid +0.6% instructions for hulls it did not need.
- **Left:** the writer's remaining `fine`-related cost is the cell notes and `canonical_changed` (~1%). The elaboration split would
  remove only the waiter side, and only if the interpreter, the compiled tier and the observers took pieces; revisit if a design
  appears whose waited parts are driven by separate processes at exactly the cuts (then the pieces would be whole signals with whole
  drivers and no one-to-many path is needed).


## Kernel round 22: the per-delta bookkeeping of CPU-style designs (yavs-kernel, #519, #521, 2026-10-25)

Task (orchestrator, 2026-10-24): the kernel is the largest diffuse share of the CPU-style designs (neorv32_single_min about 25% of cycles,
poc_arith_addw 26%, the fletcher reader 28%, hdlm_lfsr 36%); measure the fixed per-delta-cycle and per-wake costs and cut the biggest items.
No timing cores this round: every number is an instruction count, `perf stat instructions:u` of a whole run (`--threads 1 --no-cache`, bench
builds, one binary against the other) or a `tools/stepcount` window of 100 delta cycles (cycle 20000 on; 1000 and 3000 for rtl_fan and
rtl_chain), where "kernel" counts `yavs-kernel` including the `Ctx` callbacks of `process.rs`.

- **Whole-run share** (`perf record -e instructions:u`): the kernel is 54% (neorv32_single_min), 35% (poc_arith_addw), 61%
  (fletcher_bufferreader), 16% (hdlm_lfsr), 11% (rtl_fan), 66% (rtl_chain) of the instructions. No function is above 7.2% (`finish_direct`
  of neorv32); the per-delta cost is spread over the stages of one signal change. One delta cycle of neorv32_single_min (73 K instructions, 15
  process runs, 10 changed signals, 25 changed plane words, 22 idle skips) is, kernel stages only: process-side `Ctx` reads and assigns 11.3 K,
  wake 8.1 K (`take_woken` 3.8 K, `arm_readers` 3.4 K), finish 5.8 K (`update_word` about 410 instructions a changed word), commit 5.2 K,
  `run_batch` and `order` 4.0 K, the `cycle` wake loop and idle filter 3.4 K. A delta of rtl_chain (one process, one bit) is 878 kernel
  instructions: `run_one` 193, `finish_direct` 176, `wake_sole` 116, `cycle` 115, `assign_code_fast` 94, `commit_code` 80, `update` 41,
  `last_delta` 34, `run_until` 28. An activation of rtl_fan costs about 100 instructions in the `run_batch` loop (the rest of its 667 is the
  interpreter).
- **Decisions** (each a measured drop of instructions, results unchanged; full-run instructions of neorv32_single_min unless named):
  - `order()` sorts its keys with the unstable sort into a buffer kept between batches (-0.4%; fletcher reader -0.5%). A key names its process (the
    low 32 bits are the process number or its complement), so equal keys are the same process and stability buys nothing; the stable
    sort needed a scratch allocation per batch.
  - The small-list wake of `cycle` (a signal with at most 8 waiters in one list) takes any number of changed runs and wakes while it checks,
    in one pass (-0.3%; fletcher reader -0.3%, hdlm_lfsr -0.3%). A waiter that is not resident and alive hands the rest of the list to the scan;
    waking is idempotent (`ProcMeta::ready`) and in list order, so the scan wakes the others in the same order.
  - `arm_readers` tests a read of part of a signal of at most 64 elements by mask (the changed runs are folded to bits once per event, the reader
    keeps its bits), keeps a guard of one literal in the reader entry (58% of the guards of neorv32; the others stay alternatives of
    conjunctions) and is not called for a signal nobody reads (-0.84%; fletcher reader -0.71%). Readers are a `Reader` record, the guard a
    `ReaderGuard` (`One` or `Any`).
  - `update_word` refreshes the `codes` of the groups of eight elements that hold a change, not of every group between the first and the last
    (-0.2%), and `take_woken` leaves an already ordered list alone (together -0.5%; fletcher reader -0.55%).
  - **The list of woken waiters is ordered by registration only for a shuffled run** (`take_woken(.., ordered)`, `ordered = rng.is_some()`):
    the wake order decides neither the order a batch runs in nor the order it commits in (`order()` sorts the batch by process), a waiter listed
    in several chunk lists is woken once by the idempotent wake, and the shuffle takes the list in the order it is given (-0.6%). The sort and
    dedup of every multi-list event were 0.9% of neorv32.
  - The chunk index of a signal's waiters is rebuilt only when a list went empty (-0.25%).
  - **A waiter of a signal of at most 64 elements keeps the elements it waits for as bits** (`Waiter::mask`) and the changed runs are folded to
    bits once per event (`Hits`): the hit test of the scan and of the small-list path is one `and` instead of a range overlap per waiter and run
    (-0.64%). Wider signals keep the range tests.
  - **The `Ctx` callbacks of every signal read and drive are inlined into the interpreter** (-3.6%, -3.1%, -3.0% on neorv32_single_min,
    poc_arith_addw, fletcher_bufferreader on top of the commits above; cycles in the totals below): `Ctx::read_into` and
    the fast paths `assign_code_fast`, `assign_planes_fast`, `assign_bytes_fast` are `#[inline(always)]`, the public entry points `assign_code`,
    `assign_blocks` and `assign_bytes` are `#[inline]` with the slow remainder in `assign_*_slow` (`#[inline(never)]`), and `wake_sole` is
    inlined into `finish_direct`. Each of these was a call of 85 to 130 instructions whose first and last 20 to 30 were pushes, pops and
    argument marshalling (a `SigRef`, an `Option<Range>`, a `Time` and a `DelayMode` through memory); the profile of the round had them as
    separate symbols (`read_into` 3.4%, `assign_planes_fast` 4.2% of the instructions of the windows). The binary grows 0.3%. The tier of
    compiled code already inlined the `*_now` forms.
  - The small accessors of `Ctx` (`planes`, `planes_view`, `bytes_view`, `now`, `delta`, `cycle`, `timed_out`, ...) and `Buf::bytes` are `#[inline]`
    (19 to 25 instruction calls, 6 a delta on neorv32), `commit_code` is inlined into `commit_out` and `run_one` (-0.3% neorv32, -0.7% fletcher
    reader, -1.1% rtl_chain) and `arm_readers_of` into its two callers (-0.2%, -0.6%, +0.1% rtl_chain).
  - Together (main at a133e50c, whole runs): neorv32_single_min 39.82 G to 37.12 G (-6.8%), poc_arith_addw 156.74 G to 149.61 G (-4.5%),
    fletcher_bufferreader 22.60 G to 21.33 G (-5.6%), hdlm_lfsr 67.21 G to 66.41 G (-1.2%), rtl_chain 3.369 G to 3.288 G (-2.4%), rtl_fan level.
    Before the rebase, on 2cf30ee4, the same set was -7.5%, -4.7%, -6.2%, -1.2%, -2.4%. Cycles, minimum of 4
    alternating runs on one loaded core of the first CCD (no timing core was used, so these are indications): neorv32_single_min 16.16 G to
    15.04 G (-6.9%), poc_arith_addw 45.7 G to 43.6 G (-4.5%), fletcher_bufferreader 8.65 G to 8.28 G (-4.3%), hdlm_lfsr 17.7 G to 17.5 G
    (-0.9%). Per delta cycle (stepcount windows): neorv32 73.3 K to 67.0 K, addw 46.4 K to 44.3 K, fletcher reader 12.3 K to 11.6 K; tables in
    `docs/STATUS.md` "Kernel round 22".
- **Measured and not taken:**
  - Splitting the plain readers (whole signal, no guard) of `arm_readers` into their own array that is armed without a test: only 48% of the
    readers of neorv32 are plain, `arm_readers` got dearer (+145 instructions a delta) and the fletcher reader +0.8%. The cost is in the guarded and
    partial readers (10.0 M of the 13.4 M readers examined that were not armed already, 1.1 M armed), which the mask and the inline literal now
    answer.
  - Lean event bookkeeping (`Signal::set_lean_events`) for logic vectors of 9 to 64 elements: the per-element stamp loop of `update_word` is 11
    instructions a changed element (0.6% of neorv32), but only 542 of its 2021 signals qualify under the elaborator's facts and the whole-run
    effect was -0.1% (neorv32), -0.2% (fletcher reader), -0.3% (hdlm_lfsr), against a wider reach of the lean promise (an internal error for
    a `'last_event` of a part that the facts missed). Not kept.
  - `Signal::update_word` out of line (`#[inline(never)]`): +0.2% on neorv32 and addw; the call costs more than the spills it saves (the
    opposite of the `Ctx` callbacks, which are small and called from many places).
  - One lookup of the process record and a hoisted `!init && !postponed` in the `run_batch` loop: -0.4% on rtl_fan (the per-activation loop is
    ~100 instructions, 38 to set up a run, 60 to commit it), level elsewhere. Not kept; a summary flag set by the `Ctx` push paths is the next
    step (#733).
  - Waking in `finish_direct` for every signal with a small list of resident waiters, as `wake_sole` does for one (it would skip the changed list, the
    sort and the per-signal head of `cycle`, about 0.5% of neorv32): the edge-trigger and observer exclusions of `wake_sole` apply, and a wake
    before the other signals of the update are finished changes which cycles can take the clock batch. Not built then; built for signals of at
    most 64 elements as the wake plan ("Wake plan", 2026-11-08), which moved no clock batch on the CPU designs.
  - Lazy arming (comparing the event cycle of each signal a process reads when it is woken instead of arming its readers at every event) costs
    about as much as arming on neorv32 (37 woken processes per delta, each checking all its reads when it is not armed, against 53 reader entries
    examined per delta) and loses the early exit of an already armed reader. Not built.
- **Left, filed:** #733 (a summary flag for a quiet activation in the `run_batch` loop), #734 (a narrow signal's event stamps, run lists and
  codes as one mask: `update_word` is ~410 instructions a changed word), #735 (the GC observer's Hook and Mutex every delta of a serial
  process).
- **Idea of the reference simulator's kernel used (rewritten for ours):** a waiter is attached to the net it waits on, so an event on a net
  wakes its list with no range test (the reference splits nets at the waiters' boundaries); ours keeps the signal whole and, for a signal of at
  most 64 elements, makes the range test a bit test, as round 21 did for wide signals with cells. A wake is a flag test on the waiting object
  (`pending`) and an append to the run queue, in whatever order the event lists them; ours already had the flag (`ready`) and now also stops
  ordering the list it appends from. Different: the reference runs processes in queue order, ours sorts each batch by process
  (the commit order is a user decision, #252).
- **Soundness of the wake changes.** The woken set of every path is the one of the old scan (same hit, alive and hold tests); only the order
  in which `wake_proc` is called changed, and a batch is ordered by `order()` before it runs and commits (`ready_mono` records an already ordered
  list). A shuffled run (`Config::shuffle`) keeps the registration order, so a seed gives the schedule it gave. Tests:
  `signal::tests::unordered_wake_list_holds_the_same_processes`, the existing `Waiters` unit tests (now with `ordered` set),
  `idle_skip::guarded_reads_arm_only_while_the_condition_holds` (a read under one literal and under two alternatives; with the one-literal
  arm broken the check of `idle_check` stops the run), difftest 523/523 on
  interp, llvm and auto at 1 and 4 threads and with `--shuffle 7`, `cargo test --workspace`, the UVVM and OSVVM suites unchanged.
- **Found on the way (#736, fixed):** a panic while `run_batch` committed a process in place (the `idle_check` assertion, a broken invariant
  in `note_idle`) was reported for the next process of the batch, or panicked again past the end of it and hid the message; the unwind guard now
  keeps the index of the process it was running (`idle_skip::a_wrong_read_list_is_caught_by_the_check_and_names_the_process`).


## Kernel round 23: assignments in pieces stay direct entries, a quiet activation commits nothing (yavs-kernel, #521, #733, #735, 2026-10-25)

Task (orchestrator): the follow-ups of round 22 (#733 the `run_batch` loop per activation, #734 narrow-signal event masks, #735 the GC observer per
delta) and the next structural item of the fixed cost of a delta cycle. Instruction counts only (bench builds with `llvm`, `--threads 1`
`--no-cache`, `perf stat instructions:u` of whole runs, `tools/stepcount` windows of 100 delta cycles from cycle 20000), main at 27842f12
against the round.

- **Found: a record assigned field by field left the direct path (neorv32: 6 percent of a delta cycle, the largest item of the round).** `port_req(i)
  <= req_i; port_req(i).stb <= ...` is a run of assignments to the elements of one driver: a vector field, a scalar field, a vector field. A direct
  driver keeps its zero-delay entries of the run in `ProcState::out` (one element), `outv` (up to 64) and `outb`; the commit applies `out` before
  `outv`. `assign_planes_fast` and `assign_wide_fast` refused a vector after a one-element entry of the driver (they could not tell whether the skip
  test `direct_same_planes` was right with a pending entry in front of it) and `assign_code_fast` refused a scalar after a vector entry (`out` would
  be applied before it); the general path then moved every entry of the driver into its waveform (`spill_out`) and every later assignment of the run
  stayed there: `Waveform::schedule`, `apply_driver`, `compute_driving`, `update_effective`, about 1800 instructions per assignment, 2.4 of them a
  delta cycle of `neorv32_single_min`.
- **Decision: the order of a driver's entries in a run is "all `out`, then all `outv`", kept by `Ctx`.** A vector after a scalar needs no refusal (`out`
  is applied first, as made); it only gets no skip test while the driver has an entry in the run. A scalar after a vector entry becomes an `OutV` of
  one element (`planes` from the code), so it is applied after the vector it follows. `spill_out` already moves `out` first and `outv` after, which
  is the same order. The entry marks of a process of more than `MARKED_DRIVERS` drivers hold one kind per driver (the last made): every test of kind 1
  (the skip decisions) is made together with a test of kind 2 or after one, so the lossy mark is enough (`tests/direct_paths.rs` `mixed_direct_entry_kinds_apply_in_assignment_order`
  applies random mixes of scalar, vector and wide assignments with and without marks and compares the signal with a model; breaking the order
  fails it). `perf/mixed_entries.vhd` pins `update_general` at 0 and the direct commits.
  `realbench --compare` (run phase, interpreter and llvm, all 42 tests, one run per cell, instructions): geometric mean 1.00 (interpreter) and
  0.99 (llvm); `cpu` 0.97 and 0.95 (neorv32_single_min -10.1% and -11.3%); every other test within 1.00 +- 0.03 (warm-cache cells of the short
  tests move by a few percent between two builds; with `--no-cache` the cells above 1.02, checked one by one, are equal within 0.05%).
  Instructions of whole runs, main against the round: neorv32_single_min 36.90 G to 33.05 G (-10.4%; a delta cycle 70.4 K to 63.7 K in the
  program file, libc 1.3 K to 0.4 K), fletcher_bufferreader -0.8%, poc_arith_addw -0.5%.
- **#733: `ProcState::act` (`ACT_SLOW`: a timeout or an effect; `ACT_ASSIGNED`: a scheduled transaction, a direct entry or a phantom).** Every push
  path of `Ctx` sets its bit, `resumption` clears the byte, and the batch loop tests the byte instead of `sens`, `deadline`, `effects`, `scheduled`,
  `out`, `outv`, `outb` and `phantoms`: a quiet activation (a clocked process that assigned nothing) commits with two byte tests. A run also leaves
  the slot's `result` alone unless it failed (a store dropped the old value). `ProcState::check_flags` asserts in debug builds that no push path
  forgot its bit. `run_one` keeps the list tests (a single activation is nearly always an assigning one: the byte test cost 3 instructions
  there). rtl_fan 13.66 G to 13.18 G (-3.5%, 24 instructions an activation), rtl_chain -0.4%.
- **#735: `Observer::phase_due(phase)`, asked before the kernel makes a `Hook`.** `SharedGc` answers `NextCycle` from the shared heap
  (`gc_due`) without a hook: the 15-field hook was about 50 of the 80 instructions a delta that a serial process in a busy loop paid. hdlm_lfsr
  -0.2%. The lock stays (an atomic gauge in the heap would put a branch in every allocation of every heap). `phase`, `poll_end` keep their
  inlined fast path and the slow remainder out of line (`phase_observed` first version: +4% on rtl_chain, the call of a function that used to be
  inlined).
- **`SimControl::armed` is a dense `Vec<bool>`** (it was `ProcMeta::armed`, 72-byte records): the readers' loop of an event touches one byte per
  reader. -0.06% instructions on neorv32 (the loop costs 8 instructions a reader either way), fewer cache lines.
- **Measured and not taken:**
  - **Skipping the empty delta cycle after an activation whose assignments were all skipped** (asked by the LEON lane): the cycle is kept
    on purpose (delta numbers in reports, phases, `'last_event`, `docs/decisions.md` "Skipped unchanged assignments", #420), so deleting it is a
    decision for the user, not a kernel optimisation. Its cost, `tools/stepcount` on a clock and a register that re-assigns its value (3 cycles
    a period): the empty delta is 389 instructions against 2400 for each of the cycles with an activation (7.5 percent of a period). A guarded
    shortcut of `cycle` (no `update`, no change loop when nothing is due, nothing changed and nobody watches changes) made it 319 and the other
    cycles 40 dearer each (code motion in `cycle`): a net loss. The remaining 319 are `cycle` 129, `last_delta` 57, `next_queued` and `live` 85
    (the next time), `run_until` 25, `commit_callouts` 23.
  - **#734 (narrow-signal event masks):** with the profile of this round the parts are small: the folds of the changed runs to bits (`Hits::of`,
    the arm loop) are about 0.3 percent of neorv32 together, `canonical_changed` 0.5 percent (called 3.3 times a delta, 115 instructions a call), the
    per-element event stamps of `update_word` 0.76 percent. Keeping a mask next to the run list needs every producer (`note_run`, `cover`, `note_cells`,
    `finish_words_lean`) and every `changed.clear()` to keep it in step, and a stale bit is a spurious wake; dropping the list for masked signals
    saves the pushes (8 instructions a run) and still needs runs for `take_woken`. Not built; the stamps need the elaborator's facts (round 22).
  - `Shared` built once per batch: it holds slices of `SimControl`'s own fields, so it cannot persist; moving the rarely used fields (`names`,
    `live`, `interrupt`, `resolution`, `stop_severity`) behind one pointer saves about 12 instructions a batch (0.8 percent of rtl_chain, nothing
    on neorv32); not built.
  - The arm loop (`arm_readers_of`, 414 readers examined a delta cycle of neorv32, about 2.6 K instructions in `cycle` and `finish_direct`) and
    `CopyProcess::run` (2.65 runs a delta, 956 instructions each, about 10 parts): skipping a copied part whose source had no event would change
    what a deposit or a force on the target sees at the next activation; not built.

## Kernel round 24: the skip test that keeps missing, pending words in element order, the in-word commit of a register (yavs-kernel, #734, 2026-10-26)

Task (orchestrator): the small-RTL designs where yavs is still slower than sim1 under `--tier=auto` (head-to-head 6: `rtl_lfsr` 1.60, `lfsr64`
1.42, `rtl_chain` 1.29, `rtl_ff` 1.20), starting from #734; find where the per-event kernel cost goes and cut it for every clock-edge form. Bench
builds with `llvm`, `--threads 1`; `perf stat instructions:u` of whole warm runs (two untimed runs first: the first run of a binary leaves a
note in the compilation cache, the second makes the entries and costs up to 15% more), `tools/stepcount` windows of one clock period late in
the run; cycles as the minimum of 7 interleaved runs on one core claimed with `tools/claim core`. Main at 504f86ad against the round.

- **Where an activation goes** (per activation, compiled processes, one clock period): `rtl_ff` about 1100 instructions, of which the kernel
  (`run_batch` 125, `commit_codes` 55, the skip test 13, finish and commit loop 13) is about 206, the compiled body about 215 and the host layers
  between the kernel and compiled code (`InterpProcess::run`, `run_direct`, `run_cached`, `enter_on`, `view_again`, `drive_bit_now`, the
  `yavs_rt_*` callbacks, `save_kept`, `Program::func`) about 680; `rtl_lfsr` about 1530: kernel about 450 (`run_batch` 121, `finish_direct` 118,
  `commit_planes_run` 91, `direct_same_planes` 66, the inlined `Ctx` paths), compiled body 340, host layers about 600. sim1 runs both at about
  1000 to 1100 per activation in total. The host layers are filed as #766 (yavs-llvm and yavs-interp, other agents' area): the kernel alone
  cannot bring these designs to sim1. `rtl_chain` (interpreted: compiling is slower there) is 1640 instructions a delta cycle, the kernel about
  860 of them, spread over 10 functions of 25 to 260 instructions with no single item above 80 (the three `put_plane_code` of a one-element
  commit and finish). `#734` itself (the event stamps, run lists and codes of a signal of at most 64 elements) does not apply to any of the
  four: each holds its registers in one signal wider than 64 elements.
- **Edge forms.** Four `rtl_ff` variants (`if rising_edge(clk)`, `if clk'event and clk = '1'`, `if not clk'stable and clk = '1'`, `wait
  until rising_edge(clk)`) have identical work counters and identical kernel instructions per activation; the `wait until` form runs 128
  more interpreter instructions per activation (four more ops after the resumption), filed as #767.
- **Decisions** (each a measured drop of instructions, results unchanged):
  - **The skip test of a direct assignment is left out for a driver whose tests keep missing.** `Signal::direct_same` and `direct_same_planes`
    (#720: an assignment of the value the signal and driver hold makes no entry) cost 13 and 66 instructions a call and missed at every
    activation of a register whose value changes every cycle (a counter, a shift register, a toggling register): 4% of `rtl_lfsr`. Per driver
    (the first `SAME_DRIVERS` = 8 of a process, `ProcState::same`; later ones always ask), after `SAME_MISSES` = 8 misses in a row the next 248
    assignments make their entry without asking. Leaving the test out is always correct: the entry of an unchanged value commits, finishes
    with no event (`update_word` with an empty change mask, `commit_code` returning `None` for one element) and the delta cycle happens as with
    the skip. The state lives in `ProcState`, which every run writes: in the driver's `Waveform` (read only on this path) it was one more dirty
    cache line per activation and cost `rtl_ff` 3% of its cycles; one counter per process (not per driver) left neo level, because a process
    whose first assignments change silenced the test for the others. Idea of sim1: it turns off a fast driver update path when it stops
    paying (fewer than half the parts of a signal use it); ours is per driver and comes back after 248 assignments.
  - **Pending words in element order only where it matters.** `finish_pend` sorted the list of pending plane words of a signal at every update;
    the processes of the elements of a vector of registers commit in descending element order (seen on `lfsr64`, `rtl_lfsr` and `rtl_ff`; the
    batch is in process order), so it sorted a reversed list each time (57 instructions a word on `lfsr64`). Each word is finished
    on its own, so a plain signal nothing watches (`!watched`, its changed runs are only counted) takes the words in commit order; the others
    reverse a descending list instead of sorting it (`order_words`).
  - **The commit of a vector entry within one plane word** (a register of an array of registers, a whole bus word) blends with one mask and
    sets the pending bits with the same mask, instead of `put_block` and `mark_bits` each building theirs (91 to about 50 instructions an entry;
    `OutV::planes` are masked to the length, which every producer already did).
  - The test for implicit signals after the fast update paths is inlined (`update_implicit_quiet`), the call only for a design with implicit
    signals (21 instructions a delta cycle of `rtl_chain`); `cycle` calls `run_one` for a batch of one process itself, without entering
    `run_batch`; a run with one direct one-element entry pushes it without the loop.
  - Results, instructions of whole runs (`--tier=interp`, deterministic), main against the round: `rtl_lfsr` -3.9%, `lfsr64` -4.2%,
    `rtl_chain` -2.6%, `rtl_ff` -1.8%, `delta_chain` -6.1%, `lfsr64_xor` -2.9%, `ff_rtl` -1.7%, `rtl_ram` -1.2%, neorv32_single_min -0.5%;
    `rtl_fan`, `rtl_bus`, `compute_h2h`, `xor_sig`, `xor_types`, `resolved_bus` level (within 0.02%). Against sim1 (`tools/bench/run.py --ref
    sim1 --tiers auto --instructions`, instruction ratio): `rtl_lfsr` 1.59 to 1.52, `lfsr64` 1.70 to 1.61, `rtl_chain` 1.66 to 1.62, `rtl_ff`
    1.22 to 1.20.
  - Cycles (minimum of 7 interleaved runs on one claimed core of the second CCD), `--tier=auto` / `--tier=interp`: `rtl_ff` -3.5% / -2.2%,
    `rtl_lfsr` -1.9% / -0.5%, `lfsr64` -3.9% / -2.9%, `rtl_chain` -1.0% / -1.4%. neorv32_single_min: +0.6% to +1.7% cycles in four sessions
    with 0.5% fewer instructions; builds that each took one of the changes back recovered part of it, not additively (a build with neither
    the skip-test change nor the word order was still +0.85%). Not explained by branch, L1 data or L1 instruction misses (`perf stat`); by
    the convention of #576 a single design's cycles moving by a few percent are not decided on alone.
  - `realbench --compare` (run phase, interpreter and auto, all 42 tests, 3 runs a cell, one core): wall geometric mean over the tests of 1 s
    or more 1.01 (interpreter) and 0.99 (auto), summed wall 1.00 and 1.00; the `cpu` category 1.01 and 1.02 (neorv32 and LEON3); instructions
    level (the 0.01 to 0.2 s tests move by up to 4% between two runs of one binary, `--compare base base`). The CPU designs again, interpreter,
    5 runs a cell: neorv32_single_min 2.55 to 2.56 s, grlib_leon3mp 36.04 to 36.21 s; a build without the skip-test change gave the same
    (2.54 to 2.56, 36.21 to 36.51), so that change is not what costs them.
- **Measured and not taken:**
  - Pre-shifted spread tables for the `codes` refresh (`refresh_changed_codes`, about 250 instructions a fully changed word): -0.25% instructions
    on the LFSR designs for four 2 KB tables instead of one; not kept.
  - One masked blend for the `cur` and `'last_value` writes of a one-element event (`finish_code`, `finish_quick`): neo -0.2%, `rtl_chain` +0.2%
    instructions; not kept.
  - Dropping the `codes` of signals whose sources have 9 to 16 elements (the #519 rule keeps codes up to 16): about 60 instructions an entry of
    `lfsr64` and `rtl_lfsr` go to the refresh, but the interpreter reads single elements of `rtl_lfsr`'s registers through them; the rule is a
    recorded decision and is left as it is (a candidate for the elaborator's facts: which signals have one-element reads).
- **Left:** #766 (host layers around compiled clocked processes, the largest item on `rtl_ff`, `rtl_lfsr`, `lfsr64`), #767 (`wait until` form),
  the `run_batch` loop (about 120 instructions an activation spread over 30 lines), the `codes` refresh of 16-bit registers.

## Byte codes by element reads (yavs-sem facts, yavs-elab `keep_codes.rs`, yavs-kernel, #734, 2026-10-26)

- **Decision (user, 2026-10-26, on #734)**: instead of the source-width rule of #519 (`CODES_SOURCE_MAX`), the elaborator decides which logic
  signals keep the per-element byte codes (`Signal::codes`): those that have a read of a single element. Rationale: the refresh of the codes
  of a changed word costs about 250 instructions for 16-bit registers (kernel round 24), and only reads of single elements use them.
- **How**: `Db::facts()` has `elem_reads` (the signal objects with a scalar index, selection or alias of a part in an expression that is not an
  assignment, force or release target) and `elem_reads_all` (an element read through a signal parameter or an external name: any signal may be
  it). `yavs-elab` `keep_codes.rs` maps them to leaves like `lean.rs`: a leaf keeps its codes when it is one element, when an object that holds
  it has an element read (a port collapsed into its actual marks the actual's leaf), when it is a scalar field of a record inside an array
  (`SigGather` reads those one element at a time, a cost choice; #1119 below), for implicit signals; all of them when `elem_reads_all`. The others get
  `Builder::no_codes`. Port-map actuals such as `v(3)` count as reads (not told apart from other uses of the name): a safe over-count.
  `YAVS_CODES=all` keeps every signal's codes (test aid); the `no_code_signals` counter shows how many signals keep none.
- **Without codes** a one-element read comes from the planes (`Ctx::first_code`, and compiled code through `TierSig` with `codes = 0`: its
  plane path was there for buses, so `TierSig` and `rt.rs` are unchanged), and the skip test of an assignment of the value a signal holds
  (`direct_same`, `commit_code`, `commit_codes`) compares the plane bit instead (`held`), so a vector driven by element and read whole
  still skips. The width rule of #519 stays as a second condition (user, 2026-10-26, see the last bullet): a signal of more than 64 elements keeps its codes only with every source at most `CODES_SOURCE_MAX` (16) elements, checked in `Signal::sync_codes`.
- **Results** (bench builds with `llvm`, base = main without this change, instructions of whole warm runs, `--threads 1`, `--tier=interp` / `--tier=llvm`):
  `lfsr64` 0.968 / 0.952, `lfsr64_xor` 0.979 / 0.972, `rtl_ram` 0.992 / 0.992; cycles (minimum of 9 interleaved runs on a claimed core) 0.96 / 0.96,
  0.97 / 0.97, 1.02 / 0.99. `rtl_lfsr`, `rtl_ff`, `rtl_chain` read single elements of their registers (`r(i)(0) = 'U'`, `q((i+1) mod N)`,
  `c(i-1)`) and keep their codes, so this decision cannot save their refresh: instructions 1.000 / 1.004 / 1.005 (code layout; their paths are
  unchanged), cycles level within the noise of a shared host. `neorv32_single_min` and `grlib_leon3mp` level.
- **Width condition kept (user, 2026-10-26)**: with the element-read rule alone `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` lost 5% instructions (3% wall interp, 7% auto) because its wide buses have element reads. A leaf now keeps codes only with element reads AND, above 64 elements, narrow sources (the #519 rule, unchanged in `Signal::sync_codes`). `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` is level again: instructions 51.12 G to 51.17 G (interp), 49.44 G to 49.16 G (auto), cpu 3.98 s both. The skip test on the planes (`held`) is new for buses and signals without codes, so `mixed_entries` counts fewer direct entries (floors 1230 and 260).
- **Records (#1119, 2026-11-06)**: a vector field of a record no longer keeps its codes for being in a record, and a record pack keeps none when
  none of its leaves keeps them (`Elaborated::build_res`). The codes are a cache: every reader of a record's values reads the planes or falls
  back to them without codes (`SigGather`/`SigScatter` in the interpreter and in compiled code, `Ctx::elem_code`, `first_code`, `cur_code`,
  the `TierSig` reads of both compiled tiers, waves, reports, VHPI, the debugger, force and deposit, resolution, port conversions, the hang
  report), so results do not depend on this choice. The scalar field of a record inside an array keeps them by cost, not for correctness: a
  gather of a part reads each element of it through `Ctx::elem_code`, which without codes decodes the planes. A record whose fields have a
  read of one element keeps them as before. On the record pipeline of 16 units, 1 M cycles (medians of 7 interleaved runs), the time went to
  0.88 to 0.89 of before at `--tier=clift` and 0.86 to 0.89 at the default tier in every coding of the assignment (whole, aggregate, field by
  field); the same design with flat signals runs the same instructions.
- **Precise facts** (#734, 2026-10-26, next section): port-map actuals, sensitivity entries and signal parameters no longer count as
  element reads or ask for every signal.

## Element read facts without connections, sensitivity entries and parameter reads (yavs-sem `db.rs`, #734, 2026-10-26)

- **Decision**: `Facts::elem_reads` counts only reads. (1) A plain port-map actual (`Actual::Expr`, not `inertial`, of an instance or a block)
  is a connection: the read happens inside the instance on the formal. A scalar signal port read whole (any use that is not an assignment
  target, a port-map actual or a sensitivity entry) is noted as an element read of the *port object*; `keep_codes.rs` already marks the
  leaves of an object, and a collapsed port shares the actual's leaf, so `a(3)` keeps its codes only if the formal is read (modes in, out,
  inout and buffer alike; `out` ports that are only driven read nothing). Converted, individual and `inertial` actuals stay reads (the
  kernel or an interpreter process evaluates them). (2) The names of a process sensitivity list and of `wait on` without `until` are no
  reads (matched by span: `Lsp::span` is the span of its expression). (3) An element read of a signal parameter no longer sets
  `elem_reads_all`: every call with a signal actual to a signal formal is an edge `(callee, formal, root object)`; the parameters that
  read an element (directly or by passing the signal on) are found by a fixpoint in `Db::settle_elem_reads`, and the root objects of the
  edges into them get the element read. A parameter is its body region and its position (the spec and the body of a subprogram have
  different parameter objects). An external name as actual, or a callee the analysis cannot see into (formal generic subprogram, foreign,
  not yet instantiated, no body), keeps `elem_reads_all`; natives and implicit operations read no element. A scalar signal parameter read
  whole is not noted: a call actual that is a part is itself a read, as before.
- **Storage**: when the facts are recomputed they come from the raw lists (`elem_direct`, `param_reads`, `pass_edges`, `elem_ext`),
  stored per unit (unit image FORMAT 7).
- **Results** (bench builds with `llvm`, `no_code_signals` before / after of the real-world suite): `osvvm_axis_random` 0 / 21, `osvvm_axi4_random` 0 / 1,
  `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 0 / 5, `grlib_leon3mp` 0 / 317, `neorv32_single_min` 373 / 376, `uvvm_sb_slv` 0 / 0 (3 signals), fletcher tests unchanged.
  Instructions of whole runs (`--tier=interp` / `auto`): all level (1.000) except `grlib_leon3mp` 1.007 / 1.007: the 317 signals it
  now drops are written by element and skip on the plane bit (`plane_held`), which costs more than the byte compare it replaces (fixed by the next entry); wall time
  level (0.99 / 0.95, noise of a shared host). Test: `connections_and_sensitivity_need_no_byte_codes`, `elem_read_facts`.

## The skip test of a signal without byte codes reads the planes inline (yavs-kernel `signal.rs`, `value.rs`, #734, 2026-10-26)

- **Decision**: `held` (the skip tests `direct_same`, `commit_code`, `commit_codes`) reads the plane bit inline when the signal keeps no
  byte codes, through `plane_is`: the four plane words against the code's splat words, one test of the element's bit, with no code
  assembled. The out-of-line `plane_held` call is gone (it was `#[inline(never)]`; byte storage keeps an out-of-line path, `bytes_held`). The
  compares against the driver value and the driving value use `plane_is` too. `direct_same` is `#[inline(always)]`, so the drive run of
  the interpreter (`skip_code_now`) and the compiled-code direct drives (`yavs_interp::direct_drive_*`, which end in the same
  `assign_code_now`) run the test without a call.
- **Why**: dropping the codes of a signal written by element (30241dbc: 317 signals of `grlib_leon3mp`) turned the byte compare into a call
  of about 40 instructions, +0.7 percent of the run. Now the test is about 25 inline instructions on the plane path and the refresh of
  the codes is gone: dropping codes is not a loss any more. `direct_same_planes` (vectors) never used the codes.
- **Measured** (bench builds with `llvm`, `--threads 1`, interleaved on claimed cores, instructions; "before" is main at 30241dbc, "pre" the
  commit before it, with the 317 codes kept): `grlib_leon3mp` interp 425.70 G before, 421.82 G after, 422.62 G pre; `neorv32_single_min`
  interp 29.95 / 29.85 G, auto 30.47 / 30.23 G; `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` interp 51.10 / 51.07 G, auto 48.73 / 48.57 G; `lfsr64`, `lfsr64_xor`,
  `rtl_ram`, `rtl_lfsr`, `rtl_ff`, `rtl_chain` level (0.999 to 1.003, layout). Cycles are within host noise (the machine was shared; min of
  3 to 5 runs): grlib 181.9 / 183.0 G, neorv32 interp 13.28 / 13.21 G, fletcher auto 19.89 / 19.67 G. `realbench --compare` (42 tests,
  interp and auto): instruction geomean 1.00 / 1.01 (the auto rows that move are short runs whose compile outcome differs, #673). Equality:
  `YAVS_CODES=all` and the default give identical output on `grlib_leon3mp` and `neorv32_single_min`.

## Facts the declarative part leaves in a process copy (yavs-ir `opt/decl.rs`, #678, 2026-10-24)

- **Decision**: a copy of a process (`copies.rs`) takes over between two activations, so what its declarative part made is in the frame
  and is a function of the instance's frozen data. The optimiser runs that part per copy on a small abstract machine (`Ev`: registers as
  unknown, constant, address, pointer into a tracked block or heap handle; frame bytes, temporary blocks and heap objects as known or
  unknown bytes; pure arithmetic, `Load`/`Store`/`Copy`/`MakeDope`/`DopeLen`/`Pos`/`LayoutOf`/`Field`/`Alloc`/`New`/`NewFill`/`Deref`,
  and the branches those decide) and reports the frame bytes, the words that hold an address and the words that point to the
  descriptor of a heap object (`[data, desc, handle]` of a record variable) that the body never writes. The walk (`Opt::wf`,
  `Opt::rdesc`) answers the body's loads of those: a scalar word is a constant, an address word is an `AddrOf`, a descriptor pointer is
  a register whose bytes are known, so `DopeLen`, `Pos`, `SlicePos`, `SubtypeCheck`, the loads of descriptor words, `LayoutOf` (every
  record or array type whose descriptor bytes are known, in shared code too: the pool's and the instance's descriptors) and `Field` fold.
  The facts are keyed by frame offset, not by register, so they hold after every suspension without being re-made.
- **Why it is sound**: a fact needs the word to be unwritten by the body (a direct store, copy or `MakeDope` to a frame address in a
