  body block, or an address of it used other than by a load, anywhere: `frame_writes`) and every unmodelled instruction, call or store
  of a pointer into memory the machine cannot see makes what its pointer operands reach unknown for good (`Mem::poison`: the bytes stay
  unknown whatever is stored later); a branch or `Case` on an unknown value, an unknown word loaded out of memory that holds pointers, or
  more than 50 000 instructions give no facts. A check that fails would have stopped the run in initialisation, so after the switch every
  check passed. Reads of the bytes of a `for` generate's parameter are unknown, as before. The one fact taken on the language's word is
  that the descriptor of a heap object (the constraint of an object) is never written after the object is made, and that of an array
  variable in the frame (`in_descriptor`) likewise; a pointer to either may go anywhere.
- **Not done**: a branch on a package constant (`AddrSpace::Pkg`) stopped the machine (6 of the 16 big processes of the GRLIB LEON3 system
  have one): done since, see "Package constants in specialised copies" (#708). Calls are unknown, so a variable initialised by a function
  call has no fact (its descriptor does when the bounds are known).
- **Measured**: `docs/STATUS.md` "Facts the declarative part leaves in a process copy". `spec_record_var` (`crates/yavs/tests/perf.rs`) is
  the work-counter case (239 313 ops with the shared code, 151 530 with copies), `crates/yavs-ir/tests/copies.rs` the unit cases.


## Light natives in compiled code: a callback of their own (yavs-llvm, yavs-interp, #698, 2026-10-24)

Counted with `tools/stepcount` on `poc_arith_addw` under `--tier=llvm` (1078 calls of a light `ieee` native in a window of
3 M instructions): `TierHost::native_frame` 113 instructions and `yavs_rt_native` 68 per call, as much as the native (`add`
115, `to_integer` 45) it surrounds.

- **A `CallNative` of a light native (`yavs_interp::light_native`, the set `Op::CallIeee` already runs: an `ieee` native,
  few cells, no signal, not `uniform`) calls `yavs_rt_native_light`** with the arguments and results of `yavs_rt_native`, and
  `TierHost::native_light` on the host. Such a native allocates only temporary memory and never collects, so, as for
  `Op::CallIeee`: no collection check (`reclaim_pending`), no allocation-mode swap of the frame, the heap epoch is not
  read (`Mem::forget_end` replaces `forget_since`: only volatile objects can be stale), and the view update stores
  only the temporary pointer, length and capacity (no roots, base or epoch change). Kept: the frame windows of native
  frames (an operand may live in a slot of a native frame), the `ieee_fallback`/`ieee_stop` handling, the package
  initialisation and elaboration-report decline, `catch_unwind`. Why a second symbol and not a flag: no branch in the shared
  callback, and the code generator picks it at compile time with `light_native`. Shared with a second code generator:
  `TierHost::native_light` and the argument convention of `yavs_rt_native`.
- **Measured:** 113 + 68 to 82 + 73 instructions per call (-26, the rest is spread over many small pieces: two prologues and
  epilogues, the table lookups, the result tuple and the argument slice); instructions of `poc_arith_addw` -1.2 percent
  under `--tier=llvm`, -0.8 percent on the window generator. The callback layer is now about as large as the native;
  removing it needs the native inline in compiled code (#698 idea 2).

## Idle skip, round 5: variables assigned on every path, fields one by one, debug code under a false generic (yavs-sem, yavs-elab, #521, #519, 2026-10-24)

Found with the whole-picture profile of `fletcher_bufferwriter_512`: its hottest process (`ctrl_comb_proc` of the reshaper, 11.6% of
the run, a finite-state machine in the two-process style) was not pure for the idle skip, so it ran at every wake, 139 K of them
(it is woken by `clk`, which it names "for debugging", and by every input); each skipped activation saves the 13 drives and the bus
updates it would make (41 K instructions an activation). Doing it by hand in the source (assign the helper variable first, drop the
debug `report`s) took the writer from 74.2 G to 68.5 G instructions (-7.7%). Three limits of the purity analysis were the cause, and are
lifted:

- **Definite assignment, not "first statement".** A variable of the process is allowed when it is assigned on every path before it is
  mentioned otherwise (`Db::vars_assigned_first`, now `defined_before_use`): a flow analysis over `if`, `case` (what all arms assign),
  loops (nothing, they may run no iteration) and sequences, where round 2 asked for a top-level `v := ...;` first in the statement list.
  `variable t : ...; if c then t := a; x <= t; end if;` and `if a then v := 1; else v := 2; end if; y <= v;` are pure now.
- **Fields of a record variable one by one.** `v.f := ...;` (a chain of field selections from a variable) assigns that field and a
  mention of `v.f.g` is met by an assignment of `v.f.g` or of a prefix of it; a mention of the whole `v` needs a whole assignment. A
  partial update `v.f(3) := ...` is a mention (it reads the rest). `vo.a := ...; vo.b := ...;` followed by reads of single fields is pure.
- **Debug code under a condition of generics.** An `if` branch (condition and body) that is not pure, but can only run where a
  boolean of constants and generics holds (`if rising_edge(clk) and DEBUG then report ...`), is no longer a failure but a guard under
  which the process is not pure (`PureRead` with `lsp` `None`): the elaborator works the literals out per instance (as it does for
  guarded reads) and the process is pure in every instance where one is false. Where it is true (`DEBUG => true`) the process runs at
  every wake as before. The condition itself must have no effect (`Db::effect_free`: no impure function, no protected method), since
  `f(x) and DEBUG` evaluates `f` first (the reference simulator folds `f(x) and false` and drops the call, a deviation from the LRM
  (`tests/discrepancies/short-circuit-constant-false-effect`), which is why that case is only in `perf.rs`, not in the corpus).
- **Why it is the same run.** The rule of round 2 holds unchanged: an activation does what the last one did when every signal it
  reads is unchanged and no variable carries a value from one activation to the next; the three changes only accept more processes
  that satisfy it. `YAVS_IDLE_SKIP=check` runs every skipped activation and fails when it assigns something else: the 511 tests of the
  differential corpus in check mode, the new `delta/idle_vars` (blessed from the reference simulator; five pure shapes, three that
  must run every time, and an instance with the debug report on and one off), `perf.rs` `idle_vars` (off, on and check print the same,
  an impure condition reports at every wake), and the 42 real-world designs in check mode.
- **Result** (bench builds, exact instructions, interpreter): `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` 74.17 G to 69.0 G (0.93), `poc_fifo_ic_assembly`
  0.82, `fletcher_bufferwriter_prim32` 0.91, `neorv32_dual_full` 0.97, `neorv32_single_cache` 0.98, `neorv32_single_min` 0.99, the rest of the
  42 within 0.5%.
- **Left (blocks of the other hot processes of the writer):** a `report`/`assert` that is not under a condition of generics
  (`last_stage_proc`, `command_proc`: output has to come at every activation), a variable field read before it is assigned on some path
  (`vo` of a BusWriteBuffer process, `stage_v` of a pipeline barrel: they keep a value, so they are not pure), procedure calls.

## `--tier=auto` decisions follow the looks of a sampler thread, prices are fixed (yavs-llvm, #670, #673, #680, #681, 2026-10-24)

- **Causes found** (a fresh world per sample, `--threads 1`, instructions of the whole process tree, traces with `YAVS_AUTO_TRACE=1`):
  1. The compile cost was a rate learned from the compiles of the run (`us_per_instr`: half the old value plus the wall time per IR
     instruction of the last O2 compile that did not hit the cache). It started at 800, fell with the first compiles of a cold run and stayed
     at 800 in a warm run (hits teach nothing), and it priced every function of a run with one number for native-frame code, frame-mode code,
     full-pipeline compute loops and `Fast` code alike. What a function costs, so when it is compiled, depended on the order and the wall
     times of the compiles before it: `sc5_fifo_repack` ended at 35 G or 47 G according to whether `p_in` and the clocked processes were
     priced under their threshold when they crossed it (#673, #670).
  2. The sampler ran on the compile thread, so while it compiled (10 ms to 600 ms) or measured a trial (250 ms) it saw nothing, and
     the first look after that gave the whole gap to the one function it happened to catch: a function could be "seen" for 400 ms in a
     sample. Which functions crossed their thresholds, and in which order, depended on how long the compile thread had been busy.
  3. The clock was wall time. With the compile thread on the simulation's core (below) or a loaded host it counted the time the
     simulation lost to the compile as time spent in the function.
  4. `Worker::cost` priced `Fast` code like the rest (800 per IR instruction, real 70 to 130, #680).
  5. The compile thread moved to every CPU outside the mask (#681), so the compile of a run overlapped the simulation on another run's core.
  6. Smaller: a `HashSet` iterated in an order that differs in every process decided the order of callees in `tree`.
- **Decision: a sampler thread (`yavs-sampler`, `sampler_loop`) sends looks (the CPU time of the simulation threads since the last look and
  what they run) in batches of 8 to the compile thread, which takes one batch at a time and decides after each (`Worker::see`).** The
  sampler runs during compiles and sends nothing during a trial (the swaps of a trial would show as the code running). So the sequence of
  decisions depends on the sequence of looks and nothing else; no compile or trial duration reaches them. The clock is the CPU time of the
  simulation threads (process less the sampler's and the compile thread's own clocks), wall time where there is no such clock (not Linux).
  Why not the one thread of decisions.md "Tier-up (`--tier=auto`)": its reason (CPU) holds, the sampler wakes once per period as the compile
  thread did.
- **Decision: prices are constants.** `US_PER_INSTR` (800) is the price the learned rate started at and stayed near in cold runs with the
  compile thread on the simulation's core (cold compiles of the 5 designs and 19 more of tools/realbench, per-function CPU: frame-mode
  code 200 to 450 and native-frame code 350 to 1100 per IR instruction, rising with the size of the function; wall time on a shared core is
  twice that). `Fast` code has its own, 110, in the budget (`Worker::price`), a module linked from the cache 20 (`US_PER_INSTR_HIT`).
  `spent` is charged by the model, never by the time a compile took. The payback rule (`PAYBACK*`, the order of candidates) keeps 800 for
  `Fast` code too (`payback_cost`): cheap prices for it made the 2 133 IR process of the window generator compile after 0.47 s instead of never
  in a cold run and cost that design 8 to 16 percent of its cold wall time; whether big processes compile is the user's decision
  (#679, 2026-10-24: allowed, no size cap yet), not a side effect of #680.
- **Tried and not taken:** per-class and per-module prices from the measurements (`lean`, `full`, `Fast`, frame and native: 210/470, 450/720,
  110/220 CPU per IR instruction, also doubled to wall time on a shared core): more small functions compile (the tiny ones cost 3 to 9
  ms each), cold wall time of the window generator +14 to +27 percent against the learned rate, +5 percent against the flat 800. The
  benefit of compiling a small native function is lower than the payback factors assume; the flat 800 happens to stand for both its cost
  and its low benefit. A wall clock for the looks instead of CPU time: no better. Budget prices scaled 0.3 to 0.7: within 2 percent of each other, 1.0: 4 percent more
  instructions.
- **Affinity (#681, user, 2026-10-24):** the compile thread keeps the CPU mask of the process. Under single-core pinning it shares the core:
  auto walls of `tools/bench` and `tools/realbench` include the compile CPU time from here on (`tools/bench/AGENTS.md`).
- **What is still timing dependent** (measured, see docs/STATUS.md "`--tier=auto` decisions"): (a) the CPU speed of the host itself: the same
  simulation costs 1.8 to 3.4 s of CPU on a busy host (SMT neighbours, frequency), and a function whose seen time sits near its
  threshold flips (`rand_next` of `sc5_fifo_repack`, `push`, `check_axi_stream` of the window generator); (b) through the compilation
  cache: what the first run compiled is linked early in the next ones, so a flip in the first run is amplified (window generator warm: 178
  to 198 G with the same code); (c) the compile that is still running when the run ends is lost; (d) trial verdicts near their keep line. The
  way to remove (a) and so (b) is a work clock (instructions retired of the simulation threads, `perf_event_open`, with the CPU time where
  it is denied); built on 2026-10-25 (user decision of 2026-10-24): see "`--tier=auto` work clock, kinds of function" below.
- Tests: `what_is_hot_depends_on_the_looks_only`, `a_look_shares_its_time_between_the_running_functions` (`auto.rs`),
  `compile_thread_keeps_the_affinity_of_the_process` (`tests/tier.rs`); the 510-test differential corpus under `yavs-auto`, with
  `--tier-heat=1,0,0` and with 4 threads, passes.

## `--tier=auto` work clock, kinds of function, cached objects, shared code that waits for its copy (yavs-llvm, yavs-interp, #670, #673, #675, #717, #728, 2026-10-25)

- **Decision (user, 2026-10-24): the clock of the policy is the work of the simulation threads, not time.** Work is user-mode
  instructions retired, one `perf_event_open` counter per simulation thread (`yavs-llvm` `work.rs`; the interpreter tells a hook when a
  thread gets its sampling slot, `yavs_interp::on_simulation_thread`, so the main thread and every kernel worker note their thread ids;
  the sampler thread opens the counters when it starts, after `START_AFTER`, so a run under 5 ms pays one system call per thread),
  converted to the time units of the policy's constants by one fixed number, `INSTR_PER_US` (16 000, the median of what the five designs
  of #673 retire per CPU microsecond of the simulation threads on the development host: 10 000 for `neorv32_single_min` to 18 000
  for `hdlm_lfsr`; `YAVS_AUTO_IPUS` overrides it, a tuning aid). Where the kernel refuses the counter, and on other systems, the clock
  is the CPU time of the simulation threads as before (`AutoTier::clock_note` says why; `YAVS_AUTO_TRACE=1` prints it). The trial of a compiled function (`Worker::trial`) stays on CPU time: it compares the progress per second of two kinds of
  code, which retire different numbers of instructions for the same progress.
- **Each thread's instructions are charged to the function in that thread's slot** (`Runtime::thread_sampler`), not summed and split by
  the number of running functions: a worker that spins or waits has no function and adds nothing (the CPU-time clock counted the
  spinning), and a worker that spun before it ran is charged at most two periods. A look is taken when the busiest running thread has
  retired a period (`Heat::period`, 1 ms) of work, polled in steps of at least 150 us from 0.95 periods on, with the timer slack of the
  sampler at 1 us (`timer_slack_1us`), so a loaded host moves the looks in time and not in the program. Only the counters of the
  running threads are read at a poll (a read is a system call on the simulation's core: all four threads at every poll cost the
  window generator 3 percent of its wall time). A look at a fixed wall time gave 6 to 10 percent more instructions in a cold run of the
  window generator.
- **Decision: kinds of function, a price and a benefit each** (`Kind`, `Model`, `MODELS`; user, 2026-10-24: prices per class only
  together with a benefit estimate per class). A function is `Tiny` (called on native frames, under 64 IR instructions, no loop),
  `Native`, `Loop` (native with a loop), `Compute`, `Frame`, `Rtl`, `RtlFew` (a clocked process of fewer than `RTL_INSTANCES`
  instances) or `Big` (`OptLevel::Fast`). A kind has a price (fixed microseconds plus microseconds an IR instruction, compile CPU
  measured in cold runs of tools/realbench: `Tiny` 2.5 ms + 200, `Native` 2 ms + 550, `Loop` 4 ms + 800, `Compute` 4 ms + 900,
  `Frame` 2 ms + 250, `Rtl` 200, `Big` 4 ms + 110) and the speedup compiled code is expected to have (1.2, 1.55, 2.1, 2.4, 1.09, 1.5,
  1.1, 1.037). A function is a candidate once it was seen interpreted for price x speedup / (speedup - 1), the time its compile pays
  back if the rest of the run is like the part seen; the budget is charged the price and the candidates go in the order of seen time
  over that threshold. The speedups are the payback factors that were `PAYBACK` (4), `PAYBACK_COMPUTE` and `PAYBACK_NATIVE` (2)
  turned around and calibrated so that at the typical size of a kind the threshold is the one of the flat 800 us an IR instruction:
  the measured prices are 2 to 3 times lower for frame-mode code and for tiny functions, and a function of 8 IR instructions costs
  3 ms whatever its size says, so those kinds carry a benefit that is lower than the factor 2 the flat price assumed (a native
  function 1.55, a tiny one 1.2, frame-mode code 1.09). `Big` (the large combinational processes: compiled code level with the
  interpreter, #679) is pinned at 1.037 so that it is seen for 3 200 us an IR instruction as before; whether it compiles is the user's
  decision (no size cap), not a side effect of its price.
  **What the measurements did not give:** no table of prices and speedups won back the cold wall time the learned rate before d65e7a74
  had on the window generator (15.2 s against 16.5; interleaved on core 8, 8 to 16 worlds): tiny functions later (speedup 1.05 to
  1.2, fixed price), native functions earlier (3) or later (1.33), a native budget of 8 instead of 16 changed the cold median by
  less than the spread (3 percent) and the warm one by up to 7 percent either way. The model is therefore calibrated to the old
  thresholds where it has no measurement against them.
- **A function whose object is in the cache is priced as linking it** (`HIT`, 1 ms + 10 us an IR instruction: 3 ms for a process of
  200; user, 2026-10-25, #728), in the budget and in the payback rule (`Worker::cached`: an earlier run compiled a function of its name
  and size, `listed`), and a clocked process outside the band of bodies that gained does not wait `BAND_WAIT` for it (`Worker::band`).
  What a warm run compiles depends on the cache as well as on the looks, deterministically for a given cache. `rtl_ff` warm -6
  percent wall (its process was compiled at 260 ms), `rtl_lfsr` at 61 ms where it was 79 ms; `lfsr64` stays as it was (it is
  seen for 172 ms of a 165 ms run, a process outside the band whose object was never listed: it is compiled in no run).
- **`RtlFew` (#675).** A clocked process of fewer than 16 instances was refused (`cold`) however much of the run it was: the carry
  chain of `poc_arith_addw` (8 copies, 14 percent of the samples) stayed interpreted. It is a kind with a low benefit (1.1: eleven
  times its price in samples), the share rule of an eighth stays, and the measure after the swap (`Worker::trial`) takes the code
  back when it does not pay.
- **The shared code of a process that can have a copy waits for the switch** (`Worker::awaits_switch`, `SPEC_WAIT` 400 ms of sampled
  work, only for fewer than `SPEC_INSTANCES` (64) instances). The interpreter switches a process to its specialised copy at its first
  try 150 ms after the tier is set and at doubled activation counts after that, and does not switch a process whose shared code is
  compiled. A warm run linked the shared code from the cache at 12 ms (the process was listed), and a cold run could compile it before
  the switch, so the process never got its copy: the process of `hdlm_lfsr` ran the compiled shared code for 878 ms where the
  compiled copy needs 459 (30.6 G instructions against 25.5 G, +14 percent wall); which one it was depended on the clock (the CPU
  clock stayed on the good side by luck, an instruction clock at 14 000 did not). The shared code of such a process is now neither a
  candidate nor linked before 400 ms were seen. `poc_arith_addw` (processes of 8 to 63 instances): cold -10 percent wall, warm -15
  percent. Not for 64 instances or more: each copy is a share too small for the tier to take and the shared code is compiled for all
  of them, as `exec.rs` `specialise` intends (`rtl_lfsr`, 512 instances, was 20 percent slower warm when it waited: its run is
  300 ms).
- **#717.** `window` and `run_trial` take the wall clock and the nap (`Pace`), so the tests of the trial run in virtual time (`Sim`
  in `auto.rs`): the number of pairs a trial takes no longer depends on scheduling.
- **Found on the way:** the test `stuck::sigint_ends_a_process_that_never_suspends` hangs once the tier has compiled the spinning process (#737: compiled code does not poll the stop request); with the earlier compile of this change it fails every time under `--features llvm`, so it ran `--tier=interp` until #737 was fixed (it runs every tier now).
- **Measured** (docs/STATUS.md "`--tier=auto` work clock"): the clock itself, the decisions idle and loaded, the cold and warm totals.
- **Left:** which function a thread is in at a look is sampling, so the decisions of a design near a threshold still differ between
  worlds (the window generator: 6 to 8 different sets in 8 worlds, the same functions within a few milliseconds of seen time);
  trial verdicts (CPU time); the compile that is running when the run ends; through the cache a flip in a first run reaches the later
  ones. `Worker::fast` and `ra_cost` (#715, the second compile of frame-mode code) are still priced and judged by their own constants.

## IR optimiser round 14: a repeated `to_integer` is made once, the second call replays only when it can warn (yavs-ir `opt/sink/calls.rs`, `opt/sink.rs`, #520, 2026-10-24)

User decision 2026-10-24 (#520): share the `to_integer` of a check's condition and message. `simAssertion(to_integer(unsigned(a & b)) = x,
"..." & image(to_integer(unsigned(a & b))))` converts one value twice; the lowering builds each argument as a signal read, a
concatenation and a fat pair of its own, so the optimiser's value numbering (which forgets memory facts at every call) never sees one
value. After the message was sunk (round 16) the second chain and call were what remained of the message on the passing path.

- **Decision: after `sink::run` has moved the message, `Sink::share_calls` finds, in one block, a later `to_integer (unsigned)` whose
  argument is the same value as an earlier one's, and turns the later call into a branch on the earlier call's result:
  `r1 = call(x); ...; CondBr r1, FAST, R`, `FAST: r2 = r1`, `R: r2 = call(x')` (the original second call), both to `J`, the rest
  of the block. A second `sink` run then moves what built the second argument into `R`. Why: the native returns 0 exactly for a
  null or a metavalue argument (both with a warning) and for the value 0, so a first result other than 0 proves that the second call
  is silent and returns the same; for 0 the real second call runs and warns or not by itself, so message text, count, order and
  time of every warning are those of the unshared code.** The guard is the result itself (`CondBr` tests `!= 0`): no `LNum`, no new
  instruction, no change to the natives. Only `ieee::Op::ToInteger { signed: false }` qualifies (`numeric_bit` included: it warns
  only for a null vector); `signed` warns with a result other than 0 for a one-element `'1'` (`TO_SIGNED: vector truncated`, result
  -1), so it stays as it is (a test checks that).
- **"The same value" is value numbering of one block (`calls.rs`, `Vn`).** Scalars are numbered by operation and operands (a register
  the function defines once by a constant or an address is that constant or address, so `r13` and `r40` that both hold 1 are one
  number); a block `Alloc` makes is numbered by what is written into it, in order (stores, `MakeDope`, `SigRead`, `Cat`), compared
  by structure at the call (nested blocks included, depth 6). A call qualifies only when its argument is a fat pair this block
  allocated. Everything that may change what was numbered forgets it and the first calls with it: a statement marker, a suspension, a
  call other than `'image` and the light `ieee` natives (they write only a block of their own, and warn, which the replay keeps in
  order), a store through a pointer that is not a numbered block, a copy, fill, free or any instruction `writes_nothing` does not
  list. Signal reads of one block are of one value because nothing in the block can end an activation.
- `sink.rs` changes that make the second chain movable: `SigVal`, `SigReadScalar` and `SigRead` into a block the moved set made
  and `Cat` of logic vectors are movable like the string `Cat`; a moved `SigVal` takes two fresh registers (a signal reference is
  two cells); a branch made by `calls.rs` (a "replay" block) is looked at although no string `Cat` is in front of it and moves from
  3 instructions on (the call is rare); a result the target overwrites is not live out of it (the first version refused to move a
  definition of the register the replayed call writes). Moved code writes fresh registers as before.
- Tests (`crates/yavs/tests/sink.rs`, with the optimiser and without, interp and llvm): the same value in condition and message with
  every check passing and failing; a vector with `U` (both calls warn, twice per check); a vector of zeros (the replay runs and is
  silent); a null vector; another warning between the two calls; three calls of one value; a signed vector (left alone); the signal
  changing between statements; and the dump has the replay. 1300 random programs of checks over vectors of 0 to 8 elements with
  `0 1 U X Z W L H -`, concatenations, slices, `signed` and `unsigned`, signal changes between checks, compared with the build
  without the optimiser on the interpreter (and 350 under `--tier=llvm`): identical output.
- Not done: signed `to_integer` (a guard on the length and the sign bit would do); other natives that warn for a metavalue
  (`+`, `-` and compares of `numeric_std` return a metavalue result, so their result cannot be the guard); sharing across blocks
  (a call in a loop body and one after it); sharing the first chain with chains that other code built (`/ ` of numeric_std etc.).
- **Measured** (`poc_arith_addw`, bench builds, core 10): instructions 0.92 in the interpreter and under `--tier=auto`, cycles 0.89
  (window of 300 us), wall 0.95 (full length); 42 tests of `tools/realbench`, interpreter and compiled: instructions geometric mean
  1.00. Details in `docs/STATUS.md` "IR optimiser round 14: a repeated `to_integer` is made once".
- **Coordination (#697, #520):** the pass takes a native with one argument that is a fat pair the block allocated and stored
  the data address and the descriptor into. A native whose arguments are in registers (#697) is not shared until
  `Sink::shareable` and the argument test in `find_pairs` know that form; nothing else in the pass depends on the pair layout.


## llvm: a stepped definition is read back from the frame (yavs-llvm, #710, 2026-10-24)

- **Root cause of #710.** The slow path of a `LayoutOf` with a frame cache is generated at the start of the instruction, with the
  deferred registers (`Defer::pend`) as they are then. After the interpreter stepped the instruction, `layout_keep` reads the layout it made
  through `Gen::ld(dst)`, which returns a value deferred for an EARLIER definition of the same register when there is one: LEON3 reuses a
  register for a descriptor and later for the layout, so the layout words were copied from the descriptor's address into the kept
  slot, every later `Field` of that type used wrong offsets and the interpreter read outside the object. Not a limit of the deferral
  itself: it needs a register that a loop defines (deferred) and uses, and that a cached `LayoutOf` then redefines; the cap hid it for the
  large processes only. **Rule: code generated after a step in a slow path must not read a register the stepped instruction defines
  through `ld`/`pend`; `layout_keep` takes the deferred value out for its length and puts it back** (the fast path redefines the register
  with `st`, which clears it, and may still read the old value as an input). The test is `cached_layout_replaces_a_deferred_value_of_its_register`
  (`crates/yavs-llvm/tests/tier.rs`).

## Memo of pure calls (yavs-ir `memo_fn.rs`, yavs-interp `pmemo.rs`, #701, 2026-10-24)

Found with the PoC cache testbench: `ffdre(q, d, rst, INIT)` and `mux(sel, a, b)` on 2-bit vectors cost 12 000 to 20 000 instructions a call
(`resize(INIT, q'length)` alone is 60 percent of `ffdre`) and are called with the same few values over and over. Decision (user,
2026-10-24, option 3 of #701): **the interpreter keeps a runtime memo of the pure calls it ran, keyed by the bytes of their arguments, and
answers a repeat from it.** Options 1 (a function copy per constant facts of its arguments) and 2 (a once-per-site memo of `resize`) were
not taken: the first needs a second kind of copy and reserved slots and only folds the lengths, the second a persistent place for result bytes.
The reference simulator folds a pure call with constant arguments once, before the run; this memo also serves arguments that vary but repeat
(register state), which no folding can.

- **What qualifies** (`Program::memo_sig`, once per function, on the lowered code so the answer does not depend on which function ran first):
  a `pure` function (`FuncFlags::PURE`) that is not nested, cannot suspend, touches no shared state and no coverage, has no signal
  parameter, takes only `in` scalars of integer, physical, enumeration or real type and `in` arrays of those (descriptor and elements are the
  key, `Param::arr` names the array type), and returns one of those; whose instructions, and those of every function it calls, are
  computations, checks, frame, constant-pool and package-constant reads (`Inst::Alloc`, `NewFrame` and local heap objects included) with no
  signal, instance-data, enclosing-frame, shared-variable, clock, file, foreign, indirect or protected access, calling only natives from
  `native_is_pure` (the list package-initialisation caching uses); and that is worth the key: a loop, a call or 120 instructions (a
  function of a few instructions runs faster than its key is built).
- **Exactness.** The key holds every byte the call can read from its arguments (the argument words; for an array its descriptor, so bounds
  and direction count, and its element bytes, whole blocks for bit-planes) and is compared whole on a hit: the hash only picks the slot.
  Everything else the body reads is constant for the run (`Pkg` data are written during initialisation only, `Machine::wr` refuses
  later). A hit hands out a copy (a fat pair in temporary memory for an array), never the stored bytes. **Reports**: a `Report` in the
  body is allowed; `State::reports` counts the reports made (`Inst::Report`, `ieee::report`, before the severity filter), a call during which
  it moved is not kept, so a function that reports reports on every call, and a call that fails or stops is never kept.
- **Where.** Only simulation code in the interpreter: not elaboration-time evaluation (`ctx` is `None`), not under a debugger or with
  coverage counters, and `YAVS_NO_PMEMO=1` turns it off. The predecoder makes `Op::CallM` of an `Inst::Call` whose callee qualifies and runs
  every other call as before (one macro, `call_arm!`, is both arms, so an ordinary call has no test). The fast loop asks the memo
  (`Machine::memo_probe`) before it offers the call to the compiled tier (`Tier::call`): a hit is the result, a miss makes the call as before
  (compiled callee or not) and keeps the result when it returns (`memo_keep`); a call the tier does not take runs to its end from inside
  the call (`Machine::memo_run`, `call_to_end`: `exec` with the frame count as base), at most `NEST` = 8 deep (a recursive function
  memoises its top levels, the rest run as usual and the native stack stays small). Compiled code does not run in the frame of such a
  call (`Machine::is_memo_frame`): its return pops the frame and goes on in the caller without telling the loop that waits for the end.
  Calls that compiled code makes through the host's step (`call_regs`) do not use the memo: a version that ran a nested loop there
  corrupted the host's view of the frames (`--tier=auto --tier-heat=1,0,0` at 4 threads, `generics/generic_blocks_2019`). Compiled calls
  between compiled functions have their own path, below.
- **Bounds.** Per process and function a direct-mapped table of 32 entries that doubles up to 256 while keys evict each other; a key or
  result over 1 KiB is not kept (a call whose key does not fit counts as a call that did not repeat). The first 64 calls of a function in a process decide: fewer than one in eight repeating switches it off
  for that process, and for every process when three have (`Pre::memo_off`); a function that is off costs a flag test in the call. Per
  process and without locks, so hits and counters are the same at every thread count. `YAVS_COUNTERS` shows `pmemo_hits` and `pmemo_runs`.
- **Compiled code (user, 2026-10-24: "a compiled-code counterpart of the pure-call memo"; #701).** A call that compiled code makes to a
  native-callable function with a memo signature (`Gen::native_call`, from a native frame or a frame-mode function) is wrapped by two
  callbacks, and never runs interpreter code inside a host step: `yavs_rt_memo` (`TierHost::memo_probe`) builds the key from the argument
  cells (the arrays are read through the native frames' slot windows as for `native_direct`), looks it up and returns 1 with the result
  (a hit; an array result is allocated in temporary memory, the view is brought up to date as for a light native), 2 with the number of
  reports so far (a miss) or 0 (the call is made as usual and not kept); on a miss compiled code makes the call as it always did and,
  on the normal return edge only (not when the callee unwound for materialisation), calls `yavs_rt_memo_keep` (`TierHost::memo_keep`),
  which makes the key again from the same cells (the arguments are `in` and the function is pure, so the bytes are the ones the probe read;
  nothing is carried from the probe but the report count, so a call that never returns to its caller leaves nothing behind) and keeps the
  result unless a report ran meanwhile. The table, the give-up rule and the counters are the interpreter's (`pm`, `Pre::memo_off`,
  `pmemo_hits`); a key that cannot be read is no miss (it counts nowhere). The keep callback leaves `Mem::temp_seen` equal to the length
  its `sync` gave the machine's temporary area, as every callback must. Not done for calls compiled code makes through the host's step
  (a callee without native code); and the memo is asked on every compiled call of a function whose memo is off, which costs the
  callback (not visible in the measured case, `docs/STATUS.md`; an inline test of the global off flag would remove it).
- **Not done.** Records, access types, signal parameters and out parameters
  are not keyed. A table shared by the processes of one design unit would save the first call of each (about 4 percent of the PoC run is
  misses).
- **Measured** (bench builds, instructions of `--tier=interp`, `perf stat`): numbers in `docs/STATUS.md` "Memo of pure calls".
  Work-counter case `pure_memo` (`crates/yavs/tests/perf.rs`), correctness case `crates/yavs/tests/pmemo.rs` (bit-identical runs with
  and without the memo at 1 and 4 threads and with early specialised copies, a function that reports on every call).

## Package constants in specialised copies (yavs-ir `copies.rs`, `opt/decl.rs`, #708, 2026-10-24)

Decision (user, 2026-10-24): **package constant values may become facts of process copies.** The six large processes of the GRLIB LEON3 system
that branch on a package constant (`AddrSpace::Pkg`) in their declarative part had no frame facts because the abstract machine of #678 stopped
at the unknown load. Package data are written during package initialisation only (`Machine::wr` refuses a store later), and a copy is made
while the design runs, so the machine now reads them (`Opt::const_read` of `AddrSpace::Pkg`, only for the packages the process's declarative
part names: `Program::pkg_deps`, the `AddrOf Pkg` of the blocks before the body).
- **The key.** The packages' values are not instance data, and an initialiser may read the environment, so the same design can make other
  values in another run. The data of the packages a copy depends on come from a `PkgSource` (`copy_of_pkgs`; the runtime's package data), a
  digest of each (made once per package) is part of the copy's key, of `copy_tag` (compiled code of a copy is named and cached by it) and of
  the stored `CopyBlob` of the stage cache (`spec`): a changed package makes, and reads, another copy. `Copy` keeps the data it was made with
  for the lazy optimisation; `copy_of` is `copy_of_pkgs` without package data (no package fact, as before).
- **Folds also in the body** of a copy for a read of the same packages' constants, into integer registers only (the rule for instance data).
- **Measured**: `docs/STATUS.md` "Package constants in specialised copies"; unit case `a_copy_knows_what_a_package_constant_made`
  (`crates/yavs-ir/tests/copies.rs`).

## Native ieee calls: array operands as values (#697, 2026-10-24)

- **Decision (user, 2026-10-24: "IR-level operand convention for native calls"): a `CallNative` of a native `yavs.ieee.*` takes each array
  argument as four registers `data, left, right, dir` (`yavs_ir::ieee::ARRAY_REGS`: the address of the first plane block, the bounds of
  the one dimension and its direction as the descriptor stores them) and each scalar as one. The argument list is the formals in order, so
  `a + b` of two vectors has 8 registers, `resize (a, n)` 5. The verifier checks the register count from the key of the symbol
  (`ieee::arg_regs`; the `@<function id>` of a native that may give the call back is ignored); every other native keeps the fat pair.**
  Why: the fat pair `[data, dope]` in temporary memory cost `NewPair` + `FatRoot` per operand (the root is recorded until the statement
  ends: the interpreter keeps the temporary and `Stmt` does more work while one is recorded, and compiled code made a host callback for it),
  `NewDope` where lowering had to build the descriptor, and three dependent reads in the native (pair, descriptor, planes). With values,
  nothing is built and the native reads only the planes; the registers are live at the call, so the heap objects an operand points into stay
  pinned as for any `Ptr` register and no `TempRoot` is needed.
- Lowering (`expr.rs` `Conv::{Body, Fat, Flat}`, `Fx::array_cells`): `Flat` for the `ieee` natives and the user reduction idiom (which runs
  the `Reduce` native), `Fat` for every other native, `Body` for subprograms. The bounds of an operand are the registers its descriptor was
  made from when the `MakeDope` is in the same block (`Fx::made_dopes`, cleared by a `Move`, so a part register is never stale), else three
  loads from the descriptor (`dope_parts`). A descriptor that only the native read was a block that only a `MakeDope` writes: the existing
  dead-code sweep (`opt.rs` `dce`) removes the `Alloc` and the `MakeDope` once the call no longer reads them, so lowering does not have to
  know whether something else reads the descriptor.
- The old path is not kept next to the new one for "unusual" operands: an operand without a known descriptor (a parameter, a variable, the
  result of another native, an individually associated or converted formal) takes the three loads, so there is one convention to implement in
  every tier and in a Cranelift backend; a call that gives the body back (`Syn`, `Str`, `Div`, `NumGate` natives) makes the descriptors the
  body needs in temporary memory (`Machine::ieee_body`).
- Interpreter: `Op::CallIeee` copies up to `pre::IEEE_CELLS` (8) cells (was 4). `ieee::small` reads only the planes (it took the pair and
  the descriptor too), `dim_at` replaces `fat_dim`; the positions after an array operand are `A1` (4). `small_fat` is the fat-pair form the
  implicit `to_string`-family natives still use. The compiled tier needed nothing: it passes the cells of the registers to the same functions
  (`native_direct`, `step`), and a call of at most 8 registers still qualifies for the direct form.
- Optimiser: a `Load` of a word of a block that a `MakeDope` wrote on the path is the register the word was made from (`Key::Part`,
  `Opt::iat` finds the block and offset of an `Index` at a constant offset, killed by stores and calls like the other memory facts, `opt.rs`
  `forward`). Without it the loads that lowering emits for the bounds of a concatenation (a `Select` between two descriptors folded away)
  stayed in the code; with it the bounds of a freshly made vector are the registers or constants they were made from.
- The sharing of a repeated `to_integer` (#520, `opt/sink/calls.rs`) keys a call on `native, canon(data), left, right, dir` instead of the one
  fat-pair argument, so it still finds the pairs. The dump-shape test in `tests/sink.rs` does not tell (it passed with the sharing lost);
  the work-counter design `ieee_share` (ceiling 3630 ops, 3920 without the sharing, 4720 before both) does.
- Results stay a fat pair (the natives that give the call back return what the VHDL body does, somewhere else). Tried and dropped: a
  lowering that takes the data and descriptor addresses of the result block (`dst + 40`, `dst + 16`, the contiguous layout `put` writes)
  instead of loading them: the op count is the same (two `IndexImm` for `Load` + `LoadOff`) and the instruction count moved by -0.5 percent
  only, for a layout contract between lowering and the natives. A result chained into the next native (`to_integer (a + b)`) now costs the
  three loads of its descriptor (the bounds a fat pair let the native read); a three-word load op or natives returning the bounds in
  registers would remove them, not done (see STATUS.md).
- Not done: the result written into a buffer of the caller (the native allocates and appends its result block in one go, 15 to 25
  instructions with `put_small`, and the size is dynamic for most natives, so the caller would need arithmetic to size it), natives
  returning the bounds in registers (needs a multi-register result in the IR), and a three-word load op for the bounds of a result that is
  chained into the next native.
- Measured, `poc_arith_addw`, interpreter, first 300 us, `op-census` bench build before and after: ops 200.1 M to 185.8 M (`NewPair`
  11.9 M, `NewDope` 7.8 M and `FatRoot` 2.3 M gone; 5.2 M `Load`, 1.8 M `LoadOff`, 2.8 M `IndexImm` added), instructions 281.6 G to 261.1 G
  (-7.3 percent), output identical. Whole test, bench build, warm cache, core 14: interpreter instructions 220.5 G to 202.7 G (-8.1 percent),
  cycles (median of 3) 67.0 G to 61.7 G (-7.9 percent); `--tier=auto` instructions 150.4 G to 139.2 G (-7.5 percent), cycles 54.6 G to
  48.9 G; `realbench --compare` wall, interp 14.12 s to 12.66 s, llvm 15.96 s to 15.38 s, auto 10.99 s to 10.07 s. `neorv32_single_min`
  interp -1.4 percent, llvm -2.5 percent instructions; `poc_cache_cpu`, `sc5_fifo_repack`, `uvvm_util_rand`, `en_cl_fix_pkg` within 0.5
  percent (their `ieee` calls are few). Over all 42 realbench tests (interp and llvm): instruction geomean 1.00 and 0.99, no instruction
  ratio above 1.02. Work counters of the perf designs that call `ieee` natives fell by up to 29 percent (`reduce_idiom`), `slice_memo`
  rose by 1.4 percent (its bound has room); the bounds were lowered and `ieee_operands` added. Differential tests (510 designs, interp,
  llvm and auto, 1 and 4 threads) are identical.

  (-7.3 percent), cycles 136.7 G to 130.2 G (-4.8 percent), output identical. Work counters of the perf designs that call `ieee` natives
  fell by up to 29 percent (`reduce_idiom`), `slice_memo` rose by 1.4 percent (its bound has room); the bounds were lowered.

## Light `numeric_std` natives computed in compiled code (yavs-llvm `ieee_fast`, #698, 2026-10-24)

With the array operands of the `ieee` natives as values (#697) a call site has the data address and the bounds in
registers. For the operations whose own fast path is plain integer arithmetic on one word (`ieee::small`: 1 to 64
elements, only `0 1 L H`) the code generator now emits that arithmetic instead of the callback:

- **Operations:** `to_integer`; `+`, `-` (vector and vector, vector and integer, integer and vector); the relational
  operators (the same forms); `to_unsigned`, `to_signed`; `resize`; `shift_left`, `shift_right`, `rotate_left`,
  `rotate_right` and the `sll`, `srl`, `sra`, `rol`, `ror` operators; `and`, `nand`, `or`, `nor`, `xor`, `xnor`
  and `not` of `unsigned` and `signed` and of `std_ulogic_vector` (`ieee_layout` lists them).
- **One rule for what is not computed here:** every case the native does not answer in a word (a longer or null
  operand, a metavalue, `L`/`H` for the operations that move elements, a negative `natural`, an integer that does not
  fit `to_unsigned`/`to_signed`/`+ integer` (the native warns), a `to_integer` result above 2147483647, `to_signed (1, 1)`,
  `sra` of one element or by zero, a temporary area that must grow) takes the old callback (`yavs_rt_native_light`)
  from the same site, which runs the native and gives its warnings and errors unchanged. Reports therefore come only
  from the native: byte-identical output by construction. The bit tricks are the native's (`small_of`, `put_small`).
- **The result** is built exactly as `put_small` builds it: a fat pair, a descriptor and one plane block (72 bytes) in
  temporary memory, taken inline (`temp_alloc`).
- **Policy:** the site no longer counts as a callback for `--tier=auto` (`lower::leaves`).
- **Measured and not taken:** testing the temporary area, the instance data and the interpreter's top frame inline
  before `host` (frame-mode code calls `yavs_rt_host` for an address of unknown space): no change in instructions
  of `poc_arith_addw` or the window generator (within the run-to-run noise of 1 percent), so the plain `host` is used.

## Inlining: the instructions added at a call site keep the call's `via` (yavs-ir `opt/inline.rs`, #709, 2026-10-24)

- **Rule:** a call inside code that was itself inlined (a `CallProt` in the body of a wrapper the process inlined,
  taken by the second round `run_wide`) is inlined with the instructions it adds at the site (parameter moves, the
  result move, the jump into the body and the jump out) carrying the call's statement and the call's own `via`, not 0.
  With 0 the verifier saw a statement of the callee's function in code with no inlined call around it: a debug build
  could not run `poc_arith_addw`. The body's own instructions were right already.
- **Test:** `tests/sink.rs` `a_call_inside_inlined_code_is_inlined_with_the_calls_it_came_through` (the method is above
  the plain size limit until the optimiser folds a false constant away, so only the `wide` round takes it); it fails
  in a debug build without the change.

## llvm: liveness per basic block, the deferral cap is a memory guard, and the optimised register allocator measured (yavs-llvm, #710, #679, 2026-10-24)

- **Decision: `regs::Live::new` solves liveness per basic block and sweeps each block once for the rows** (it iterated over every
  instruction, up to 64 passes over `n * words` words). With the old cap lifted the LEON3 `iu:comb` copy (17 600 IR instructions, 11 100
  registers) made `Live::new` 11.8 percent of the instructions of the simulation thread of a run with a WARM compilation cache (the code of
  every function is generated for the cache key before the object is found), 2.8 percent of them without the cap raised; with the
  per-block solution it is not in the profile. `MAX_WORDS` is 1 << 25 words (256 MiB of rows), a memory guard only: a function over it
  gets no deferral. The rows are the same bits as before (checked on the 844 functions of a LEON3 run and by the unit test
  `rows_match_plain_iteration_for_a_function_over_the_old_cap` against plain iteration).
- **What the lifted cap gives (measured, LEON3 60 us, `iu:comb` forced, `--tier=auto --tier-heat=1,0,0`, core 11, medians of 7 interleaved,
  simulation thread):** instructions 86.59 G to 86.35 G (-0.3 percent), cycles level within the noise of the host (32.6 G against 31.7 G in
  one session, 37.3 G against 33.8 G in another: identical builds differ by that much between sessions). No gain to speak of because
  `Gen::std` defers a result only inside a loop (`Defer::loopy`; outside loops a deferred value would be stored at every guard exit it is live
  at), and `iu:comb` has hardly a loop. The neorv32 `exec_comb` (a loop) was under the cap already. `neorv32_single_min`,
  `fletcher_bufferreader`, `fletcher_bufferwriter_512`, `sc5_fifo_repack` with `--tier-heat=1,0,0`: instructions identical to the
  last digit, cycles within 0.5 percent. Default `--tier=auto` (`realbench --compare`, medians of 3): wall within 0.96 to 1.01, the whole
  LEON3 run 55.78 s to 55.80 s (instructions 665.97 G to 663.81 G).
- **The reloads of the three function arguments (task of #679): measured, and the lever is the register allocator, not the IR.** Machine code
  of the `comb` copy as `llc -O0` makes it with the generator's own switches (`Fast`: FastISel and the fast register allocator):
  20 306 basic blocks for 17 614 IR instructions, 308 884 of 812 000 instructions are `(%rbp)` accesses (38 percent), 46 977 of them the
  reloads of the three arguments (`env` 10 548, `regs` 13 869, `mem` 22 560: 5.8 percent of the instructions). They are not alias
  reloads: the fast register allocator spills every value that is live across a block at its definition and reloads it at its first use in
  each block, and the code has one block per IR instruction (every guard and every slow path's join start a block), so nothing the IR says
  (`noalias`, `readonly`, loading once in the entry block, passing through phis, calling conventions on the cold callbacks) changes that: a
  value in a phi or an argument is a live-across value all the same. x86 has no reserved-register switch to pin the views.
  **Measured lever: the optimised register allocation path at the same code generation level** (`-optimize-regalloc -regalloc=greedy` in
  `YAVS_LLVM_ARGS` on top of `CODEGEN_ARGS`; FastISel stays): static `(%rbp)` accesses -25 percent (216 008 against 289 193), instructions
  -7 percent; **dynamically, LEON3 60 us window, simulation thread: instructions 86.36 G to 78.62 G (-9.0 percent), cycles 30.9 G to 27.0 G
  (-12.8 percent)**, output identical to the interpreter's over the whole 1060 us run; the same switch with `--tier-heat=1,0,0` on the other designs (simulation thread, medians of 5): cycles `neorv32_single_min` -5.9 percent (instructions -2.2), `fletcher_bufferreader` -6.1 (-1.1), `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` -7.0 (-2.6), `sc5_fifo_repack` -1.2 (-0.3). Cost: the code generation of the 17 600-instruction
  function goes from 1.2 s to 10.8 s (2.1 s to 12 s the first compile), small functions at the `O0` level +45 percent. It is process-wide
  (an LLVM command line option), so a per-function choice needs the option set around the code generation of those modules only
  (`Module::emit`, under a lock the default code generations share) and a policy for which functions pay it (the hot large frame-mode
  functions the O2 recompile skips today: `level_for` sends them to `Fast`). That is a compile-cost policy decision, not made here;
  see #715.
- **Measured and not kept:** `-regalloc=basic` (static `(%rbp)` accesses +7 percent), `llc -O1` (35 s code generation for the function,
  553 000 instructions: -32 percent, `(%rbp)` accesses 107 702).

## The optimiser keeps the one definition of a constant that another block reads (yavs-ir `opt.rs` `kill_unreachable`, #714, 2026-10-24)

- **Rule:** `merge_consts` makes registers defined once by the same constant or address one register, wherever the
  definition is (frames start with such registers), so a `Const` in the `then` branch of a callee can be the register
  the `else` branch reads. When `tidy` after inlining folded the branch condition, `kill_unreachable` emptied the block
  with the only definition and the register was never defined: it read 0 (`put 0=0` for `put 20=0` in a release build,
  a verifier error in a debug build). A `Const`, `ConstF` or `AddrOf` of the frame, instance data or a constant that
  is the register's only definition in the function now stays while a reachable instruction (also in an operand list)
  reads the register; `drop_declarations` does the same for the declarative part.
- **Test:** `tests/sink.rs` `a_constant_shared_by_two_branches_survives_the_folding_of_one`.

## Carry-in aggregates and copies of the same module (yavs-lower, yavs-elab, yavs-llvm, #713, 2026-10-24)

Profile of `poc_arith_addw` by layer and by process (32 adder instances, 40.1 M process runs in 3.03 M delta cycles): the `z <=
... + ... + (0 to 0 => cin)` processes are 47 percent of the runs, the `s <= std_logic_vector(z(...))` conversion copies 31 percent,
and `--tier=auto` compiled every adder process with the full `O2` pipeline, one after the other. Decided by the performance agent
(no user ruling needed: no behaviour changes).

- **Decision: a choice range of at most four static elements in an aggregate of a one-dimensional array (`(0 to 0 => cin)`,
  `(3 downto 2 => x)`) is written element by element (`AGG_UNROLL` in `yavs-lower/src/expr.rs`); null ranges write nothing.** Why: the
  loop made the process a compute loop for `--tier=auto` (`auto::compute`: loops that do not leave compiled code), which asks for the
  full `default<O2>` pipeline (58 ms of passes for a 135-instruction process, against 6 ms for `LEAN`), and it kept the signal write
  out of the `CopyDrive` fusion; the straight code is 9 operations shorter per activation. A longer range stays a loop (a fill or a
  runtime loop as before). The element value is evaluated once either way.
- **Decision: a slice of a signal of a plain array type read as a value (`a(M-1 downto 0)`, the prefix a signal name) reads the
  sub-signal the slice selects (`Fx::sig_slice` with `sig_steps`, as `sig_part` does for the rows of an array of arrays).** Why: the
  lowering read the whole signal into a temporary and then copied the slice out of it (`AllocReadVec`, `SigReadVec`, `AllocLCopy`,
  `LCopy`); two operations and the bytes of the whole signal per slice, which for the slice of a wide bus is the whole bus. Bounds
  and the run-time error of a slice outside the signal are those of the other path (`walk_steps`, checked equal on both).
- **Decision: a concurrent `target <= conv(source);` where `conv` is a conversion of an array to an unconstrained array type (an array of
  the same element type, as `unsigned(v)` and `std_logic_vector(u(5 downto 2))`) is a kernel copy like `target <= source;`
  (`Walker::copy_source`, `same_array_values`).** Why: the conversion moves no value (the copy is positional), and these statements
  were 31 percent of the process runs of the adder testbench, each an interpreted process of 11 operations. A conversion to a
  constrained subtype (its length is checked), or between element types, is not a copy. #529 listed this shape as not covered.
- **Decision: `compile_one` compiles the copies of a process once per distinct module (`Jit::twins`).** A copy
  (`Program::copy_of`) is generated under the fixed name `ftwin`; its key is the hash of that module (bitcode) with the level, the
  `full` flag, the part and the native flag; the module is renamed to `t<key>` and compiled once per `Jit`, and another copy with the
  same key is those entry points. Why: instances that differ in data the code does not read (here the 24 and 8 adder processes
  that differ only in `ARCH`/`SKIPPING`/`P_INCLUSIVE`) are different functions with different copy tags but two or three distinct
  modules, and each was compiled alone (54 ms each on the cold path, 1.4 s of CPU in all, on the one core a pinned run has). A twin
  counts as linked from the cache for the auto budget (`objcache::note_twin`: it is charged the cache price, not the compile price,
  or the budget ends before the checker process is reached). The compilation cache has one object per module, found by the name
  its content gives, so a warm run finds it in whatever order the copies switch. Only copies are keyed this way. Same idea as the
  reference simulator's elaboration, which reuses the lowered code of instances that are equal (we do it after specialisation, on the
  generated module, so it holds whatever made the instances equal); nothing of its code or data layout is used.
- Not done / found on the way (issue #713): the auto policy refuses the loop-free CCC adder process (`cold()`, share under one
  eighth of the run at decision time); forcing it saves 0.3 to 0.5 s of 8.4 s. The checker process is compiled at 4.7 s of a cold run.
  Both are the auto policy's (#673, #675); the native operand convention (#697) and the callback layer (#698) own the two
  `ieee` calls per adder activation (228 instructions of callback per call); `enter`/`view_again` cost 217 instructions per compiled
  activation (compiled frame views).

## Cranelift tier, round 3: frame-mode host accesses, first-level rules per generator, variants charged to the budget (yavs-clift, yavs-llvm, #481, user, 2026-10-24)

The user asked for the policy constants tuned for Cranelift's cheaper translation, so that `clift-auto` ends clearly below the
interpreter on the window generator, `neorv32_single_min`, `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` and `poc_arith_addw`, and for the registers of
frame-mode code across blocks. Instructions of the whole process tree (`perf stat`, `--no-cache`, so every run is as cold as the first
one and the figures repeat), one `clift`-only release binary built with `tools/build-bench.sh`; 51 designs of `tools/bench` and
`tools/realbench` of 1 G instructions or more (the geometric mean is over them).

- **Decision: frame-mode code reaches an address of unknown space through `yavs_rt_host`, as the reference lowering does (#634); the
  inline chain of tests stays in native-frame variants.** Why: the chain (frame, temporary area, instance data by the high half of the
  address, then the object table) was 38 instructions and about 60 Cranelift instructions per access. It was 29 percent of the
  Cranelift instructions of `fletcher`'s frame-mode code (69 000 to 49 000), 18 percent of the compile time (2.89 to 2.36 G
  instructions on the compile thread), and 20 percent of the instructions executed in the two hot processes of `poc_arith_addw`
  (8 800 to 6 960 samples of a perf run). Measured against the same binary with the chain (`HOSTCALL=0`, panel of 51): geometric mean
  0.912 against 0.920, `xor_sig` 0.627 against 0.694, `xor_types` 0.598 against 0.686, `rtl_ff` 0.900 against 0.939. The earlier claim
  that those two processes ran 2.5 times the instructions of the LLVM code compared the generated code only: the reference
  lowering makes such accesses in a callback (and `Cat` of unknown length, which Cranelift does inline), which that count did not
  include; in whole-run instructions `poc_arith_addw` was 125 G before this round, 114 G after, and 115 G for warm LLVM `auto`.
  Since the merge with #711 the guesses of the shared `track` (`LikelyTemp`: a call's result and the words loaded from it;
  `LikelyHeap`: a pointer loaded from a variable's slot) are tested inline first in frame-mode code, as there: the temporary area
  by its address tag and length, the heap guess by the object table, and the runtime when it was wrong.
- **Decision: the clocked-process rules that depend on what the code costs to make are one struct (`Tune`), `Tune::MAIN` with the
  LLVM values and `Tune::FIRST` for a first-level generator: at least 64 IR instructions (was 120), no wait outside the 160 to 300
  band (was a quarter of a second), four instances (was 16) and a thirty-second of the run (was an eighth).** Why: Cranelift
  translates a fifth as slowly as LLVM and the trial takes back what does not gain. Sweeps of the three rules together (the panel;
  geometric mean 0.915 for the old values, 0.912, 0.910 and 0.908 for 2/64, 1/none and 4/32 instances/share, differences within
  the run-to-run noise of the policy): the designs that gain are those whose processes the old rules kept interpreted:
  `poc_arith_addw` 0.784 to 0.736 (eight processes of 86 IR instructions made eight times), `rtl_ff` 0.962 to 0.902, the stream
  repacker 0.842 to 0.816; no design got worse beyond its run-to-run spread (the verification-library testbenches spread most:
  1.2 to 1.5 of the interpreter's instructions in every setting, with the old binary too, #673). The payback factor, the budget
  percent, the callback limit and the budget factors of native and clocked functions were swept too and none moved a result
  beyond that noise, so they stay; a price of 33 microseconds per IR instruction (the measured mean) moved nothing beyond the
  spread of `poc_arith_addw` (its trial of `_p8` decides between 112 G and 119 to 151 G), so 45 stays. `YAVS_FIRST_TUNE=rtl_min=N,band=0|1,instances=N,share=N`
  replaces `YAVS_FIRST_RTL_MIN` and `YAVS_FIRST_BAND` (measuring aid).
- **Decision: under `--tier=auto3` a function compiled by Cranelift is compiled again by LLVM after 300 times its first-level
  threshold of running compiled (`Tune::o2_after`; was 30, and `YAVS_O2_AFTER`).** Why: the second level does not pay on these
  designs, it only adds LLVM's compile time to the run. `auto3` cold (`--no-cache`), instructions in G, window generator /
  `poc_arith_addw` / `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` / `neorv32_single_min`: 30 times 199.7 / 114.0 / 55.0 / 38.4, 100 times 195.8 /
  115.1 / 55.0 / 38.3, 300 times 191.0 / 113.9 / 55.0 / 38.3, 1000 times 190.5 / 112.5 / 53.9 / 38.2, no second level 188.1 /
  114.1 / 54.9 / 38.2; Cranelift alone is 188 / 114 / 55 / 38 and cold LLVM `auto` 230.1 / 115.9 / 56.5 / 38.3. 300 keeps the
  upgrade for what stays hot for a long run, at 1.5 percent over no second level on the window generator; the compute designs
  of `tools/bench` run for under a second and never reach it with either value (3.9 G for `compute_h2h`).
- **Decision: the policy tells its generators which functions it compiles together (`Generator::tree`), and the Cranelift generator builds
  native-frame variants of those only (`Jit::allow`); the variants a root's compile made are charged to the budget.** Why: building
  a function made a variant of every function in its native set. `peek` of the verification library (201 IR instructions, 9 ms in the
  model) took 112 ms: 26 variants of `log`, `alert`, `check_value` and the like, none of them seen running, which the policy had
  left out of its tree (`left_out`). Those variants were then also never charged: the callee's own compile found its variant
  and charged nothing, so the budget (2 percent times a factor of 16 for functions called natively) was spent more than three
  times over.
- **Decision: a Cranelift error from `define_function` (the verifier is on in debug builds) panics in debug builds with the function's
  Cranelift IR, and the panic of the compile thread is re-raised when the tier stops.** Why: a function that was silently left
  interpreted hid a dominance error in the previous round until the verifier was switched on by hand. A release build still leaves
  the function interpreted and says so with `--verbose`. `tests/verifier.rs` checks both paths.
- **Decision: compiled calls of memoised pure functions ask the memo (`yavs_rt_memo` before, `yavs_rt_memo_keep` after), as the
  LLVM lowering has since #701.** Why: Cranelift code made every such call; the window generator did 8 percent more instructions
  than with the memo (174 G against 189 G), `pure_memo` answered 0 of its 435 repeated calls (`clift::pure_memo` in `perf.rs`,
  and the Cranelift cases of `tests/pmemo.rs`). The probe and the keep are the shared callbacks of `rt.rs`; `CallProt` stays out, as there.
- **Tried and dropped: counting the `WaitOn`s of a wait that names the same signals every time as one callback in the callback rule
  of a first-level generator (`yavs_rt_wait_same` runs the whole list as one call).** Why it looked right: `counter_increment` of
  `neorv32_single_min` (45 `WaitOn`s of 399 IR instructions) is refused as "53 leave the compiled code" and pays when forced
  (-0.6 G). Measured with the rule: no panel gain (geometric mean 0.927 with it against 0.921 without, medians of 3 runs) and the
  neorv32 testbench 38.9 G against 38.3 G (medians of 5), so it was removed again; the benefit model on main decides such cases.
- **Not done: registers kept in Cranelift variables across blocks of frame-mode code.** Measured first, with the machine code of the
  hot processes attributed to the IR instructions (`YAVS_CLIFT_CODEDIR` writes the IR pc of every stretch of machine code next to
  it; `perf script` addresses give the executed instructions per IR instruction): in the loop-free processes of `poc_arith_addw`
  (87 IR instructions in one block on the hot path) the stores to the register array are 6 percent of the instructions generated
  code executes, which is 1 percent of the run, and the model of the reference lowering stores at once outside loops for the same
  reason (a deferred store must be written in every failing guard's exit block: code and compile time grow with guards times live
  registers). What remains in those processes is `Cat` of unknown length (22 percent), the entry and exit (19), two `CallNative`
  (15), `SubtypeCheck` (10): the work itself. The frame-mode loops of `xor_types` are 0.58 of the interpreter's instructions against 0.33
  for warm LLVM `auto`; its hot loop is a `CallNative` (a conversion), a `SubtypeCheck` and an `LCopy` per iteration (25, 27 and
  20 percent of the generated code, and 16 percent of the run in `yavs_rt_host`), so the gap there is in what is lowered
  inline, not in registers. No design of the four targets has a hot frame-mode loop; a design that has one decides whether the
  loop-only form (variables as phis in loops, as the reference lowering does) is worth its code.
- **Finding: the floor of `neorv32_single_min` is the tier, not the policy.** With nothing compiled (an experiment build that made every
  price huge) `clift-auto` runs 38.2 G against 37.7 G for `--tier=interp`: 0.43 G in the interpreter loop of a run with a tier
  (the watch bookkeeping of `run_ops::<_, true>`) and 0.07 G on the tier-up thread (#544). Compiling single functions changes it by at
  most +-0.3 G: only `counter_increment` pays (-0.6 G) and the callback rule keeps it interpreted (53 of its 399 IR instructions leave
  the compiled code, the limit is one in ten). A policy that picks by measured benefit (the work in progress on main) can get the
  design level; constants cannot.

## Cranelift tier, round 4: merge with main, what a first-level compile owes (yavs-llvm, yavs-clift, #481, #718, #544, #732, user, 2026-10-25)

The user resumed the Cranelift work after the pause for usage: merge main first (the generic `Worker` against #715, #725, #719,
#711, #726, #730 and #519), then the verification-library testbenches that run above the interpreter under `clift-auto` (#718), the
floor of `--tier=auto` (#544) and the vacuous bounds of the Cranelift perf cases (#732). Method as in round 3: instructions of the
whole process tree (`perf stat -e instructions:u`), `--no-cache`, one release binary from `tools/build-bench.sh --features
llvm,clift`, medians of 3 runs, no timing cores (cycles were not measured). Runs in parallel (four at a time) spread more than
serial ones: the policy decides on sampled CPU time, so a loaded host moves what compiles (#673), most on `uvvm_axistream_vvc`
and `uvvm_util_rand`.

- **The merge.** `OptLevel::FastRa` (#715) is an `OptLevel` like the others and the LLVM generator maps it to its own JIT (`jitr`);
  the policy keeps `Worker::fast` and `PAYBACK_RA`. The sampler of #725 starts from the compile thread as there. The shared native
  predicates (`yavs_llvm::native`) take `uniform_regs` (`Gen::uniform_fast` is LLVM only: the policy counts it inline for both) and
  `SigReadScalar` in native frames (#730); the Cranelift lowering did not have that last one (a signal operation made the function
  frame-mode only, and the compile of its native part failed, which the policy treats as a refusal of the whole function), so it
  lowers the table read in native frames as well, where the view has no answer the frame is materialised
  (`clift::sigfun` in `perf.rs`: 900 calls, `cb_step` 4). `Tune` stays per generator.
- **Finding (#718): the compiled code of library functions the interpreter calls gains nothing in instructions, and any compiled code
  makes the interpreter slower.** Forcing one function at a time (`YAVS_AUTO_FORCE`, every other rule off; deterministic):
  `uvvm_sb_slv` 13.34 G with nothing compiled, 14.38 with `match_identifier` (114 IR), 15.39 with `peek`, 16.57 with `log`;
  `find_expected_position` 13.34. The extra instructions are two things: the translation (`match_identifier`: 0.28 G on the tier-up
  thread; `peek`: a tree of 14 variants, 13 of them callees the sampler never saw, 100 ms; `log`: 3 G) and what the simulation thread
  executes once anything is compiled (`match_identifier`: +0.75 G, +0.31 G of it in `run_ops::<true, false>`, the interpreter loop
  of a run with compiled code, which executes 5 percent more instructions per op than the watching loop `<false, true>` of a run with
  a tier and no code). With the earlier policy the simulation thread executed about 1.6 G fewer instructions than the interpreter and
  the tier-up thread 3.7 G.
- **Decision: `Tune::FIRST` has two payback rules, `tree_payback` 8 and `payback_rtl` 16.** A root owes 8 times the price of the callees
  compiled with it (on top of the payback of its own price) before it is picked (`Worker::pick`, `repaid`); a clocked process
  16 times its own price (`threshold`). A nested subprogram entered in frame mode has no native variant to pay for and is exempt.
  `Tune::MAIN` is unchanged (0 and 0). Instructions in G, `clift-auto`, interpreter / before / now: `uvvm_sb_slv` 13.05 / 15.95 /
  14.01, `uvvm_util_rand` 15.16 / 18.69 / 15.64, `osvvm_axis_random` 4.72 / 5.56 / 4.95, `poc_cache_cpu` 8.80 / 9.54 / 9.42; the
  geometric mean of the eight library testbenches of the table in STATUS.md goes from 1.115 to 1.050 of the interpreter. The four
  designs: window generator 167.6 / 171.9 (+2.6 percent, 0.385 of the interpreter), `poc_arith_addw` 116.0 / 112.0,
  fletcher 52.9 / 53.6 (0.98), neorv32 41.5 / 40.9 (the tier's floor, 1.03 of the interpreter). `uvvm_axistream_vvc` is worse than
  before (1.09 to 1.16 of the interpreter's instructions where it was 1.04 to 1.10): a long run (2.7 s) in which the old policy
  compiled `check_value`, `await_cmd_from_sequencer` and others that gain. Why: the rest of the sweeps below show no setting that
  keeps both; the multiplier of 8 is the smallest that gets the short testbenches near the floor.
- **Sweeps and what they showed.** All on `clift-auto` with `YAVS_FIRST_TUNE`: the payback of native, compute and other
  functions at 8 and 32 and the native budget factor at 1, 4 and 16 (`peek` is in the compute class, which is paid back after 2
  times its price: its loops leave the compiled code rarely, which says nothing about whether compiling pays) moved `uvvm_sb_slv` by less than the spread of
  the runs; the price of the whole tree paid back 2, 4, 8 and 16 times (every class) gives `uvvm_sb_slv` 15.6, 14.3, 14.3 and 13.4 and
  the window generator 170, 176 and 187 for the first three (`fletcher` 56.0 at 8), which is why only the callees get the
  large multiplier; a payback for clocked processes of 4, 8 and 16 gives `poc_cache_cpu` 9.54, 9.42 and
  9.12 (no change on the processes of `hdlm_lfsr`, 39.1 G against 66.8 interpreted). Cranelift's `opt_level=none` and the
  single-pass register allocator (`YAVS_CLIFT_OPT`, `YAVS_CLIFT_RA`) did not lower the total (15.5 and 16.8 against 15.8).
- **Tried and dropped.** (1) No candidate that is a native-called function (the interpreter's calls into compiled code are the cost):
  `uvvm_sb_slv` at the floor, but the window generator 466 G against 169 and `poc_arith_addw` 153 against 125: the native roots
  are where those two designs get their gain. (2) No callees brought along because the caller calls them on every run
  (`Worker::hot`): no change, the sampler sees them anyway. (3) The first compile of a run needs a function that is a tenth, a
  fifth or a third of the sampled time (the interpreter loop tax is paid once): `uvvm_sb_slv` at the floor with a fifth, but
  fletcher 55.9 to 56.7 G against 53.4 and the idea needs the benefit model of the work-clock lane to decide per class. (4) Counting
  only the callees the sampler never saw as the tree: `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 40.0 G but `uvvm_sb_slv` 15.1.
- **Not fixed: the interpreter loop of a run with compiled code costs 5 percent more instructions per op than the watching loop of
  a run with a tier and nothing compiled.** It is the other half of #544 and shared interpreter code: a run whose compiled code
  saves less than that tax ends above the interpreter, however cheap the compiles are. The short testbenches stay 2 to 7 percent
  above (`uvvm_sb_slv` 1.07, `poc_cache_cpu` 1.07, `osvvm_axis_random` 1.05).
- **Decision (#544, all generators): the class rules of `Worker::threshold` (`natively`, `is_compute`, `is_rtl`) are asked only of a
  function at or above the base threshold of the heat.** Why: `natively` runs `native_set`, which walks everything the function
  can call and optimises each callee on the way (`Program::func`), and `see` asked it of every function the sampler ever saw, so the
  compile thread optimised library functions the run never executes (`hdlm_axi_fifo`: 323 function bodies optimised by the
  interpreter, 385 under the tier). A function below the base is no candidate whatever its class says (the class rules only raise
  the threshold), so nothing changes in what compiles. Instructions in G, interpreter / before / now,
  default policy: `hdlm_axi_fifo` 2.41 / 2.50 / 2.41 and `olo_base_cam` 2.68 / 2.81 / 2.68 under `clift-auto`, 2.51 and 2.81 /
  2.42 and 2.68 under LLVM `auto` (+7 and +5 percent with nothing compiled, `--tier-max-size=1`, before). The floor of
  the large runs (the watching loop, 0.5 G of `neorv32_single_min`) is untouched.
- **Decision (#732): the `cb_*` counters are printed for a build with `clift` and without `llvm`, and a counter a bound names must exist
  in a build that counts (debug, `op-census`).** Why: `callback_counts` was printed only with `llvm`, and `check_bounds` let any `cb_*`
  be absent, so every `Max` bound of the `clift` perf cases passed for any value (several were also the LLVM numbers: `cb_signal` of
  `reg_planes` was bounded at 108 and is 4). The bounds are the numbers of the Cranelift code now, each case has a floor on its
  drives or memo calls, and `llvm_sigfun` runs under `clift`.

## Cranelift tier, round 5: merge with main, a compiled-code cache (yavs-clift, yavs-llvm, #481, user, 2026-10-26)

The user decided to continue Cranelift toward replacing LLVM: a Cranelift-only build was level cold (0.46 of sim1's full total against
0.45 for LLVM `auto`) and 10 percent behind warm (0.28 against 0.25) because it had no compiled-code cache. Order: merge main, then
the cache.

- **Prices after the merge.** Main replaced the flat price per IR instruction and the `PAYBACK*` multipliers by a `Model` per `Kind`
  (price and speedup; the seen time before a compile is the price times `speedup / (speedup - 1)`). A first-level generator now
  prices every kind at `FIRST_US_PER_INSTR` (45 us an IR instruction, what Cranelift takes) with the speedups of `MODELS`; `Tune`
  stays the per-generator part: `Kind::RtlFew` is a clocked process of fewer than `Tune::instances` instances (4 for Cranelift,
  16 for LLVM), `cold` uses `Tune::share`, and `payback_rtl` and `tree_payback` come on top of the kind's need. Why: the merge
  should not move what Cranelift compiles. Measured cold on this tree (instructions, ratio to the interpreter, medians of 3):
  window generator 0.388 (round 4: 0.383), `neorv32_single_min` 1.025 (1.025), `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` 0.996 (0.978),
  `poc_arith_addw` 0.680 (0.714).
- **The Cranelift lowering keeps step with main**: the head of a fused scalar drive is `ScalarDrive::head` (#668), `Inst::Zero`
  is zeroed in place, a process that never suspends leaves compiled code at its retreating `Br` for the interpreter, which
  polls the stop request and bounds the activation (#737, #583, as the LLVM lowering since cd611e21), and `Drive`,
  `DriveSlot` and `SigRead` are lowered in native variants (`yavs_rt_drive_nat`), since the shared `native_set` takes functions
  with them (#730); without that their callers lost their variants under Cranelift.
- **The cache is Cranelift's own incremental cache over the work library's objects store** (`src/cache.rs`,
  `Jit::define_code`), one entry per Cranelift function (`clif-<key>.img`). The key is Cranelift's hash of the function body and
  the target, which leaves out the names of the functions and data the body refers to (relocations resolved when the code is
  linked), plus the yavs build and `yavs_ir::opt::fingerprint`. Why: a key over the CLIF text would have to rename the module's
  function and data ids, which depend on the order of the compiles, and hashing the text costs more than the hash of the
  structure; Cranelift's serialisation and relocation fix-up come with it. The body is generated again on a hit (the lowering
  and the inliner): neorv32 eager translates in 4 079 ms cold and links in 536 ms warm (1 804 functions). The callees a body
  calls are declared in id order, so a body is the same every run (one function in 1 804 missed every warm run before).
- **Policy.** The cache the policy probes, lists and notes is the one of the generator that makes a function's first code
  (`Worker::lead`). A probe's cached-only compile makes nothing the store lacks and does not remember a variant that failed so;
  a frame-mode body is defined once. A link from a first-level generator's cache is priced at `FIRST_HIT` (4 us an IR
  instruction, from the neorv32 figures), LLVM's at `HIT`. `--tier=auto3` uses the Cranelift store for its first level and the
  LLVM store for its O2 compiles. Not with `--no-cache`.

## Cranelift tier, round 6: merge with main, the ports, compute code quality (yavs-clift, yavs-llvm, #481, #583, #757, #763, user, 2026-10-26)

- **Merge** of `origin/main` (#756 frame blocks, #757 element loops, #583 the spin counter). Three LLVM-side changes of main
  reach the Cranelift lowering the same way, through the shared `rt.rs`, which now also holds `fuse_layout`,
