  `batched_drives` and `batch_pure` (moved from `yavs-llvm/src/lower.rs`, unchanged): the register-held jump count of a
  process that never suspends (a Cranelift variable, stored back by the exit block; the process stays compiled under
  the 10^9 bound, which closes #763 for this tier: `process/no_wait_infinite` passes), the element loops of a variant
  (`yavs_rt_eloop`), and the fused layout word (`yavs_rt_layout_word`). The kept-drive skip of the kernel (9c54654a)
  is reached through the drive batch, which the Cranelift lowering lacked: ported (`Batch`, 918 kernel calls against
  153 in `llvm_drive_batch`, now 153). Work-counter bounds for the four under `clift::`; `clift::layout_field` has a
  ceiling of 3 400 layout calls against LLVM's 1 648, because this lowering has no inline layout cache in frame mode,
  so the process's `LayoutOf`s go to the memo too (they were stepped before).
- **`--tier=clift-auto` gets the layout slots** (superseded by the user's decision in round 8: a switch of its own) (`yavs_interp::layout_slots`, as `auto` and `auto3`; an agent's choice, pending
  the user's confirmation: the user ruled on the memory of the slots for LLVM only, and a switch of its own for the #756
  gate is the alternative). Why: since #756 the
  slot pass keeps the 32-byte blocks the interpreter fuses out of the frame unless layout slots are on, and compiled
  code is slower with them (an `Alloc` in the temporary area before every signal read and concatenation). The merge
  alone took warm `clift-auto` on `poc_arith_addw` from 98.5 G to 101.5 G instructions and 34.9 G to 39.8 G cycles; with
  the slots 99.7 G and 36.2 G. The slots themselves cost memory in process frames that Cranelift code does not use.
- **Code quality of frame-mode code**, found by comparing the hot functions of `poc_arith_addw` and the window generator with
  LLVM's (paired `perf` profiles, samples per IR instruction from `YAVS_CLIFT_CODEDIR`): guesses of a register's space
  survive a fall-through block start (the entry after a call: 1 of 3 `yavs_rt_host` calls of an adder process); dope reads
  use the register's facts; small `Copy`s of a known size are words (`memmove` was 3.4 G instructions against 0.4 G for
  LLVM); a 32-byte temporary of run-time size is zeroed by stores (a `memset` and then 8-byte reads of the same bytes
  stalled on store forwarding: a fifth of the cycles of the adder process); `index_muls` as in the LLVM lowering.
- **Tried and dropped** (eager `--tier=clift` A/B on claimed cores, which is deterministic where warm `auto` is not, #673):
  the register array's address in the pinned register (regalloc kept it in a stack slot and reloaded it before 15
  percent of the instructions of a large process; pinned, the reloads are gone, cycles are level and instructions 2
  percent up from the copies `get_pinned_reg` makes); the register cache kept across the join of a slow path (minus the
  instruction's registers): 1 percent more instructions and cycles, longer live ranges. Cranelift's `opt_level`
  `speed_and_size` against `speed`: the same instructions on `poc_arith_addw`. The inline threshold (`YAVS_CLIFT_INLINE`,
  largest inlined body in Cranelift instructions) on the window generator: 0 gives 144.5 G instructions, 150 (the default)
  144.7 G, 300 145.4 G; 600 fails with an internal error (#765). Inlining larger bodies buys nothing here.
- **What is left** is the code of the hot functions themselves, which LLVM's optimiser makes about 1.35 times shorter and
  runs at a higher IPC: the frame-mode code of a process stores every register it defines and reloads it after every
  join and callback, the base pointers live in stack slots, and the pointer chains of the test runner's accessors
  (`get`) wait on the object table. The next step is deferred register stores with liveness and values carried across
  blocks in frame mode, as the LLVM lowering has (decisions "Tight compute loops").

## Cranelift tier, round 7: deferred register stores, values across entries, shared copies (yavs-clift, yavs-llvm `rt.rs`, #481, 2026-10-26)

- **Registers the interpreter preloads are never stored** by frame-mode code (`Gen::preset`, `rt::preloads`), as in the
  LLVM lowering: a `Const` or a non-`Up` `AddrOf` defined once is in every frame the interpreter makes. Eager
  `--tier=clift` `poc_arith_addw` 109.9 G to 108.0 G instructions.
- **Deferred register stores in processes** (the LLVM lowering's "Tight compute loops", first part): the definitions
  of a `quiet` instruction (arithmetic, compares, moves, constants, addresses, `Load`, `Index`, `DopeLen`, `SigVal`;
  `Store`, `Copy`, `Zero`, checks and `MakeDope` pass them) stay Cranelift values (`Gen::pend`) and are stored where
  the frame is looked at: an exit (`leave_at`, the registers live at its pc by `regs::Live`; at another pc than the
  instruction's own its definitions too), the block of a slow path (`snaps`: the values from before the instruction,
  stored before the step), the start of any other instruction (`spill`: it may call out), a block start a jump leads
  to. A register live over more than `MAX_SPAN` (4) instructions is stored at the definition, as in the LLVM lowering.
  Only processes (`FuncKind::Process`): the liveness and the stores cost every compile, and the hot frame-mode code
  is processes' (functions run on native frames).
- **Values across joins and entries.** A slow path's join takes the definitions of the fast path as block parameters
  and the slow block loads them from the frame after the step (`join_with`); the result of a direct native call and
  of an in-place `ieee` native likewise. A block start no jump leads to (the entry after a call, a wait, a report)
  takes the live values in hand as block parameters, and the facts of `known` carry over (the only way there is the
  instruction before it, compiled or interpreted); the switch over the entries is now made last (`dispatch`), where
  a stub for such a block loads its parameters from the frame. Why: the hottest IR instruction of the adder processes
  of `poc_arith_addw` began by loading again the native's result the instruction before had just stored.
- **Measured** (eager, combined `llvm,clift` bench build, claimed cores, `perf record` samples per function): the
  adder processes `f96` and `f93` 13 and 8 percent fewer instructions, 7 and 9 percent fewer cycles; `procChecker`
  (`f38`) 17 and 9 percent. Against the LLVM tier's eager code the adder processes are now level (`f96`) and 3 percent
  faster (`f93`), `f38` 37 percent faster. The whole eager run: 2 percent fewer instructions, cycles within the
  noise (the processes are a quarter of it). Measured the same way (fixed-period sampling) before the round, eager
  `f96` took about 1.07 times LLVM's cycles; under `--tier=auto` the copies of the next point were most of the gap.
- **Copies of a process with the same code are one definition** (`Jit::bodies`): the key is Cranelift's
  `compute_cache_key` of the body with the external names it refers to, for copies only (`Program::base_of`), the
  same idea as the LLVM tier's twins. `--tier=clift-auto` defined 36 copies of the adder processes where LLVM's
  cache shares 4; each copy ran cold in the caches. Warm `--tier=clift-auto` `poc_arith_addw`: cycles 32.9 G to
  29.5 G (LLVM `auto` 26.9 G), instructions level.
- **A 16-byte load across two 8-byte stores waits.** `yavs_rt_drive` read the plane block of a waveform element as four
  words, which the compiler paired into a 16-byte load across two of the `Copy` stores (Cranelift's words; LLVM's
  `memmove` is one 32-byte store, which forwards): 95 percent of its samples on that load, 3.7 percent of the run.
  `Copy` of up to 64 bytes now stores pairs of words as 16 bytes and the drive callbacks read the block as one
  32-byte copy (`rt::plane_block`, two 16-byte loads at the pairs' offsets): `yavs_rt_drive` and `drive_now` 2 880
  to 1 410 samples of about 57 000. Tried first and dropped: one 8-byte load per word (`black_box` on the index) moved
  the stall into `drive_now`, which reads the block it is passed in 16-byte halves.
- **Compile cost.** The share key hashed every frame-mode function (`sha256` 270 M instructions in the eager compile of
  the window generator) and the list of deferred registers was a scan of all registers per slow path: keys for
  copies only, a list of the deferred registers (`plist`). Eager `--tier=clift --no-cache` of the window generator up
  to time 0: 38.29 G instructions before the round, 38.13 G after.
- **Not changed:** the native variants of the test runner's accessors (window generator, item 3 of #481): eager, the
  Cranelift variants of `get` and `set` take fewer cycles than LLVM's eager code, `unsafe_pop` and `decode` 1.4 and
  1.5 times; under `auto` LLVM's code is faster. `procChecker` under `--tier=auto` takes 1.5 times the cycles of
  LLVM's O2 code.
- **#765, the internal error with `YAVS_CLIFT_INLINE=600`:** Cranelift's inliner (0.137, `create_global_values`) copies
  a callee's `GlobalValueData::Symbol` as it is, with the callee's `UserExternalNameRef`, which in the caller names
  whatever the caller declared under that index: an inlined `encode (boolean)` read one of its caller's constants as
  its string's descriptor. Function references are translated, symbols are not. A body with a symbol (a constant
  copy or a `std_ulogic` table, `symbol_value`) is no longer inlined (`Inl`); a callee under the default threshold
  (150) can have one too. Test: `crates/yavs/tests/clift_inline.rs` (an inlined
  callee returning string literals; the old build printed `<0:>` for `<0:TF>`). An upstream report is the user's call.

## Cranelift tier, round 8: the object table by machine, the layout slots apart, constant descriptors (yavs-clift, yavs-ir `opt`, yavs-llvm `auto.rs`, #481, user, 2026-10-26)

- **Merge** of `origin/main` (2ebc8fb5 the object table keyed by machine, c2dd4b2c the `auto` policy of #762, f320c0dc and the
  rest). The Cranelift lowering reads the tag and the entry offset of the keys (`Mem::slot`, `MEM_TAGS`, `MEM_MIXES`,
  `Gen::obj_tag`) for its inline lookups (`obj_lookup`: the heap's tag for a heap object or a guess, the address's space
  otherwise) and its `Deref` hit test (handle and tag), as the LLVM lowering. `compiled_instances` runs the Cranelift
  tiers too. The policy's compile wrapper of #762 (frame-mode code linked along with native-frame code the cache had)
  goes through the generator of the compile (`Worker::hits_of`, `cached_only`), not the LLVM cache; the price of a module
  is the function's (main dropped the halving per part), `FIRST_HIT` and `FIRST_US_PER_INSTR` for the first level.
- **The #756 gate has a switch of its own** (user, 2026-10-26: `--tier=clift-auto` spends no process-frame memory on the
  layout slots by default). `opt::frame_blocks` keeps the 32-byte blocks the interpreter fuses in the frame without the
  layout slots (`frame_blocks_on`, fingerprint `blocks`); `clift-auto` turns it on, `YAVS_CLIFT_LAYOUT_SLOTS=1` gives it
  the layout slots as before (a measurement knob; a command-line option instead is the user's call). Measured, realbench
  `--compare --runs 5` `poc_arith_addw`, cores 10 and 11: warm 6.10 s and 93.52 G instructions without the slots, 6.07 s
  and 93.60 G with them, peak RSS 43.5 and 43.8 MB; cold 6.26 and 6.32 s. The slots buy nothing for Cranelift code; the
  blocks in the frame are what mattered (round 6: without both, 3 percent more instructions and 14 percent more cycles).
- **A copy that shares another's body counts as linked from the cache** (`Jit::bodies` calls `cache::note_hit`, as the LLVM
  tier's twins `note_twin`): the budget charged a full compile (45 us an IR instruction) for code that was not compiled.
  `YAVS_AUTO_TRACE`, cold `--tier=clift-auto` `poc_arith_addw`: 30 of 74 copies are shared bodies, now ` hit` at 4 us an IR
  instruction; spent 59.8 ms of the budget where the old price would have been about 169 ms.
- **Positions in constant descriptors** (`Gen::const_dim`): a `Pos` whose descriptor register holds a constant-pool address
  reads the dimension's words when the code is made; with a direction of 0 or 1 and a range that is not empty the position is
  one unsigned compare of the index minus the low bound and, downward, a subtraction; anything else keeps the generic code,
  whose slow path is the interpreter's error. A `BinRange` with constant bounds checks them with one unsigned compare
  (`range_exit`). Eager `--tier=clift` (claimed cores, medians of 3): `poc_arith_addw` 105.8 G to 103.0 G instructions, the window
  generator 150.8 G to 149.0 G; warm `clift-auto` `poc_arith_addw` 93.6 G to 90.7 G instructions, 30.2 G to 29.5 G cycles. Test:
  `crates/yavs/tests/clift_const_dims.rs`.
- **Tried and dropped:** values of earlier instructions kept in hand across the joins and callbacks of an IR block (`clear`
  forgot every value but the deferred ones; a callback writes only its instruction's registers): eager `poc_arith_addw`
  0.9 G more instructions, cycles level. Regalloc spills the longer live ranges to the stack, which costs what the reload
  from the register array did. The block-parameter plan of the LLVM lowering for loops (registers carried across the blocks
  of a loop) was not ported for the same reason: the hot loops here (`procChecker`) hold dozens of live registers.
- **Where the rest is** (`perf record`, warm `auto`, `poc_arith_addw`): `procChecker` takes 1.55 times LLVM O2's instructions and
  1.64 times its cycles, so the gap is the amount of code, not its IPC. In the Cranelift code the `Load` and the `Store` back
  of the same heap word (the assertion counter of the inlined `simAssertion`) each do the whole object-table look-up from
  the address register reloaded from the frame (the `Store` alone has 9 percent of the process's samples), the `Mem` pointer
  is reloaded from a stack slot before each use in a look-up, and an overflow test sets a flag byte and tests it (`seto`,
  `test`, `jne`). An object kept in hand after a `Deref` in frame-mode code (as native frames do) is the next step there.
  The copies of the adder processes take 1.18 times LLVM's instructions.

## Cranelift tier, round 9: objects in hand in frame mode, one branch per compare, the native chain by space (yavs-clift, #481, 2026-10-26)

- **Merge** of `origin/main` (31ea022e the shared std store, 7076335e `WaitEdgeSuspend`, db3176aa the callee-aware
  payback rule, b73eda27 and eb4b4963 of the optimiser, the rest). Nothing of it touches the compiled tiers but the
  space facts of #768 (`regs::Sp::Likely`, a pointer loaded from a variable's slot), which the Cranelift lowering
  reads as `Known::LikelyHeap` as the LLVM lowering does; the interpreter's new op and the policy apply to both
  generators unchanged. Two new policy tests of `auto.rs` use helpers that exist with LLVM only: `#[cfg(feature =
  "llvm")]` on them, since this branch compiles `auto.rs` for Cranelift too.
- **The object a `Deref` found stays in hand in frame-mode code** (as in native frames): the fast path passes the
  entry's pointer and length and the value to the join as block parameters; the callback's way checks the entry
  again and the interpreter's step passes length 0 (a valid pointer for no bytes), so a way that cannot vouch for the
  entry sends every access to its slow path, never to a wrong object. The `Load` and the `Store` back of the
  assertion counter of `procChecker` no longer look up the object table each. Eager `poc_arith_addw` 103.0 G to
  101.7 G instructions; against the LLVM tier's eager O2 code (`YAVS_LLVM_FAST_MIN` raised) `procChecker` is now
  1.03 times its instructions (was 1.55 under `auto`).
- **Overflow tests of an addition or subtraction of a constant** compare the result with the operand (`add`, `cmp`,
  `jcc`, where `sadd_overflow` was `seto`, `test`, `jne`: Cranelift 0.137 folds the flags of `uadd_overflow` and the
  multiplications into a branch but not those of the signed additions), and a `BinRange` whose constant bounds lie
  inside `MIN + c ..= MAX` (c > 0; the mirror for c < 0) has none: every wrapped sum is outside the bounds, so its
  range test leaves at the same pc. 0.1 to 0.4 percent of the eager instructions.
- **One branch per compare** (`Gen::brif_split`, used by `guard`, `exit_if`, `branch` and every plain `brif`): a
  branch on the `band` or `bor` of compare results is a compare and a conditional jump each; Cranelift made the
  truth values (two `setcc`, `and`, `test`, `jne`) for every bounds test and object-table hit. Only truth values are
  split (compare results and such combinations); a `band` of words keeps its meaning.
- **`Pos` of a descriptor that is not a constant has one arm per direction** (the LLVM lowering's), instead of
  selects over both directions and three tests.
- **The native-frame chain goes by the address's space** (`Gen::host`, `view_try`, `obj_try`): a frame address is
  tested against the frame's own slots, a native caller's (`Mem::nslots`) and the interpreter's top frame; another
  against the temporary area and (reading) the instance data, then the object table; `yavs_rt_host` last. Before,
  every access made selects over the frame, temporary and instance views (seven loads from `Mem`) before the first
  test. Tried and dropped: the object table first for addresses outside a frame (the LLVM lowering's order; window
  generator +3.0 percent instructions, its natives read call results in the temporary area more than heap objects),
  and the object table first unless the register holds a likely temporary (+2.6 percent).
- **Address parameters used in loops are resolved at the entry of a native frame** (`param_addrs`, `yavs_rt_region`,
  `Known::Param`), as in the LLVM lowering: an access tests the held region, the ordinary lookup when it fails.
  `unsafe_push` and `decode` of the window generator 39 and 30 percent fewer instructions, the window generator as a
  whole 0.2 percent fewer (`yavs_rt_region` 0.8 G). The samples of `set` (`f24`, no loop, no address parameter, its
  code unchanged) rose from 768 to 1 439 in the same pair of eager profiles, not explained; the LLVM tier's eager O2
  `set` has 1 794.
- **Measured** (eager `--tier=clift`, combined bench build, claimed cores, second of two interleaved runs, a private
  copy of the world per binary: the eager code cache of a world holds about four builds' functions, `OBJ_MAX_ENTRIES`):
  the window generator 148.3 G to 123.2 G instructions and 41.9 G to 36.9 G cycles, `poc_arith_addw` 103.0 G to
  99.7 G. Warm, the combined build: `--tier=clift-auto` window generator 126.1 G instructions and 40.1 G cycles
  against `--tier=auto` 137.8 G and 44.2 G, `poc_arith_addw` 87.4 G and 27.6 G against 85.9 G and 27.9 G.
- **The adder copies of `poc_arith_addw`** (item 3 of the round-8 list, 1.18 times LLVM's instructions under `auto`):
  against the LLVM tier's eager O2 code their own instructions are 1.6 to 1.9 times, but the LLVM lowering leaves their
  `Cat` to the interpreter (`cat_block`, `cat_words`, `cat`: 4 030 samples) where the Cranelift lowering makes it inline;
  the compiled code plus those callbacks is level (9 268 samples against 9 306, eager, `instructions` every 3 M).
- **Ideas of the reference simulator** (sim1, rule 22): its IR tells an overflow-checked addition from a plain one and
  checks overflow on the width of the type's representation, and its code generators branch on the flag the addition
  sets; ours decides from the constant bounds of the `BinRange` that no test is needed, and compares the sum with the
  operand because Cranelift does not fold the signed overflow flag into a branch. Its bounds checks are a compare and a
  conditional compare with one jump; Cranelift has no conditional compare, so ours is a jump per compare. Its access
  values are host pointers, so there is nothing to look up; keeping the object a `Deref` found in hand for the rest of
  the stretch is the nearest this design (addresses as space, index and offset, an object table) gets to that.
- **Not taken:** the `Mem` pointer stays in a stack slot that regalloc reloads at most block starts of a lookup
  (`procChecker` after the round: 4 percent of its samples on those reloads, and the function is 2 percent of the
  run); a pinned register was tried in round 6. The native variants of the window generator still take 1.2 times
  the instructions of LLVM's O2 code (`get` 1.25, `unsafe_push` 1.5, `decode` 1.3), its frame-mode processes 1.8
  times. In warm `clift-auto` `poc_arith_addw`, `drive_now` takes 850 samples of 29 600 where LLVM `auto` takes
  17: the first-level rules compile the `_p1` processes (four copies, `instances` 4 of `Tune::FIRST`) that the LLVM
  rules leave interpreted; `YAVS_FIRST_TUNE=instances=16` or `share=8` did not change the run in two measurements
  each (warm `auto` runs vary by 1 to 2 percent).

  load of the native's result and the jump back each take 60 to 90 machine instructions. The frame's register array
  and the `Mem` pointer live in stack slots and are loaded again before nearly every access (the function is 26 KB, the
  register allocator spills both), the temporary-area guess of the native's result is tested in full every iteration,
  and `SubtypeCheck` recomputes both lengths from the dopes with conditional moves where LLVM's O2 hoists all of it.

  realbench set in instructions (1.004 warm, 0.98 cold; cycles 1.013 and 0.987) and passes every
  difftest candidate, but warm compute loops run up to twice LLVM's instructions (h2h warm 1.18). Go once:

     level (`yavs_ir::opt`, so both generators gain), measured on `xor_types`, `lfsr64`, `compute_h2h`, `hdlm_lfsr`;
  2. the compiled copies of clocked processes lose their cache misses (`fletcher_bufferwriter_512`, `grlib_leon3mp`,
     `sc5_fifo_repack`);
  3. a cache hit costs what it is priced at (`FIRST_HIT` over the whole tree, or a key over the IR that skips generation:
     the maintainer's decision that #785 left open for LLVM applies here too);
  4. the release side: the `clift` feature in the default features and in the archive without LLVM (#780); the default
     tier and `--version` are done.
  Until then the useful step is the archive without LLVM: a Cranelift build is faster than the interpreter-only build
  everywhere it compiles, needs no LLVM, and its policy is the same `auto`.
- Gates on 921b3059 (code of this round): fmt, clippy `-D warnings` for default, `llvm`, `clift`, `llvm,clift`; `cargo test

## Frame-mode code tests the temporary area and the object cache inline for addresses it can guess (yavs-llvm `Gen::host`, `rt::track`, #711, 2026-10-24)

- **Finding:** the `yavs_rt_host` calls of `llvm_ieee` (`cb_host` 1416, then 2019 after the in-place `numeric_std`
  natives, #698) did not come from the native frame of the function that reads the parameters: 2116 of 2119 came from
  the frame-mode code of the process, which always asks `yavs_rt_host` for an address of unknown space (#634). The
  natives had read their operands inside the runtime callback; the inline code reads them through `host`. By space:
  the temporary area (the fat pair a call or native returned, the two words loaded from it, the dope and plane block
  they point at, the words of a layout: 80 percent in `poc_arith_addw`, 76 percent in `llvm_ieee`) and heap objects
  (process variables: the plane reads and the `LCopy` and `LSet` writes, 52 percent in `sc5_fifo_repack`). The earlier
  trial (below, "Measured and not taken") put its tests into the native-frame chain, which these designs do not use.
- **Decision:** `rt::track` gives a register a guess, not a fact: `Known::LikelyTemp` for the result of a `Call`, a
  `CallNative` and a `LayoutOf` and for the 8-byte words loaded from such an address (also through `Move` and `Index`),
  `Known::LikelyHeap` for an 8-byte word loaded from the slot of a local variable (`Known::Frame` that is no parameter's
  slot, or `Known::Up`: a caller passes any space, a variable's object is a heap object). Frame-mode `Gen::host`
  tests a guess at run time before it asks the runtime: `LikelyTemp` is `hi == TEMP` and the bounds against the view's
  length; `LikelyHeap` and `Known::Heap(None)` (a `Deref` of this stretch) are the object cache entry (`obj_entry`,
  the first test of the native-frame chain). A miss takes the call as before, so a wrong guess costs the failed test
  and never a wrong read. A guess is never `Known::Temp`: that path checks only the offset, so a wrong fact there would
  read silently wrong data. A native frame ignores `LikelyHeap` (it finds its own slots by their address) and keeps its
  chain.
- **Also:** `track` cleared the fact of register `r + 1` for every definition of `r`; it does it only for a signal
  reference (two cells), as the other analyses of the file do (`preloads`, `fixed_consts`). In `Load r18 <- [r17]`,
  `Load r17 <- [r20]` the second no longer loses the fact of `r18`.
- **Measured** (bench builds, core 12, `perf stat` user cycles and instructions, medians of 5 interleaved runs, base
  3df7bc44; the host was loaded, single cells vary by 2 to 3 percent): `cb_host` in a debug build (`--tier=llvm`, windows of
  3, 10 and 2 us): `llvm_ieee` 2119 to 8, `poc_arith_addw` 343 248 to 26 313, `sc5_fifo_repack` 659 398 to 35 600, the
  window generator 104 834 to 54 875 (the rest: `CONST` reads by `LCopy` whose constant has no global; package and
  protected-object addresses of native frames). Cycles, `--tier=llvm`: `poc_arith_addw` -0.8 percent, `sc5_fifo_repack`
  -2.4, window generator -1.0 (instructions -0.9, -1.0, -0.6); `--tier=auto`: `poc_arith_addw` -3.0 percent (instructions
  -1.8), the window generator -1.4 (the instructions of the same binary swing 165 to 180 G between runs under `auto`),
  the others level within the noise (`sc5_fifo_repack`, `uvvm_sb_slv`, `osvvm_axis_random`, `neorv32_single_min`,
  `fletcher_bufferwriter_512`: -0.1 to +1.3 percent). **Cost:** the tests are code. LLVM
  instructions before optimisation, `--tier=llvm` (every function compiled): `neorv32_single_min` +2.0 percent,
  `poc_arith_addw` +9.2, `uvvm_sb_slv` +9.7, `osvvm_axis_random` +13.2; the temporary area tests are two thirds of it
  in `poc_arith_addw`, half in `osvvm_axis_random`. `--tier=llvm` runs of library testbenches are mostly code
  generation, and take that much longer (`osvvm_axis_random` +4 percent cycles of a run of 11 s in a first
  measurement); `--tier=auto` compiles what is hot only.
- **Not done:** native frames of the window generator miss in `Mem::find` for package and protected-object addresses
  (`PKG`, `SHARED_HEAP`: about 3 000 `host_miss` per us). The test sequences could be smaller (the `hi == TEMP` test
  and the mask as one subtraction and compare).

## llvm: element access in native frames, and what the cycles of a protected accessor are (yavs-llvm `lower.rs`, #493, 2026-10-24)

Where the cycles of the test runner's pointer-table accessors go (window generator, `get` of the string table, about 130 cycles
and 285 instructions per call before this round): the instructions of the call and return are about 55, and the rest is four
object look-ups (access value, key, entry, pointer), three array positions (descriptor, direction, range test, scaled offset,
bounds) and the load, one after the other: each hop of `st.idxs(ref)`, `st.ptrs(s.id)`, `ptrs(id)(index)` waits for the load
of the access value before its key can be made, for the entry before the object is known and for the descriptor before the
position is known. Sampled, the stalls sit on the compare of the entry after each access value loaded from a heap object.
So both the length of the chain and the number of instructions matter, and what shortens neither does not pay (below).

- **`Pos` has one arm per direction** (L, `Gen` `Inst::Pos`): upwards `i - l` against `r - l` and `l <= r`, downwards `l - i`
  against `l - r` and `r <= l` plus `dir == 1`, a phi for the position, instead of selects over both and the three tests
  of the generic form (`dir <= 1`, `lo <= hi`, range). Any other direction still leaves for the interpreter. The two forms
  accept exactly the same positions (the null range, the full `i64` range and the extremes included). Test:
  `crates/yavs/tests/compiled_arrays.rs` runs ascending, descending, null and one-element ranges, records and
  the errors of an index outside the range in every tier (the same text and status). Measured alone: window generator
  `--tier=auto` warm 171.9 to 165.9 G instructions, 52.6 to 50.6 G cycles.
- **A multiplication by a constant that only feeds the `Index` after it is one test of its operand** (L, `index_muls`,
  `Cur::imul`, `Cur::fused`): the offset `pos * size` of an element was a checked multiply (the overflow test is six instructions
  for a power of two) followed by the 4 GiB guard of `Index`. With the operand at most `(0xffff_ffff - held offset) /
  (factor * stride)` neither can fail, so the test is the only one and the `Index` after it has none; the operand outside the
  bound (also a negative one) leaves for the interpreter at the multiplication, where the `Index` would have left anyway. Without
  a held object of known offset the operand is held to `0xffff_ffff / factor` and the `Index` keeps its test of the sum alone.
  Only a product defined once and used once, by the next instruction, which is no entry point; a stride of 0 never.
- **An entry of the object table is one cache line, and its key is built from the whole value** (L, `Obj` aligned to 64
  bytes, `OBJ_SHIFT`, `Gen::obj_entry`): the index sits at bits 32 and up of an address and of an access value, the shared-heap
  flag at bit 61 and bit 57, so `((v >> 26) & 0x3fc0) ^ ((v >> 52 or 48) & 0x200)` is the offset of the entry: two chains
  side by side and one exclusive or, no scale by 40, and an entry never straddles two lines. Same entry as `obj_at`
  (test `obj_entry_expression_is_obj_at`). The table is 16 KiB per machine instead of 10.
- **Measured** (bench builds; the window generator in the world of `tools/realbench`, core 9, `perf stat` of the main thread,
  medians of interleaved runs). `--tier=llvm` (deterministic): window generator 218.39 G instructions and 76.6 G cycles, then
  214.33 G / 76.9 (descriptor), 211.54 G / 76.1 (multiplication), 210.98 G / 73.9 (entry); `protected_queue` 5.329 G and 1.361 G
  cycles, then 4.932 / 1.247, 4.748 / 1.229, 4.655 / 1.165. `--tier=auto`, 12 untimed runs of a private world before the timed
  ones (the set of compiled functions keeps growing for about ten runs: fewer warm-up runs compare a settled build with an
  unsettled one), 5 interleaved runs: 159.8 to 152.1 G instructions and 50.6 to 48.3 G cycles. `tools/realbench --compare`
  (same worlds, warm): wall 11.77 to 10.84 s (0.92), instructions 0.93; cold 15.69 to 15.75 s (instructions 0.96); against the
  reference simulator, instructions warm 2.47 to 2.26 times, cold 3.31 to 3.12. Regression set (17 tests: the verification
  libraries' queues and scoreboards, `neorv32_single_min`, `poc_arith_addw`, `fletcher_bufferwriter_512`, `sc5_fifo_repack`):
  instructions within 1 percent of the base, wall within the run-to-run spread (`poc_arith_addw` 8.61 s both, 7 runs).
- **Measured and not taken: LLVM inlines the native callee** (a private `alwaysinline` copy of each small callee in the caller's
  module, same code and exits, so no new semantics; `always-inline` ahead of the pipeline). Protected accessors of
  at most 100 IR instructions inlined into their callers: `protected_queue` `--tier=llvm` -4.7 percent instructions, cycles level;
  window generator `--tier=auto` warm -2.5 percent instructions, cycles +1 percent (limits 70 and 120 alike); callees under 45
  instructions (`"and"`, `"srl"`, wrappers): nothing. Every small callee inlined in `--tier=llvm` (limits 60 and 100): +15 and +66
  percent instructions, +30 percent and 2.6 times the cycles (the bigger module is generated and hashed in the main thread).
  The accessors wait for loads, not for the call and return, so removing 55
  instructions of overlapped work buys nothing; a larger unit costs compile time and instruction cache. The IR inliner's
  limit of 60 (above) and the full `O2` pipeline for the accessors (`YAVS_LLVM_PIPELINE`): no change either.
- **Left**: the chain itself. Ideas that would shorten it need the interpreter's heap (a handle that carries its slot, #655 was
  slower with a flat view), or lookups kept across calls (needs inlining and alias scopes for object bytes against `Mem`, and a
  memory-aware CSE in the pass pipeline, which costs compile time); the address of a by-reference parameter in a native frame
  (a variable of a caller) is looked up again at every access (about 25 instructions), a held-pointer fact for registers that hold such an address
  is the next candidate.

## llvm: `OptLevel::FastRa`, the optimised register allocator for hot large frame-mode functions (yavs-llvm, #715, 2026-10-24)

- **Decision (maintainer, 2026-10-24):** a large frame-mode function that `--tier=auto` compiled at `Fast` (FastISel and the fast register
  allocator) is compiled again in the background with the optimised register allocator (greedy, FastISel kept) once it has run compiled long
  enough to repay the compile (payback rule); only those functions, never the first compile and never a short run.
- **How it is made: per target machine, not by an LLVM option.** `-optimize-regalloc` and `-regalloc` are process-wide command line options,
  and `-optimize-regalloc` is tri-state: a later parse can set it true or false but not back to "unset", which the other levels need (unset
  means "by code generation level"). Toggling them would also need a lock around every code generation of the process. `OptLevel::FastRa`
  instead is a target machine at code generation level `Less` (the optimised allocator is chosen by the level) with `LLVMSetTargetMachineFastISel`
  on, and `Module::optimize_as` marks every function `optnone noinline` after the passes (`jit::no_opt`) so that the machine passes `Less`
  adds over `None` (block placement, tail merging, peepholes) skip it. Without `optnone` `Less` was worse: 27 s of code generation for the
  17 600-instruction function and +5 percent instructions against `Fast` on the LEON3 window (the extra passes lengthen the hot path), with it
  15.9 s and the same instructions as the option route (whole LEON3 program: 122.7 G and 127.4 G instructions in two runs against 122.8 G and
  127.0 G with the options on; `llc` object 4.80 MB against 5.14 MB). ORC cannot be given the FastISel setting, so a `FastRa` module is always
  emitted to an object (`Module::emit`) and added with `Jit::add_object` (`objcache::add`), also without a compilation cache; the object is
  stored under its own key (`{opt:?}` is in it), so a warm run links it. A `FastRa` module has its own `Jit` in the worker (`jitr`): the O2 and
  `Fast` modules of a function use the same symbol names.
- **Policy hook (auto.rs; constants are autoclk's to tune with the pricing, #670):** `Worker::fast[id]` is set when a frame-mode function
  that does not run on native frames (`natively`) was compiled at `Fast`; `Worker::threshold(id, true)` for it is `PAYBACK_RA` (12) times
  `ra_cost` of its IR instructions (`n * (100 + 0.05 n)` microseconds of CPU time), in microseconds of CPU time seen running compiled: the 6
  to 13 percent the allocator gives is expected for the rest of the run, which is expected to be as long as the past, so the compile repays at
  about twelve times its cost. For a 17 600-instruction process that is about 210 s of compiled running; for 400 instructions 0.6 s. The look
  that crosses it asks for the second compile (`pending.later`, the O2 recompile's queue), `compile(.., o2 = true)` makes it `FastRa`
  instead of `Fast`. With a heat of budget 0 (`--tier-heat`, tests) the O2 threshold applies as before and every second compile of a function
  of `FAST_MIN` IR instructions or more is `FastRa` (it was `Fast` again, a wasted compile): the differential tests with
  `--tier-heat=1,0,0` run the new level on every big process. `spent` is charged the `Fast` price as before (the budget is for first
  compiles; the payback rule is the stricter test here).
- **Cost (CPU time of the compile thread, `YAVS_AUTO_TRACE`, LEON3 with every function compiled, host loaded so SMT-shared; these fit
  `ra_cost`):** 350 to 700 IR instructions 13 to 90 ms; 1 000 to 1 900 0.11 to 0.33 s; 3 600 to 7 000 1.2 to 2.3 s; 9 000 to 13 000 2.6 to
  5.7 s; 17 500 to 19 900 17.5 s (`Fast` for the 17 500: 2.6 s on that host, #715 measured 1.2 s against 10.8 s unloaded). One function of 1 767 instructions took
  2.2 s that the model does not see.
- **Gain (forced: `--tier=auto --tier-heat=1,0,0`, bench builds, core 11, medians of 5 interleaved, simulation thread `perf stat --no-inherit`,
  warm cache; `FastRa` against `Fast` for every function of 300 IR instructions or more):**
  `neorv32_single_min` cycles -3.8 percent (instructions -1.5), `fletcher_bufferreader` -5.0 (-0.9), `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` -4.3 (-2.0),
  `grlib_leon3mp` whole run -7.8 (-2.2), `vai_window_gen_interlock` -2.0 (-0.5), `sc5_fifo_repack` and `poc_arith_addw` +0.6 and +1.7
  (no function over the size: noise). The 6 to 13 percent of #715 were measured with the option on from the start and with only the hot
  function forced; here every big function is recompiled and the hot ones are a part of the run.
- **Default `--tier=auto`:** a run that does not keep a big process compiled for the payback time compiles exactly what it did before
  (nothing of the realbench tests above reaches a payback of 12 times the compile within its length); the gain is for long simulations
  of big processes. Comparison of default `--tier=auto` before and after: see docs/STATUS.md "llvm: FastRa".
- **Not done:** the warm run does not look the `FastRa` object up before the payback time (that generates the module a second time, 0.3 s for the
  largest process); a `Part::Native` function does not get it (it runs its native-frame code); the compile is not charged at its true price
  to `spent`.

## llvm: 1 024 entries in the object table (yavs-llvm `rt.rs`, #719, 2026-10-24)

The host calls for package (`PKG`) and shared-heap addresses (#719) are conflict misses of the direct-mapped table, not a space the
lookup does not hold: counted by the space of the address at `host_miss` and by the spaces of the old and new entry at every
`put_obj` (a temporary instrumentation), the window generator makes 1.2 M misses of shared-heap and 0.3 to 0.55 M of package
addresses in a run, with 5 M replacements of one shared object by another and 0.45 M by each other between a package and a shared object. A
buffer the queue allocates whose index agrees with the pointer table's in the low eight bits makes every access of the table miss
for as long as the buffer is read (about 3 of 256 buffers meet one of the four hot objects), and a package variable (space 2, no flag bit)
shares entries with private and shared heap objects of the same low index. With 1 024 entries (64 KiB per machine, one per thread
and one per nested activation) the misses fall to a third (shared heap 0.3 to 0.38 M, package 0.09 to 0.17 M) and with 4 096 to
a sixth (the rest first touches of new objects); the same run needs fewer callbacks: `--tier=auto` warm (12 untimed runs, 5
interleaved) 149.3 to 148.3 G instructions and 44.1 to 43.4 G cycles, `--tier=llvm` 181.8 to 180.8 G with cycles level; 4 096 gave
180.7 G (not taken: 256 KiB to clear for every nested activation). A key that separates the spaces (package, shared, private) needs
more operations in every look-up of an address of unknown space and every `Deref`; ways or a victim entry are the next step if a profile
shows the misses of new objects.

## The sampler thread starts after `START_AFTER` and ends with the compile thread (`yavs-llvm` `auto.rs`, #725, 2026-10-25)

- **Finding:** since #670 `--tier=auto` ran a sampler thread that slept in 1 ms steps for the first 5 ms and then for the
  sampling period, and `AutoTier::stop` joined it: a run that ended while the sampler slept waited for the sleep (up to
  1 ms of wall time with no CPU use). On the tiny-test corpus that is 0.4 ms of 5.3 ms per test on average, and 1 ms of
  1.9 ms for a test that runs 1 ms. `perf stat` showed it as equal `task-clock` and a longer elapsed time.
- **Decision:** the compile thread starts the sampler once its first wait (`START_AFTER`) is over and the run has not
  ended, so a run shorter than that never creates the thread (about 0.1 ms less: a `clone3`, a stack and a context
  switch); the sampler waits with `park_timeout` (`nap`), and the compile thread unparks and joins it when it ends. `stop`
  joins the compile thread only. Test: `auto_tier_stops_without_waiting_for_the_sampler` (a sampling period of half a
  minute).
- **Measured** (warm `tests/corpus/delta/concurrent_assign.vhd`, `perf stat -r 300`, core 14, bench builds): elapsed
  3.23 ms to 1.87 ms; `task-clock` 1.81 to 1.44 ms; user instructions equal (3.20 M). The binary of head-to-head 3
  (4b80445d) takes 2.30 ms on the same core and test.
- **Tiny-test corpus** (456 tests of `tests/corpus`, warm analyze plus run per test, 15 interleaved rounds, cores 13 and
  14, `true` subtracted, bench builds with `llvm`): geometric mean of the per-test time 1.065 for the build of head-to-head
  4 (46e827ad) against the one of head-to-head 3 (4b80445d), 0.916 with this change; median test 5.1 ms to 4.3 ms. The
  head-to-head 4 figure of 5.7 ms against 5.3 ms was this, not a slower start-up: process start (the dynamic loader,
  about 460 page faults) is 1.0 of the 1.9 ms of a `run`.
- **Not fixed here:** +171 k user instructions (5.7 percent of a 3 M-instruction run) since 4b80445d: ae1826dd about +90 k
  on the main thread (the analysed image holds more per declaration: `Decl`, `Symbol` and `Span` decoding), 12a37bc7 about
  +80 k of which the main thread's functions show +5 k (not located); 0.03 ms. Position-independent linking costs 0.2 to 0.3 ms per process start: #727 (a
  decision for the user).

- **Not fixed here:** +171 k user instructions (5.7 percent of a 3 M-instruction run) since 4b80445d: 12a37bc7 +80 k
  (`stage_extent` keys of the stage cache), ae1826dd +156 k (idle skip analysis of concurrent conditional assignments).

## Cold path of serial processes, port propagation, same-value drives (yavs-interp, yavs-kernel, #720, 2026-10-24)

Whole-run profile of `grlib_leon3mp` (`--tier=auto`, warm, `docs/STATUS.md` "grlib_leon3mp whole-run profile"). Nothing big is compiled and
compiling it is no win today (#679), so these are costs of the interpreter and the kernel that are in every tier.

- **Decision: a serial process builds its shared-heap roots into reused buffers (`Machine::rscratch`, the vectors of its `SharedState::procs`
  entry; `Refs::pinned_into`).** A serial process publishes at every suspension. With the four SDRAM models of the system waking 8.4 M times the
  fresh vectors were 3.8 percent of the cycles plus the reallocations (2.2 percent in `grow_one`). The roots are the same; the collector
  and the gc-stress corpus see no difference (gc-stress corpus and the first 3 us of the system pass).
- **Decision: an in-port edge with one actual, one formal and no conversion passes the value down by copying storage to storage
  (`SimControl::push_down`).** The general edge still builds values and runs `convert`. Idea of the reference simulator used: the signals of a
  port are linked records and the resolved value is copied between their storage directly, with no buffer; ours still copies (a formal is a
  signal of its own, `--no-collapse-ports` and the `inout` ports are not collapsed), but without allocating: the `inout` data and clock nets
  of the system reach about 30 formals each (1.82 M pushes in the first 200 us).
- **Decision: a zero-delay assignment of one logic element that changes nothing, to a direct driver, is not made (`Ctx::assign_code_fast`,
  `Ctx::skip_code_now`, `Signal::direct_same`).** The conditions are those under which `Signal::commit_code` would have returned `None`: the signal
  allows skipping (nothing reads its activity), it and its driving value hold the code, and the driver has no entry of this run, so the last
  assignment still wins. The run's delta stays: `SKIPPED` in `ProcState::phantoms` makes `take_phantoms` report it (the kernel's `empty_delta`),
  `cycles` and the delta structure of every test are unchanged. It is not a phantom on the driver's waveform: a phantom sends a second
  assignment of the same run to the same driver down the general path (first version: the LEON3 interpreter run went from 248 G to 291 G
  instructions) and `flush_phantoms` reads the lagging driver value of a direct driver. 92 percent of the 133 M direct code commits of the
  LEON3 run changed nothing.
- **Decision: a run of two or more scalar drives of frame slots in consecutive statements is guarded by one op (`Op::DriveRun`, `pre::drive_runs`,
  `Machine::drive_run`).** The statement is `[Stmt, SigVal, LoadSlot, Aff1?, LSetDrive]` after the predecoder's fusion; the first `Stmt` of the run
  becomes the op, which ends that statement like the `Stmt` and then skips, from the front, the drives that change nothing (`skip_code_now`:
  the checks of the fast path, with the zero delay, the scalar logic signal and the code at most 8 tested first) while setting the registers
  the skipped ops would write (the signal reference pair, the loaded byte, the mapped code), so a later reader of those registers sees what
  the ops left. It goes on after the run when all were skipped, else at the `Stmt` of the first drive that is not, which runs its ops as before;
  nothing is rolled back. The IR is not changed (compiled code and the IR dump are as before; a compiled frame that returns to the
  interpreter at the `Stmt` pc runs the op). Why: the SDRAM model `state_register` wakes on a clock that toggles every 0.5 ns (4 instances,
  8.4 M wakes) and ends every wake with 13 scalar and 3 vector drives of process variables; 90 percent of the wakes are not a clock edge and
  assign what the signals hold. A drive was 460 instructions (a microbenchmark: `Stmt`, `SigVal`, `LoadSlot`, `Aff1`, `LSetDrive` is 300 in the
  loop, 90 in the assignment, 110 in the commit), a skipped one in a run is about 150. Not covered: vector drives (`CopyDrive`, #723), a drive from
  a register or a signal read, a run broken by another statement.
- **Decision: a zero-delay vector assignment of up to 64 elements that changes nothing is skipped the same way (`assign_planes_fast`,
  `Signal::direct_same_planes`).** The condition adds that the driver has no entry of this run of either kind: an earlier assignment to the same
  elements must still be overridden by this one (perf case `drive_vec`: `w(7 downto 0) <= lo; w(7 downto 0) <= x"00";`). 83 percent of the
  direct plane commits of the first 400 us of the LEON3 run were skipped; cycles are unchanged. Interpreter instructions 240.9 G to 237.4 G.
- **Decision: `Host::push_native` takes the preloaded registers from `Pre::preloaded`.** It walked the callee's IR at each materialisation of a native
  frame (13 percent of the S-record start-up of the system, 0.9 percent of the steady state).
- **Tried, not landed: the clean-up of `opt/cfg.rs` (threading through short-circuit chains) on processes.** On the LEON3 system it takes the
  chains `a and b and c` of the SDRAM model from `EdgeBr, Const, CondBr, Const, CondBr` to one branch (-0.8 percent of the interpreter's
  instructions). In five work-counter designs `ops` rose by 2.7 to 9 percent (`inline_calls`, `elem_loops`, `reduce_idiom`, `wide_vec`,
  `sink_msg`): a loop entered from a copy of its test is no longer the fused `CmpBrStep` latch (the test is copied into the entry and the step
  stays a `Bin`, `Br`), and a block that suspends gets code behind its `Suspend` (the verifier's "live across a suspension point"). A version
  that threads only the `Const`-then-`CondBr` joins and leaves loops alone is untried.
- **Tried, not landed: runs of logic scalar leaves in `SigGather`/`SigScatter`.** A plan-level run (leaves next to each other in one kernel signal and in
  the value, read as a slice of the signal's codes, driven through `planes_of` of the bytes) works, but the records of the LEON3 system mix scalars
  with vectors: the runs are 2 to 16 leaves, the plans have 9 to 79 leaves, and the interpreter's instructions did not move (241.7 G against
  240.9 G). The per-call cost of the two instructions (about 2500 instructions for 19 leaves) is the plan lookup with its descriptor comparison and
  the vector leaves, not the scalar ones.
- **Found, filed:** processes with nested subprograms are never specialised (#721: `state_register` keeps its layout work, 25 percent of its ops);
  the pure-call memo costs 10 percent of the S-record start-up (#722); the vector drives of a wake that does nothing (#723); the cold
  activation path of serial processes (#724).

## Uniform in compiled code, and `Mem::find` knows the enclosing frames (yavs-llvm `lower.rs`, `rt.rs`, #519, 2026-10-25)

Profile of `sc5_fifo_repack` first (`--tier=llvm`, bench build, core 12; the design has 45 clocked processes, 50 000 clock periods, 2.54 M process
runs, 21.3 M element drives): generated code 40 percent of the cycles, the drive and commit path 27, process entry 6, and the random numbers of the
testbench (`rand_next`, 8.3 M calls of `math_real.uniform`) 11: `yavs_rt_native`, `native_frame`, the native and five `Machine::load`/`store` about 19 ns a call.

- **Finding:** a compiled call of `uniform` went through `yavs_rt_native` into `TierHost::native_frame` (the same call as any `direct_native`), which
  decodes three addresses again in the interpreter's `load`/`store`: 10.6 percent of the run.
- **Decision:** `Gen::uniform_fast` computes it in the code: the three addresses through `host` (the seeds are variables of the enclosing process, passed by
  reference to a nested procedure), the seeds compared against their limits, the generator's step in integers and one `fmul` (the arithmetic of
  `yavs_interp::ieee::uniform_step`, which the interpreter's `Op::Uniform` and the native share), the seeds and the real written back in the native's order. A
  seed out of range, which the native reports, or an address `host` does not find takes the slow path of the site, which is the unchanged
  `native_direct` call (it has stored nothing by then). A second implementation of the generator, as `ieee_fast` is one for `numeric_std`; one function
  (`uniform_regs`) decides it for the code generator, `is_inline` and the `--tier=auto` callback count (`leaves`), so the three agree. Tests: the
  generator's sequence and both bad-seed reports in a process, a nested procedure and an architecture procedure (native frame), `--tier=llvm`, `auto` and the
  interpreter equal (`compiled_natives.rs`); `perf.rs` `llvm_uniform` (400 calls, `cb_native` at most 4).
- **Also:** `Mem::find` (what `yavs_rt_host` asks first) finds the slots of the first two enclosing frames, which the view carries
  (`TierFrame::up`, `up_slots`, `up_len`). `rand_next(iseed1, iseed2)` passes the addresses of the process's variables, a frame address that is no `Up` address
  of the generator's tracking: each access was a `host_miss`, `yavs_rt_obj` and `TierHost::object`, 3.7 and 2.8 percent of the cycles once the native was inline. Length 0 in the
  view (a frame a native window holds) misses as before. Package and protected-object spaces stay #719's.
- **Measured** (bench builds, core 12, `perf stat` user cycles and instructions, medians of 5 interleaved runs, base c7f56056): see docs/STATUS.md.

- **Cranelift too (2026-11-03):** `Gen::uniform_fast` in `yavs-clift` computes it in place the same way. `native::leaves` already counted the call as inline for every generator, so the policy priced Cranelift's `rand_next` as if it stayed in compiled code while each call went through `yavs_rt_native`.

## A copy splits the position of an index into a check and a subtraction (yavs-ir `opt.rs` `pos_to_check`, `tidy`, #519, 2026-10-25)

- **Finding:** in the specialised copies of `sc5_fifo_repack` the descriptors of the signal arrays are instance data and fold (`DopeLen` is a constant, the
  lengths in the index arithmetic are constants), but every `Pos` of a non-constant index stays one: the interpreter's `AffP` loads the three words of the descriptor
  and computes the length at every execution (12 ns in the census, 8 percent of the time of the ops; 36 M of 457 M ops), and compiled code decodes it with about 20 instructions. No
  pass could see the bounds: they were data behind an address.
- **Decision:** in a copy, a `Pos` in an ascending descriptor of instance data whose first reader in the block is an add, subtract or multiply (an index into the
  linear position of a multi-dimensional array) becomes `Check { Index, idx, left, right }` and `Bin Sub idx, left`. The `Check` is inserted
  before the `Pos` (`inserts`), so it is in the code only after `compact`; a second walk of the finished code (`tidy`, now with the instance view) lets
  the value numbering see it, which drops the repeated checks of one index (`Key::Check` keys a register defined more than once at its version now, as
  every other key does: the loop variable of a `for` loop). The failure is the one of `Pos`: `check_fail` of an index prints `index X outside of range L to R for NAME` with the
  name of the same check message, as `pos_fail` does (`tests/spec.rs` `index_failures_in_a_copy_are_those_of_the_shared_code`: shared code and copy, same text). `dce` counts the registers
  the inserted instructions read (the constants of the bounds were dropped as unread, which made `Check` read undefined registers) and applies the renames to them.
- **Not done:** a descending range stays a `Pos`: the message of an index check says `to` (the lowering gives every `Pos` the check message `Dir::To`, `Pos` itself prints the descriptor's
  direction) and the optimiser cannot add messages to the program; a check message per direction at lowering would admit them. `Pos` whose result an `Index` reads
  stays one, so as not to lose the fused `PosIndex*` ops.
- **Measured:** `sc5_fifo_repack` `--tier=interp` (copies are made there too) instructions 40.19 to 38.31 G (-4.7 percent), user cycles 11.31 to 10.95 G (-3.2 percent), medians of 5
  interleaved runs, core 12; 17 other realbench designs within 0.1 percent in instructions, the small designs by their initialisation (docs/STATUS.md). Shared code is unchanged (`--tier=llvm`,
  and `--tier=auto` while the shared code runs); a compiled copy has the checks and subtractions instead of the descriptor decode of `Pos`.

## Functions that read signals run on native frames (yavs-llvm `lower.rs` `nat_inline`, #519, 2026-10-25)

- **Finding:** a call from compiled code to a procedure or function that reads a signal was a step of the interpreter (`Host::step` `Call`, a frame pushed, the
  callee's frame-mode code entered from the callback, `ret`): 77 ns a call against 7 ns for a callee on a native frame (3 M calls of a nested procedure `v := (v + s) mod 1000`:
  0.27 s against 0.06 s without the read of `s`; #730), because `SigReadScalar` was not among the instructions a native frame lowers (`native_local` wants every instruction
  inline). `rand_next` of `sc5_fifo_repack` (a nested procedure that draws a `real` and compares it with a `real` signal) is called 1.9 M times in 400 us: about 5 percent of the compiled run.
- **Decision:** `SigReadScalar` is a native-frame instruction (`nat_inline`; `SigVal` already was). The code is the frame mode's (`Gen::sig_read_scalar`: the byte of the
  codes, the plane bits, or the bytes of a scalar element from the view's `TierSig` table, which a native frame reaches through the `Mem` it is given); where the table has
  no answer (no kernel, a signal beyond the table, a signal that keeps neither) `Gen::signal` on a native frame materialises it and the interpreter reads, as for every
  native-frame instruction with a slow path. `perf.rs` `llvm_sigfun` (a function and a procedure reading a logic and a real signal, 900 calls: `cb_step` 904 to 4, `llvm_native_frames` 0 to 3).
- **Measured** (`--tier=llvm`, bench builds, core 12, medians of 7 interleaved runs, user cycles / instructions): `sc5_fifo_repack` 6.68 to 6.23 G (-6.6 percent) / 24.77 to 23.22 G (-6.2 percent);
  the micro design 0.27 to 0.07 s.
- **Found on the way (#729):** under `--tier=auto --tier-heat=1,0,0` the native-frame code of a function is made once, at the first level (O0), and the O2 recompile gives
  the frame-mode code only: a function that now runs on native frames keeps O0 code in the heat mode (`sc5_fifo_repack` 25.0 to 27.6 G there, though the llvm tier gains). The default policy
  compiles at O2 at once and is not affected; the differential tests use the heat mode.

## Copies of processes with nested subprograms and serial processes, files do not need the shared state, scratch sets (yavs-ir, yavs-interp, yavs-elab, #721, #724, 2026-10-25)

Found with the whole-run profile of `grlib_leon3mp` (#720); the SDRAM model `state_register` declares `Init_mem` and `Burst_decode` in its declarative
part, reads an S-record file and holds access objects, so it was neither specialisable nor on the quick path.

- **Decision: a process with nested subprograms, or that is serial, can have specialised copies (`Program::specialisable` no longer asks for
  `!nested` and no `TOUCHES_SHARED`).** The copy keeps the frame layout of the lowered code, so a nested subprogram reaches the variables through
  the static link as before. Three pieces make that correct: (1) `Machine::static_link` finds the parent frame by the process, not by the function
  id of the frame (the root frame holds the copy after the switch: `base_of`); (2) `closed_frame` of the LLVM tier asks for functions nested in the
  process the copy is of; (3) `opt/decl.rs` takes the frame writes of the nested subprograms into account (see next). The switch itself is tried in
  `InterpProcess::exec` as it is in the quick path, between two activations with no frame above the root, and `specialise_later` is called for serial
  processes too.
- **Decision: the facts of a process's declarative part (`decl_facts`) are computed for a process with nested subprograms.** The subprograms nested in
  it (and theirs) reach its frame by `AddrOf { space: Up(depth) }`; `Opt::nested_writes` classifies every use of such an address exactly like the
  process's own uses of its frame addresses (`Opt::classify`, shared with `frame_writes`): a `Store` or `Copy` to it is a write of that range, any other
  use except a `Load` is a pointer that may reach the whole object (`frame_range`), and a register holding such an address that is defined twice gives up
  on the whole frame. Frame bytes and words that no code writes and no pointer reaches stay facts as for a process without nested subprograms. The
  descriptor of an array variable is never written after the declaration (the one fact taken on the language's word, as before), so the layouts and
  bounds of the variables the nested subprograms do not assign are folded.
- **Decision: integer `**` folds (`fold_int` knows `IntOp::Pow`, with the interpreter's rules: natural exponent, `0`, `1`, `-1` bases, overflow and
  negative exponents are left to the run-time error).** `2 ** addr_bits - 1` with a generic made the bounds of every array variable of a copy unknown to
  the declarative part's evaluator and to the optimiser. `decl.rs` tracks blocks of up to 256 KiB (was 64 KiB): the 8192 access cells of the SDRAM
  model's `ram_stor` are 64 KiB and a branch on the length of the object it makes stopped the evaluation.
- **Decision: the per-thread scratch of registers and temporaries has four sets, found by the function of the root frame (`Scratch`,
  `SCRATCH_SLOTS`).** One set meant that processes of different functions waking in turn (the two copies of one process, the stages of a pipeline) each
  filled the register file template at their activation (`borrow_fill`: a copy of 40 KB for the SDRAM model). With copies the four SDRAM models alternate
  between two functions, which is what showed it (+11 percent of the interpreter's instructions before this change, with copies at all). The set that is
  given up when all four are in use goes round robin.
- **Decision: file natives mark the function `TOUCHES_FILES`, not `TOUCHES_SHARED` (`FuncFlags`, `Program::uses_shared_state`).** Both make the process
  serial for the kernel (`Program::is_serial`: the bytes on disk and what is read back do not depend on `--threads`). Only `TOUCHES_SHARED` (shared
  variables, protected objects, the shared heap) needs the `SharedState`: the lock, taking the state in and out of the machine, `publish_shared`, the
  roots, the allocation in the shared heap (#303) and the cold activation (`run_cold`). A process that only reads or writes files, which is every
  testbench process that writes with `textio` to a file or `OUTPUT`, now runs on the quick path (`Machine::run_quick`) with its own heap; it is still run
  alone by the kernel. #724 asked for the quick path while an activation touches no shared state; this is the same at function granularity and
  without a fall-back in the middle of an activation. A process that really touches shared state (VUnit's logging and checks use protected objects) keeps
  the cold path: the fall-back at the first shared access is not done.
- **Not done:** the guard for `CopyDrive` entries of `drive_run` (#723) and the memo's give-up rule at the start-up (#722) are the next steps; see `docs/STATUS.md`.

## Address parameters of native frames are resolved once per activation (yavs-llvm `rt.rs` `param_addrs`, `Gen::host`, #726, 2026-10-25)

- **Finding:** an address a native frame gets as a parameter (a by-reference scalar, a dope or string pointer, a vector) is in an unknown space, so `Gen::host` looked it up at
  every access: the own-frame test, the caller-slot table, the object entry, the top frame, the temporary area, the instance data, `yavs_rt_host` (about 25 instructions
  for a caller's frame, more elsewhere). `decode` of the test runner's codec (`index` inout, `result`, `code`, two descriptors) does about ten such accesses an
  iteration and was 6.6 percent of the window generator's instructions (`--tier=llvm`, 180 G). The reference simulator's by-reference argument is the machine pointer itself,
  so an access to it costs nothing; ours costs the translation, and the idea taken is to pay it once instead of at every access.
- **Decision:** `param_addrs` picks the 8-byte parameters a function loads in its straight-line entry block into a register that is defined once, never read before, and whose slot nothing else
  touches (every use of the slot's address is a load of 8 bytes: the argument is the caller's for the whole call), and that the function uses as an address (`Load`,
  `Store`, `Copy`, `Pos`, `DopeLen`, `SubtypeCheck`, `LGet`/`LSet`/`LFill`/`LCopy`, `LEq`, `MemEq`, directly or through the single-definition `Index`/`Move` registers derived from it)
  at least three times, one of them inside a loop (a backward branch). At the entry the native function calls `yavs_rt_region(env, mem, addr, depth, flags, out)` once per such
  parameter and keeps the host pointer of the region's start and its length (`Cur::pres`); the register is `Known::Param(k)` in every block (`base_known`, and again after its
  definition, which `track` clears), `Index` and `Move` carry it, and `Gen::host` tests the access against the pair (6 instructions) and takes the old lookup when the test
  fails, whatever the reason (a parameter can point anywhere; a failed test never goes to the slow path by itself). A register `Index`ed from the parameter in another block stays on the
  old lookup (it has more than one definition).
- **What is held:** the slots of a native caller (`Mem::nslots`, between the interpreter's top frame and this frame) for every function, since that frame lives as long as the callee. The top
  frame, the temporary area, instance data (not for writing) and a heap object of the object table only when the function is a *stable activation* (`stable_activation`): its
  instructions are an allowlist none of which allocates, calls, ends a statement, derefs or leaves the function other than by failing, so nothing it does (steps of its own
  instructions included) frees or moves a heap object, grows the temporary area or pushes a frame. A function with a call keeps the pointers of the callers' frames and asks the
  lookup for the rest. A parameter resolved for writing (a write use exists) asks the heap object for write access once, like the entry of an activation does
  (`TierHost::wrote`); a region that cannot be written has length 0 for that parameter and its accesses take the old lookup.
- **Cost:** one callback per resolved parameter and activation, counted as `cb_region`. The three-use rule is the break-even (about 45 instructions for the callback against
  about 18 saved per access); without the loop requirement the realbench wall geomean was no better (1.04, a loaded host) and the instructions equal, so it stays.
- **Tests:** `compiled_param_regions.rs` (arguments in a native caller's frame, a process variable, the temporary area and a heap object; a stable callee and one that allocates
  between its accesses; errors; identical output in the interpreter, `--tier=llvm`, `--tier=auto` heat mode at 1 and 4 threads; `cb_region` > 0).
- **Measured** (bench builds A = before, B = after, same origin otherwise; fresh world per binary and tier, 12 untimed runs of each, medians of 5 interleaved runs, core 9, host load 17 to 20):
  window generator `--tier=llvm` instructions 179.6 to 176.0 G (-2.0 percent), cycles 66.4 to 63.2 G (-4.9 percent; on a quiet host an earlier pair 58.3 to 57.1 G, -2.0 percent); `--tier=auto` warm
  instructions 147.0 to 143.4 G (-2.4 percent), cycles -0.2 percent (a quiet-host pair: -3.3 percent); `decode` 6.6 to 3.5 percent of the instructions. `tools/realbench` `--compare` over
  the 42 tests of the suite (`--tier=auto` warm and cold, 6 cores): wall geomean 1.00 and 1.00, instructions 1.00 and 0.99; the window generator is the one test that gains (warm 9.89 to 9.37 s,
  cold level); no other test moves outside the noise of its run (the short ones by their initialisation). `neorv32_single_min`, `poc_arith_addw`, the OSVVM and UVVM queue tests: instructions within 1 percent.
- **Not done:** an `Index` register with several definitions (the limit register of the loop head in `decode`, one access an iteration) keeps the old lookup; holding it would need a test of the
  address's high half at each access. Functions that call between their accesses keep only the callers' frames (heap and temporary regions would have to be found again after each call;
  the object table does that at an access already). Tag: LLVM-only (the pins are `Gen` values; a second code generator would reuse `param_addrs`, `stable_activation` and `yavs_rt_region`).

## Waits on a clock edge: `Inst::WaitEdge` (yavs-ir, yavs-lower, yavs-interp, yavs-kernel, #519, 2026-10-25)

- **What:** a `wait until` whose condition has a clock edge as a conjunct of `and`s (`wait until rising_edge(clk) and ready = '1';`,
  `x'event and x = '1' and en = '1'`, either order) lowers to `WaitEdge { sig, kind }` before its `WaitOn`s (`yavs-lower` `edge.rs`
  `wait_edge`, the same `Db::edge_shape` idioms as `Inst::Edge`). The interpreter's op calls `Ctx::wait_edge`, which stores the edge's
  `edge_key` in `ProcState::wait_key`; the commit of the wait registers all its waiters (the clock's and those of the other signals of the
  condition) with the trigger of that edge, interned beside the elaborator's (`SimControl::trig_ids`, `dyn_trigger`). The wake path
  that already held back a process whose edge trigger does not hold (`hold`, `uniform_trigger`, the cached wake lists) then leaves it
  suspended for the falling edge and for events of the other signals in cycles without the edge.
- **Why it is the same run:** the condition is false in every cycle without that edge (an `and` of a false conjunct), so those wake-ups
  only evaluated it, found it false and waited again. It was the one place where a testbench process woke without being able to do anything
  (every `wait until rising_edge(clk)` inside a process that also waits for other things, so no elaborator trigger).
- **Rules:** a wait resumes only through the trigger; its timeout (a deadline in the queue) is independent of it. A wait with another edge
  or none registers its waiters again (`ProcMeta::wkey` against `ProcState::wait_key`, in `commit_rest` and in the two hot commit paths).
  A process with an elaborator trigger ignores it (`known_edge` set). `known_edge` is never set from a dynamic trigger: the same IR runs in
  procedures called from postponed processes, which may resume in a later cycle. Not emitted in a postponed process, and not
  where coverage counters count the evaluations of the condition (statement, branch, condition, expression: the counts of the false
  evaluations would change); `Config::edge_triggers` off (debugger, VHPI) turns the trigger off.
- **Tests:** `delta/wait_edge` (12 processes: loop, rising then falling, `or`, timeout, `wait on ... until`, procedure with the wait on
  two clocks, legacy form, two clocks in turn, postponed, array element clock, wait for between; identical to the reference simulator at
  1 and 4 threads, shuffled, in every tier), kernel scenario `wait_edge_resumes_only_on_the_edge`, work-counter design `wait_edge`
  (1507 to 1207 process runs).
- **Measured** (bench builds, interpreter, exact instructions): `hdlm_lfsr` 0.98 (67.3 G to 65.9 G; auto 0.94), `fletcher_bufferreader` 0.98,
  `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` 0.99; a skipped wake costs ~650 instructions. `realbench --compare` over the 42 tests, interpreter and auto:
  instruction geometric mean 1.00 in both, wall 1.00 (noise at load 20), no test with a reproducible slowdown. The gain is real but small:
  it is the testbench processes' falling-edge wakes, 4% of the writer's wakes.
- **Idle skip, round 6: measured, not built (same task).** Per-process counters (a local profiling patch: time, runs, runs that drove nothing
  and made no effect, per process; the reason the purity analysis refused each process, in all 42 designs): of ~300 s of process time in the
  interpreter, the processes that the idle skip does not take and that drive nothing in more than half of their runs cost ~1.6 s (0.5%):
  `window_hold_check` (a checker with state in `prev` variables, 2% of `vai_window_gen_interlock`) and the like are checkers that keep
  variables between activations, not skippable. The processes with the idle skip's refusals the brief named (`report`/`assert`, field read
  before assignment, procedure calls) in the fletcher writer all change their outputs in nearly every run (null runs: 0 of 137 K for
  `ctrl_comb_proc`, 0 of 69 K for `last_stage_proc`, `StreamPipelineBarrel` `reg_proc` once), so skipping them would skip nothing. The
  testbench processes' null runs are real work that drives no signal (the per-element check loop of `bus_proc`). No further idle-skip rule
  is worth its verification cost on this suite.

## llvm: smaller frame-mode code: short-lived deferred values, address copies per block, calls for the cold decodes (yavs-llvm, #679, 2026-10-25)

Cause found with a per-IR-kind attribution of the machine code (`YAVS_LLVM_KINDLOC=<file>`: every LLVM instruction gets a debug line, the
number of its IR kind, 1000 more in a cold block; with `YAVS_LLVM_OBJ` the bytes per kind and, with `perf record`, the executed
instructions per kind): the unoptimised code generator keeps every value that crosses a block in a stack slot, and a frame-mode process
is thousands of tiny blocks (one per guard). Most of the bytes were values alive across blocks and their reloads, not the guards.

- **Decision: a definition is deferred (kept as a value, stored at exits) only when its register is live over at most `MAX_SPAN` (4) IR
  instructions** (`lower.rs` `Defer::keep`, `regs.rs` `Live::spans`). A long-lived deferred value is stored again at every call and
  guard exit it is live at, and is a cross-block value (a stack slot) anyway; storing it once at the definition is smaller (exec_comb
  of neorv32 -26 percent bytes) and not slower. 2 and 16 were measured worse (more iTLB/L1i misses at 16, more stores at 2).
- **Decision: the sensitivity list `WaitOn` is a call `yavs_rt_wait_again(env, lo, len)` that reads no register**, with the old
  instruction as the slow path (`yavs_rt_wait_on` is gone). The registers live at the call were stored before every one of the
  list's calls, which is most of the bytes of a process with a 40-signal list.
- **Decision: address arithmetic is copied into the blocks that use it after the passes** (`jit.rs` `remat_geps`, unoptimised code
  generation only): early-cse merges the constant-offset `getelementptr`s of a block with those of a dominating block and the merged
  address becomes a stack slot; a copy per block folds into the load or store.
- **Decision: `SigRead` of up to 64 elements and `SigReadScalar` of a signal without codes are calls of pure runtime functions**
  (`yavs_rt_codes`, now two codes groups per SSE2 step, and the new `yavs_rt_scalar`), not unrolled plane arithmetic and a three-way
  size switch per site. The inline byte read of a signal that keeps codes stays.
- **Decision: one range test for a constant size** (`Gen::in_range`: `o + n <= len` as one add and one compare when `n` is a small
  constant, `o` below 2^32 + 2^63 so the sum cannot wrap), instead of `n <= len && o <= len - n`; `TierFrame::temp_cap` is capped at
  `u32::MAX` (an offset in the temporary area is 32 bits) so `temp_alloc` needs one bound.
- **Decision: the tests of `Gen::host` for the temporary area, the frame and instance data are made in the block of their own try**
  (they were made at the top, and each result crossed the blocks of the earlier tries).
- **Not kept (measured):** skipping a store of a register an earlier callback call already stored in the same straight run (the marks
  needed a valid-block analysis; it removed 4 percent of the bytes of exec_comb and was superseded by `MAX_SPAN`); a shared
  out-of-line exit stub per guard (the exits are already one `ret` block per 256 predecessors; the bytes per exit are the stores of the
  live registers, which are the frame values and cannot be shared per site).

## `--tier=auto`: the class rules of the threshold are asked of a function at or above the base threshold (yavs-llvm `Worker::see`, #544, 2026-10-25)

- **Decision: `Worker::see` evaluates `Worker::threshold` (the class rules: `is_rtl`, `is_compute`, `natively`) only for a function whose
  time is at least the base threshold of the heat; below it the base is the threshold.** Why: the class rules only raise the base,
  so a function below it is no candidate whatever its class says, and `natively` is `native_set`, which walks everything the function
  can call and optimises each callee on the way (`Program::func`). `see` asked it of every function the sampler ever saw, so the
  compile thread optimised library functions the run never executes: `hdlm_axi_fifo` had 385 function bodies optimised under the tier
  against 323 in the interpreter (`opt_funcs`), 0.17 G of its 2.41 G run. Nothing that compiles changes. Instructions with the
  default policy, `--no-cache`, interpreter / before / after (the Cranelift tier on the same tree; LLVM `auto` the same): `hdlm_axi_fifo`
  2.41 / 2.50 / 2.41 G, `olo_base_cam` 2.68 / 2.81 / 2.68 G. Test: `a_function_below_the_base_threshold_is_not_analysed`.
- Left (#544): the floor of the large runs, the watching form of the interpreter loop (`neorv32_single_min` 0.5 G), and the analysis a
  function above the base still needs (everything it can call is optimised once).

## Cold compiles: the passes without the quadratic alloca walk, exits that record less (yavs-llvm, #740, 2026-10-25)

- **Finding (where cold minus warm goes):** head-to-head 4, 41 tests, seconds summed: 52 of 192 s cold against 139 s warm. Analysis of the libraries one call per file 37 s (70 percent;
  per file about 13 M user instructions at the median, 4 M of them the floor of a process, a flat profile; the unit cache already saves three quarters of it), the run phase 13.6 s
  (`vai_window_gen_interlock` 4.9 s, `poc_arith_addw` 3.3 s before the addw rounds, neorv32 0.2 to 0.35 s, `sc5_fifo_repack` 0.16 s), elaboration 2.0 s. For `vai_window_gen_interlock` the cold run
  executes 63 G instructions more than the warm one (210 against 147 G): 14 G of compiling on the compile thread and the rest code that runs in the interpreter until the compiled code
  arrives. `sc5_fifo_repack` compiles one function (34 ms of CPU) and the warm run has it from 80 ms where the cold run first sees it hot at 2 s: policy, not compile cost.
- **Finding (what a compile costs, `YAVS_LLVM_TIMES`, 55 compiles of window_gen, wall on a shared core):** generation 1.5 percent, verifier 2, key 1.3, passes 34, code generation 62, store
  and link under 1 (13 ms of writes, no `fsync`). Of the passes, `instcombine` was 78 percent. `opt -time-passes` and a profile show `ValueHandleBase` list traffic: `instcombine`
  walks all users of an alloca (`isAllocSiteRemovable`, a vector of tracking handles) each time one of its users changes, which is quadratic for a buffer of thousands of stores
  (4 000 stores through constant byte offsets of one alloca that escapes to a call: 3.9 G instructions, 500 stores 0.1 G; the same stores through an argument pointer 0.13 G). The
  buffer is the one a native frame's exits record the registers live at their pc in (`Nat::spill`): one module, `golden_window`, had 3 800 users of it.
- **Decision: `LEAN` runs in two stages** (`jit.rs` `optimize_as`): `sroa,early-cse`; then every alloca that is left and has `HIDE_MIN` (32) users or more is put behind
  `llvm.launder.invariant.group` (`hide_allocas`), so that `instcombine` sees a call result; then `instcombine,simplifycfg,adce` (`dce` for the huge modules, as before), and the calls are
  taken out again (`unhide_allocas`) before code generation, so the codegen sees the alloca as before. The machine code is byte for byte the same (58 dumped modules of the window generator run
  compared object by object), the passes take about 15 percent of what they took (all 85 modules, `instcombine` alone: 13.7 G instructions to 2.0 G net of the 2.1 G start-up of the 85 `opt` runs). A `Fast` or `FastRa` module and `LEAN_HUGE` take the same path; the full `default<O2>` of compute loops and `YAVS_LLVM_PIPELINE` are unchanged. Test: `tests/jit.rs`
  `a_big_escaping_buffer_survives_the_lean_passes`.
- **Decision: an exit does not store the registers the interpreter preloads** (`Nat::pre`, `regs::preloaded`): `TierHost::materialise` keeps the preload of such a register and ignores the recorded word
  (`exec.rs` `push_native`, since #720), the stores were dead. 37 percent of the stores to the buffer in the window generator run stored a constant.
- **Decision: the exits record the core registers in one block** (`regs::entry_core`, `Gen::core_stub`): the registers defined once by an instruction of the function's first block (which no
