  frame address operand fetches the slots pointer of the stretch on the main path first (#751: a
  fast path inside the instruction's own branches defined it where it did not dominate later uses,
  and functions failed verification).
- **Out of the loop**: `ZeroReadVec`, `ZeroCat`, `ZeroLCopy` and `ZeroCatLCopy` run out of line
  (`op_zero_read_vec`, `op_zero_fill`), only `ZeroSlot` and `SlotBr` are arms of `run_ops`: every
  frame form tried as an arm of the loop (A had `ZeroReadVec` there) made the binary run 1 to 3
  percent more interpreter instructions on every design, the pass off included, through code
  generation of the loop. The price: a design that concatenates into a temporary every cycle
  (`rtl_lfsr`, `lfsr64`) runs 2 to 4 percent more cycles in the interpreter than with the in-loop
  `AllocCat`.
- **Interpreter alone keeps the fused 32-byte blocks (#756, user, 2026-10-25)**: the price above
  was recovered in the optimiser: under `--tier=interp` (not `auto`, not `llvm`: `layout_slots_on`)
  an `Alloc` of 32 bytes that the next instruction (constants and addresses skipped, as the
  predecoder does) fills as a signal read, a concatenation of logic or an `LCopy` stays an
  `Alloc` (`slots.rs` `fused_in_loop`), so `AllocReadVec`, `AllocCat` and `AllocLCopy` run in the
  loop as before the frame temporaries. Other blocks (waveforms, descriptors, the rest) are
  frame bytes as before. Tried first: a `frame` flag on the in-loop `AllocCat` and `AllocReadVec`
  arms in place of `ZeroCat` and `ZeroReadVec` (one branch in the arm): the loop executed 2.8
  percent more instructions on `rtl_lfsr` with the pass off (code generation of `run_ops` again,
  #508), so it was dropped. The fingerprint needs no new switch (`layouts` is the same tier
  split). The compiled tiers keep the frame forms: they gain from them, and `--tier=llvm` is
  unchanged. Rationale: interpreter cycles of the designs that concatenate every cycle, back to
  before #668, at the price of the frame form for those blocks (the marker of their statement
  stays) only where the interpreter runs everything.
- **Why**: the same binary with the pass on against off, instructions (steady-state cache):
  interpreter -3.5 to +1.4 percent on the seven designs of #668 (`grlib_leon3mp` +0.5,
  `poc_arith_addw` +1.4), the LLVM tier -0.6 to -3.9 percent; against main the interpreter is -3.5
  to +0.9 percent (geomean -0.9), the LLVM tier -0.4 to -3.9; the head-to-head designs 1.010 in
  interpreter cycles and 0.980 in the LLVM tier; realbench (42 tests) wall geomean 0.99 interpreter
  and 1.00 LLVM tier, CPU time 0.99 and 1.00, `cpu` category 0.97 both (`docs/STATUS.md`
  "Temporaries of a process in its frame"). Over the two sets the interpreter's cycles are not
  worse (rule of the user, 2026-10-23), the LLVM tier is better.
- **Not done**: a `NewPair` or `NewDope` frame form (the zeroing goes there by coverage, so the
  stores or the `MakeDope` alone remain); following a pointer through memory (a group of blocks
  that hold each other's addresses), unused on the designs measured.


## llvm: large compiled processes lose to their callbacks, not to their code bytes: layout words from the memo, kept drives skip unchanged elements, objects stay in the table (yavs-llvm, yavs-interp, yavs-kernel, #679, 2026-10-25)

Cause found with a profile of the main thread split by symbol and by the call site in compiled code (`perf record -j any_call` branch stacks: the
last branch out of compiled code names the site; `YAVS_LLVM_PCLOC`, a new variant of `YAVS_LLVM_KINDLOC`, maps a site to the IR instruction of
its function): in the steady state of the LEON3 window (after the S-record load) with every function compiled (`--tier-heat=1,0,0`) the compiled
code itself took 8.4 k cycle samples where the interpreter's loop took 15.1 k for the same work, at about the same IPC (1.37 against 1.44). The
whole loss was work only the compiled tier does: object lookups in the runtime (`yavs_rt_host`, `yavs_rt_obj`, `TierHost::object`, the constant
bytes `Machine::obj` copies), stepped `LayoutOf` on native frames (`yavs_rt_xstep`, `native_step`, `layout_words`, the memset and memmove of
`layout_of`), and the kernel's work for kept scalar drives of unchanged values (`assign_codes_now`, `commit_codes`), about 1.2 times the compiled
code. The front-end stalls of the brief were mostly in those callbacks (IPC 0.6 to 1.0). A hot/cold split or a denser lowering of the compiled
bodies would have worked on the half that already beat the interpreter, so neither was built.

- **Decision: a `LayoutOf` that would be stepped and whose layout only one word is read of by the instructions right after it (a `Field`, a
  `Load` of word 0, an `Index` by a constant then a `Load`; no entry between) is one call `yavs_rt_layout_word(env, ty, desc, dsz, k)`**
  (`lower.rs` `fuse_layout`, `LayoutFuse`; frame mode and native frames): the generated code reads the descriptor bytes through `Gen::host` and
  the interpreter's layout memo (`TierHost::layout_word`, `Machine::layout_word_of`, the memo `layout_build` fills, now `memo_fill`) answers with
  the word, the `FieldOf` and `LayoutWord` ops of the interpreter in compiled code. The call reads no machine memory, forgets no object and
  writes no register; where it declines (`u64::MAX`: no layout, an error) the code leaves to the interpreter at the `LayoutOf`, which runs all
  of them and reports. Why: the native-frame step of these `LayoutOf` (the GRLIB AMBA records passed to `ahb_slv_dec_cache` and the integer
  unit's procedures, whose layout depends on generics) was the largest single callback site, about 2 k samples of 32 k.
- **Decision: `Ctx::assign_codes_now` (the kept scalar drives of compiled code, #676) skips an element the signal and the driver hold already,
  as `assign_code_fast` does** (no entry of the driver before the call, none for the element earlier in the call). Compiled clocked processes
  drove every element; the kernel committed every one (`commit_codes` 206 samples against 3 in the interpreter). `llvm_drive_batch`: kernel
  entries 817 to 103 (the interpreter makes 463: its skip test stops at the first entry of the driver). Kernel tests
  `a_batched_element_assigned_twice_keeps_the_last_code` and the random model test with runs of elements.
- **Decision: the object table keeps every constant for the run, holds 4 096 entries, and a process's record holds up to 64 objects**
  (`rt.rs` `Mem`): `RT_KEEP` (16 constants kept at a change of machine, else none) is gone; the walks that drop entries at a change of machine,
  a host call or the end of an activation visit only the entries that are not constants (`Mem::occv`, `retain_some`), so keeping constants
  costs those walks nothing; `MINE` 4 to 64 with an O(1) membership test (`mine_at`, `mine_gen`), frame and temporary objects no longer take
  a place in the record, and a record is written up to its last entry. Why: a big process uses more than 16 constants and more than 4 heap
  objects, so every activation after another process found them again in the runtime; host misses in the LEON3 window 13.4 million to 2.8
  million.
- **Measured** (LEON3 150 us, bench builds, `perf stat --no-inherit` of the simulation thread, medians of 3 interleaved on one claimed core):
  see docs/STATUS.md "llvm: callbacks of large compiled processes".
- **Not done:** a hot/cold split of large processes and a denser lowering (above: not the lever); processes that touch more than 64 objects
  per activation still find the rest again (SDRAM models with rows as heap objects); the scalar drive path costs about twice the
  interpreter's `drive_run` (the per-element callback and closure).
- **The reference simulator (rule 22).** Its compiled code has no address translation at all: memory is raw pointers, record layouts are known
  when the code is generated and constants are linked into the code. The ideas taken are its outcome, not its code: resolve an object once and
  keep it (here for the run, in the object table and the process record), and answer a layout from what is already known (here the
  interpreter's memo) instead of building it per access. Nothing was copied.

## A process that never suspends leaves compiled code at its jump back (yavs-llvm, #583, #737, #759, 2026-10-25)

(Superseded 2026-10-26 by "stays in compiled code under a bound of 10^9 jumps back" below.)

Compiled code polled only the stop bit at the retreating `Br` of a process without `MAY_SUSPEND` (#737), so the activation bound
of #583 (`SPIN_LIMIT`, interpreter only) did not hold under `--tier=auto` or `--tier=llvm`: the `process/no_wait_infinite` corpus
file ran until the host ran out of memory (the compiled loop queues a transaction every iteration), which turned the llvm CI jobs
red. The retreating `Br` now always leaves compiled code; the interpreter steps it (stop request, spin count, `E3009`) and, as
before, re-enters compiled code at the next entry. Cost: a never-suspending loop runs at interpreter speed plus an exit per
iteration, acceptable because such a process is already warned about (`W3102`) and bounded at `SPIN_LIMIT` jumps. Test:
`stuck::a_process_that_never_suspends_ends_with_an_error` in every tier. Open: the compiled loop of `a <= not a` keeps growing
memory where the interpreter replaces the pending transaction (#761).


## `--tier=auto` run-to-run profile (yavs-llvm, yavs, #754, #755, 2026-10-25, user decision 2026-10-25)

User decision (#754): a profile of the last run, kept next to the compiled code (same keying and invalidation as the object cache), so that what a
run found hot and did not compile is compiled at the start of the next run, what a trial took back is not, and the first run decides exactly as before.
Measured with bench builds (`tools/build-bench.sh --features llvm`) of main and of this change, pinned to core 8 (the compile thread shares it),
fresh worlds (a copy of the pristine world per binary and sample, the analysis caches of the binary filled by two untimed runs, the compiled-code
cache emptied), medians of 4 to 6 worlds; the Nth run is the Nth run of one world. Tables: docs/STATUS.md "`--tier=auto` run-to-run profile".

- **What is kept** (`profile.rs`, `objcache::profile_key`): one small text entry in the object store of the work library, per build, optimiser switches,
  command line (`yavs_llvm::set_run_id`, set by `yavs run` from a digest of its arguments: generics, stop time and the test case a runner names make
  other runs) and program (a digest of the set of function identities: name, kind, parent's name and kind, size and the count of equal ones before it; the reserved
  slots of copies are left out; #774: elaboration may lower the functions in another order in the next run, so the key and the stored names are by
  identity, not by id). Contents:
  `base` (the simulation CPU time of the last judged run), `hot` (rank, the microseconds seen, judged or not) and `lost` (ranks; at most 48 and 256), by
  process (a copy counts for its process, ids of copies are not the same in two runs); a rank is the place in identity order, mapped to and from ids
  when the profile is read and written. A text that is not exactly this version's is no profile.
  Written by `AutoTier::stop`, atomically (`Store::put`), last writer wins. Not written by a run under 100 ms of simulation CPU time (host noise is
  a few percent of that), not read or written under `--tier-heat`, without a compilation cache or a run id, or with `YAVS_AUTO_PROFILE=off`.
  `--dap` defaults to `--tier=interp`, and `--vhpi` runs are compiled as any other, so neither is special.
- **Why `stop` writes it and not the compile thread:** a run ends while the compile thread is inside a compile more often than not (a cold run of
  a short design: every time), and the CLI then leaves without waiting for it. The thread publishes a `Snapshot` (bounded: processes seen for 20 ms)
  at every decision; `stop` makes the profile of it, with the CPU time of the simulation threads (the process's less the compile thread's, taken
  before the thread can end) since the thread started.
- **Decision: only processes are compiled early, of the kinds the model says gain (speedup 1.4 or more: not large combinational processes, not
  clocked ones of few instances), seen for a thirty-second of the sampled time (a clocked one an eighth, as `cold`).** Forced early, in whole-run
  experiments: the 25 hottest functions of the window generator made its warm run 19 percent slower (its hot processes forced alone: no gain either, 0 to +2 percent), the hot
  functions of `uvvm_util_rand`, `uvvm_sb_slv` and `olo_fix_cordic_rot` gained nothing (and their compiles cost more CPU than the whole 0.8 s
  run), and one large combinational process of `neorv32_single_min` (`exec_comb`, 3660 IR, 6 percent of the run, kind `Big`) cost 30 percent of
  the run. The functions' prices are measured (native-frame code) and right; the processes' are a model of functions applied to frame-mode code
  (`sc5_fifo_repack`: 5 ms and 100 to 280 us an IR instruction against the model's 4 ms and 900 us), so the rule leaves hot ones for a run that is
  over by the time it would compile them. A function a process calls is compiled with it as always (`tree`).
- **Decision: the payback rule with the whole run in place of the part seen so far.** A listed process is compiled at its first look when the time
  the last run saw it, over `EARLY_RUNS` (4) runs of that length, reaches the rule's threshold (`Worker::threshold`: the price of its kind, a link
  where the cache has it, its payback). The compile is outside the budget (`early_root`: nothing is charged to `spent`, `cold` does not hold it) and
  is not measured by a trial (its share of the run is not known at the start). The shared code of a process that can have copies is not compiled
  early: its processes switch to the copies, which are. Without this rule the first early run of `poc_cache_cpu` spent 0.4 s of compile in a 0.65 s
  run for processes of 10 percent of its time that gained nothing.
- **Decision: the loss list is filled by the run as a whole too.** Functions compiled early for the first time are judged by the run after: at least
  3 percent less simulation CPU time than the run before (`profile::better`) keeps them (`hot` judged, `base` is this run), anything else puts them
  on `lost` for good and keeps `base`. A trial that takes a process back (`Worker::trial`) puts it there too. One run is lost to a loser at most:
  the neorv32 process above, listed after one run, was lost after the next, the run that compiled it (the old policy's trial could not have caught it,
  its share was under an eighth). A later run only adds: a function that becomes hot after the earlier ones joined is judged on top of them (hill
  climbing, one step a run; `sc5_fifo_repack` needs the third run for all six processes).
- **Decision: `SPEC_WAIT`, `SPEC_INSTANCES`, `SPEC_STALL` and `awaits_switch` are gone** (orchestrator's note on #749). Since compiled shared code
  switches to its copy at its next activation (#679), the shared code of a process that can have copies does not need to wait for the switch.
  `YAVS_AUTO_SPECWAIT=0` against the 400 ms: no change in wall, cycles or instructions on any of the 42 designs of `tools/realbench` (`auto` and
  `auto-cold`, median of the default runs, load average 7 to 8: ratios 0.57 and 1.5 on `leon3mp` and the window generator were the host, instructions
  1.00) or on `sc5_fifo_repack` (32.06 against 32.06 G instructions, 9.28 against 9.34 G cycles) or `hdlm_lfsr` (1.40 against 1.44 s); on the head-to-head designs only
  `lfsr64` moved: -9 to -13 percent (a process of fewer than 64 instances in a 170 ms run waited 400 ms of sampled work for a switch the compiled
  shared code makes at once). `NativeFlags::resumed` (interpreter, #749) is not read any more.
- **Measured, not changed:** the window generator's "-15 percent" of the round 5 notes (every kind compiled at its first call) is not there in this
  setting: its hot processes forced alone gave 0 to +2 percent, and with the profile it ends 2 to 4 percent faster by the fourth run. The warm run
  of `poc_arith_addw` ends 1 to 5 percent faster (the clocked processes of 16 to 63 instances are compiled at their first look).
- **Cost:** the run that compiles the listed processes for the first time pays the compile on the simulation's core when pinned (`sc5_fifo_repack`:
  the second run +8 percent, about 20 cold compiles of 40 to 65 ms of CPU each; with a free core it is background work). The cache holds them from the
  third run on. A run with nothing listed does what it did, plus one entry written (cold: 0.99 to 1.00 of main over the 42 designs).
- **Not done:** early compile of functions (see above; a function-level verdict needs a measure per function, which neither the trial nor the
  whole-run CPU time gives); a fixed convergence in two runs (the judged set grows by what becomes hot once the first ones are compiled); a profile
  shared between command lines of one program.

### #755: `auto_tier_compiles_a_long_loop_of_one_call`

The test timed the compile against the end of a call (3 million iterations): with a collection at every safepoint or a loaded host the compile the
sampler decided on during the call finished after it. It now waits for the compile (60 s at most) after the call returns; what it checks (the loop is
compiled and swapped in while one call runs, the result is right) does not depend on who finishes first. The interpreter sees a newly flagged function
at the next activation or within 128 events since interp750; the test does not depend on that, only on the compile finishing.

## Element loops in compiled code (yavs-llvm, yavs-interp, #757, 2026-10-26)

`poc_stat_histogram` ran 1.2 times the reference simulator warm (2.5 cold, instruction ratio 3.4, the highest of
the batched head-to-head 6). Warm under `--tier=auto` three compiled functions (`get_row`, `to_slm`,
`to_slvv_8`: a matrix row to a vector, a vector of vectors to a matrix, 2048 elements a clock) were 70
percent of the instructions, and the per-element copy loop inside them cost about 190 instructions an
iteration in native-frame code (two object-table look-ups, checked index arithmetic and four plane words
read or written per element), where the interpreter does the same loop as one op (#520).

- **The interpreter's loop, in the IR, behind one helper call** (`yavs_interp::elem_loops`, `eloop.rs` of
  both crates, `yavs_rt_eloop`): the lowering looks for the IR shape of a `for` loop (a head, straight-line
  body blocks, `Cmp Eq ind, bound`, a step block `ind += step`) whose body is index arithmetic (`Bin` add,
  subtract, multiply by an unchanging value, `Pos`, `DopeLen`, `Load`, `Index` by a constant, `Move`,
  `Const`) with one `LGet` and the `LSet` of it, or one `LSet` of an unchanging code. At the head of such a
  loop in native-frame code it asks the helper for all the iterations but the last; the generic code runs
  the last one (so the exit, every register the body defines and every failure are the generic code's, as
  in the interpreter). The helper evaluates the body once as affine pairs, checks every position,
  descriptor and element range at the first and last iteration and does a copy of planes, or an in-order
  element loop where the vectors overlap or run in opposite directions, or a fill; anything else returns 0
  and the generic loop runs from its first iteration, failing at its own index with its own message.
- **Hooked at the head, not on the entry edge**: the generic code's back edge reaches the head too, so a
  loop the helper declined asks again at every iteration. The hook is therefore only called with at least two
  iterations to go (`ind != bound && ind + step != bound`), and a decline is rare (an out-of-range element,
  an overlapping source, memory the table does not reach). Not done: remembering a decline per loop
  activation (a flag that needs a reset on the entry edge).
- **The program is a module constant** (an 8-byte aligned `[N x i64]`), the registers it reads go in an
  `alloca` array: nothing about the loop lives in a host table, so the compilation cache key (the bitcode)
  determines the code whatever order the run met the functions in. `yavs_interp` holds the analysis (it
  forbids `unsafe`), `yavs-llvm` the raw-pointer runtime.
- **Only native frames, only a frame that is not closed**: the calling frame's own slots are passed to the
  helper (a descriptor in a slot is the usual case; `Mem::region` finds the frames above it only), and a
  closed frame keeps its slots in registers. Frame-mode code has no hook (the interpreter does the loop
  there, or the generic code does).
- **`yavs_rt_lcopy` of at most 64 elements inside the blocks it was given** reads the run into registers and
  writes it (the helper's `get_run`/`put_run`) instead of staging eight blocks on each side with a
  `memset` of both (the out-of-line copy of every native-frame `LCopy`: the result of `get_row` into the
  element of `to_slvv_8`, 2.6 million calls in the histogram run).
- **Measured** (bench build with `llvm`, pinned core, warm, `--tier=auto`, `perf stat`): `poc_stat_histogram`
  16.0 G to 13.5 G instructions, 3.19 G to 2.76 G cycles (-14 percent), run phase 0.67 to 0.59 s; the
  other 36 tests of `tools/realbench --compare` (run phase, `auto` warm, 3 runs) are level (wall and
  instruction geomeans over the 37 tests 0.99, no other test moved by more than the noise). The helper
  costs about 1000 instructions a call for a loop of nine steps (an eight-element row), so a short loop
  gains less than a long one. What is left of the histogram
  gap is the per-call cost of a function returning an unconstrained array (frame, descriptor and result
  copy, about 1000 instructions) and the layout work around it, not the element loops.
- **Not done**: bodies with more than one `LGet`/`LSet`, loops that count by anything but 1 or -1, a body
  that carries a value to the next iteration, loops over integer arrays (the interpreter's loops stop at
  the same places, `YAVS_DUMPIR` says why one is rejected there; `YAVS_LLVM_KINDLOC=1` prints the loops
  the lowering found). Tests: `crates/yavs/tests/compiled_loops.rs` (the `loops.rs` design under
  `--tier=llvm` and `--tier=auto --tier-heat=1,0,0`: same output and exit status as the interpreter, also
  for the loop that leaves its vector), `perf/llvm_eloop.vhd` (`cb_eloop` floor, no step or deopt), unit
  tests of the runtime against the plain loop in `eloop.rs`.

## Element loops planned in the compiled code itself (yavs-llvm, #757, 2026-10-27)

The helper of "Element loops in compiled code" cost about 1000 instructions (190 cycles in a microbenchmark, 400 in the
histogram run) for a loop of eight elements: it interprets the loop's program of steps, one `match` and one checked affine
pair per step, and asks the object table through a trait object for every vector and descriptor. `poc_stat_histogram` calls
it 2.6 million times; `eloop::run`, `LoopObjects::region` and `yavs_rt_eloop` were 38 percent of its warm cycles.

- **The steps become straight-line code** (`Gen::eloop_plan`). Each value of the program is a pair (value at the first
  iteration, change per iteration) of LLVM values; the checks of `eloop::run` are the same ones as integer arithmetic with
  overflow flags (`sadd`, `ssub`, `smul`): the position of an index in a dimension at the first and the last iteration,
  lengths, loaded words, an element range inside 2^32 and inside the object, nothing read among the elements written. One
  set of flags, tested before every memory access that depends on them; any failure takes the generic loop with nothing
  written, as the helper's decline did. Only the elements are done by a call, `yavs_rt_eloop_exec` (the plane copy, the fill
  and the in-order loop of `eloop::exec`), which returns how many iterations it did (fewer only for a source element that is no
  code); the loop variable moves by that many steps and the generic code runs the last iteration as before.
- **Which steps change is known when the code is made** (`eloop::invariant_steps`): `elem_loops` only accepts bases, codes
  and descriptors that do not change, and a product has one factor that does not, so a step either has change 0 (no code for
  it) or depends on the loop variable (and `step`, 1 or -1, is checked once). A program it does not accept (it accepts
  everything `elem_loops` makes today) keeps the helper call (`Gen::eloop_call`); `YAVS_LLVM_ELOOP_HELPER=1` forces it for A/B
  measurements and for the test that runs the loops design both ways. The helper and `eloop::run` stay, for the shared
  runtime (#481).
- **An address is resolved once per use, not once per step.** A base the generator knows (a held parameter region, the frame,
  a constant, the temporary area, instance data, an object in hand) goes through `Gen::host` inline as in any access; the others
  (a fresh frame the caller made, a heap vector) through one call, `yavs_rt_eloop_host`, which finds what `LoopObjects`
  finds (also the slots of the calling native frames) and bounds-checks `extra + n`. An inline probe of the object cache entry
  in front of that call was tried and dropped: the new frame of `get_row` is not in the cache yet (the call loads it), so
  the probe only added instructions (10.4 G to 10.7 G, cycles +3 percent). Superseded by "Native-frame calls find their fresh frames, results and argument regions inline": the fresh frame is a known temporary now and the call is gone.
- **`eloop::exec` decides overlap by host addresses**, not by "same object": the byte ranges of the blocks each stream
  touches are compared as addresses, which is what the code handing it pointers (not objects) needs, and is as exact for the
  helper.
- **Measured** (bench build with `llvm`, `--tier=auto`, histogram warm, one claimed core, `perf stat`, best of 5 interleaved):
  13.10 G to 10.40 G instructions, 2.78 G to 2.24 G cycles (-19 percent); realbench run phase `--compare` (5 runs): wall 0.79 s to
  0.52 s warm, 1.06 s to 0.92 s cold. The loops design runs identically in the interpreter, under `--tier=llvm` and
  `--tier=auto --tier-heat=1,0,0`, each with and without the helper (`compiled_loops`).
- **What is left in the histogram** (perf, warm): `get_row`'s own code 26 percent of the cycles (the plan, and the frame, layout
  and result around the loop), `to_slvv_8` and `to_slm` 16, `exec_planned` 6, `yavs_rt_eloop_host` with its object look-up 10
  (for the fresh frame and the vector read), the interpreter's part (`run_ops`, `op_loop`) 10.


## Native-frame calls find their fresh frames, results and argument regions inline (yavs-llvm, #757, 2026-10-28)

What was left in `poc_stat_histogram` after the planned element loops was the path around each call of a short native-frame
function (`get_row` 2.6 million times, `to_slm`), not the loops: per call two `yavs_rt_eloop_host` callbacks and a
`yavs_rt_region` callback, a parameter region test that always failed and fell into the whole lookup chain, the chain again for
the call's result, and a runtime call to copy eight elements. The fixes are general, for every function on a native frame:

- **`NewFrame` is a temporary-area address** (`rt::track`, `regs::spaces`): the object of a local composite is made there, as
  `Alloc`'s is, so `Known::Temp` and its one bounds test, in its block and across blocks. (`cat_block`'s "fresh block" rule is the
  interpreter's own, which reads the space of the address, so it holds for these objects too.)
- **`Known::LikelyTemp` in native frames too** (`Gen::host_lookup`): a call's result, the words loaded from it and a layout get the
  temporary-area test first, then the native chain as before (own frame, the callers' slots, the object table, the views,
  `yavs_rt_host`); frame-mode code keeps going to the runtime on a miss. A held parameter region that misses (`Gen::host`) takes
  the same order: what an activation cannot hold is mostly an argument in the temporary area.
- **Element-loop memory is found by `Gen::host`** (`Gen::eloop_host`): the plan's vectors and descriptors of unknown space get the
  inline chain, the temporary area first. `yavs_rt_eloop_host` is gone (an inline probe of the object table in front of it was
  slower when the fresh frame was not a known temporary, decisions above; it is now).
- **Activations that move only the temporary area hold every other region** (`rt::fixed_activation`, `yavs_rt_region` flag 4):
  `stable_activation`'s allowlist plus `Alloc`, `NewFrame`, `Stmt`, `TempRoot`, `MakeDope` and `LayoutOf`. None of them frees or
  moves a heap object or pushes a frame, also in its slow path (native frames materialise there, or `native_step` does a layout in
  the temporary area); the temporary area itself may grow, so it is not held. A function that returns a vector was never stable,
  so its descriptor parameters were never held and every access took the full chain.
- **The entry finds a held region in the object table inline** (`Gen::func`, native prologue): where the activation holds objects
  (`stable` or `fixed`), the parameter's entry of `Mem::objs` is probed before `yavs_rt_region` (not for a frame or the temporary
  area, which stay the runtime's to judge); a hit is the region.
- **A planned copy inside one plane block each side is inline** (`Gen::eloop_plan`): the same step of 1 or -1 on both sides, the
  elements of each side within one 64-element block, the two blocks' bytes apart (the test `eloop::exec` makes) is the plane copy
  of `exec` as four masked word moves; anything else calls `yavs_rt_eloop_exec` as before.
- **Not changed:** the optimisation level of native frames (#729/#785): the full `O2` pipeline on these three functions was measured
  level with `LEAN` (cycles 1.89 against 1.88 G); the cost is in the generated code, not in what LLVM does with it.
- **Measured** (bench builds, `--tier=auto` warm, one claimed core, `perf stat`, interleaved, against `8e4cd334`): histogram
  instructions 10.42 to 6.97 G, cycles 2.21 to 1.49 G; step by step (cycles): fresh frames and the element-loop temporary test
  -14 percent, `LikelyTemp` in native frames -3, `fixed_activation` -11, the plan through `Gen::host` -3, the entry probe -3, the
  inline copy -5. `llvm_eloop` work counters: `cb_region` 160 to 1, `cb_host` 22 to 0. realbench run phase `--compare` (42 tests):
  see docs/STATUS.md.
- **sim1:** its argument is a machine pointer and a function's result a pointer into a bump-allocated thread-local area, so neither
  costs a lookup; the idea taken is to treat fresh objects and results as what they are (temporary-area addresses, one test) and
  to resolve an argument's region once, inline where the object table has it. Its element-wise loops were not taken (decisions
  above).

## A process that never suspends stays in compiled code under a bound of 10^9 jumps back (yavs-llvm, yavs-interp, yavs-kernel, #583, #761, 2026-10-26)

Supersedes the "leaves compiled code at its jump back" decision above (user, 2026-10-26): the bound on a process that never
suspends is **10^9 jumps back** (was 10^7, interpreter only) and compiled code keeps running compiled under it.

- **One counter, in the machine** (`Machine::spin`, reached by compiled code through `TierFrame::spin`). Compiled code of such a
  process keeps it in a local that LLVM holds in a register across the loop (loaded at the entry, stored back in every exit
  block, `Gen::spin_out`), adds one at each retreating `Br` next to the stop poll and leaves to the interpreter, which steps the
  `Br` and counts it as before, at every `SPIN_CHECK` (2^20) th jump and on a stop request. The count starts at
  `end - limit`, `end` being the limit rounded up to a multiple of `SPIN_CHECK`, so the one test "a multiple of `SPIN_CHECK`"
  serves the trim and the limit in both tiers and they report the activation at the same jump. At the limit the interpreter
  reports `E3009` exactly as before (message, exit status 1, wave file finished). A counter kept only in memory cost 23 percent
  of a compute loop (the store to load chain); the register-held one costs 0 to 4 percent (below), a counter test per iteration
  being the floor.
- **`YAVS_SPIN_LIMIT=N`** replaces 10^9 (tests and the `spin=N` difftest header: 10^9 jumps take seconds compiled but minutes in a debug
  interpreter). An unparsable value stops the run with a message naming it.
- **The leak of #761 was not in compiled code**: a process that never suspends lists one direct entry per assignment for its
  whole activation (`ProcState::out`, `outv`, `outb`, `scheduled`, `phantoms`, a waveform's `phantom` ranges: the kernel
  commits them when the activation ends), about 24 bytes per assignment in both tiers (the interpreter's 250 MB at 10^7 was this
  too). At 10^9 that is 24 GB. `Ctx::trim_run` now keeps of identical entries only the last (what the commit would leave),
  called by the interpreter's `Br` step at every `SPIN_CHECK` jumps, so the lists stay below about 25 MB per assigning statement.
  Not covered: a loop of a process that does suspend (it lists the same entries until its next wait), and a body that assigns
  very many distinct elements per jump.
- **Measured** (compute loop of 10^8 iterations with real arithmetic and a tight integer loop of 3x10^8, `--tier=llvm`,
  aligned release build, core 10, 5 runs each): against the stop poll alone the counter costs +3.6 percent (0.56 s to 0.58 s) on the
  first and 0 on the second; a process that exits at every jump back (the previous state) ran at interpreter speed plus an exit per jump.
- Tests: `stuck::a_process_that_never_suspends_ends_with_an_error` (E3009 in every tier, one side or the other of an exact limit),
  `stuck::a_long_loop_without_a_wait_runs_to_its_finish`, ignored `stuck::the_default_bound_is_a_billion_jumps_back`,
  `rss::a_loop_without_a_wait_keeps_memory_flat`, perf case `llvm_nowait` (2 exits for 2.5 million jumps),
  corpus `process/no_wait_infinite` (`spin=3000000`, `ignore=stderr`: only yavs prints the W3102 warning).


## llvm: an object table keyed by machine (yavs-llvm `rt.rs`, `lower.rs`, yavs-interp `TierState`, #679, 2026-10-26)

Over the whole LEON3 run with every function compiled, the tier's own work at the start of an activation was 4 percent of the
simulation thread's cycles (`Mem::load_objs` 3.1, `begin_kept` 0.8): the object table was one per thread and keyed by address,
so a change of machine dropped the other machine's instance data and heap objects (a walk), and the process's record of up to 64
objects was entered again at every activation. The SDRAM models (`state_register`, four instances of one process) and the TLBs
have short activations, so this paid for itself on every wake.

- **Decision: an entry's key is the address high half or-ed with a tag, one tag per address space** (`Mem::tags`, `Mem::slot`;
  the 32-bit high half leaves bits 32 and up free): instance data, package data and shared variables carry the machine's tag,
  heap objects the machine's heap tag (valid for one heap epoch), constants the runtime's tag, frame and temporary objects the
  activation's tag. Dropping a group of objects is taking a new tag (`Mem::issue`, a counter of the thread's table): the old
  keys simply miss, no walk. Why: the objects of every machine survive other machines' activations, so the per-activation walk
  and restore are gone (`load_objs`, `save_objs`, `begin_kept`, `settle`, `retain*`, the `occ`/`occv` summaries and the `mine`
  record are removed).
- **Decision: the entry is also moved by an offset of the tag** (`Mem::mixes`, `mix`: a multiplicative hash of the tag, scaled
  by the entry size, xor-ed into `obj_at`). Why: the instances of one process use the same addresses for their own objects (the
  same instance-data and heap indices); without the offset they would take the same entries and evict each other at every
  alternation.
- **Decision: a process's record (`yavs_interp::TierState`, 4 words) holds the table's identity, the heap epoch, the heap tag
  and the machine tag**; the next activation keeps the machine tag when the identity matches and the heap tag when the epoch
  matches too (`Mem::begin`). A call from the interpreter (`Tier::call`, no record) keeps the tags of the last activation or call
  on the thread when it is of the same machine (and epoch). The heap epoch counts every deallocation and edit in place (garbage
  collection deallocates), so the heap objects of a machine stay valid while it is unchanged: a host call that changed it takes a
  new heap tag (`Mem::forget`, was a walk keeping the machine's objects); frames and temporaries take a new tag at the end of an
  activation that found one and after every host call. With `TIER_STAMPS` (someone compares heap objects by write counts) every
  activation takes a new heap tag, so every write of an earlier-found heap object is seen again (was: `TierHost::wrote` for the
  kept writable objects, now removed; a ponytail in `Mem::begin`).
- **Decision: the table has 16 384 entries** (`OBJS`, one cache line each, one megabyte per simulation thread, built zeroed in
  place: `Mem::new`; the empty entry is all zero, a key of tag 0, which no space has). Lookups of the whole LEON3 run that had to
  ask the interpreter (`yavs_rt_obj`): main 15.7 million, keyed with 4 096 entries 21.7 million (the objects of all machines
  compete for the entries), 16 384 entries 7.2 million, 65 536 entries 6.6 million. What is left is mostly heap objects found
  again after a `textio` read edited a line in place (2.2 million new heap tags, in `HRead` and `state_register`), which the old
  table dropped too. Tags run out after 2^31: the table is emptied and gets a new identity (`Mem::wipe`), so no record names a
  tag twice.
- **Generated code** (`Gen::obj_tag`, `Gen::obj_entry`): a heap access and `Deref` read the heap space's tag and offset at fixed
  offsets of `Mem`; an access of unknown space indexes `MEM_TAGS`/`MEM_MIXES` by the space bits of its address (two loads from
  one line). The `Deref` hit test compares the access value and the tag (two machines hold the same access values). The callbacks
  that may take a new tag all receive `mem`, so LLVM reloads the tags after them.
- **Measured** (whole LEON3 run, bench builds, `perf stat --no-inherit` of the simulation thread, one claimed CCD1 core, cells
  interleaved, medians of 4, warm compilation cache; heat = `--tier=auto --tier-heat=1,0,0`; auto worlds settled by four runs
  each since the run-to-run profile): see docs/STATUS.md "llvm: an object table keyed by machine".
- **Cost:** native-frame code pays for the tag in its inline lookups of unknown space (two more loads of `Mem`): `poc_stat_histogram`,
  whose time is element loops on native frames, +2.8 percent instructions and +3.2 percent cycles; the 42 designs of
  `tools/realbench` are level in the geometric mean (docs/STATUS.md).
- **Not done:** the kept drives (#679's second half) are still above the interpreter's drive path: about 9 percent of the heat run's
  samples in the drive callbacks and the kernel functions they reach (`assign_codes_now` 2.2, `drive_now` 1.6, `yavs_rt_drive` 1.4,
  `drive_bits` 1.0, `direct_same`, `direct_same_planes`, `Ctx::assign`) against about 5.7 in the interpreter (`drive_run` 2.0,
  `direct_same_planes` 2.2, `direct_same`, `Ctx::assign`). Inside `assign_codes_now` most samples are loads that miss: the driver's
  `direct` flag, the waveform's pending list, the signal. A batch has 3.8 entries on average. Loading the waveform words of `yavs_rt_drive` one by one (the profile showed most of its
  samples on a merged 16-byte load) changed nothing measurable and was not kept.
- **The reference simulator (rule 22).** It needs no object table: compiled code holds raw pointers, and each instance's data is
  reached through its own context pointer. The idea taken is the outcome: a process's objects belong to that process and do not
  have to be found again because another one ran. Nothing was copied.

## `--tier=auto` first-run latency: prices of compute loops by mode, frame-mode code of native loops on demand, copies repay their own compile, memo votes by callers (yavs-llvm, yavs-interp, #757, #762, 2026-10-26)

Policy owner's round after the batched-analysis basis made short runs (0.3 to 3 s) decide the totals against sim1. Measured with bench builds of
`0dcfa551` ("main") and of this change, a fresh copy of the pristine world per binary and round, the analysis caches filled by two untimed
`--tier=interp` runs, then four consecutive `--tier=auto` runs (run 1 = cold, run 3 = what `tools/realbench` times as warm), one claimed core of
CCD1 for all cells of a test, 5 rounds interleaved, medians, wall from `perf stat duration_time`. Tables: docs/STATUS.md "`--tier=auto`
first-run latency".

- **Cause: the compute model priced both kinds of compute loop as neither.** `Kind::Compute` (4 ms + 900 us an IR instruction) covered the
  native-frame code of a compute function and the frame-mode code of a process with a loop. Measured compile CPU: native-frame code 33, 53 and
  62 ms for 79, 107 and 153 IR (`get_row`, `to_slvv_8`, `to_slm` of `poc_stat_histogram`; the model said 75, 100, 142), frame-mode code 21 to
  75 ms for 91 to 448 IR and 146 ms for 949 (the model said 86 to 410 and 860). **Decision: frame-mode compute loops are a kind of their own,
  `ComputeFrame` (15 ms + 110, speedup 1.8); `Compute` (native frames) keeps its price and speedup.** The speedup of `ComputeFrame` is what
  the trials of `sc5_fifo_repack` measure (a `p_col` copy seen for 19 percent of the run gave 1.09 to 1.13 times the progress: about 1.75 for
  its own time; all six processes forced were 26 percent of the run, #675) and stays above `profile::EARLY_SPEEDUP` so the profile keeps
  listing such processes. `Compute` at its measured price was tried twice and dropped: at speedup 2.4 it compiled the string loops of the
  verification libraries early, which run no faster compiled and, linked from the cache, made every warm run slower too (`uvvm_sb_slv`
  `match_identifier`: 8 percent more instructions warm and cold; `uvvm_axistream_vvc` cold +16 percent with
  `convert_byte_array_to_slv_array` and its callees, 0.5 s of compile CPU at 1.9 s of a 2.9 s run); at speedup 1.3 (the old thresholds) the
  budget still let a clocked process whose tree holds a compute callee in at the end of a 0.6 s run (`poc_cache_cpu` cold +11 percent, the
  compile still running when the run ended). The old price is the guard against both; what tells the winners (`poc_stat_histogram`:
  element-loop copies, 3 to 4 times faster compiled) from these losers was not found (the histogram's functions have more loops than element
  loops, so a kind by the loops' shape does not separate them; a per-function verdict would, the profile judges processes only). `Loop`
  (native frames with a loop that is no compute loop) is priced for its native-frame code alone, 4 ms + 550 (the price of `Native`; it had paid
  for two modules).
- **Cause: the frame-mode code of a native function with a loop was compiled right after its native-frame code** (`Part::Both`, 176 of
  426 ms of compile CPU in a cold `poc_stat_histogram`), though no native frame of it ever left to the interpreter there, and the second
  module was priced as a link (the cache list had the name from the first module), so the budget saw 1.8 ms for a 39 ms compile.
  **Decision: such a function is compiled as native-frame code alone; its frame-mode code is compiled once the function is seen interpreted
  again for that code's payback (`Worker::frame_at`), as a root of its own without callees** (a native frame left to the interpreter goes
  on interpreted, which is what the samples see; the callees its native code left out were never seen running, and compiling them with the
  frame-mode code brought sixty logging functions of the window generator along). Under `--tier-heat` (no budget) both modules are made at
  once as before, so the CI legs keep covering frame-mode code of such functions. `price_of` no longer halves the price of a part. A
  function whose native-frame code exists (linked from the cache by the probe, or compiled as a callee) that becomes a candidate gets a
  `frame_at` instead of a compile of its frame-mode code (that was the old path to it: a warm run compiled 40 ms of frame-mode code per
  such function), and a native-frame module the cache had brings its frame-mode module along when the cache has that too (a link,
  `Worker::compile`). Found on the way, #764: in some second runs a memoised function with published native-frame code keeps running
  interpreted (`to_slvv_8` of `poc_stat_histogram`, depending on the order its callers' code is linked, never with `YAVS_NO_PMEMO=1`);
  `frame_at` then compiled its frame-mode code after about 250 ms. Fixed in 9418e648 by another agent; with it the second run is level with main.
- **Cause: every copy of a hot process was a candidate.** The seen time of a process counts for all its copies (#661), and once the process
  was hot every copy that ran was compiled; copies differ in their constants, so each is a module of its own (50 ms each in
  `sc5_fifo_repack`, seen for 5 to 250 ms each). With the cheaper frame-mode price that turned into twenty cold compiles and a cold run 8
  to 13 percent slower (autopol2's finding). And the cache list keys functions by name and size, which copies share, so one compiled copy
  made every other copy of the process look cached (priced as a 6 ms link). **Decision: a copy of a process that is not a clocked process
  (`rtl`) is a candidate once the process is hot and the copy itself was seen for its own payback (`need` of its own length); clocked
  processes keep the pooled rule (`poc_arith_addw`, #675), and the cache list names a copy by `Program::copy_tag` (`Worker::list_key`; a
  copy linked as the twin of another is listed under its own name too).** The profile's early path is unchanged: a listed process still
  compiles every copy at its first look (that is what the warm runs gain).
- **#762: the memo of a pure function stays on for all processes until `VOTES` (3) have given it up**, so a function two processes call
  (`get_row` of `poc_stat_histogram`: the testbench and the unit) kept every compiled call going through `yavs_rt_memo` and
  `TierHost::memo_probe` (7.3 percent of the warm run's cycles, `Machine::memo_probe` with its `pm.take()` and `is_off` scan). **Decision: off
  for all once `VOTES` or every process that called it so far has given it up** (`Pre::memo_users`, counted at a process's first call of the
  function). Accepted: a process that starts calling after the others gave up does not get the memo. After: the memo symbols are 0.7
  percent of the cycles. Counter `pmemo_off` (functions whose memo is off for all), test `perf/memo_giveup.vhd`. The idea of a flag that
  compiled code tests before the callback was not needed.
- **Not done, why:** compiling on spare cores (every timed comparison pins the run and its compile thread to one core, so it cannot show
  there, and the budget would need a second rule for it); a cheaper first level for frame-mode copies (`Fast` code is about 1.7 times slower
  and the copies' gain is 1.75 at O2); batching copies with equal code (twins, #713, already compile once; the `sc5_fifo_repack` copies
  differ).

## The HRead digit loop: table reads before the first pass, facts about the words of one block, slices of constant length (yavs-ir `opt.rs`, `opt/inline.rs`, yavs-interp `ieee.rs`, #744, 2026-10-26)

The S-record start-up of the twelve memory models of `grlib_leon3mp` is the digit loop of the `HRead` of GRLIB's `stdio` package: `SV(4*i to 4*i+3) := FromChar(S(i)); if Is_X(SV(4*i to 4*i+3))`
for every hex digit, run from the textio package at start-up (more than half of the profile of the first 1 us, `--tier=interp`, after #722). The cost is general: every
`v(a to a + k) := f(x)` or `g(v(a to a + k))` on a slice of constant length pays for a descriptor, a length check, a layout and a position per statement. The loop took 33 interpreter ops
per digit (the table read of #722 built a fat pair in a block of its own and read both words back; both slices made a descriptor of their length and checked it against the length of the
result; the second slice repeated the position of the first); it takes 13.

- **A result-table read is made before the first optimiser pass** (`opt/inline.rs` `tab_calls`, called by `optimize_body_with`), not by the inliner after it. The reads of #722 are inlined
  after the register sharing (`renumber`), where most registers are defined more than once and the optimiser does not follow their values; the loads of the two words of the pair
  `tab_forwarder` builds were never forwarded from the stores that built them. Before the first pass the registers of the read are new and defined once. Only reads that are one path
  (the argument type is an enumeration, every value tabulated: no range test, no call) are taken early, and the call's statement stays on the inlined instructions (no `via`
  entry: a table read cannot fail, so a trace needs no frame for it). A table with a range test or a validity mask keeps the inliner's join and call path. `YAVS_NO_CASETAB=1` and
  `YAVS_NO_INLINE=1` turn it off.
- **Facts the walk keeps** (`opt.rs`): a `TempRoot` writes no memory (it registered the pair block and so forgot every fact, a load right after it read memory again); a store forgets
  the facts about another word of the same block only when its bytes overlap (`kill`: two `Index` results of one block by constants, `iat`), so the pair's two stores no longer
  forget each other; a stored address that a register holds (an `AddrOf` result defined once) is what a load of that word gives back; a load is aliased to a register only of the same
  register type; a frame address that `Copy`, `LCopy`, `LFill`, `LSet`, `LGet`, `MemEq`, `Zero`, `MakeDope`, `DopeLen`, `SlicePos`, `Pos`, `SubtypeCheck` or `LayoutOf` read or write through
  does not escape (`escapes`: the facts about the descriptors of a frame slot survived no copy into a vector before); a second `SlicePos` of the same slice of the same descriptor is
  the first one (`Key::Slice`).
- **The length of `MakeDope [x + p, x + q]`** for one register `x` defined once and constants `p`, `q` is `q - p + 1` (0 if that is negative; `downto` the other way round): the
  additions are checked, so on the path that continues it is exact (`note_affine` keeps `aff`, `affine_len`). `DopeLen`, `LayoutOf` of the slice and the `SubtypeCheck` of its length against
  the pool descriptor of a table result fold, and the descriptor goes with its block.
- **A block that is only stored into goes** (`drop_stored_only_blocks`, in `dce`): an `Alloc` defined once whose every use is the address of a `Store` or the base of an `Index`
  that only addresses stores (the fat pair of a table read once its words were forwarded) loses the `Alloc`, the stores and the indexes. `dce` runs before `drop_statements` at the end
  of `run` so that the markers of statements whose temporaries are gone go with them.
- **Interpreter** (`yavs-interp` `ieee.rs`): `is_x` of a vector reads the plane words in place (it made a `LogicVec` with a heap vector for every call, a few percent of the loop with `malloc` and `free`); `to_bitvector (std_ulogic_vector, bit)` is a native (the 1164 body is an
  element loop with a `case`: 6 to 9 percent of the start-up through `HRead (bit_vector)`).
- **Measured** (bench builds with `llvm`, `--tier=interp` unless said, cores 8 to 15 by `tools/claim core`, `perf stat`; before = the commit before this change). `grlib_leon3mp`, the first 1 us
  (elaboration and S-record start-up): warm compilation cache 51.89 G to 31.54 G instructions (-39.2 percent), 13.82 to 13.91 G cycles to 8.33 to 8.48 G, CPU time 2.72 s to 1.65 s (3 interleaved
  pairs); empty cache 60.69 G to 40.39 G instructions (-33 percent), 3.30 s to 2.24 s CPU. The whole run (`--stop-time=1060500ns`, `tools/realbench --compare`, median of 3, core 8): `--tier=interp`
  36.02 s to 34.87 s wall, 449.1 G to 428.1 G instructions; `--tier=auto` 36.54 s to 35.38 s, 439.4 G to 428.9 G; with an empty cache 36.95 s to 35.68 s (interp), 37.19 s to 36.53 s (auto) (the start-up is about a thirteenth of the run). The first 1 us, same core, interleaved: `--tier=auto` 35.5 G to 27.1 G instructions, 2.0 s to 1.45 s; `--tier=llvm` 84.3 G to 72.5 G, 7.5 s to 6.85 s. A reproducer with the shape of
  the loop (240 000 `HRead` calls of 32 bits, 7 digits each): 76.1 M to 39.4 M ops, 7.43 G to 4.17 G instructions, 33 to 13 ops per digit; one digit of 8 bits: 56.9 M to 41.1 M ops.
  Breadth (`tools/realbench --compare`, 42 tests, run phase, `interp` and `auto`, one run per cell): geometric mean of the instruction ratios 0.99 and 1.00 (every test within 5 percent
  but two `auto` cells at 1.05 and 1.07 that repeat at 1.00 and 0.99 over 5 runs), of the CPU-time ratios 0.96 and 1.01; empty cache (`interp-cold`, `auto-cold`, so the optimiser's first
  run): instruction ratio geometric mean 1.00 and 1.00 (small tests +1 to 2 percent, the cost of the extra `dce` and the table pass on the first call of each function). The standard `hread` of
  `ieee.std_logic_textio` (2008) into 32 and 64 bit vectors, 20 000 lines of six words: 7.30 G to 5.58 G instructions, 0.38 s to 0.29 s wall (same core, interleaved). `tools/bench` designs `textio_heavy`, `file_io`, `strings_heavy`,
  `ieee_heavy` and `report_heavy` run the same instructions (to 0.03 percent); `textio_heavy` alone has 3.7 percent more cycles over 8 interleaved pairs with 7.6 percent more L1 instruction cache
  misses, the layout effect of #576 (the executed instruction counts are equal). `case_tab` fell from 17.4 k to 13.2 k ops, `spec_nested` (the copy) from 312 k to 218 k and `slice_memo` from 1.5 k to 1.4 k (their ceilings are lowered), the
  work-counter case `hread_loop` bounds a digit loop of this shape.
- **Tests**: `opt` (`a_slice_whose_bounds_differ_by_a_constant_has_that_length`, `a_block_only_stored_into_goes`, `registering_a_root_forgets_nothing_about_memory`, the words of a
  descriptor that a store beside them does not change), `ieee_native` (`to_bitvector` of random operands, natives on and off), perf case `hread_loop`, and the differential cases of #722
  (`casetab`). The `make_temporary` of the `opt` tests keeps its block as a root, and the `opt_slots` tests put a store through an unknown pointer between the writes and the reads of a
  block: both blocks were only written or read back from the stores, which the optimiser now follows.
- **Not done** (issues): `Init_mem` of the SDRAM model (element-by-element fill of a row through an access value, 18 percent of what is left of the start-up, #768); the fixed cost of an
  `HRead` call (two frames with descriptors, two natives, the `Copy` of the descriptors: 86 ops for one digit, #771); a copy-free `Is_X` of a slice (the slice is copied into a block first: `Alloc` +
  `LCopy` + native, #770); the table path with a range test or a validity mask (integer arguments) still has the join and the pair (#769). Range proofs for `4 * i` and `4 * i + 3` against the
  integer range (two `BinRange` per digit stay) are not planned.

## The watching loop calls native-frame callees itself (yavs-interp `run_ops`, #757, #750, 2026-10-26)

The `--tier=auto` round before this one found that compiling the string loops of the verification libraries as native-frame code made the runs slower
(`uvvm_sb_slv` +8 percent) and kept the `Compute` price high for that reason. The compiled code was not the cause: forced alone at its first look,
`match_identifier` fell from 113 to 32 profile samples (3.5 times faster) while the run took 8.5 percent more instructions, and `perf` put 50 percent of
the cycles in `run_ops::<true, false>`. A call of any function the tier had flagged made the watching loop (`run_ops::<false, true>`) hand over
(`Flow::Retier`), and the activation stayed in the loop with the tier to its end: no lean calls, no skipped parameter loads, a slot store and a flag look per
entry, about a fifth more per op over the rest of a testbench process's long activation.

- **Decision: a callee the tier calls on a native frame (`NAT_CALL`) is called by the watching loop through `Tier::call` itself** (`native_tier!`, the
  runtime's tier for a callee whose `Pre::native` is set; a memoised callee goes through `memo_call` with the tier, so a miss is a native call as in the loop
  with the tier, not `memo_run`). The hand-over stays for a callee with frame-mode code (`NAT_CODE`) or one to be compiled (`NAT_ASK`): its frame is
  entered and its compiled code run by the loop with the tier. `NativeFlags::retiers` counts the hand-overs (`YAVS_COUNTERS` `retiers`); the
  `sim.rs` tests pin none for a native-call callee and some for a frame-mode one. A materialisation (`Called::Pushed`) returns `Flow::Call` to
  `exec_fast::<false, true>`, which interprets the pushed frames.
- **Measured** (bench builds of main 9b5ce798 and of this change, `YAVS_AUTO_FORCE` of one function at its first look with every other kind priced out,
  warm run, instructions of the process): `match_identifier` 11.57 G to 9.97 G (nothing forced: 10.74 G), `STD_MATCH` 12.49 G to 10.69 G,
  `uvvm_axistream_vvc` with `to_string` 41.9 G to 38.4 G (nothing forced: 36.25 G); the histogram's element-loop functions unchanged. `--tier=interp`
  instructions equal (24.2485 G against 24.2486 G on `poc_stat_histogram`). All 42 of `tools/realbench` (`--compare`, `auto,auto-cold`, run phase,
  cores 13 to 15, default runs): wall geometric mean 0.99 warm and 1.00 cold, instructions 1.00 and 1.01, sum of the walls 0.97 and 1.01;
  `uvvm_axistream_vvc` warm instructions 0.91 (the three native functions the policy compiles there no longer cost the rest of the activation),
  the other moves are within the host spread of that pass (load average 9 to 12).
- **Left:** a callee with frame-mode code still hands over (`check_value` of `uvvm_sb_slv` forced: 10.79 G to 12.65 to 14.47 G warm), the general
  cost of the loop with the tier is #750.

## The loop with the tier calls untouched callees lean; the watching arm of `run_quick` reads `any` once (yavs-interp `run_ops`, `run_quick`, #750, 2026-10-26)

Question (#750, after round 20 and #757): what is left of the cost of a tier that compiled nothing, and does the loop with the tier
(`run_ops::<true, false>`, entered by an activation whose root has compiled code or by a hand-over) pay per call what the plain loop does not?

Method as in round 20: main-thread instructions (`perf stat --no-inherit`, warm world, deterministic to 0.05 percent), `tools/stepcount --ops`
over equal windows (`--to` a kernel cycle count) of `--tier=interp` against `--tier=auto --tier-heat=2000000000,0,16000`, per-instruction
counts of `run_quick` and `run_ops` (`objdump` with the executed counts), bench builds with `llvm`, `YAVS_STD_CACHE` private.

What the counts said (nothing compiled, `poc_cache_cpu` and `neorv32_single_min`, 1.0128 and 1.0124 over `--tier=interp`):

- 75 to 80 percent of the difference is per activation, in `run_quick`: 28 instructions (`Suspend` +28 an op, `WaitSuspend` +26, `WaitEdgeSuspend`
  +22 in the equal windows; `run_ops` itself costs the same per activation in both loops): the tier / `any` / `cont` tests, the thread-local
  slot, `NativeFlags::activated` (two loads and a test), the slot store with `runtime id << 32 | function`, the `SlotIdle` store.
- The rest is the tick of a jump (`cmp` of the target with `k`, then the countdown on a taken jump back: 2 instructions on a forward jump, 4 on a
  backward one, `CmpBr` +3, `Br` +3, `CondBr` +1.5). The spilled hoisted address of round 20 does not show any more (`AffP`, `Load`, `DerefImm` equal).
- With a tier the loop `run_ops::<true, false>` made every call through `call_pre` and started the callee at `Code::first`: no lean call, no
  skipped parameter loads, for callees that have no compiled code and never will (the `Pre::native` byte is clear).

Landed (`exec.rs`):

- **`run_quick` reads `NativeFlags::any` once** and counts an activation (`activated`) only when it is set (`count_on` sets it): the watching
  arm drops about 6 of its 28 instructions. `Machine::tiered` is `any && root_flagged`.
- **`plain_callee!`: the loop with the tier makes a lean call and starts a callee past its prologue (`Code::skip`) when the callee's
  `Pre::native` byte is clear** (it was `!TIER`). A callee the tier flags while its lean frame runs is entered by `enter!` at that op, as the
  watching loop's hand-over already did for frames it had called lean; compiled code enters a lean frame only at an IR pc past the prologue,
  and a pc that is no entry is interpreted to the next jump (`tier_go`). Test
  `a_callee_the_tier_never_touched_is_called_lean_in_the_loop_with_the_tier` (trace equal to the interpreter's, callee flagged half way).
- **Not landed:** skipping `ready!` at the entry of an untouched callee in the loop with the tier (about 7 instructions a call, 1 percent of a
  forced `uvvm_sb_slv` run, inside the spread of its compile timing); ticking every taken jump by the countdown alone (tried in round 20, worse);
  a cheaper slot protocol (the sampler needs the function per activation and the idle mark, so the stores stay).

Measured (main-thread instructions, `--tier=auto` over `--tier=interp`, nothing compiled, before to after; both ratios from the same two
binaries, interleaved, 3 rounds, core 8 to 15): `poc_cache_cpu` 1.0128 to 1.0112, `neorv32_single_min` 1.0124 to 1.0112, `osvvm_axis_random`
1.0053 to 1.0053, `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` 1.0039 to 1.0034, `uvvm_util_rand` 1.0054 to 1.0061, `uvvm_sb_slv` 1.0082 to 1.0081,
`uvvm_axistream_vvc` 1.0043 to 1.0044, `poc_stat_histogram` 1.0034 to 1.0034; geometric mean 1.0070 to 1.0066. `--tier=interp` instructions
are equal to 0.03 percent. So the no-compiled-code case still costs 0.3 to 1.1 percent of instructions (the per-activation 22 and the jump tick);
the cycles of the same pairs move by +-2 percent either way (host spread, #576), the cycle geometric mean is 1.00. The case that
changed is a function with compiled code and callees without: `uvvm_sb_slv` with `check_value` forced (frame-mode code, the callee that hands over,
#757): 12.44 G to 11.5 to 11.9 G main-thread instructions and 3.80 to 3.95 G to 3.50 to 3.70 G cycles (5 runs each, warm, compile-timing spread).
`tools/realbench --compare` (14 tests, run phase, `interp` and `auto`, core 8): wall geometric mean 1.00 and 1.00, instructions 1.01 (tiny
tests, 0.01 G) and 1.00; the long `interp` runs are equal to 0.1 percent.

Checks: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` default and `--features llvm`, `cargo test --workspace` default and with `llvm`, difftest 531/531 at 1 and 4
threads for `yavs-interp`, `yavs-auto`, `yavs-llvm` and `yavs-auto` with `--tier-heat=1,0,0`.

Left: the per-activation set-up of the watching arm (about 22 instructions: tier test, thread-local slot, tag, two stores) and the tick of a
jump; both are the price of the sampler's slot protocol. A change of that protocol (say, the slot written only while the sampler looks) belongs
to the policy owner. The loop with the tier still checks the flag table at every call and return (`bind!`).

## `wait until <edge>` costs what the sensitivity-list forms cost: `Op::WaitEdgeSuspend` (yavs-interp `pre.rs`, `exec.rs`, #767, 2026-10-26)

- **Cause** (`tools/stepcount --ops`, one clock period): the process `begin wait until rising_edge(clk); ... end process;` has an elaborator edge trigger,
  so the kernel side was already the same as for `process (clk) if rising_edge(clk)`. The interpreter still ran, at the end of every activation, `BrBody`
  (the pause check of the jump to the body block), `Stmt`, `SigVal` + `WaitEdge` (a reference to the clock, then `Ctx::wait_edge`, which does nothing when the
  trigger's `known_edge` is set) and `WaitSuspend`: about 128 instructions an activation more than the other forms (+8.9 percent of a 4096-register design in
  the interpreter, +11.9 percent in `--tier=auto`).
- **Decision:** `pre::superops` makes the sequence `SigVal` (one element), `WaitEdge`, `WaitSig`, `Suspend` on the same element (same instance signal and
  the same offset register or equal known offsets, the reference read only by the `WaitEdge`) one op, `WaitEdgeSuspend`, in the style of `WaitSuspend`: a
  `Stmt` before it is part of it, and a `Br` or `BrBody` to it is a copy of it that runs as op `at` (the `BrBody` copy keeps the pause check of `prestart`, the
  `body` field). The op does `Ctx::wait_edge` (a load and a test when the trigger is known) and `wait_on_again` on the element directly from
  `inst.sigs` (`Machine::wait_edge_sig1`); an element out of the fast path runs the two steps with the checks of `sig_elem`. A `wait until` that is not an
  edge on one element (an `and` with other signals, `or`, a timeout, another signal in the `on` list) keeps the instructions as they were.
- **Not done:** the `--tier=llvm` code of such a process (every function compiled, the `WaitEdge` goes to the host through `signal`) still costs more than the
  sensitivity forms (about +18 percent in the same design): #772, next to #766.
- **Measured** (bench builds, `rtl_ff`-style design of 4096 one-bit registers and 2000 cycles, `--threads 1`, warm cache, `perf stat instructions:u`, cores 8 to 15 by
  `tools/claim core`; sensitivity `rising_edge`, `'event`, `not 'stable`, `wait until rising_edge`): interpreter before 8.730, 8.737, 8.737, 9.780 G, after 8.705, 8.713, 8.713,
  8.756 G (wait form +12.0 percent over `rising_edge` before, +0.6 percent after: 128 to 6 instructions an activation); `--tier=auto` before 9.003, 9.010, 9.010, 10.077 G,
  after 8.978, 8.985, 8.985, 9.036 G (+11.9 to +0.65 percent). The other forms gain 0.3 percent (the pass). Cycles (same runs, interleaved old/new pairs, best of 2, G): interpreter wait form
  2.98 to 2.81 (`rising_edge` 2.84 to 2.77), `--tier=auto` 3.05 to 2.81 (`rising_edge` 2.90 to 2.84); the wait form is within 1.5 percent of `rising_edge` in both.
- **Tests:** work-counter test `edge_cost_parity` (`perf/edge_cost.vhd` with each of the four forms: equal `ops`, a ceiling for each); `edge_forms` bound lowered; `delta/wait_edge`
  and `edge_idioms` run the wait shapes in every tier. Difftest 531 of 531 for interp, auto and llvm at 1 and 4 threads and auto with `--tier-heat=1,0,0` at 4 threads.

## Table reads with a range test or a validity mask: the rest of the block goes into the table arm (yavs-ir `opt/inline.rs`, #769, 2026-10-26)

The result-table read of #722 for an argument of an integer type tests the range, and for a table with values that report (a mask of valid values) tests the mask; both
send the other values to the call. The read was inlined by the late inliner as blocks that join again, so the optimiser, which does not follow registers there, never saw the stores that
built the fat pair of an array result and read both words back for every call (about 30 ops per digit of a nibble loop, against 13 for a character argument whose table holds every value).

- **Decision: every read of a result table is made before the first optimiser pass (`tab_calls`), the late inliner leaves calls of table functions alone** (`tabbed`). A read that branches
  becomes the range test, the mask test, the table arm and the call arm; the rest of the block after the call (at most `MAX_TAIL` = 64 instructions, no suspension, no other branching read) is
  **copied into the table arm** with every register it defines renamed (`rename_tail`), so the table arm is straight-line code from the test to the end of the block and the loads of the pair find the
  stores that built it (the pair goes, as in #744). The call arm keeps the original rest of the block. A register the copy defines that the code outside the rest reads, or that the rest reads before
  it defines it, is moved back to its own name before the terminator. A longer rest, or one with another branching read, takes the old shape: arms that join. The call that stays in the call arm
  is not read again: the late inliner skips calls of table functions, so a miss costs the test and the call, not a second test.
- **Why copy the rest instead of joining with the words of the pair.** Joining the two words (data address, descriptor) as registers would need every use of the pair rewritten and loses that the
  descriptor of the table path is a constant (its length check folds). The copy costs code only on the table arm; its size is capped and counted against the growth cap of the inliner.
- **Measured.** Perf case `tab_tail` (new: an integer type of 21 values, 16 tabulated, 8 digits stored into a slice): 22 072 ops to 15 764 (-29 percent). A loop of 160 000 such reads: 26.8 to 18.9
  ops per digit; with a proven range (`i mod 16` into `type nib_t is range 0 to 15`) the test folds and the digit costs 11.8 ops (24.8 before). `grlib_leon3mp` has no such table (its `FromChar` takes a
  character): unchanged.
- **Tests**: perf case `tab_tail` (a ceiling that fails if the pair is made again), the `casetab` differential test (new `digvec` and `digsum`: array results by an integer type with a mask, reports
  for the digits that are no table entry, rest-of-block copies with live-out registers), run with the tables on and off at 1 and 4 threads and in every tier.

## Loop-invariant loads and dereferences in loops that write only logic elements (yavs-ir `opt/licm.rs`, #768, 2026-10-26)

`Init_mem` of the SDRAM model of `grlib_leon3mp` (a procedure declared in a process) fills a freshly allocated row, `Bank0 (Row_index) (i) (j) := '0'`, in two nested loops: 18 percent of the first
1 us after #744. Each element store read the access value of the row from the frame of the process (`AddrOf Up`, `Load`), dereferenced it and computed the positions and lengths of the descriptors,
nine ops per element, because the loop-invariant code motion moved only computations, never a load or a dereference, and not the address of a frame up the static links.

- **Decision: in a loop whose only writes are element writes of logic arrays (`LSet`, `LFill`), a `Load` (not of a signal), a `Deref` and the descriptor reads (`Pos`, `DopeLen`) are invariant when
  their operands are; the address of a frame up the static links (`AddrOf Up`) moves like a computation that cannot fail.** The existing rule for what may fail is unchanged: a `Deref` (null or
  dangling handle) moves only from the effect-free start of the header, and the preheader replays that start as the first pass would run it, so the first failure and its message are the unmoved
  code's. A loop that stores a word, frees, allocates or calls keeps its loads and dereferences in place.
- **Why this is sound.** Element planes of a logic array are never read as words (`Load`), never hold handles and never hold descriptors: the lowering reads them with `LGet`/`LCopy`, which are not
  moved. `AddrOf Up` yields the address of a frame in the static chain of the running call, the same for the whole run of the loop; it is not moved out of the loop's other blocks (`speculable` still
  excludes it), only from the start of the header, because a loop that does not run does not compute it.
- **Effect.** The inner loop is left with the element position and the store, which `ElemLoop` (`eloop.rs`, #520) already runs as one op: 9 ops per element became 8 ops per row of 17 elements
  (the issue's reproducer: 5.08 M ops to 0.26 M). `grlib_leon3mp`, first 1 us, `--tier=interp`: `Init_mem` 420 of 1888 profile samples to 29; 31.37 G to 25.96 G instructions (-17.2 percent),
  8.3 G to 6.9 G cycles. Work-counter ceilings lowered because the ops fell: `elem_loops` 35.6 k to 27.8 k, `licm_loop` 26.4 k to 19.8 k, `wide_vec`, `case_tab`, `idle_vars`.
- **The compiled tier keeps what a moved load knew.** Compiled process code (`--tier=llvm`, `auto`) reaches a vector through a pointer loaded from a variable's slot; the generator knew that
  pointer (probably a heap object, so its accesses try the object cache inline) only in the block of the load, and a load that moved to a preheader lost it: every element access of the loop
  asked the runtime (`llvm_eloop`: `cb_host` 22 to 1671). The space analysis of the generator (`yavs-llvm` `regs.rs` `spaces`) now carries "probably heap" for the pointer loaded from the slot of a
  variable (not a parameter's) or of an enclosing subprogram's through the blocks, as it carries the definite spaces.
- **Tests**: perf case `row_fill` (a procedure of a process fills rows behind access values: a ceiling on the ops), the difftest cases `access/row_fill` (nested fills, an empty range over a null access
  value) and `access/row_fill_null` (the failure of a null access in a nested loop comes after the report that precedes it in the body, as in the reference), the loop tests of `yavs-lower`.

## `is_x` of a slice of a logic vector tests the planes of the source: `Op::IsXSlice` (yavs-interp `pre.rs`, `exec.rs`, #770, 2026-10-26)

`Is_X (SV (4*i to 4*i+3))`, in the digit loop of every textio `HRead`, copied the slice into a block of temporary memory (`Alloc` + `LCopy`, fused into `AllocLCopy`) and called the native on the
copy (`CallIeee`: the cells of the call, the lookup of the function, a result through `Machine::set`): three ops and about a tenth of the digit loop's instructions.

- **Decision: the predecoder fuses `Alloc` of 32 bytes, the `LCopy` of at most 64 elements into it and the `CallIeee` of the `is_x` of a vector into `Op::IsXSlice`**, when the copy is read by
  nothing else (`live_after`) and lands at element 0. The op tests the plane words of the source block where they are (shifted by the element offset, masked to the count); it does not allocate the
  temporary. Anything else (more than 64 elements, a slice that crosses a block, an unreadable source, no elements) runs the `Alloc` alone and the ops that follow, as before. The same op shape
  fits the other natives that read one small vector (`to_x01` and the like make a vector and stay on `AllocLCopy`); only `is_x` is fused here.
- **Why not a form of the `ieee` arguments that passes an element offset.** Every native reads its operand from element 0 of the planes (`dim_at`, `Machine::planes`); an offset would be an
  extra cell for each of them and a shift in each, to save one copy of at most 32 bytes. The copy is cheap; the call around it was the cost.
- **Measured** (bench build with `llvm`, `--tier=interp`, `tools/claim core`, same core, interleaved, `perf stat`): `grlib_leon3mp`, first 1 us, 25.966 G to 23.072 G instructions (-11.1
  percent). A 128-bit `HRead` repeated 20 000 times: 992 M to 798 M instructions with #771's branch fold (-19.6 percent; 31 digits each).
- **Tests**: difftest case `ieee/is_x_slice` (every `std_ulogic` value at every position of vectors of 150 elements, ascending and descending, slices of 1 to 70 elements that stay in a block or
  cross its edge), perf case `hread_loop` (ops 7594 to 7156 together with #771).

## A branch whose arms lead to the same block is a jump (yavs-ir `opt/cfg.rs`, #771, 2026-10-26)

The fixed cost of one `HRead` call is about 86 interpreter ops for one digit (#771). Part of it is the descriptor of each local array: `SV (0 to SL-1)` tests whether the range is null, and the
arm for a null range is a block that only jumps to the block of the other arm, so the test decided nothing (three of them per call).

- **Decision: `cfg::equal_arms` turns a `CondBr` whose two targets lead to the same block (through up to four blocks that are only a jump) into a `Br`**; the compare that fed it goes with
  `dead_defs`, the emptied arm with the clean-up that follows. It runs first in `cfg::run`, for every subprogram that cannot suspend, loop or not.
- **Measured.** `HRead` of 8 bits, 20 000 calls (bench build, `perf stat`): 245.8 M to 231.1 M instructions together with #770 (two `is_x` per call); the branch fold alone is 0.3 percent of
  the first 1 us of `grlib_leon3mp`, three ops of 86.
- **Not done in #771** (what is left of its cost, with the profile of the first 1 us after #768 and #770: `HRead` 61 percent of the samples, its digit loop 45 percent): the `Read` of a string
  as a native on `data, left, right, dir` instead of a fat pair (`NewPair`, `FatRoot`, `CallNative` per call); descriptors of local arrays whose shape depends on `VALUE'Length` made once per
  length (`NewDope`, `MakeDope`, `LayoutWord`, `NewFrame`, `Copy` are five ops for each of `SV` and `S`); `Stmt` markers of statements the fusion left without a temporary; the two
  `BinRange` of `4 * i` and `4 * i + 3` and the `SlicePos` of a slice whose position the loop's range already bounds.
- **Tests**: `opt` (`a_branch_whose_arms_lead_to_the_same_block_is_a_jump`); perf case `hread_loop` lowered (7594 to 7156 ops with #770).

## `--tier=auto`: a compile pays for the callees it brings, `Compute` at one and a half times its measured price (yavs-llvm `auto.rs`, #757, 2026-10-26)

Follow-up of "`--tier=auto` first-run latency": the lower `Compute` price (native-frame compute loops, measured 33 to 62 ms of compile CPU for 79 to
153 IR) had been dropped because it compiled losers. Measured with bench builds, fresh copies of the pristine `tools/realbench` worlds, two untimed
`--tier=interp` runs, then `--tier=auto` runs, all cells of a design on one claimed core of CCD1, instructions of the whole process.

- **The losers were not the compiled code.** After "The watching loop calls native-frame callees itself" the string loops are winners (`match_identifier`
  3.5 times faster, `uvvm_sb_slv` warm 7 percent fewer instructions at the measured price). What remained was cold-run cost, two kinds:
  - **The tree.** The payback rule (`need`) prices the root alone, while `tree` compiles every native-frame callee not compiled yet. A cheaper `Compute`
    let `convert_byte_array_to_slv_array` (303 IR) in with ten callees, 700 ms of compile CPU in a 3 s run (`uvvm_axistream_vvc` cold +8 to +17
    percent), and a clocked process whose callee `mux` is a compute loop into the budget at the end of a 0.6 s run (`poc_cache_cpu` cold +11 to +13 percent).
  - **The run length.** At the measured price `match_identifier` compiles at 0.5 s of a 0.8 s run, when the payback rule assumes the rest is as long
    as the part seen (`uvvm_sb_slv` cold +4 percent): no rule that reads only the looks can tell that run from the histogram's.
- **Decision: `pick` compiles a candidate only when its tree repays** (`Worker::repays`): the sum over the tree of each function's seen time over its
  kind's payback is at least the sum of the prices of the tree. The root's term is the payback rule itself; a clocked process keeps its own rules and its
  seen time pays only for its callees. A candidate that does not repay yet waits without moving `pick_at` (asked again at the next look; `YAVS_AUTO_TRACE`
  prints a `waits` line once). **A program the profile says ran before shares the cost among `profile::EARLY_RUNS` runs** (the cache makes the compile a link in
  the runs after, as the profile's own early compiles assume): without that the rule kept the big trees of the window generator (`push_variable_string`,
  `encode`) and of `uvvm_axistream_vvc` out of every warm run (warm +6 to +8 percent against the change before).
- **Decision: `Compute` is priced 12 ms + 510 us an IR instruction** (one and a half times what it measures; it was 4 ms + 900), speedup 2.4 unchanged.
