- **Decision: `Op::CallIeee` holds its argument registers.** `native` and the registers are `u16`s, the unused cells repeat the first register, `bit` is the `NativeRef::ty.is_some()` that `numeric_bit` natives test (nothing else of the type is used): no operand list, no `prog.natives` entry at run time. A call whose numbers do not fit (`pre::call_ieee`: a register or native id above 65534, more than 8 cells) stays an `Op::CallNative`. The `IsXSlice` fusion reads the operand register from the op.
- **Decision: a native may have a `FastFn`** (`ieee::lookup_fast`, `Runtime::fast` by native id): `fn(&mut Machine, &[u64]) -> Option<u64>` for the cases that report nothing and fail nowhere. `Op::CallIeee` calls it first and, on `Some`, stores the result and goes on: no frame pc, no `ieee_fallback`/`ieee_stop` test, no native lookup. On `None` it runs the native exactly as before (`ieee_after`, out of line, for the fallback to the VHDL body and the stop). The natives call their fast path first as well, so a callback of compiled code (`yavs_rt_native_light`) takes it too; `add`, `compare`, `resize`, the shifts, the gates and `not` lost their copies of the one-word code (`add_small` stays for the truncation warning of `to_unsigned`/`to_signed` values that do not fit, `to_integer` for its warning). Covered: `+`/`-`, comparisons, `to_integer`, `to_unsigned`/`to_signed`, `resize`, `sll`/`srl`/`sra`/`rol`/`ror` (one word), the gates, `not` of `unsigned` and `std_ulogic_vector`, the scalar `is_x`, `??`, `to_x01`, `to_x01z`, `to_ux01`, the reductions and `is_x` of vectors (their code reads the planes in place already; the fast path skips the call bookkeeping), and `to_x01`, `to_x01z`, `to_ux01`, `to_bitvector` of up to 64 elements, whose result block is computed from the operand's planes in one word.
- **Decision: `put_down`/`put_small` are inline, `temp_words` skips `Vec::resize` when the area is already 8-aligned and builds the address without `mk_addr`, `small_of` reads the planes without the copy through the stack (`block4`), and the element mask is `u64::MAX >> (64 - n)` (`low1`).** `put_down` as a call cost 7 push/pop pairs and a result through memory.
- **Decision: vectors of 65 to 1024 elements without a metavalue are word-wise** (`ieee_wide.rs`): `wide_of` reads the planes into a 16-word buffer (and refuses a metavalue, or an `L`/`H` for the operations that keep the elements), the operation runs on words (carries across them for `+`/`-`, a top-down compare, `trim` of the bits above the length) and `emit` writes the fat pair, the descriptor and the blocks straight into temporary memory. Taken: `+`, `-`, the six comparisons (two vectors, vector and integer, integer and vector), `to_integer` (the value must fit INTEGER; a leading sign or zero words are checked), `to_unsigned`/`to_signed` to 65 or more elements, `resize`, `sll`/`srl`, the six gates and `not` (vector and `numeric_std`); later also `rol`/`ror` of operands without `L`/`H` and `*` of a product of 65 to 1024 elements (#1108: vector by vector and the integer forms, the integer converted at the vector's length and fitting it; compiled code calls the native for them since a wide value does not fit the in-place arms). Not taken (the general path, unchanged): a metavalue in an operand, `sra`, vectors or products above 1024 elements, and every case that warns or fails. Rejected: a growable buffer for longer vectors (nothing in the 42 realbench tests is above 1024; the buffers are 128 bytes each and only wide calls zero them).
- **Not done: the slice copy before a native** (`Alloc`, `LCopy` of at most 64 elements into it, `CallIeee`; `IsXSlice` is the one fusion of this shape). Counted: 163 of the 701 `CallIeee` sites of `neorv32_dual_full` and 233 of 925 in `grlib_leon3mp` have an `LCopy` before them, but in the 5 M instruction window of `neorv32_single_min` `LCopy` + `AllocLCopy` + `Alloc` are 1.5 percent of the instructions and only part of them feed a native; none of the five target tests has any (one of 167 sites in `fletcher_bufferwriter_512`). A fused op would need the native's cells (three more registers) plus the operand's: 20 bytes of the 24 an `Op` has, one fusion per native shape. Left until a profile asks for it.
- **The compiled tier** (`yavs-llvm`) computes the one-word cases of `+`, `-`, comparisons, `to_integer`, `resize`, shifts and gates inline (`ieee_fast` in `lower.rs`) and calls `yavs_rt_native_light` for the rest; that callback now reaches the fast paths above, so the wide cases and the scalar conversions the tier does not inline are cheaper there too. `poc_arith_addw` in `--tier=auto` is unchanged (its operators are inline), `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` in auto is 1.4 percent lower.
- **Tests:** `native_wide_matches_bodies` (`crates/yavs/tests/ieee_native.rs`): 14 lengths at and around the word boundaries up to 513, mixed lengths, `L`/`H` and metavalues in some operands, all-zero, all-one and one-hot vectors, integer operands of both signs, resizes, shifts by 0 to beyond the length, `to_integer` of wide vectors; native and body outputs must be equal. A mutation (the initial carry of the subtraction flipped) fails it at line 28. The existing differential tests (`native_matches_bodies_*`, numeric_bit, integer64) pass natively and with `YAVS_IEEE_TIER=llvm`.
- **Measured** (`tools/stepcount --ops`, 5 M instructions after 3000 `run_batch` entries, `--tier=interp --threads 1`, bench builds of main `f877e389` and of this change; instructions an op, before to after):

  | op | window | before | after |
  |---|---|---:|---:|
  | `CallIeee` | `poc_arith_addw` | 323.4 | 219.5 |
  | `CallIeee` | `vai_window_gen_interlock` | 233.0 | 162.8 |
  | `CallIeee` | `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` | 398.4 | 331.5 |

  | `CallIeee` | `neorv32_single_min` | 300.3 | 230.3 |
  | `CallIeee` | `grlib_leon3mp` | 352.8 | 294.7 |

  `poc_arith_addw` by function: the arm 158 to 94 instructions, `add` 94 to 96 (with `put_down` inlined into it; was 94 + 44), `to_integer` 24 to 16. (`poc_stat_histogram` has too few `run_batch` entries for a window to open.) Whole runs, `perf stat instructions:u` of warm worlds (two untimed runs), `--threads 1`, G:

  | test | tier | before | after |
  |---|---|---:|---:|
  | `poc_arith_addw` | interp | 136.42 | 130.76 |
  | `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` | interp | 49.76 | 48.60 |
  | `sc5_fifo_repack` | interp | 34.27 | 34.20 |
  | `poc_stat_histogram` | interp | 22.58 | 22.47 |

  | `grlib_leon3mp` | interp | 389.98 | 389.29 |
  | `poc_arith_addw` | auto, main thread | 78.93 | 78.88 |
  | `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` | auto, main thread | 47.17 | 46.52 |

  (The whole-run counts of `auto` without `--no-inherit` include the compile threads and move by 2 to 5 percent between identical runs.)

  `realbench --compare` over the 41 tests that pass on both sides (`--phases run --tiers interp,auto`, core 8, base `12e07dce`, bench builds): geometric mean of instructions 1.00 (interp) and 1.00 (auto); wall 0.99 (interp) and 1.02 (auto; the categories with a 1.20 are tests of 0.02 to 0.05 s, instructions equal); `poc_arith_addw` interp wall 8.24 to 7.56 s, `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` 4.06 to 4.03 s, `neorv32_single_min` 2.51 to 2.47 s. `grlib_leon3mp` is reported failed by the tool for both binaries (its pass text sits beyond the 200 characters the tool keeps).

## Signal I/O of large processes: whole values by groups made at bind time, gathers and scatters through the signal callback (yavs-interp `gather.rs`, yavs-llvm `lower.rs`, #790, 2026-10-27)

Task (orchestrator): the large straight-line processes that are only level when compiled (GRLIB `iu:comb`, fletcher `ctrl_comb_proc`) spend their
time in the runtime functions both tiers share (`sig_gather`, `scatter_leaves`, `drive_run`, `lcopy`). Measured first (bench builds, GRLIB to
300 us, `tools/stepcount --ops`, a counting probe build): `SigGather` 2.17 M calls, 19 leaves and 3.7 kernel signals each; `SigScatter` 2.43 M
calls, 18 leaves and 5.9 kernel assignments each (the runs of #686 already merge the leaves of a pack: one assignment per run of a driver);
39 percent of the scatters are of values with arrays of records. Per call the instructions are lean (about 12 a leaf read, 22 a leaf driven
with its kernel share); the cycles were not: a quarter of `sig_gather` and up to 40 percent of `sig_scatter` sat on the reload of the plan taken
out of the machine and of the instruction's result, and the scatter of a value with arrays of records assigned every instance of a leaf on
its own (the instances lie mirrored in the kernel, last first, and the loop went first first, so no two joined a run).

- **Decision: the instances of a whole value are listed when the plan is bound** (`Bound::items`: leaf, value offset, kernel element, a logic
  leaf's instances last first; at most 4096 instances, else leaf by leaf as before), **in groups**: `reads`, the logic items of one plane word
  of one kernel signal, read from that word kept in registers (one signal lookup a group instead of one a leaf, the code of a scalar from the
  four plane bits); `runs`, the logic items next to each other in one kernel signal up to 64 elements, whose planes are built in registers and
  assigned once (the driver of every item checked equal at run time, else the old per-leaf path). A part of a value (`Part`) keeps the leaf loop;
  its logic instances are now taken last first too, so they join a run. Why at bind time: the layout of a whole value is fixed per instance
  (`InstSig::off`), so the grouping is paid once per machine and plan.
- **Decision: the plan is boxed in the machine's list and given back on both arms of the result**, and a descriptor in constant space found equal
  once is recognised by its address (`MPlan::at`): moving the 32-byte plan and the result through the stack were store-forwarding stalls.
- **Decision: compiled frame-mode code runs `SigGather` and `SigScatter` through `yavs_rt_signal`** (`TierHost::signal`, the interpreter's
  functions without the generic step), not `yavs_rt_step`; a native frame keeps its own way. No callback or `TierFrame` changed (heads-up on #481).
- **Measured** (bench builds, `perf stat` user instructions, warm worlds, claimed CCD1 core; cycles on a host at load 13 to 16 are within its
  noise and not quoted as a result): GRLIB to 300 us, `--tier=interp`, 117.10 G to 115.77 G instructions (-1.1 percent), whole run 389.6 G to 384.6 G (-1.3 percent), `--tier=auto` with `iu:comb` forced compiled 395.3 to 396.3 G against 389.8 to 391.7 G (-1.4 percent); a synthetic process
  that reads and drives a 40-leaf record with an array of four records every clock: interpreter 14.74 G to 11.97 G (-19 percent, cycles
  -15 percent), `--tier=llvm` 14.25 G to 11.31 G (-21 percent, cycles -18 percent). `tools/realbench --compare`: see docs/STATUS.md.
- **Measured, not kept:** a grouping check against `InstSig::ty.len` (the leaf's own length, not its kernel signal's) left every pack leaf
  ungrouped (+2.8 percent instructions); the items path for flat values with the leaf data behind an index
  (+0.5 percent against the zip over the leaves; the items now carry length, size, kind and bias).
- **Found, filed:** the kernel's vector entry of a direct driver reloads its planes with 16-byte moves after storing them a word at a time as the
  argument of `direct_same_planes` (#793): 25 to 37 percent of `scatter_leaves` cycles in the synthetic design, not visible in GRLIB.
- **Not done:** per-leaf code generated for gathers and scatters of a static layout (constant leaf offsets in the compiled code): after the groups
  the gather of a pack is one signal lookup, four loads and a few shifts a leaf; what is left of a compiled `iu:comb` is its interpreted
  callees and the kernel's per-drive work (`DriveRun` 257 instructions a scalar drive, `LSetDrive` 244, mostly `skip_code_now` and
  `assign_code_fast`), which are #720 and #730. A gather into its destination (`Alloc t; SigGather t; Copy v <- t`) would save one copy of
  about 400 bytes a gather (885 MB of gathers in the GRLIB window), under half a percent.
- **The reference simulator (rule 22):** a waveform over a range of one signal is one call that walks the signal's parts in order, with the
  values in the signal's own layout. The idea taken: one assignment per contiguous range of a driver, values handed over in the kernel's layout
  (plane words) without staging. Ours groups at bind time and keeps the bit-planes. Nothing was copied.

## Large value copies: records built in their own object, no zero fill before a copy (yavs-ir `opt.rs`, yavs-interp `exec.rs`, #792, 2026-10-27)

Task (#792, from the calls round 3 finding of #730): `uvvm_axistream_vvc` spent 15 percent of its cycles in libc `memmove` and 3 percent in
`memset`, in copies of 512 bytes and more called from `run_ops` arms. A counting `memcpy`/`memmove`/`memset` interposer with frame-pointer
call chains (size class in the key) and a throwaway per-op print of the IR site (function, pc, bytes; not kept) found the owners. It is not log
strings (`Cat` is 50 MB of 23 GB): it is **one 689 KB record**, UVVM's `t_vvc_cmd_record` (a 16 KB `data_array`, four word arrays, two
300-character strings), moving through the command path 12 to 15 times per command (22 000 whole-record passes in the run, 13 GB of the 23 GB of
`memcpy`/`memmove`/`memset` traffic; the rest is the frame fill of calls, 3.7 GB, and `lcopy_wide`, 2.6 GB):

| site (UVVM) | ops | passes | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `await_cmd_from_sequencer` (4 VVCs) | `Copy` shared to out parameter | 4764 | required assignment |
| `set_general_target...`, `reset_vvc_transaction_info`, `fetch_command...`, `send_command_to_vvc`, `fetch` (heap to variable) | `Copy` | 1100 to 1200 each | required assignments |
| `set_global_vvc_transaction_info` | five `LCopy` of 64K to 512K elements | 2143 | required assignments |
| `fetch`: `variable v : t_generic_element` | `Alloc` (memset), 5 `LFill` of 'U', `NewFrame` (memset + copy) | 1181 | **removed** (4 of 5 passes) |
| `send_command_to_vvc`: `variable v : t_vvc_cmd_record` | `Alloc`, `LFill`s, `New` (copy) | 1191 | **removed** |
| queue `add`: `new t_element'(...)` | `Alloc`, `Copy`, `NewFill` (copy) | 1181 | **removed** (2 of 3 passes) |

- **Decision: a large initialised record variable or heap node is created in its own object, then filled** (`Opt::defaults_first`, last in
  `Opt::run`, after the constants are merged). The pattern is `Alloc t` (constant size of 4 KiB or more), stores, fills and copies into `t`,
  then `NewFrame`/`New`/`NewFill` copying `t` into the variable's memory. The `Alloc` becomes a `NewFrame` (frame object) or a `NewFill` and
  `Deref` (heap object) of the same size filled from one zero byte, the later `New*` goes (a `Move` for `NewFrame`), and everything that wrote
  `t` writes the object. Conditions: both instructions in code that runs once per activation (no cycle), `t` defined once, and every use of
  `t` or of an address derived from it (`Index`, `Field`) a `Load`, `Store` (as the address), `Copy`, `LFill` or `LSet` through it, in a
  block not reachable from the copy and before it (a `TempRoot` of `t` is dropped for a heap object, whose handle is a live register). The
  existing instructions only: the compiled tiers need no change. The one zero byte is a 1-byte `Alloc` inserted before; the size register is the
  `Alloc`'s own (the `New`'s may be defined later). Run after `merge_consts`: the instructions it inserts name final registers.
- **Decision: `LFill` of the code 0 into that fresh zero object is dropped** (`zero_fills_after`) when it overwrites nothing written since: the
  default of a `std_ulogic` array is 'U' (code 0, all planes zero). A straight chain of blocks (each the only successor of the one before),
  constant offsets and lengths (constants set in the stretch and those the optimiser has not inserted yet count); anything else ends the scan.
- **Decision: `NewFrame` appends its copy** (`Machine::temp_append_copy`) instead of `temp_alloc` (zero fill) followed by the copy; the case that
  remains is a `NewFrame` the pass above cannot take. **Zero fills of up to 32 bytes in `temp_alloc` are one fixed-size store** (13 M libc
  `memset` calls of 25 to 100 bytes in this testbench).
- **Not done, and why:** the required assignments above (11 of the remaining 17 GB) need copy-on-write or sparse values in the flat memory
  model: a design change, left. Compare-before-copy was measured (4 KB chunks, two 689 KB buffers differing in a few bytes, 8 buffers in
  rotation): 30 us against 26 us for the plain copy, so no. The frame fill of a call (`fill_below`, 650 bytes, 5.7 M calls, 3.7 GB) is the
  #730 finding (5 ns a call). Ceiling of this task: about 5 of 23 GB; the traffic is 17.7 GB after it (interposer), cycles -8 percent.
- **Tests:** `crates/yavs/tests/value_move.rs`: `large_variables_built_in_place` (defaults, assignments and later changes of a frame variable,
  a variable of a waiting procedure and a queue node stay separate objects, interpreter and compiled tier), `large_variables_are_made_before_they_are_filled`
  and `fills_of_zero_over_a_fresh_object_are_dropped` (the optimised IR: `fill: 1`, no `NewFill` copying a temporary, no `LFill`). No work-counter
  design: the counters count ops and wakes, not bytes, and the IR tests pin the shape.
- **Measured** (bench builds of main `ac8d4e88` and of this change, interleaved A/B on one timing core, 7 runs after a warm-up, median ratio B/A
  of `cycles:u` and `instructions:u`): `uvvm_axistream_vvc` interp 0.920 cycles (0.956 instructions), auto 0.917 (0.965); `uvvm_sb_slv` 0.972 / 0.992;
  `uvvm_util_rand` 0.992 / 1.009; `osvvm_axis_random` 0.973 / 1.000; `osvvm_axi4_random` 0.960 / 0.955. Instructions fall 1 to 4 percent
  everywhere (the small zero fills).
- **Copy-on-write of large objects: measured, not built (#798, 2026-10-27).** Bench build of `743536eb`, timing core, a counting
  `memcpy`/`memmove`/`memset` interposer with a time stamp counter around each call and around the whole process (not kept):
  - `uvvm_axistream_vvc`: copies of 256 KB or more are 9.9 percent of the whole process (interp) and 10.8 percent (auto), 10.2 GB in
    19 300 calls. About 13 350 are whole-record passes of the 689 KB command record (sizes 688 135 to 688 918 bytes), about 8 100 are
    256 KB field copies (`set_global_vvc_transaction_info` assigns five array fields of an element of a shared array: a part of an
    object, which object-level sharing never reaches). One pass costs about 13 us (L3 bandwidth: source plus target are 1.4 MB, more
    than the L2), so a faster copy routine is no lever either.
  - Per command and VVC, the whole-record passes that sharing would turn into a reference count: `await_cmd_from_sequencer` in the
    three VVCs the command is not for (they copy `shared_vvc_cmd` and never write their copy), the queue insert, the fetch. Those that
    stay (a write after the share clones the whole object): the sequencer's field writes into `shared_vvc_cmd`, the executor's writes
    into its copy. Net ceiling about 6 to 7 percent of this one test (interp and auto).
  - The other seven tests of the `protected` category (`osvvm_axis_random`, `osvvm_axi4_random`, `uvvm_sb_slv`, `uvvm_util_rand`,
    `uvvm_methods_log`, `uvvm_func_cov`, `hdlm_axis_bfm`): copies of 256 KB or more are 0.05 to 1.2 percent. The command record is
    large only for VIPs with a large data maximum (AXI-Stream 16 K bytes; Avalon-ST, GMII and RGMII smaller); the other VIPs have
    records of a few KB. Expected realbench geometric mean: about 0.2 percent.
  - sim1 assigns a record with a plain copy too (no sharing), and its layout uses a byte per `std_logic` against our half byte (bit
    planes), so its record is twice as large. `uvvm_axistream_vvc` under `--tier=auto` is 0.72 of sim1 (wall, instructions 1.00).
  - What it would take: large variables (process, subprogram, shared) and large heap nodes in objects of their own, addressed through a
    pointer slot (lowering and elaboration); heap slots holding shared storage with the clone in `Heap::data_mut`; a heap epoch bump at
    every share (compiled code keeps writable host pointers to heap objects between activations, an ABI point for both compiled
    backends); constants as a share source; state images and the collector over shared storage; the optimiser's copy patterns.
  - **Decision: not built.** A gain of about 6 percent on one test, none elsewhere, no gap to sim1, against a change of the memory
    model across lowering, interpreter, both compiled backends, the collector and state images. Revisit if a design whose run is
    dominated by whole-object copies of large values shows up (the interposer census above is the first check).
  `realbench --compare` (42 tests, `--phases run --tiers interp,auto`, 3 runs, cores 13 and 14, host load 37 from an unrelated job, base `ac8d4e88`): geometric
  mean of instructions 0.99 interp and 0.99 auto, wall 1.00 and 1.00 (single small tests moved by 40 to 60 percent on noise at equal instructions, e.g.
  `neorv32_dual_full`); the protected category (the verification-library testbenches) wall 0.95 / 0.96, `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 0.92 / 0.86 (instructions 0.96).
  Interposer census of `uvvm_axistream_vvc` (interp): `memcpy` 16.4 to 14.9 GB, `memmove` 1.2 to 0.17 GB, `memset` 5.3 to 2.3 GB, `memset` calls 26.9 M to 12.1 M.

## Kernel round 26: the slot of the process ahead, a batch of element drives as one vector entry (yavs-kernel, #795, #676, 2026-10-27)

Task (orchestrator): the small clocked RTL designs still above sim1 under `--tier=auto` (head-to-head 7, full total, warm: `rtl_lfsr` 1.35,
`lfsr64` 1.10, `rtl_ff` 1.02) and the kernel-bound `sc5_timestamp` and `hdlm_lfsr`. Bench builds with `llvm`, `--threads 1`; `tools/stepcount`
windows, `perf record`, IBS op sampling (`ibs_op`, data source per load) and `perf stat` of warm runs on claimed cores of the second CCD.

- **Where the time is** (instructions an activation, compiled, one clock period, main at 3a29884f): `rtl_lfsr` about 1390, of which the kernel
  about 330 (`run_batch` 148, `finish_direct` 118, `commit_planes_run` 60), the host layers between the kernel and compiled code about 490
  (`InterpProcess::run`, `run_cached`, `view_again`, #766) and compiled code about 360; `rtl_ff` about 1100 with the kernel about 210. The
  kernel lines are 2 to 28 instructions each. The largest single item of the warm runs is outside the kernel: the interpreted start before the
  compiled process is used (`rtl_lfsr` about 51 ms of 303, `lfsr64` 20 to 37 ms of 148, #728). A falling clock edge with nothing to resume
  is about 1240 kernel instructions (`cycle` 440, the timed update and `finish_quick` 330, `rearm` 115, `last_delta` and `next_queued` 140).
- **Decision: the batch loop prefetches the next process's slot.** The serial arm of `run_batch` (batches of 128 or more processes, three
  steps ahead, as round "Prefetch of the next process in a batch") also asks for every cache line of the process's `Slot` (`SLOT_LINES`: 368
  bytes rounded up plus one line, a slot need not start on a line). IBS sampling of `rtl_ff` put 8 of its about 25 L2 misses an activation on
  `ProcState` fields (`resumption`, `has_entries`, the `out` and `sens` vectors' headers, `wait_same`). Cycles, warm `--tier=auto`: on a
  host whose other cores were busy (load 25 to 38) `rtl_ff` medians -15 to -25 percent (L2 misses 219 M to 136 M), on a quieter host (load
  13) -1 to -2 percent with L2 misses 87 M against 86 M: the slots stay in the cache there. Instructions +0.6 percent (the hints).
  `rtl_lfsr`, `lfsr64`, `rtl_fan`, `rtl_chain`, `rtl_bus`, `lfsr64_xor` level. Also prefetching the waveform buffer, the `out` and `outv`
  buffers, `sens_prev` and the `ProcMeta` line one or two steps ahead was measured: no gain over the slot alone.
- **Decision: a batch of element drives that covers a run is one vector entry.** `Ctx::assign_codes_now` (the kept scalar drives of
  compiled code, #676) of 4 or more elements that together cover one run of at most 64 elements of the driver's range, in any order, an
  element twice taking the later code (`codes_run`), is one `assign_planes_fast` of the run: one skip test, one `OutV`, one commit and one
  pending word, instead of one `Out`, one `commit_codes` step and one pending bit per element. Anything else (a gap, a code above 8, an
  element outside the driver) keeps the old loop. Leaving the per-element skip out is safe as in round 24: an entry of an unchanged value
  commits and finishes with no event. Kernel round 19 had tried the same promotion per call in the interpreter path and at commit time
  (`hdlm_lfsr` -0.9 percent, `sc5_fifo_repack` +1.9); here the whole batch is in hand, so nothing is extended or scanned.
  `hdlm_lfsr` (`--tier=auto`): one-element commits 16.1 M to 1.1 M, instructions 21.8 G to 20.5 G, cycles -9 to -13 percent, realbench
  run wall 1.42 to 1.34 s. Test: `direct_paths::a_batched_run_of_elements_is_one_entry_with_the_last_codes`.
- **Measured** (`tools/realbench --compare`, 42 tests, run phase, interp and auto, 3 runs, core 12, main ac8d4e88 against both changes):
  wall geometric mean 0.98 / 1.00, instructions 1.00 / 1.00, CPU 0.99 / 1.00, summed auto wall 0.98; `sc5_fifo_repack` auto instructions
  1.06 in that run is the compile outcome (its direct commit counters are identical, three more runs 21.2 to 21.6 G against 21.7 to 22.9 G).
  Head-to-head designs against sim1 (full total, warm / cold, load 13 to 20): `rtl_lfsr` 262 ms, `lfsr64` 131 ms, `rtl_ff` 545 ms warm,
  level with main; the ratios move with sim1 only. Edge forms: the four `rtl_ff` spellings keep identical counters. Difftest 542/542 at 1 and
  4 threads for interp, auto, llvm and auto with `--tier-heat=1,0,0`.
- **Not done:** the falling-edge path (spread over 30 items of 5 to 40 instructions), the codes refresh of 16-bit registers (round 24,
  a recorded decision), #793 (the store-forwarding stall of the vector entry: not among the hot instructions of `yavs_rt_drive` in
  `rtl_lfsr` or in a synthetic design of four 8-bit registers per process with the skip test active).
- **The reference simulator (rule 22):** its cycle was read (one pass over the time-ordered event heap, deferred queues of drivers and
  processes, the driving and effective values in level order); neither change takes an idea from it. Nothing was copied.

## Kernel round 27: adjacent vector entries of a direct driver join (yavs-kernel, #676, #793, 2026-10-28)

Task (orchestrator): the kernel side of element drives and their commit (`sc5_fifo_repack` 1.12 warm / 1.97 cold against sim1, process
`p_col` with 21.3 M element drives) and the store-forwarding stall of #793. Bench builds with `llvm`, warm worlds captured from
`tools/realbench`, a separate world per binary, A and B interleaved on one claimed core of the second CCD, `perf stat` user counts.

- **Where the time is** (`sc5_fifo_repack`, `--tier=auto`): per clock and lane `p_col` drives one byte part of `sort_data(col + 1)` and one
  bit of `sort_valid(col + 1)`. The drive side is about 25 percent of the cycles (about 70 cycles an element), the commit side about 10 (about
  28 an element), the host layers around the compiled processes about 16, interpreted processes about 13; IPC 3.5. Each byte part was an
  `OutV` of its own, and each scalar a flush of compiled code's kept drives (`Batch`) of one element: the byte drive between two scalar
  drives flushes the batch.
- **Decision: a vector entry of a direct driver that continues the run's last `OutV` of the same driver, up or down, within 64 elements,
  joins it** (`Ctx::extend_outv`, from `assign_planes_fast` and from the one-element-after-a-vector branch of `assign_code_fast`). It is
  tried only when the driver has vector entries in the run (the skip test of a first entry is unchanged), and only the list's last entry
  is looked at: nothing of the driver can follow that entry, so the order of entries holds. Kernel round 19 had promoted one-element
  entries to vectors, which cost `sc5_fifo_repack` instructions; this joins vectors to vectors and leaves one-element entries alone.
  `sc5_fifo_repack` (`--tier-heat=1,0,0`, compile outcome fixed): instructions 20.55 G to 19.96 G (-2.9 percent), cycles -2 to -3 percent;
  the synthetic record-scatter process (a record of an array of eight records driven every clock) -1.8 percent instructions, cycles
  level; `hdlm_lfsr` level (heat and interpreter). `realbench --compare` 42 tests, run phase, interp and auto: instruction geometric
  mean 1.00 / 1.00, CPU 0.98 / 0.97, wall of tests of 1 s or more 1.01 / 1.01 (noise, load 13). Counters: `drive_vec` 175 to 135 vector
  commits, `mixed_entries` 1270 to 903. Test: `direct_paths::adjacent_parts_join_one_vector_entry`.
- **Measured, not kept (#793):** the stall is real in compiled code too (45 percent of the `yavs_rt_drive` samples of `sc5_fifo_repack`,
  26 percent of `scatter_leaves` in the record design). `direct_same_planes` `#[inline(always)]` removes the reload (the `OutV` planes are
  then written from registers) and 2 percent of the instructions of the record design, but cycles rose 2 to 3 percent there (interpreter and
  auto) and about 2 percent on `sc5_fifo_repack`: the samples moved to the next consumers. The cycles on that load are the wait for the
  planes' inputs, not a forwarding penalty that goes away with the load.
- **Measured, not kept:** the second pass of `codes_run` last element first, ORing planes with no clearing: `hdlm_lfsr` +1.8 percent
  instructions (a branch per element).
- **Not done, recorded:** not flushing compiled code's kept scalar drives at a vector `Drive` of another driver. The IR driver index is a
  longest-static-prefix slot; elaboration merges the slots of one net into one kernel driver and collapsed ports can share a net, so no
  static proof of "another driver" exists: it needs a runtime compare or a per-slot kernel-driver flag in the frame (#766). A staging
  buffer per direct driver in place of the entry lists (the reference simulator writes the value into the driver and queues one deferred
  update per driver) is #802, a decision. `grlib_leon3mp`'s per-scalar-drive cost (`DriveRun`, `LSetDrive` into `skip_code_now` and
  `assign_code_fast`, kernel round 25) is not touched by this round.
- **The reference simulator (rule 22):** its fast driver path was read (zero-delay drive of a sole-source driver writes the value into the
  driver's waveform and queues one deferred update per driver, or per signal for a signal of such drivers); the join of adjacent entries is
  not from it; the staging idea of #802 is. Nothing was copied.

## Kernel round 28, not landed: a staging buffer per direct driver (yavs-kernel, #802, 2026-10-28)

Task (maintainer decision on #802: prototype and measure; land only if `sc5_fifo_repack`, `hdlm_lfsr` and `grlib_leon3mp` gain
clearly). Bench builds (`llvm,clift`), warm worlds from `tools/realbench --prepare`, a world per binary, A and B interleaved on
one claimed core of the second CCD, `perf stat` user counts; host load 13 to 43, so instructions are the firmer number.

- **The prototype.** `ProcState::out` and `outv` (the direct entry lists, their order rule, `has_entries` scans, the marks of
  logic drivers, `extend_outv`, `codes_run`, the per-driver skip-test state `same` and `trim_run` of those lists) gave way to
  staged plane words: every direct driver owns one word (mask plus four planes) per plane word of the signal its range touches,
  in its process's state (`DriverInfo::stage` is the index of its first), and the process lists the words it wrote in the run.
  A drive blends its planes into the word (the last write wins by construction; a batch of element drives is gathered per
  word in registers first); the commit walks the listed words once, a word of one element through `commit_code` (so
  `pend_one` stays), others through a new `commit_word` (one masked blend, pending bits by the same mask, the skip test as one
  compare of the masked word with `cur` and the driving value). A general assignment moves the driver's words into the
  waveform as one transaction per run of the mask. Byte drivers (`OutB`) were left alone. Checked on the prototype: the
  kernel tests (with the twin test below) and the three worlds below run to their pass; not run on it: the workspace tests,
  the work-counter bounds, the llvm and clift tests, difftest and `realbench --compare`.
- **Measured** (A main, B the prototype; the `grlib_leon3mp` auto row is an earlier build of B that copied the staged words
  into a batch list after each run, the other rows the final one that commits them from the process's state; one A run of
  `grlib_leon3mp` auto at 385.6 G is a different compile outcome and left out). The issue estimated 10 to 15 percent of
  `sc5_fifo_repack`; about 1 to 3 percent is what it gives:

  | test | tier | instructions A | B | cycles A | B |
  |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | `sc5_fifo_repack` | auto, `--tier-heat=1,0,0` | 18.45 G | 18.28 G (-0.9%) | 6.73 G | 6.51 G (-3%) |
  | `sc5_fifo_repack` | interp | 32.84 G | 32.53 G (-0.9%) | 9.92 G | 9.84 G (-1%) |
  | `hdlm_lfsr` | auto, `--tier-heat=1,0,0` | 22.81 G | 23.01 G (+0.9%) | 9.21 G | 9.21 G |
  | `hdlm_lfsr` | interp | 59.89 G | 58.97 G (-1.5%) | 16.78 G | 16.09 G (-4%) |
  | `grlib_leon3mp` | auto | 372.1 to 372.8 G | 382.3 to 382.6 G (+2.6%) | noise | noise |
  | `grlib_leon3mp` | interp | 376.2 to 387.9 G | 397.7 to 398.6 G (+3 to +6%) | 185.6 G | 194 to 196 G (+5%) |

- **Decision: not landed** (the bar was a clear gain on all three). `grlib_leon3mp` loses because most of its direct drives
  hold the value the signal has (kernel round 25: 96 percent of its wide words): the assign-time skip test answered those
  without an entry, while staging writes every drive and asks at commit, which costs more. `sc5_fifo_repack` gains a little:
  its drive side is dominated by the layers around the kernel call, not by the entry lists (profile of B: `yavs_rt_drive` 6.3
  percent, `Ctx::assign_codes_now` 4.8, `direct_drive_bits` 4.4, the commit 4.4, `finish_direct` 4.0), and each scalar drive
  is still one kernel call of one element because compiled code flushes its kept scalar drives at every vector drive.
- **What it would take** (expectations, not measured): the assign-time skip for a drive whose word is not staged yet (round
  24's gated test) should bring `grlib_leon3mp` back to about level, which still leaves no clear gain; keeping compiled code's
  scalar drives across a vector drive of another kernel driver (a per-slot kernel-driver flag in the frame, #766), so that a
  run of element drives reaches the kernel as one call, is the larger lever for `sc5_fifo_repack` and does not need the
  staging buffer.
- **Kept:** `direct_paths::direct_drives_match_the_general_path`, a twin test of a 140-element direct driver across plane words
  (single elements of any code, batches with holes and repeats, vectors across a word boundary, wide vectors, delayed
  assignments before and after zero-delay ones of the run) against the same process on an identity-resolved signal (the
  general paths), reporting `'driving_value`, value, `'event`, `'last_value`, `'last_event` and `'active`.
- **The reference simulator (rule 22):** its fast driver path writes a zero-delay value of a sole-source driver into the
  driver's one pending slot and queues one deferred update per driver (or per signal) per delta. The prototype took that idea
  (one staged value per driver, one commit per word); it differs in keeping the staged words in the process's state, so
  parallel runs write only their own state, and in committing per plane word of the signal. Nothing was copied.

## llvm: a heap change drops only the objects it changed; interpreter calls keep the machine's objects; native code published past never-run callees (yavs-llvm `rt.rs`, `auto.rs`, yavs-interp `heap.rs`, `exec.rs`, #520, #797, 2026-10-27)

- **Problem.** In `vai_window_gen_interlock` under `--tier=auto` the compiled test-runner library code (queue, string and integer-vector
  pointers on the shared heap) ran 3.75 million `TierHost::object` callbacks a run (about 4 percent of the cycles at a low instruction
  count: cache misses in the slot lookup). Two causes: every deallocation anywhere moved the heap epoch and so the heap tag of `Mem`,
  dropping every heap object found before (the library frees messages and strings all the time); and a call from the interpreter
  (`Tier::call`, `call_on`) of another machine than the last one began without a record, so it issued new machine and heap tags. A third
  cause hid the compiled code itself: native-frame code waited for its whole transitive native set to be compiled (#797).
- **Decision: each heap logs the slot of its last `HEAP_LOG` (16) epoch changes** (`Heap::log`, written by `release` and `edit`), the view
  carries both epochs and both logs (`TierFrame::heap_epoch` is now the process heap's alone, `shared_epoch`, `heap_log`), and `Mem`
  drops only the table entries of the logged slots when it is at most 16 changes behind (`Mem::drop_changed`, from `forget` and `begin`);
  further behind it takes a new heap tag as before. The process record keeps both epochs (`TierState` words: identity, process heap epoch,
  heap tag and machine tag in one word (tags are below 2^31), shared heap epoch; still four words, the fifth cache line of the machine is full).
  Why: an object's host bytes move or go only at its own deallocation or edit (objects never move otherwise), so the other entries stay true.
- **Decision: `call_on` begins with the calling machine's record** (`TierHost::tier_state`, kept again with `set_tier_state` after the call,
  `TierState::at` left alone): the record names the machine's tags and epochs whoever ran in between.
- **Decision (#797): `Worker::publish` asks `Worker::ready`**, a walk over the native callees that stops at a callee that is `left` or was
  never seen running. Such a callee is compiled by no one until it runs; then it is seen and compiled like any other function, and until then
  a call to it materialises the frames (counted: up to 18 000 materialisations a run in the queue loop and 76 000 to 79 000 in the window
  generator, 38 000 to 148 000 with a walk that stopped at `left` callees only, against 285 000 to 1.2 million steps out of compiled code
  a run of the queue loop in its slow mode).
- **Measured** (bench builds, warm worlds two runs old, claimed core of CCD1, interleaved): a test-runner queue loop (push, pop, set, get, 300 000
  times) 17.8 to 18.4 G user instructions to 16.2 to 16.6 G, `object` callbacks 6.5 million to 0.59 million; window generator warm, five rounds
  at load 2 to 10 after a reboot: 8.70 to 7.84 s median wall, 114.5 to 109.8 G instructions, 41.6 to 37.8 G cycles, `object` callbacks
  3.75 million to 1.30 million; cold level (12.5 against 12.6 s). `tools/realbench --compare` against ac8d4e88 (42 tests, core 8): wall
  geometric mean 1.00 warm / 0.99 cold, instructions 1.00 / 1.00; window generator 0.93 / 0.97 wall; `uvvm_sb_slv` 1.05 / 0.99 in that pass,
  1.00 / 0.96 in a rerun of seven runs (both binaries 10.35 G: run-to-run spread of `--tier=auto`, #673).
- **Not done (measured, left):** the 1.1 million steps of `random_frame` (the protected-method calls of the random package: `CheckMinMax`
  and `LocalRandInt` are frame-mode only because their error paths call the alert procedure, so each call is a step plus a compiled callee,
  about 0.3 percent of the run); `FToIRange` (560 000), `LFill` (390 000) and `LogicOp` (333 000) native steps of `Scale`, `get_range`,
  `decode` and `"and"` in native frames; the remaining 1.3 million `object` callbacks (first finds and table conflicts).
- **The reference simulator (rule 22):** its compiled code holds raw pointers into a memory space and a deallocation touches only the object
  freed. The idea taken: a deallocation invalidates that object alone. Ours keeps generational handles and the object table and drops one
  entry per logged change. Nothing was copied.
## Interpreter execution of large processes: jump threading in processes (yavs-ir `opt/cfg.rs`, `opt.rs`, #791, 2026-10-27)

Task (orchestrator, gap scan 2026-10-26 row 1): the large straight-line processes `--tier=auto` leaves interpreted (`iu:comb`,
`dctrl`, the SDRAM model's `state_register`, `ctrl_comb_proc`). Op census of a whole `grlib_leon3mp` run (`--tier=interp
--threads 1`, 2.73 G ops): the most frequent adjacent pair was `Const -> CondBr` (100.9 M, 3.7 percent of the ops), the false arm of a
short-circuit `and`/`or` storing a constant flag that the join block tests at once; 88 M of them in the two `state_register` codes
(`if (Burst_length_1 = '1' or Write_burst_mode = '1') then`). The clean-up that removes that shape (`cfg.rs` thread, #444) ran only on
subprograms that cannot suspend.

- **Decision: `cfg::run` also runs on a process, after the memo of instance-constant values** (which wants the blocks as lowered:
  run before it, `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` lost memoised values and its loop latches and took 0.7 percent more instructions with 2 percent
  fewer ops). Not with a debugger keeping variables or with coverage counters. Three rules for a process:
  - the block the process pauses at before its first run (`Func::body`) is never taken over or jumped past;
  - a block that reads or defines a register defined once by a constant or an address is not copied: no register of a process may be read
    across a suspension (the verifier's rule), so its copy would need definitions of its own, each an executed op where the frame's
    preloaded value costs none (tried: materialised constants cost a loop latch in `wide_vec`, +5 percent ops);
  - a loop test whose next block jumps back with an add or subtract is not copied, also before the clean-up made that block `[Bin, Br]`
    (a checked add, a move into the variable): the predecoder's `CmpBrStep` needs the three in order.
- **Decision: `dead_defs` bounds its work by the registers it tracks (multiply defined, droppable), not by all registers** (`nb * m`
  under 2^24 instead of `nb * n` under 2^22): `iu:comb`, `dctrl` and `state_register` have thousands of blocks and registers and were
  skipped, so the flags a decided branch leaves stayed as executed `Const`s.
- **Decision: a dead block of a copy (`drop_declarations`) jumps to the next block, not to itself.** A block that jumps to itself is a jump
  target, so the predecoder stopped its fusions there (a `WaveBuf` with its `LSet` and `Drive` behind a dead arm: `spec_record_var`
  -0.9 percent ops); the next block is the convention of `emit` and `kill_unreachable`, which the predecoder runs through.
- **Measured and dropped: a layout memo keyed by a heap descriptor's address and the object's write stamp** (52 M of the 68.5 M `FieldOf`
  of `grlib_leon3mp` read a descriptor in a heap object). Windows of 4 M instructions showed no hits and 7 to 20 more instructions an
  op: the objects are written between the reads.
- **Tool: `op-census` tables of ops by function and by position** (`crates/yavs-interp/AGENTS.md` section 5): they found the shapes above
  (`state_register` op 3617 `Const`, op 3618 `CondBr`) and showed that a census binary built in a target directory shared with another
  checkout ran stale `yavs-ir` code (cargo's fingerprints follow the other checkout's files): one target directory per checkout.
- **Measured** (bench builds of ac8d4e88 and of this change, `perf stat` user instructions and cycles of warm worlds, three runs each,
  interleaved on one claimed core of the second CCD, host load 20 to 28, so cycles are indicative only):

  | test | tier | instructions before | after | cycles before | after |
  |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | `grlib_leon3mp` | interp | 383.86 | 372.75 (-2.9%) | 245.7 | 237.7 |
  | `grlib_leon3mp` | auto | 382.32 | 371.56 (-2.8%) | 223.7 | 208.6 |
  | `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` | interp | 48.23 | 47.52 (-1.5%) | 22.66 | 22.48 |
  | `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` | auto | 45.26 | 46.17 | 24.81 | 24.34 |
  | `fletcher_bufferreader` | interp | 18.83 | 18.62 (-1.1%) | 9.53 | 9.38 |
  | `fletcher_bufferreader` | auto | 18.77 | 18.49 (-1.5%) | 9.46 | 9.36 |
  | `neorv32_single_min` | interp | 27.49 | 27.11 (-1.4%) | 14.59 | 14.12 |
  | `neorv32_single_min` | auto | 27.54 | 27.29 (-0.9%) | 14.74 | 14.53 |

  (`auto` counts move 2 to 5 percent with the background compilation; `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` auto was 46.10 before in a quieter
  pass.) Ops of the whole `grlib_leon3mp` run (`op-census`, interp, 1 thread): 2.727 G to 2.469 G (-9.5 percent); `CondBr` 155.4 M to
  48.7 M, `Const` 104.3 M to under 16.8 M (out of the top 40), `Br` 62.6 M to 46.1 M, `CmpBr` 153.2 M to 164.4 M (the copied tests); the pair `Const -> CondBr`
  100.8 M to none. `tools/realbench --compare` (42 tests, run phase, interp and auto, one claimed core, load about 22): wall
  geometric mean 0.99 (interp) and 0.98 (auto), summed wall 0.96 and 0.96, instructions 0.99 and 0.99; `grlib_leon3mp` wall 37.8 to
  34.2 s (interp) and 37.4 to 34.3 s (auto); no test above 1.05 in instructions (`neorv32_single_cache` interp wall 1.12 at 0.98
  instructions, a single noisy cell). Difftest 542/542 at 1 and 4 threads with interp, auto and llvm.
- **The reference simulator (rule 22):** its lowering evaluates both operands of `and`/`or` with a plain logical operation when the right
  operand has no side effects, and branches only otherwise, so it never keeps a flag for the join to test. Ours keeps lowering as it is
  and threads the branches in the optimiser, where the left operand's branch already exists; evaluating cheap right operands without a
  branch is the other option, not taken. Nothing was copied.
- **Left:** the per-op cost of `FieldOf`/`LayoutWord` on run-time record descriptors (150 to 250 instructions, 4 to 5 percent of
  `grlib_leon3mp`): the descriptors are in temporary memory or written heap objects, so a key needs the optimiser to prove them unchanged
  (or fold them, as the copies do for instance data); `AllocLCopy` followed only by `LGet` (a bit of a copied slice, 15 M in GRLIB's
  `ahb_slv_dec_cache`); the signal and drive ops of #790.
## llvm: compiled code found before it is generated (yavs-llvm `objcache.rs`, `lower.rs`, yavs-ir, yavs-elab, #785, maintainer 2026-10-27)

- **Decision (maintainer, 2026-10-27, on #785; supersedes "Key: the generated LLVM IR" of "Compiled code in the compilation cache" for
  `--tier=auto`):** a compiled-code cache hit is found by a key computed before generation, so a hit skips generation; a CI check mode
  generates anyway and fails when one pre-key maps to another module.
- **The pre-key** (`objcache::pre_key`): the build and cache format (every key), `yavs_ir::opt::fingerprint`, `jit::target_id` (triple,
  CPU, LLVM version, code model, code generator switches, pipeline), the program's identity, the process the function is or is a copy of,
  the function's IR as handed out (`Program::func`, serialised: its optimisation, and for a copy the data folded into it), the level
  (profile- and size-driven, as asked), `full` and the part. **Program identity** is new: `Program::identity`, the key of the stage-cache
  entry the program was read from or stored to (the lowering key: the same requests on the same analysis give the same program, ids and
  all; `StageCache::identity`, set by `Elaborated::lower`); a program not cached (coverage, captured sessions, constant pools too large,
  the first run of a closure) has none and generates as before. A run with a tuning switch that changes generated code
  (`objcache::GEN_SWITCHES`: `YAVS_LLVM_ABLATE`, `DUMP` (so dumps are made), `ELOOP_HELPER`, `KINDLOC`, `KINDS`, `NO_ELOOP`, `PCLOC`) has no pre-keys.
- **What generation decides is stored, not keyed:** the entry (kind `pre`) names the object key (the IR key as before), whether the
  native-frame code verified, and a copy's twin key, which names its symbols; a hit checks the JIT's twins first (two equal copies link
  one module), then links the object and looks its entry points up (`lower::linked`). Every compile and every IR-key hit writes the
  entry; an entry whose object is gone is a miss.
- **Inputs considered:** function ids are baked only into native-frame code (deoptimisation and step calls), and only functions that are
  not copies have it; a copy's id depends on the switch order and is not in the key (its frame-mode code does not contain it). Known
  facts, layouts, constants and the native set come from the program and the function. Copies differ by their folded IR, which is keyed.
  The eager `--tier=llvm` program module keeps the IR key (one module per run; no pre-key).
- **Check mode** (`YAVS_LLVM_PREKEY_CHECK=1`, set for the whole CI `llvm` job): a pre-key hit generates the module anyway and an entry that
  names another object, native flag or twin key is an internal error that aborts the run, naming the function and both objects.
  Exercised by `spec::a_warm_run_links_by_the_pre_key_and_the_check_agrees` (copies switched in another order at 1 and 4 threads) and
  the difftest candidate `yavs-auto-warm` (a second `--tier=auto` run of every test). A deliberately missing input (the level left out
  of the key) aborted the first warm run that recompiled at O2.
- **`HIT`** is 1 ms + 1 us an IR instruction (was 1 ms + 20 us): `YAVS_LLVM_TIMES` `prehit total` (GRLIB warm with the large
  copies forced, bench build): 0.1 to 0.7 ms for functions of up to 220 IR instructions, 0.3 to 1 us an IR instruction from 1 000 to
  20 000 (19 867 IR: 9.5 ms, of which reading the object 0.4 and the link 0.15, the rest the key and the look-ups; that function's compile
  is 839 ms and its IR-key hit was about 790). The first run after the program changed has no pre-keys yet and pays generation again; the
  price ignores that one run. A program without an identity (never has pre-keys) prices a hit at 1 ms + 20 us an IR
  instruction, as before (`HIT_GEN`).
- **Pre entries share the object store** and its limits (4096 entries, least recently used first): one more small entry per compiled
  function. ponytail: a store of their own if a large design's objects get pushed out.
- **Measured:** GRLIB warm with the large copies forced, compile thread: 35 IR-key hits took 5.26 s on main, 52 pre-key hits 0.07 s (the
  queue got further: 9 functions more compiled in that run). Check mode on the whole difftest corpus (`yavs-auto-warm`,
  `--tier-heat=1,0,0`, 4 threads): no difference (the one test that differs, `textio/file_append_2019`, appends to a file the first run
  wrote); GRLIB warm under check mode: 35 checked, none different. `tools/realbench --compare` with #679: `docs/STATUS.md`.
- **The reference simulator (rule 22):** its normal runs generate the design's code ahead of time per design unit, so it has no
  per-function look-up at run time to compare with; nothing was taken from it.

## `--tier=auto` run-to-run profile: seen time summed over the runs (yavs-llvm `profile.rs`, `auto.rs`, #679, maintainer 2026-10-27)

- **Decision (maintainer, 2026-10-27, on #679; replaces "seen, over `EARLY_RUNS` (4) runs" of "`--tier=auto` run-to-run profile"):** a process
  the profile lists (any admitted kind, `BigLoop` among them) is compiled early once the time the earlier runs saw it, summed, repays its
  price by the payback rule (`Worker::threshold`, a copy by its own kind), instead of one run's seen time times four. The loss list still
  drops losers. `EARLY_RUNS` stays only where a program that ran before shares the price of a tree among runs (`Worker::repays`).
- **How:** `profile::next` adds each run's seen time to a listed process's (`hot` entry, saturating; it used to keep the largest); the
  text format is 3 (a format-2 profile is no profile, and the build is in its key anyway). `load_profile` and `see` compare the sum with
  the threshold. The sum is of earlier runs only: the process compiles at its first look in the run after the sum crosses, so the run
  that compiled it early has it for the whole run and is judged fairly against the run before.
- **Measured** (bench builds, `vai_window_gen_interlock`, `YAVS_AUTO_TRACE`, eight consecutive runs of one fresh world, claimed CCD1 cores,
  other agents busy). On main (12e07dce) `walk_control`'s one run (about 0.4 s) times 4 passed its threshold, so it compiled early from run 2
  and both hot processes were kept (run 2 9.27 s simulation CPU against 11.84). With the sum it compiles early in run 5 (the sum crosses
  its threshold of about 1.7 s after four runs) and is kept (7.68 s against 8.25); `bus_process` compiles early from run 2 as before.
  Runs 2 to 4 are 0.1 to 0.5 s slower than main's, runs 5 to 8 equal (7.5 to 7.9 s both). Before main's latest interpreter changes the
  same sequence showed the other side: a joint early trial of both in run 2 was judged not better and lost both, and with the sum
  `bus_process` alone was tried first and kept. `walk_control` is under 5 percent of a run, so its early compile gains 2 to 7 percent of
  the run, near the 3 percent of the judgement.

## `--tier=auto`: a warm run compiles what the cache holds once its cache price repays (yavs-llvm `auto.rs`, #728, maintainer 2026-10-27)

- **Decision (maintainer, 2026-10-27, option (c) on #728):** the default `--tier=auto` prices a function whose object is in the compilation
  cache at the cache price, so a warm run compiles it as soon as it is seen; `--tier-heat` and an environment switch keep the fixed model
  price for the deterministic count tests. Extends "A function whose object is in the cache is priced as linking it" (2026-10-25), which
  priced the hit (`HIT`) but kept two fixed costs in front of it.
- **What changed:** (1) a cached function does not wait for `Heat::threshold` (the floor of 2 ms + 40 us an IR instruction every
  function is seen for), only for its payback rule at the cache price (`Worker::floor`, `need`: 3.6 ms seen for a clocked process of 200 IR
  instead of 10 to 15); (2) a candidate whose whole tree is in the cache is picked ahead of the budget (`Worker::pick`, `links`): its
  price there included opening the LLVM library (`LOAD_US`, 10 ms), which kept `rtl_lfsr`'s process refused until 35 ms of the run were
  seen. `--tier-heat` (budget 0) keeps both; `YAVS_AUTO_PRICE=model` makes no function count as cached (model price, floor and budget for
  every function, the same counts cold and warm). `Worker::cached` is worked out once per function (`in_cache`, reset when the run
  lists the function).
- **Measured** (bench builds, both with #785 and #679, warm worlds, 9 interleaved runs, one claimed CCD1 core, `perf stat` of the whole
  run): `rtl_lfsr` 0.909 instructions, 0.94 CPU, 0.93 wall (`_p1` linked at 28 ms of the run, was 57); `rtl_ff` 0.99 / 0.92 / 0.92;
  `lfsr64` 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.99 (its copy is compiled early by the run-to-run profile already, at 30 ms).

## Compiled clocked RTL processes, round 10: the view made inside the tier, the entry's copies and drops (yavs-interp, yavs-llvm, yavs-ir, #766, 2026-10-28)

Task (#766): the host layers between the kernel and compiled code, about 490 of the 1 390 instructions of a `rtl_lfsr` activation in kernel
round 26. Method as in rounds 8 and 9: bench builds with `llvm`, `tools/stepcount` windows of 2 048 (`rtl_lfsr`, `lfsr64`) or 4 096 (`rtl_ff`)
compiled activations (entries of `AutoTier::run_cached`, `--tier=auto --tier-heat=1,0,0`, `--threads 1`), cycles as the minimum of 7
interleaved warm runs on one claimed core of the second CCD. `perf record -e '{cycles,instructions}:u'` gave each layer the same share of
cycles as of instructions (`InterpProcess::run` 13.7 / 14.0 percent, `run_cached` 10.0 / 9.7, `view_again` 11.4 / 15.6): the layers are
instruction-bound, so this round removes instructions; the prefetch rounds had taken the misses.

- **Decision: `Tier::run_cached` takes the interpreter's own host, `&mut yavs_interp::Host`** (was `&mut dyn TierHost`; `Host` is `pub` with
  private fields), and `rt::enter`/`enter_on` are generic over `rt::View` (`dyn TierHost` and `Host`), so a process activation makes its view
  with `Host::view_root_again` inlined into the tier instead of the virtual `TierHost::view_again` (its call, six-register prologue and
  epilogue, and the reload of the host's fields). `Tier::run` and `Tier::call` keep `dyn TierHost`; the callbacks get `dyn TierHost` as
  before. `view_root` and `tier_cov` are `#[inline]` for that. A second code generator changes its `run_cached` parameter type and gets
  the saving by calling `enter` with the host (heads-up on #481). Why: about 18 instructions of every compiled activation, no state kept.
- **Decision: `run_direct` reads the root function through `Program::func_inline`** (the body of `Program::func`, `#[inline(always)]`;
  `func` itself is unchanged for its other callers), tests `Host::fault` in place instead of moving the 32-byte `Option<Fault>` out, and
  ends the host with `mem::forget` once the fault is known to be `None` and `up` is dropped (the drop of the `None` fault was a call of
  its drop glue). The view writes `TierFrame::flags` once, the stack bound of `enter_on` is the address of its `Env` (no `black_box`
  store and reload), and `Mem::keep_heap` compares the two epochs word by word (the array compare went through the stack).
- **Measured** (instructions an activation, stepcount, base 3d0e1f3d / round 10): `rtl_lfsr` 1 422.5 / 1 380.6, `lfsr64` 1 475.1 / 1 433.2,
  `rtl_ff` 1 116.5 / 1 074.5. By layer (`rtl_lfsr`; `lfsr64` and `rtl_ff` alike): `InterpProcess::run` with `run_direct` and `Program::func`
  203.9 / 181.9, `AutoTier::run_cached` with `enter_on` and `view_again` 311.8 / 291.8, `yavs_rt_wait_same` 21.9 / 21.9: the host layers
  538 / 496. Cycles, minimum of 7 warm runs, core 9: `--tier=auto` `rtl_ff` -2.6 percent, `lfsr64` -1.6, `rtl_lfsr` -0.9, `rtl_chain`
  -2.0 (interpreted, same instructions: noise); with `--tier-heat=1,0,0` `rtl_ff` -3.2, `rtl_lfsr` -1.9, `lfsr64` -1.4, `rtl_chain` +0.3.
- **Not done, and why.** What is left of the 496 is the work itself in steps of 3 to 15 instructions: the view's 35 fields (about 75), the
  object table's tags (`Mem::begin` and `save_tag`, about 55; a generator-proven "no object table" flag stays not now, decision of
  2026-10-26), the tier's policy bookkeeping in `run_direct` (sampling slot, `activated`, `execs`, about 30), the `Env` and the thread's
  `Mem` (about 35), the record's copy in and out (about 15). Every activation is another machine, so nothing of the view or the tags can be
  kept on the thread; a persistent per-process view stays ruled out (#634). Tried and dropped: putting `rt_run` back without its drop test
  (a nested `run_quick` in a callback may refill it: a leaked runtime for 3 instructions).
- **The reference simulator (rule 22):** its process entry calls the compiled closure with the process's state pointer and nothing between
  the scheduler and the code. The idea taken: the code that makes the activation's context is static code in the caller, not a virtual
  call back into the host. Ours keeps the per-activation view (#634). Nothing was copied.

## Compiled clocked RTL processes, round 11: lean activations (yavs-llvm, yavs-clift, #766, 2026-10-28)

Task (#766, maintainer 2026-10-28: the per-activation "no object table" flag, ruled "not now" on 2026-10-26, may be tried for compiled
processes that touch no heap or access objects; per-process persistent state stays ruled out, #634): skip the object table's set-up and
end for those processes. Method as in round 10: bench builds (`llvm`, and `clift`), `tools/stepcount` windows of 2 048 (`rtl_lfsr`,
`lfsr64`) or 4 096 (`rtl_ff`) entries of `AutoTier::run_cached` (`--tier=auto --tier-heat=1,0,0`, `--threads 1`).

- **Decision: a process is `lean` when `yavs_llvm::regs::no_table` passes**, an analysis of the IR shared by both code generators: no
  `Call`, `CallForeign`, `CallIndirect`, `CallProt`, `New`, `NewFill`, `Free`, `Deref`, `PkgAlloc`, no `Handle` register, no
  parameter, and every address register (`Ptr`) defined only by `AddrOf` of its frame, the instance data or a constant, `Alloc`,
  `NewFrame`, `LayoutOf`, or `Index`/`Field`/`Move`/`Select` of such registers (a flow-insensitive fixpoint), and defined before it is
  read. Any other definition of an address (a `Load`, a native's result) fails it, so a new instruction fails it until someone decides
  otherwise. Natives (`CallNative`) are allowed: they run on the interpreter's own memory. Why: the addresses such a process uses are
  found by the generated code or by `Mem::find` in the frame, the temporary area or the instance data; only constants without a module
  copy reach the table, under the runtime's tag, which stays checked.
- **Decision: a lean activation does not set or save the table's machine and heap tags** (`rt::enter` with `lean`, `enter_on::<_, true>`):
  `Mem::begin_lean` instead of `Mem::begin` (the runtime's constants tag is still renewed on a new runtime), `TierState::at` written
  instead of `save_tag`, and, since it calls nothing, no `set_nslots`, `ntab`, `stack_lo` or `ndeopt`. `begin_lean` forgets the table's
  owner (`cur_owner`): a `forget` on a cold path (a stepped instruction) may set this machine's heap epochs, which the next `begin`
  without a record must not take for the previous owner's. The flag is published with the code (`AutoTier`: the top bit of
  `Entry::nregs`; `LlvmTier`, `ClifTier`: a vector filled at compile time). The entry has two monomorphic copies and makes the view
  once before choosing between them (two inlined views made `view_root` a call). Why: the tags were about 70 of the instructions of
  every activation of a small clocked process; per-process state is not needed for it.
- **Decision: the check mode** (debug builds, and release builds with `--features table-check`) poisons the machine and heap tags of
  a lean activation with a tag never issued, so any inline lookup misses into the runtime, and `Mem::get`, `Mem::put_obj` and
  `yavs_rt_fast` panic on an object of those spaces (`check_lean`); the tags are put back at the end. `cb_lean` counts lean
  activations (`YAVS_COUNTERS`, debug). The difftest ran with it (below), and forcing every process lean made `lfsr64` abort at
  once, so the check sees a wrong flag.
- **Measured** (instructions an activation, stepcount, base e1e9dc1f / round 11; host layers as in round 10):

  | | `InterpProcess::run` + `run_direct` | `run_cached` + `enter_on` + view | `yavs_rt_wait_same` | host layers | whole activation |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | `rtl_lfsr`, LLVM build | 181.9 / 181.9 | 291.8 / 216.0 | 21.9 / 21.9 | 495.6 / 419.8 | 1 384.6 / 1 308.8 |
  | `rtl_lfsr`, Cranelift build | 181.9 / 181.9 | 291.8 / 216.0 | 21.9 / 21.9 | 495.6 / 419.8 | 1 465.3 / 1 389.5 |
  | `rtl_ff`, LLVM build | 182.0 / 182.0 | 291.9 / 216.0 | 22.0 / 22.0 | 495.9 / 420.0 | 1 196.5 / 1 120.5 |
  | `rtl_ff`, Cranelift build | 182.0 / 182.0 | 291.9 / 216.0 | 22.0 / 22.0 | 495.9 / 420.0 | 1 233.5 / 1 157.5 |
  | `lfsr64` (not lean), LLVM build | 184.9 / 184.9 | 291.9 / 295.9 | 22.0 / 22.0 | 498.8 / 502.8 | 1 442.6 / 1 446.6 |
  | `lfsr64` (not lean), Cranelift build | 184.9 / 184.9 | 291.9 / 295.9 | 22.0 / 22.0 | 498.8 / 502.8 | 1 986.2 / 1 990.2 |

  A process that is not lean pays 4 instructions (the flag's test and mask). Cycles, minimum of 7 interleaved runs of a private world
  per binary on one claimed core of the second CCD (host load about 20), base / round 11: warm `--tier=auto` `rtl_lfsr` -5.9 percent
  (LLVM build) and -5.8 (Cranelift build), `rtl_ff` -3.9 and -5.9, `lfsr64` +1.7 and -0.7 (not lean: noise), `rtl_chain` level;
  cold `rtl_ff` -3.2 and -9.4, `rtl_lfsr` +1.0 and -2.5. Against sim1 (median wall, same core): warm `rtl_lfsr` 1.33 to 1.26 (LLVM
  build), 1.45 to 1.43 (Cranelift build); `rtl_ff` 1.00 to 0.94 and 1.08 to 0.97; `lfsr64` 1.08 to 1.07 and 1.23 to 1.20; `rtl_chain`
  0.74 and 0.72 both. `tools/realbench --compare` (42 tests, run phase, 3 runs, cores 11 to 14): LLVM build wall geometric mean 1.02
  (interp) / 1.00 (auto), instructions 1.00 / 1.00; Cranelift build wall 1.03 / 0.99, instructions 1.00 / 1.00. The single-test flags
  (`uvvm_axistream_vvc` and `sc5_fifo_repack` auto instructions 1.08 to 1.13, `grlib_leon3mp` wall at equal instructions) were the
  policy's compile timing and load: 5 more runs gave 0.92 to 1.02. `hdlm_lfsr` and `neorv32_single_min` (LLVM build, 5 runs): instructions
  1.00 warm and cold.
- **Not lean, and why.** `lfsr64`'s processes keep `v : unsigned(15 downto 0)` in a heap object (`New`, `Deref` in the first block, the
  pointer loaded from frame slot 0 at every activation): they touch the heap, so they keep the tags (#851: such a variable could live
  in the frame). `hdlm_lfsr` and `neorv32_single_min` gained nothing in instructions (their busy processes call subprograms or use
  vector variables). Left on the entry: the view's fields (about 80), `Env` (13), the thread's `Mem` (16), `run_direct`'s copy of the
  record in and out (about 12: a lean activation only needs `at`, but the interpreter does not know the flag; passing it would change
  the `Tier` trait).
- **Measured, not kept: kept scalar drives across a vector `Drive` of another kernel driver** (suggested by kernel rounds 27 and
  28 for `sc5_fifo_repack`, whose copies of `p_col` hand one kept bit over before each byte drive). A vector `Drive` whose slot no
  kept site uses skipped the hand-over unless a kept entry was of the same kernel driver, tested at run time (a mask of bit
  `id % 64` of each kept entry's kernel driver; a machine-wide "all slots apart" flag was tried first and never held:
  elaboration merges the adjacent per-lane ranges of `sort_data` and of `sort_valid` into one kernel driver each), and `Copy`
  joined `batch_pure`. Correct (the order test below fails when the test is forced off), `cb_drive` -18 percent on
  `sc5_fifo_repack` (Cranelift, `--tier-heat=1,0,0`), but instructions (main thread, heat, `--no-cache`): `sc5_fifo_repack` LLVM
  -0.7 percent, Cranelift +0.6; `hdlm_lfsr` LLVM -0.1, Cranelift +1.1 (the mask costs about 10 instructions at every kept drive in
  Cranelift code, which does not share the loads). An avoided hand-over is about 33 instructions: the layers around the kernel
  call are not in the call count, they are per element in `direct_drive_bits` and the commit. Not landed; what would be left
  to try is the test in a callback only at a vector drive with entries pending (no cost per kept drive). Kept: the order test
  `crates/yavs/tests/compiled_drive_order.rs` (slots merged into one kernel driver and slots apart, every generator against
  the interpreter).
- **The reference simulator (rule 22):** its code generator marks a process that keeps no state of its own between activations, and
  the scheduler then passes it no state at all; every process is entered with one call and its state pointer. The idea taken: what an
  activation sets up is decided when the code is made, from what the code can reach. Ours keeps the per-activation view and the shared
  table and only drops the tags for processes that cannot reach them; nothing was copied.

## Compiled clocked RTL processes, round 12: one function per tier, and what was left out (yavs-interp, yavs-llvm, yavs-clift, 2026-11-04)

Task: the shortest path from the kernel's run loop to a compiled process, keeping sampling, tier switches, stop requests and debugger paths. Method: `tools/stepcount/step` over 100 kernel cycles of GRLIB and 20 of Microwatt, `--threads=1`, forced Cranelift (`--tier=clift --no-cache`) and at first entry (`--tier=auto --tier-heat=1,0,0 YAVS_SPEC_AFTER=2`), instructions per compiled activation in `InterpProcess::run`, `run_cached`, `Mem::sync` and the scratch.

| window | seam per activation | window per cycle | activations per cycle |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GRLIB forced | 567 to 510 | 29 201 to 29 026 | 2.80 |
| Microwatt forced | 477 to 398 | 183 205 to 181 867 | 14.45 |
| GRLIB at first entry | 596 to 546 | 10 438 to 10 297 | 2.67 |
| Microwatt at first entry | 437 to 374 | 159 609 to 158 451 | 15.40 |

- **Decision: a compiled activation is one function per tier** (`Tier::direct`, `DirectFn`, `yavs_llvm::rt::direct_entry::<T>`, kept in `Runtime::direct` with the tier's address). `InterpProcess::run` does the activation count and the flag load in no frame of its own (`Machine::direct_ready`) and jumps to the entry; `InterpProcess::activate` holds `Machine::run_direct`, with the tier's `run_cached` and `rt::enter` inlined. The frame of `run` (nine instructions in, nine out) and the virtual call are gone. The first activation of a process and one with a scratch or a specialise to do go through `run_prepared`, an activation that is not compiled through `run_interpreted` (at most 0.14 percent more instructions under `--tier=interp`, geomean 0.9998). A tier without an entry (the stub tiers of the tests) goes through `direct_dyn` and `run_cached` as before.
- **The tier's record is reached through the host** (`Host::record`, `View::record`), no copy in and out: 12 instructions. The pointer is read at `Mem::begin` and written at the end, never held across compiled code.
- **The rest of the entry:** `view_hot` (a `hot` process in its root frame: register and slot bases 0, no shared heap, no debugger; `view_root` corrects the flags and heap fields for the other callers), `Host` without `up` (`ret` looks the function up), `Env::pending` boxed and tested in place, `Mem::sync` tests in line, `NativeFlags::activated` only when the flag byte has `NAT_COUNT`, `ClifTier::funcs` holds `lean`, the `any` load is gone (a set `NAT_CODE` implies it), `STAMPS` a byte. All of the above together: -62 instructions per activation on GRLIB, -93 on Microwatt.
- **Tried and not kept.** `Host::f` looked up on demand: a look-up per activation goes, but half of them make a callback that needs it, and `signal` gained 8 instructions a call for the test: -22 per activation against -39 with the look-up kept. A temporary area shrunk instead of leaving residency: nothing, the swaps on GRLIB are four instances of a 7 234 register process that share one scratch set. `RESIDENT_REGS` at 65 536: +229 per cycle, `RESIDENT_TEMP` at 256 KiB: +371 (the budget counts it per process); sharing one register file among instances is also a cache gain, so these swaps stay. The scratch slot chosen by key: nothing, the scan is short.
- **Not built.** The view stays rebuilt at every activation, as round 7 decided. A persistent block for its rare fields: about 25 instructions at most, and each reader (`rt.rs` callbacks, both code generators) gains a load, so it nets 10 to 15: not worth moving fields read by generated code that no local run covers for the LLVM tier. `Mem::begin` and `save_tag` of a process that is not `lean` (about 100) are what remains: tags and mixes per space are read at fixed offsets by generated code.
- **Whole runs** (port to the base of 2026-11-06, main-thread instructions of warm `--tier=auto` runs, bench builds, three runs each): Microwatt 0.9934, `grlib_leon3mp` 0.9943, `neorv32_single_cache` at `--tier=clift` 0.9956. Output and exit status equal on all.
- **Cycles are undecided.** Plain PGO builds with an A/A of two builds, warm, two cores, with the two changes below: Microwatt 0.982 +-8.3 percent (A/A 1.039 +-8.9), GRLIB 1.003 +-10.8 (A/A 1.005 +-11.5), `neorv32_single_cache` 0.971 +-2.8 (A/A 0.995 +-3.2). A quiet sitting decides.
- **With it, two smaller cuts.** `wake_sole` arms the idle-skip readers only of a signal it takes out of `changed_sigs` (kernel "Wake at finish"). The three entries compiled code calls natives through (`native_frame`, `native_direct`, `native_light`) read the native's `R<Option<u64>>` tag and value apart (`native_result`): the 16-byte copy of the two words a native stores one by one cannot be forwarded from those stores and waits for both to retire. Non-forwardable store-to-load conflicts on Microwatt 1 278 to 1 129 per kernel cycle; instructions unchanged.

## README and public docs (maintainer, 2026-10-28)

- **The README links the evidence instead of repeating it.** Correctness: `docs/conformance.md` (generated); speed: `docs/performance.md` (method, headline geometric means, every testbench; updated with each head-to-head run); supported language features: `docs/language-support.md`. The README keeps one line per topic.
- **The private test-runner interface is not named in tracked docs.** The README says only that yavs is compliant with OSVVM, UVVM and VUnit.
- **LLVM is scheduled for removal.** The README presents the Cranelift code generator as the one bundled in the binary and LLVM, linked as an external library, as supported for now.

## One release archive per platform (release workflow, #780, 2026-10-28)

- **One archive per platform** (user, 2026-10-28): `yavs-<version>-<target>` (`.tar.gz`; `.zip` on Windows), built with `--features clift`: the Cranelift compiled tier, `--tier=auto` by default, `yavs --version` says `compiled tier: cranelift`. There is no `-nollvm` suffix any more and the LLVM archive (with `lib/libLLVM.so.21.1` on Linux) is no longer released. Supersedes the "Two archives per platform" bullets of "Release archives with and without the compiled tier"; the rest of that section (glibc 2.17 floor, Windows imports, dry run) stands where the build is still done.
- **LLVM stays in the code and CI**: the `llvm` feature, its tests and the llvm CI jobs keep running until the LLVM removal. Only the release stops shipping it. `E0127` (libLLVM cannot be loaded) can no longer occur in a release build; the code stays.
- **`tools/release/build-libllvm.sh` is no longer used by the release.** The script is left in place (a later decision removes it or not); the libLLVM build and cache steps, the Windows LLVM action, the Windows import check for LLVM and the `LICENSE-LLVM` file are dropped from `release.yml`. `.github/actions/llvm-windows` stays for `ci.yml`.
- **Smoke test** (each platform, from the extracted archive): `--version` says `compiled tier: cranelift`, a design runs with the default, `--tier=auto` and `--tier=clift`, `--tier=llvm` fails with `E0120`, `yavs-gui --version` runs; on Linux the same again in centos:7 (glibc 2.17) on x86_64 and arm64.
- **Install docs** (`docs/install.rst`, `docs/usage.rst`) describe one archive and do not mention LLVM.
