## Parallel kernel, step 1: a batch is pooled by its estimated work (yavs-kernel `run_batch`, `pool_batch`, #497, #481 item 3, 2026-10-28)

- **Decision: a batch goes to the pool when the estimated work of its parallel processes, less the largest one, passes
  `POOL_WORK_NS` (20 us)** (`SimControl::pool_batch`), not from a count of 32 (`PAR_BATCH`, gone). The largest process is
  left out because a batch whose time is one process cannot be split; serial processes do not count. Why: the work per
  process differs by two orders of magnitude between designs, so any count sends cheap batches of 32 to 64 processes to
  the pool, where the hand-over costs more than the batch (rtl_bus, lfsr64, lfsr64_xor at 0.35x to 0.62x of one thread).
- **Decision: per-process costs are learnt from inline runs only** (`SimControl::cost`, ns): one activation in
  `COST_EVERY` (16) of each process is timed, at a position that moves from batch to batch (scrambled, so a batch that
  comes every 2^k batches still sees every position), into an average of halves; a process not yet timed counts 0, so a
  design starts inline. One in `PROBE_EVERY` (64) of the batches that would pool runs inline to refresh the costs. A
  pooled run measures cold caches and would confirm its own choice (the prototype's finding, design 4.1).
- **Decision: the timing is in a second copy of the inline loop** (`batch_loop!(true)`), taken only with a pool; the run
  without a pool keeps the loop without the test. The one compare per activation cost rtl_fan 0.4 percent of its
  instructions at one thread.
- **Decision: the live-output scan runs only when the batch has a serial process** (#502), and the serial processes of a
  pooled batch run in batch order after the parallel ones, none after a process that stopped the batch, live while no
  earlier parallel process wrote: what the inline loop does. The old scan locked every parallel slot after the pool
  returned, though nothing read the answer without a serial process.
- **Decision: `Config::pool_all` (`YAVS_POOL_ALL=1`, a hidden test aid) pools every batch of two or more**, so the
  differential corpus and the kernel's determinism tests exercise the pooled path; `Stats::pooled_batches` counts the
  pooled batches (`YAVS_COUNTERS=1`). The corpus passes at 1, 4 and 4 shuffled threads with and without it.
- **Measured** (`docs/STATUS.md` "Parallel kernel, step 1"): lfsr64, lfsr64_xor and rtl_bus go from 0.35x to 0.62x of one
  thread to 0.98x to 1.01x at 2, 4 and 8 threads; designs whose batches still pool keep the old pooled path's losses
  (rtl_lfsr 0.71x to 0.86x, the soft core 0.57x to 0.83x), which step 2 addresses.

## Parallel kernel, step 2: pooled batches run in pieces of the slot array (yavs-kernel `run_batch`, `learn_pooled`, #481 item 3, 2026-10-28)

- **Decision: a pooled batch is cut into pieces of consecutive process numbers** (`PIECES_PER_THREAD` (4) per thread), each
  with its own sub-slices of the slots, metas and idle flags (`split_at_mut`, `Piece`): no lock per process, safe Rust.
  The workers and the kernel thread claim pieces from an atomic counter (`in_place_scope`); the pool has `threads - 1`
  workers, so `--threads N` is N busy threads and a run pinned to N cores is not oversubscribed. Why: the old pooled path
  locked every slot twice and committed every process on the kernel thread, reading lines another core had just written
  (`docs/design/parallel-kernel.md` 3.3), while the kernel thread waited in `install`.
- **Decision: the usual clocked process (waited again, only scheduled drivers) is committed in the worker** as the inline
  loop does, into the piece's buffers (`Early`: queue entries, direct entries, phantoms, idle counts; kept between
  batches), which the kernel thread applies after the join; the order of direct entries across processes does not matter
  (sole sources), the queue is sorted. The others go to `commit_rest` in batch order.
- **Decision: every pooled batch takes the pieces; serial processes are left by the workers and run after the join on
  the kernel thread in batch order** (none after a process that stopped the batch, live while no earlier parallel process
  wrote), so `--shuffle` runs them in the shuffled order at any thread count; after a stop nothing later in the batch is
  committed. Initialisation and postponed batches run inline (their commits differ; `pool_all` leaves them inline too).
- **Decision: the threshold learns from the pooled batches** (`learn_pooled`): the time of a pooled batch over its
  estimate inline is averaged (weight 1/16); when the average reaches even the threshold rises to twice the batch's
  splittable work, a batch at least a fifth faster lowers it to its splittable work (not below 20 us), and one in 64
  batches between the two is pooled to test it. Why: the processes of a soft-core processor carry much state, which another
  core's caches lack; with the fixed threshold the dual-core neorv32 ran at 0.6x to 0.8x of one thread. A single sample
  raised the threshold on a late worker wake-up and cost rtl_fan a third of its gain, hence the average.
- **Measured** (`docs/STATUS.md` "Parallel kernel, step 2"): 4 threads rtl_fan 2.6x, rtl_ff 2.1x, rtl_lfsr 1.9x of one
  thread; 8 threads 3.9x, 3.0x, 2.4x; the soft-core runs and the designs that never pool stay at 0.94x to 1.0x.
- **The reference simulator (rule 22)** runs the processes of a delta one after the other on one thread (a deferred task
  list with a prefetch of the next task); its work queues for other jobs keep per-thread task lists that idle threads
  steal from. The idea used is work handed out in pieces that idle threads take, not per process; ours keeps the
  batch-order commit of effects on the kernel thread and adds the learned inline-or-pooled choice. Nothing was copied.
- **Step 3 (parallel update, design 4.5): one half does not pay, the other is left unfinished.** Many independent signals
  below the 256 cut-off: on the soft core (the design with many) the whole update is about 6 percent of a one-thread run,
  well under a microsecond per delta, against a hand-over of several microseconds per pooled step, and its batches do not
  pool anyway: does not pay. One wide signal split by element range: with steps 1 and 2 the threads are balanced at 4
  threads and the kernel thread spends 13 percent (rtl_ff: `commit_codes`, the gather after the join) and 17 percent
  (rtl_lfsr: `finish_direct`, `commit_planes_run`) of the run in that serial commit and update; a split saves at most
  three quarters of it (about 10 to 13 percent of the run at 4 threads, more at 8). It needs a split view of `Signal`
  (planes, codes, stamps, pending bits and changed runs per 64-element range) with every invariant of `Signal::codes` and
  the stamps held per piece: not done in this round (#481, open scope).

## Concurrent copies committed by the kernel, not run in the batch (yavs-kernel `forward_copies`, #519, 2026-10-28)

- **Found by profiling the fletcher testbenches against sim1** (`--tier=auto`, Cranelift build first, then the LLVM build; `perf` instructions
  and cycles of the whole run, `YAVS_COUNTERS`): no single hot spot; the kernel is 46 to 54 percent of the run, the processes (interpreted,
  compiled and their runtime calls) 35 to 45. Half of all process runs are `CopyProcess` runs (writer 4.71 of 9.08 M, reader 3.96 of
  7.87 M; `neorv32_single_min` and `poc_cache_cpu` 18 percent, `sc5_fifo_repack` 18), each paying the batch (`run_one`/`run_batch`, `Ctx`,
  `resumption`, the `OutV` list, `commit_out`) for a read and a commit: about 280 instructions a copy beyond the copy itself.
- **Decision: a copy resumed in a cycle is made by the kernel after the wake loop and before the batch** (`SimControl::forward_copies`):
  the source parts are read from `cur` and committed to the copy's drivers (`Signal::commit_planes`, a run of `OutV` blocks through
  `commit_planes_run` for parts over 64 elements, `commit_bytes`), the copy counts as a process run and leaves the ready list. The values
  are the ones the copy would read in its run (nothing changes `cur` in the process phase) and the commit is the one its run would make
  (zero delay, its own direct drivers, which nothing else writes), so the next update sees the same pending elements; the order of
  commits across drivers does not matter (`changed_sigs` is sorted).
- **Which copies** (`copy_forwards`, at build): every part to a direct driver of the copy (`DriverInfo::direct` for logic; `bdirect` for one
  element of a byte signal of the source's element size), not postponed. At run time the copy's waits must be resident
  (`ProcMeta::perm`, so the wait it would make is the one standing); its waveforms are idle there by construction (a `debug_assert`).
  Not in the delta before the delta limit, so the limit's report and loop search still see the copies of the last batch. Other copies run
  as before.
- **Measured** (bench builds, `--tier=auto` warm, one claimed core of the second CCD, medians of 3 interleaved runs, host at load 27 to 50,
  so instructions are the figure): Cranelift build `fletcher_bufferreader` instructions 0.93, cycles 0.93; `fletcher_bufferwriter_512`
  0.91 to 0.97 and 0.88 to 0.93; `neorv32_single_min` 0.97, `poc_cache_cpu` 0.98 to 0.99, `sc5_fifo_repack` 1.00. LLVM build 0.92, 0.98,
  0.98, 0.98. `tools/realbench --compare` over 42 tests (Cranelift build): wall 0.97 interp, 0.96 auto, 0.98 auto-cold,
  instructions 1.00, 0.99, 1.00. Work-counter designs `copy_chain` (912 of 936 copies) and `copy_forward` (a 200-element bus, a slice, an integer and a record).
- **The reference simulator (rule 22):** it runs a concurrent signal assignment as an ordinary compiled process and queues the update of
  each driver as a deferred work item. The idea taken is only that the work of a driver update needs no process context; ours goes
  further and makes no activation for a plain copy at all. Nothing was copied.
- **Left** (measured, not done): the wake of the copy is still paid (waiter lists); `Signal::commit_planes` is about 65 instructions a block;
  the kernel's own gates, muxes and programs still run in the batch; the rest of the fletcher gap is diffuse: per-delta work of `cycle` and
  `finish_direct`, the interpreted record gather and scatter of two-process designs, and compiled straight-line processes that are no
  faster than interpreted ones (#679).

## Thread budget: a token pool in `MAKEFLAGS` (yavs `jobserver.rs`, yavs-kernel `Tokens`, #801, 2026-10-28)

Superseded on 2026-10-29 by "Thread budget: a token server in `YAVS_TOKENS`" below: the `MAKEFLAGS` client is removed.
The kernel decisions (cap, take only for a batch worth pooling, `TOKEN_IDLE`) stand.

- **Decision: `--threads N` is the cap, the tokens decide how many of the N threads run.** With N above 1 and a pool in
  `MAKEFLAGS` (`--jobserver-auth=R,W` or `fifo:PATH`, the last one wins; `--jobserver-fds` too), the simulation owns one
  implicit token and takes at most N - 1. The rayon pool of N - 1 workers is still built at the start (a pool cannot be
  resized, parked workers cost nothing); a pooled batch is cut for, and spawns, one worker per token held, and the
  parallel signal update splits into at most that many pieces plus one (`with_min_len`). Why: the maintainer's
  mechanism (b) in #801; a cap keeps a simulation from taking a whole pool that its batches cannot use.
- **Decision: tokens are taken only when a batch is worth pooling (`pool_batch` said yes), without blocking; with none
  the batch runs inline** and is not counted in `Stats::pooled_batches`. A batch on fewer threads than the pool has does
  not teach `learn_pooled` (its time says nothing about the full pool).
- **Decision: tokens are held across batches and given back after `TOKEN_IDLE` (64) batches in a row that did not pool
  (`run_one` counts), whenever `run_until`/`step_*` return (the kernel's `guard`, also on errors), and by the CLI before
  every exit while a run may hold some** (`jobserver::close` in `exit_after_signal`, the broken-pipe exit; a first
  SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP with no other handler now exits 130 after giving them back). Why: a read and a write per pooled
  batch cost a few percent of a batch at the 20 us threshold; the count is a `ponytail:` (a long serial batch right
  after a pooled one keeps them meanwhile).
- **Decision: in-tree client, no `jobserver` crate.** About 100 lines, no `unsafe`: the descriptors are reopened through
  `/proc/self/fd/R` (Linux) and a named pipe by its path, read and write, `O_NONBLOCK` (from `libc`, a new direct
  dependency already in the lock file). A new open file description leaves the parent's descriptor blocking. Only `R`
  is used, read and written. The bytes read are written back unchanged. Descriptors elsewhere (`/dev/fd` shares the
  description) and the Windows semaphore form have no client yet (`ponytail:`).
- **Decision: a pool that cannot be used is error `E0128` at the start of `run`, before analysis (exit 2)** (user,
  2026-10-29): closed descriptors, not a pipe, a path that is not a named pipe, a form with no client. The note gives the
  cause, the help the fix: pass the pool on, or, for a parent that does not share its pool with this run, remove
  `--jobserver-auth` from the child's `MAKEFLAGS`. Why: fail early, no silent fallback (rule 1, as #801 asked); a
  warning was considered first because a parent may keep `--jobserver-auth` while closing the descriptors, and the
  user chose the error. `MAKEFLAGS` is read first thing in `run`, before any file is opened, so a closed descriptor
  number is not yet reused by one of ours, and only a FIFO is accepted.
- **Decision: `MAKEFLAGS` is not read at all with `--threads 1` or `--dap`.**
- **Known cost, not measured: a simulation under an empty pool is not the `--threads 1` run.** It keeps the per-process
  cost sampling of a run with a pool (about 1 to 2 percent, `docs/parallel.md`) and makes one failed non-blocking read
  per batch worth pooling. The sampling is what tells it when a batch is worth a token, so it stays; #801's bulk gate
  (within 2 percent of today) has not been measured.

## Thread budget: a token server in `YAVS_TOKENS` (yavs `tokens.rs`, vunit-yavs `tokens.py`, #801, 2026-10-29)

- **Decision: one cross-platform token mechanism, a token server on a localhost TCP socket, replacing the `MAKEFLAGS`
  (GNU make jobserver) client in yavs and the fifo jobserver of vunit-yavs** (user, 2026-10-29, on #801). The runner
  listens on 127.0.0.1 at a free port and gives each test a random secret of its own; yavs gets
  `YAVS_TOKENS=<port>:<secret>`. Why: the same code on Linux and Windows (the fifo form had no Windows client), and a
  closed connection gives every token back, so a crashed or killed simulation can no longer lose tokens.
- **Decision: a level protocol with numbered answers** (agent). yavs sends `<want>` only when its demand changes (N - 1
  or 0, the kernel's `take`/`give`); the server answers the k-th line at once with `<k> <lent>` and again when it lends
  more, `lent <= want`. yavs uses only answers to its latest line, so a late answer to an older `want` (sent before a
  `0`) can never make it run on tokens already lent elsewhere. The secret is message 0, answered `0 0`, so a wrong
  secret is seen at the start. Why: a pipe of token bytes lets the server read back unused tokens, a socket does not;
  with the demand known the server parks no token where it cannot be used, and the 50 ms reclaim tick and its
  "one more than in use" heuristic are gone.
- **Decision: the server never takes a token back**; tokens return by a lower `want` or a closed connection. The first
  simulation to ask may get every free token; what it gives back goes breadth first, newest test first (`lend_order`,
  unchanged), capped per test by `yavs.max_threads - 1`. Free tokens are `N - max(k, 1) - lent` for `k` running tests.
  Why: the kernel holds tokens only while it pools and gives them back after 64 groups that did not; a revocation it
  would see only at its next take.
- **Decision: no explicit give-back on exit paths in yavs.** The operating system closes the socket on every exit
  (normal, error, Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, a kill, a crash); `exit_after_signal`, the broken-pipe exit and the signal hook that
  existed only to return tokens are removed, and with them the `libc` dependency of the `yavs` crate.
- **Decision: an unusable `YAVS_TOKENS` is error `E0128` at the start of `run`** (the user's 2026-10-29 rule for the old
  pool, kept): not `<port>:<secret>`, connect refused or timed out (10 s), the secret not answered with `0 0`. The secret
  is never printed. A server that goes away during the run is not an error: the rest of the run is on one thread
  (output does not depend on tokens). Not read with `--threads 1` or `--dap`.
- **Decision: the runner passes `--threads=N` itself when its token server runs** (user, 2026-10-29): `yavs.max_threads`
  (or `--yavs-max-threads`) when set, else the `-p N` value, so idle slots speed up the tail of a regression without
  further options. The opt-in flag keeps its name `--yavs-jobserver` (agent: 0.10 users keep their command lines) and
  works on Windows now.

## Test runner package vunit-yavs (python/vunit-yavs, 2026-10-28)

- **One Python distribution** `vunit-yavs` (import `vunit_yavs`) in `python/vunit-yavs` holds everything yavs-specific on the
  runner's Python side: the simulator interface (declared by the `simulator` key of its `vunit_pkg.toml`, added with
  `add_package("vunit-yavs", allow_setup=True)` before anything else), `--yavs-debug`, the thread cap, the jobserver, the version
  check. Nothing yavs-specific goes into the runner itself (user, 2026-10-28). Licence MPL-2.0, the licence the interface was first
  written under (agent; the user to confirm).
- **`--yavs-debug[=PORT]`** (agent, 2026-10-28; the user asked for `--debug`): default 4711 (the editor extension's attach port),
  `0` a free port; `yavs run --dap=PORT`, the address printed on the terminal. The `yavs-` prefix because the runner parses its
  argv once before packages are added, with prefix matching, and takes a bare `--debug` as another simulator's `--debugger`. One
  simulation: refused with `--gui`, `--elaborate` or `-p` above 1 at the start; a second simulation is refused before yavs starts
  (the interface sees no test list earlier). A suite run in one simulation (several tests) is one session.
- **Thread cap** (user, 2026-10-28): sim option `yavs.max_threads` over the runner argument `--yavs-max-threads N`, passed as
  `--threads=N` before the raw flags (an explicit `--threads` in `yavs.sim_flags` wins); unset passes nothing; not under
  `--yavs-debug` or for `elab`.
- **Jobserver** (user, 2026-10-28): opt-in `--yavs-jobserver`, POSIX only (an error on Windows), only with `-p N` above 1. One
  private GNU fifo jobserver per test (`MAKEFLAGS=-jN --jobserver-auth=fifo:PATH`, replacing an outer value; joining an outer
  jobserver is not supported) in a temporary directory, since `MAKEFLAGS` cannot hold a path with spaces (agent: the user asked
  for the test output directory). Free tokens `N - max(k, 1) - lent` for `k` running tests; lent breadth first, newest test first,
  capped by `yavs.max_threads - 1`; a test that left tokens unread at the last 50 ms tick gets at most one more than it uses.
  Steady-state total `N`, not a hard cap (a test starting while all tokens are out runs at once). Tokens held at a simulation's
  exit, or at the end of the run, are a warning. Superseded on 2026-10-29 by the token server ("Thread budget: a token server in
  `YAVS_TOKENS`").
- **Releases** (user, 2026-10-28): tag `vunit-yavs-v<version>` runs `.github/workflows/vunit-yavs-release.yml` (tests against the
  yavs binary release of the package's `YAVS_MIN_VERSION`, then PyPI by trusted publishing; no TestPyPI step, user 2026-10-29); the binary release now runs on
  `v[0-9]*` only, so neither tag starts the other workflow. `python/vunit-yavs/RELEASING.md` has the order. The package is released on its own (user, 2026-10-29): its version is independent of yavs's, and a package release that needs a newer yavs raises `YAVS_MIN_VERSION` first. Superseded on 2026-10-30: "One release with every artifact" (one release, one version, `vunit-yavs-release.yml` removed).

## CLI corrections from the documentation audit (#845, #850, #835, #838, #839, #836, #837; agent, 2026-10-29)

- **Help names the build** (#845, #850): the `--tier` help and `--explain E0120` say which compiled tiers the executable has (`elab::tiers_built`, from the cargo features) and what each tier needs; option help names no developer document.
- **`--tier` under `--dap`** (#835): checked like without it (`use_tier(None, ..)`: a tier the build lacks is `E0120`, exit 2); a debugger session still runs the interpreter and compiles nothing.
- **Empty and missing libraries** (#838): the contract wins (a missing or empty directory is a valid empty library, also for the `--work` library of `run` and `elab`, which never create it); the miss is `E0104` "top level not found" with the directory named in the help. `L0031` stays for a unit the design needs.
- **`--threads=0`** (#839): a usage error (fail early, no silent fallback), where the contract said it was treated as 1; the test runner never passes 0.
- **JSON stream** (#839): the batch stop note of `analyze` is a note diagnostic with an empty code in the JSON and short formats, so those streams hold only diagnostics. `finish(N)` still exits with N when it fits 1..125 (so `finish(2)` is exit 2): left to the user to decide.
- **`--ieee-warnings`** (#836): `on|off`, off drops warnings of the `ieee` library (natives and bodies) by origin file, not by severity of the caller.
- **Conditional analysis definitions** (#837): `-D` is passed to `elab` and `run` like `--psl`, not recorded in the library manifest (no format change; one rule for the options that change how a source is read).

## Weak dependencies: an architecture named before it is analysed (#819; maintainer, 2026-10-31)

- An entity aspect or binding indication naming an architecture (`entity work.e(a)`) is accepted at analysis whether or not the architecture exists yet. The record of the unit lists it under `weak` (manifest format 4): the closure pulls it in when it exists and it orders no file, because the architecture's file depends on the entity, often in the naming file. A missing architecture is `E1002` at elaboration of the instance. A library of an older format is refused with `L0004` and analysed again once.

## Deferred constant used early, null range choice (#861, #860; user, 2026-10-30)

- **Deferred constant used in its package body before the full declaration** (#861): an analysis error, `E1226` (option a), kept. No run-time error and no per-revision split.
- **Null range choice next to other associations in an aggregate** (#860): `E1326` in 1993 files only (option a); 2008 and 2019 accept it. See `docs/design/lrm-checks.md`.

## Attributes of an unconstrained deferred constant (#1076; maintainer, 2026-11-02)

- Accepted in the package body, in a subprogram and after the full declaration, with the bounds of the full declaration's value; `E1226` in the package declaration and in a body declaration before the full declaration. See `docs/design/lrm-checks.md` L175.
- A subprogram of the body above the full declaration that reads such bounds, called while an earlier declaration of the body is elaborated, is erroneous (LRM 14.4.2) and a run-time error (`E3009`, maintainer, 2026-11-02). Each such deferred constant has a flag in package data that its full declaration sets when elaborated; a bounds read (`Fx::dope_of`) checks it only when its source position is above the full declaration in the same file, so subprograms below the full declaration, other units and every other read pay nothing. The check is plain IR (a load, a branch, `Unreachable` with the message), so every tier has it. It holds in a nested package and in an instance of a generic package that is a library unit or sits in a package body. An instance declared in an architecture, block, generate, process or subprogram (also one inside another instance) has no package initialisation, so its flag is a cell of the region's instance data (an instance constant the elaborator computes right after the full declaration's value, `inst_object`) or a frame slot set after the full declaration (`Fx::decls`); `dope_of` reads the bounds from the full declaration's object (`deferred_full`), so `'length` and the other attributes give the bounds and elements of its value in every tier (before, `'length` read 1 and the process case was an internal error, #1079). A bounds read of an instance with no flag is an internal error, never a silent skip.

## One release with every artifact (release.yml, tools/release/bump.py, RELEASING.md, #903, maintainer, 2026-10-30)

- **One release per version holds everything** (maintainer, 2026-10-30): the simulator archives (Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64,
  Windows x86_64), the vunit-yavs wheel and sdist (also on PyPI), the VS Code extension `.vsix`, the conformance report, one
  `SHA256SUMS` over all of them and one set of release notes (`release_notes/<version>.md`, a summary line and at most 10
  one-line bullets first, as before; the package's and the extension's fragments are part of it). Marketplace and Open VSX
  publishing stays for later (the hook is described in `release.yml`). Rationale: one place and one version for users.
- **Lockstep versions** (maintainer, 2026-10-30): the Cargo workspace, vunit-yavs (`pyproject.toml` and `YAVS_MIN_VERSION`) and the
  extension (`package.json`, the minimum yavs in its README) carry the release version; every release bumps all three with
  `tools/release/bump.py X.Y.Z`. The extension went from 0.1.0 to 0.11.0 on `main` to join (agent, 2026-10-30; nothing was
  released with that version).
- **No development versions** (agent, 2026-10-30): `main` carries the last released version everywhere until the release commit.
  `tools/release/bump.py --check` (the `versions` job of `ci.yml`, and `release.yml` with the tag's version) fails when a spot
  differs. Rationale: the Cargo workspace already worked this way; a plain equality check needs no rules. Replaces the `.dev0`
  step of the old vunit-yavs release steps. The package tests take the version from `YAVS_MIN_VERSION`, so a bump needs no test edit.
- **The separate flows are gone** (maintainer, 2026-10-30): `vunit-yavs-release.yml` (`vunit-yavs-v*` tags) and
  `vscode-release.yml` (`vscode-v*` tags) are removed; their tags and releases stay. `release.yml` tests the package (on all three
  platforms) and the extension (`vscode.yml`, Linux x86_64) against the archives built in the same run, not a downloaded release.
  `vscode.yml` on its own builds yavs from the same commit, so it no longer names a yavs version.
- **PyPI after the GitHub release** (agent, 2026-10-30): the `pypi` job (environment `pypi`, trusted publishing) runs after the
  release is created, so a refused upload is re-run alone. PyPI must list `release.yml` with environment `pypi` as a trusted
  publisher (a one-time maintainer step, `RELEASING.md`); without it the job fails and names that step.
## Typo suggestion distances (#894, 2026-10-30)

Use `strsim::osa_distance` in semantic suggestions and `strsim::levenshtein` in library
suggestions, preserving the existing thresholds and character-based distances. This removes
duplicate implementations without changing diagnostics (issue #894; implemented by codex/strsim894).

## Elaboration range index and limitation diagnostics (#889, 2026-10-30)

- Rebuild the package range-owner index when `Db::units.len()` grows, retaining already
  evaluated bounds. A package loaded on demand must reuse its initialised subtype bounds
  rather than invoke impure bound functions again (#848; agent codex/elab889).
- Unsupported elaboration features use E2199; unsupported command combinations use E0199.
  E9999 denotes internal errors only. Suite drivers treat the new limitation codes as no
  language rejection, preserving their verdict rules (#868; agent codex/elab889).

## Resolution functions in native code and nested regions (#889, 2026-10-30)

- Wrap predefined and native resolution functions in the normal callable array ABI before
  invoking the existing native with a fat pair. Resolution uses the existing implementations
  rather than trying to lower a missing VHDL body (#608; agent codex/resolvers889).
- Bind a block or generate resolution function to the enclosing elaborated region that
  declares it, walking outward from the signal. Its region data supplies captured constants,
  generics and iteration parameters; lower its containing architecture even if it has no
  processes (#817; agent codex/resolvers889).

## CI matrix (#888, 2026-10-31)

- Every push and pull request runs Linux x86_64 only (`ci.yml`: fmt, clippy, tests, the Cranelift
  tier with the difftest smoke, the analysis corpora, vunit-yavs). Reason: three platforms on every
  push cost about 30 minutes each and made red runs mostly platform noise (maintainer, 2026-10-30).
- A `plan` job in `ci.yml` adds the Windows jobs (`check`, `clift`, `vunit-yavs`) when the push or
  pull request touches path, file or process sensitive code: `crates/yavs`, `yavs-cache`, `yavs-lib`,
  `yavs-ffi`, `yavs-vhpi`, `tools/`, `python/vunit-yavs/` (with the token server), `editors/vscode/`,
  `.github/` and `Cargo.lock` (the last four crate and file entries are the agent's reading of
  "path, file or process sensitive"). Superseded by "CI scope": the pattern is `WINDOWS` in
  `tools/ci-plan.py`.
- `nightly.yml` runs `ci.yml` on main every night with every platform (Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64,
  Windows x86_64). A red run opens one issue labelled `nightly`, or comments on the open one.
- A release tag or a release dry run (`release.yml` calls `ci.yml`) and a manual run of `ci.yml`
  run every platform, because `github.event_name` in a called workflow is the caller's.
- Pushes to main are never cancelled by a newer push (a group per commit), so every main commit has
  a CI result; branches and pull requests still cancel older runs.
- Job names stay `check (<os>)`, `clift (<os>)`, `corpus`, `vunit-yavs (<os>)`, `versions`. A skipped
  platform has no job, so only the `ubuntu-24.04` names can be required checks on main
  (maintainer, 2026-10-30; agent cc-host1/ci).

## CI scope (#1014, 2026-11-01)

- **Decisions (maintainer, 2026-11-01):** the goal is faster feedback per commit, with docs-only commits very quick and runner minutes secondary; no coverage is lost, only path filters, dedupe and caching; Windows and other non-Linux jobs run on source, build and platform files and skip docs, test data and tooling; the change applies to later commits only.
- `tools/ci-plan.py` (the `plan` job) sets the scope from the changed files. **none:** files no job reads (prose, release note fragments, tools CI does not run): no build. **light:** user guide pages, `docs/examples`, `python/vunit-yavs`, `editors/vscode`: only the Rust and package tests that read them, or all package tests when the package changed. **full:** anything else, including a file on no list, and every schedule, manual and tag run. Rationale: tests read the pages (`docs_examples`, `docs_debugger`, `env_registry`, the `reference` unit tests, `test_docs.py`), so a page change is not simply skippable; a new test that reads a listed file changes the lists in the same commit.
- `ci.yml` and `docs.yml` have no workflow path filter, so every commit has a CI run and a waiter never hangs. `check`, `clift`, `corpus` and `vunit-yavs` are required checks on main and a skipped matrix job does not report its expanded name, so the `skipped` job reports the left out names as passed.
- Windows: every crate, `lib/`, and the build files (`Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `.cargo/`, `ci.yml`). This replaces the crate list of "CI matrix": a Windows-only bug in `yavs-lint` (d0e8826a), a crate not on that list, is why a list is not safe. Off: `tools/`, `editors/vscode/`, other workflows, docs and test data under `crates/*/tests`. A `python/vunit-yavs` change runs only `vunit-yavs` on Windows. The nightly run covers the rest within a day. The pattern is `WINDOWS` in `tools/ci-plan.py`.
- `conformance.yml` had a `paths` filter (removed by #1033, see "Conformance runs nightly"), and a push of a tag or a manual run ignored it. It no longer cancels on main: half of its runs were cancelled by a newer push, so a result-changing commit often had no result and a report needed a quiet main.
- Audit evidence: the comments on issue #1014.
- **`[profile.test] opt-level = 1`** (user asked to try it, agent chose by measurement, 2026-11-01): `check` on Linux about 29 to 9 min, on Windows about 30 to 16, `clift` on Linux about 17 to 7, the same pass, fail and ignore counts. `debug-assertions` and `overflow-checks` are set explicitly and `crates/yavs-logic/tests/profile_checks.rs` fails if they stop working. Splitting `yavs-lower tests/corpus.rs` and `tests/wave.rs` into parallel jobs is **not** kept: on top of opt-level 1 it saves about 1.5 min on Linux and 3 on Windows, and it needs an aggregate job for the required check name, and a way to skip them that does not pass libtest options to the `harness = false` test `yavs-cache/tests/huge_heap.rs`. Numbers: issue #1014.
- Verified on real runs: 256762b1, a change to `ci.yml`, ran every Linux job and Windows; all four required checks passed, and its `conformance` run finished although newer commits arrived. Not verified by a run: the tag path of `conformance.yml` (GitHub documents that `paths` does not apply to tag pushes; the next release shows it).

## Verifier sweep of the perf branches (2026-11-06)

- **The `sweep` job of `ci.yml` runs only by hand on a `perf/` branch** (agent, 2026-11-06; the maintainer sees every change to what CI runs): a release build with debug assertions, `tools/realbench/sweep.py` over the realbench tests whose sources `tools/fetch-corpus.sh` fetches, each compiled whole and run to 1 ns with `YAVS_VERIFY_IR`. It is the gate an optimiser or lowering change on a perf branch passes before it lands there: a lost definition on a large design passed whole-run equality once and only the verifier saw it. Not on pushes to main: about half an hour of runner time, and main gets perf work only through a merge that ran it.
- **`YAVS_VERIFY_IR` turns on every IR check a debug build makes** (agent, 2026-11-06): the reads-before-writes dataflow of the verifier and the verify after inlining and after optimising each function, so a bench build can run the sweep too. Unset, release builds keep the lazy verify of #479.

## Vendor libraries from the user's install (#119, 2026-10-31)

- **UNISIM and UNIMACRO come from the user's own Vivado install; sources are never redistributed or committed** (user, 2026-10-30). Intel and Lattice libraries later.
- **Decision (maintainer, 2026-10-31): no vendor command.** A `yavs vendor vivado` command and a helper in `vunit-yavs` existed for a few hours on main, unreleased, and were removed: "I simply need to be able to build the vendor code with good performance." The way to build is `yavs analyze` over the install's files and VUnit's `add_library` with `add_source_files`, a few lines in `docs/libraries.rst`. The command did nothing plain analyze cannot do: a shell glob is a valid order for `unisim`, and `unimacro` needs only its component package first.
- **`unisims/secureip` and the XPM macros are not supported:** the secureip files need a library the install holds only in encrypted Verilog, and an instance stays unbound as for every missing entity (`W2108`). The XPM macros are SystemVerilog.
- **Vendor libraries stay out of the user guide** (maintainer, 2026-10-31, "Keep the vendor stuff out of the manual"): the page `vendor-libraries`, its mentions and the context7 rule are removed unreleased; the decisions above and the tests in `crates/yavs/tests/vendor.rs` stay.
- **`vunit-yavs` analyzes consecutive files in one call,** as "Batched analysis calls" decided for integrations; it had not done so yet. A first compile of the libraries took twice as long, one process per file.

## Surfer through WCP (#876, 2026-10-31)

- Opt-in by `--surfer` only; default file next to the work library; 1 s refresh; the viewer never changes the status, and W0131 stays a warning under `-W error`; goto_declaration jumps to source; the stepped process's signals coloured; a marker at each breakpoint; records and arrays one level; at most 200 signals on their own (user, 2026-10-30, #876).
- **A viewer is a trait of `yavs-dap`, WCP lives in the binary** (agent, 2026-10-31): `Viewer` in the session keeps the DAP crate free of a protocol it does not need. Its codes are `E0130` and `W0131`.
- **1 s stays the default** (agent, 2026-10-31): only runs with `--surfer` pay for it. Measured with `--wave` on two long RTL benches, one thread, `--tier` default, median of three on a loaded host, so noisy: wall time about 2 to 5 percent more than no clock flush, the file at most 1 percent larger.
- **Colours are reset to the default theme's green** (agent, 2026-10-31): WCP cannot clear an item's colour.

## The waveform file at a debugger stop (#961, 2026-10-31)

- **A stop writes what the stopped process reads, at the stop time** (agent, 2026-10-31): checked in the file: the time table ended at the last completed step, because changes wait for the end of their time step so that a step's deltas collapse. A stop now writes the pending ones. The price is a second value at the same time when a later delta changes the signal again, only in debugger sessions; readers take the last value of a time.
- **A repeated value marks a stop time with no change** (agent, 2026-10-31): a file's time ends at its last change and FST has no other mark. The first recorded signal repeats its value at that time; it shows no edge.
- **Variables at a stop: what can be read** (agent, 2026-10-31, #965): between cycles every process is suspended and all are read. Inside a process its frames give its own variables, and the shared ones through it, since it holds the shared state; a read through another route would deadlock. The other processes are out of reach while the kernel runs one (the serial loop holds their slots), and the Variables view shows only the stopped process, so they follow when the time step ends. `execs` stays, so that end reads the stopped process again.

## Surfer and a hidden window (#952, 2026-10-31)

- **The cause, what is known**: Surfer handles WCP commands in its `App::ui` only and has no `App::logic` (source of the 0.7.0 tag and of a later main), and the window toolkit runs `ui` only for a window it may paint. Measured on the real program on a private X server: with the window's state set to minimized it answered nothing for 35 s, and when restored it gave all answers at once, in order; an X11 window merely covered kept answering. From the toolkit's source (the later main only): on Wayland a redraw waits for the compositor's frame callback, and without one only `logic` runs. That a desktop compositor withheld those from the covered window of the report is inferred, from one run with the window covered and one beside the editor; a covered window on a private headless compositor kept answering.
- **yavs does not work around it** (agent, 2026-10-31): Surfer has no option for it and a client cannot make it draw, so the messages and `docs/waveforms.rst` say what to do. A change in Surfer (commands handled in `logic`) would remove the cause.
- **One command's trouble never ends the connection** (agent, 2026-10-31): a read timeout is a stall, an error answer concerns that command, and only a read end or a failed write (half a frame leaves nothing to follow it) ends the thread. Surfer's queue holds 100 commands and then it stops reading, so while it owes answers nothing is sent but one `get_item_list` per user `wave add` (a new command asks it to draw); news is kept as state and later news replaces earlier.
- **5 s to count as a stall, six of those for a load** (agent, 2026-10-31): a Surfer that draws answers in milliseconds, and `wave add` holds the debugger for that long, so it is short. A load of a large file is slow without being stuck, and it is not waited for by blocking: `wave add` and the rest wait in the thread's state.
- **A load without `waveforms_loaded` gives up, not the connection** (agent, 2026-10-31): Surfer sends the event only for a load that works. After the wait a `get_item_list` tells a Surfer that does not draw from a load that failed; in the second case the count is reset and it is told.
- **Told when it happens and W0131 at the end, both** (agent, 2026-10-31): the notice reaches the person at the prompt, W0131 stays the record in the run's log. A stall that ended leaves no W0131.

## VS Code and test runner: install and forget (#902, 2026-10-31)

- **"yavs: Attach" needs no launch.json** (user, 2026-10-31): a dynamic configuration, a palette command, F5 with nothing configured; port 4711, a question only if nothing listens. The look at the port is a connection closed at once, so the server does not take such a connection for its one session.
- **Preprocessed files map at the debugger, per file** (agent, 2026-10-31): `--source-map=COMPILED=ORIGINAL`; the test runner package knows the pairs, and the design's paths are mapped where the debugger reads them. Location and check preprocessing keep lines (test in `vunit-yavs`). Diagnostics keep the compiled path, which is the file yavs read.

## Interactive console (#904, 2026-10-31)

- **The console is a DAP client of the DAP server, in the same process** (agent, on the maintainer's "no second implementation", 2026-10-30): a pipe as the connection, each line an `evaluate` with context `repl`, all commands in `yavs-dap/src/console.rs`. The terminal, `--do`, `source` and an editor's Debug Console share one parser and one run control.
- **Generic commands in yavs, VUnit's in `vunit-yavs`, through a hook** (user, 2026-10-30): plain names in yavs; `vunit_*` with VUnit's wording in the package; recompiling depends on what only the test runner knows. The hook has `reload` (elaborate again) rather than a console word, as a user at the plain console has `restart` and nothing to compile with (agent, 2026-10-31).
- **`restart` is a new build from the same elaboration** (user, 2026-10-30: no VHPI save and restart needed): breakpoints are kept as asked for and resolved again, which `reload` needs anyway. Refused with `--vhpi` and `--load`, whose state cannot be reset (agent, 2026-10-31).
- **The stop at time 0 is before the first cycle** (agent, 2026-10-31): breakpoints can be set on a process's first statement. `run` past the end prints a line and is no error, as a simulator's run past the end; `step` is an error.
- **`--do` without `--interactive` is a batch** (agent, 2026-10-31): it ends at the end of the script, with status 1 at a failing command. Stop notices go to standard error so that standard output equals a batch run.
- **A breakpoint under `vunit_run` prints `Test Run Failed!`** (user, 2026-10-30, exact VUnit behaviour): the test suite did not finish.
- **Lean calls are off under a debugger** (agent, 2026-10-31, #863): the debug loop runs a function's prologue, which reads the parameter slots a lean call leaves empty.
- **A condition is checked when it is made** (agent, 2026-10-31, #957): the evaluation runs over the types of the signals the process sees and the names of its variables (`Typed`, `make_cond` in `yavs-dap/src/lib.rs`), so an unknown name, a literal that does not fit, operands of different types and a result that is not boolean are errors with the text and help of the stop. A process variable (its type is not in the program) and what depends on a value (a division by zero, an index, a null access) wait for the stop; the reply names the variables not checked. One path for a line breakpoint, a signal breakpoint, a client's breakpoint and `run until`. In a subprogram any simple name may be a local of the caller, so an unknown one is not an error there.
- **A time prints in the largest unit that holds it whole, and a fraction of the resolution is an error** (agent, 2026-10-31, #958): `literal_image` for physical values (`10 ns`, not `10000000 fs`), as a stop prints a time; the debugger's literals refuse `0.5 fs` instead of rounding it (`'value` and TEXTIO keep rounding). A time or physical value without a unit says that it needs a unit and gives an example (`10 ns`).
- **A breakpoint that is refused gives its number back, and `break list` shows the line it stops at** (agent, 2026-10-31, #956); `deposit` takes no `-out`, and a flag that is not last is named in the error of the value (#960).
- **Generics are names in expressions; value errors are in plain words** (agent, 2026-10-31, #970, #972): a generic of the process's instance (top level between cycles) with a scalar or character-array value is read like a signal, after locals and signals; the debugger's literal errors (`typed_literal`, with #953) name what was typed, the target and an example; a unit that is none of the type's and a literal in a condition say what they were compared with.
- **`drivers` shows a driving value only for a signal with a driver; `where` prints dotted names** (agent, 2026-10-31, #974).


## yavs-gui removed (#871, maintainer, 2026-10-29)

- **`yavs-gui` is removed from the releases and the repository** (maintainer, 2026-10-29). Why: the debugger is
  any DAP client (VS Code, `yavs run --dap`); a second client with its own EUPL-1.2 licence, a pinned git
  dependency and a display requirement was not worth shipping. Removed: `gui/`, `.github/workflows/gui.yml` and
  its call from `release.yml`, the GUI's dependabot entry, `docs/design/gui.md`, `yavs run --gui` (`src/gui.rs`)
  and its test, the install and troubleshooting rows, the README licence paragraph.
- **`E0122` is retired and never reused** (codes are stable, `crates/yavs-diag`): its `--explain` text is gone,
  `yavs run --gui` is a usage error like any unknown option.
- **Release archives:** `yavs`, the licences without `LICENSE-EUPL-1.2-yavs-gui`, and `README.md`. The release
  smoke test no longer runs `yavs-gui --version`; the glibc 2.17 check covers `yavs` only. This supersedes "Smoke test"
  of the Cranelift release entry and "One release archive" of the GUI section above, for future releases.
- **The published 0.9.0 release is not changed:** its archives still contain `yavs-gui` and
  `LICENSE-EUPL-1.2-yavs-gui` (changing assets would change published checksums). The removal starts with the next
  release.
- **DAP extensions kept:** `yavs/waveSubscribe` and the requests added for the GUI stay in `yavs-dap`, tested and
  usable by any client. #396 and #397 (structured stops, source locations) stay open as DAP requests.
- **Python runner package:** `-g/--gui` is refused at the start with a message pointing to `--yavs-debug`
  (fail early, no fallback), and `supports_gui_flag` is dropped.

## VUnit integration round (#112, #114, #120, #892; 2026-10-31)

- **The runner's own suites run through `tools/suites/vunit_suites.py`, unchanged** (agent, #112): the script registers the `vunit-yavs` interface and runs each `run.py` as `__main__`; no copy or patch of a suite. VHDL-2019 is measured but not a target: the suites' location tests fail identically on the reference simulator (same failing set, test by test).
- **A file list for a runner's batch compile is not used** (agent, #114): the runner writes the list with the locale encoding and `\r\n` line ends in text mode, yavs reads UTF-8 (a BOM and `\r\n` are accepted, anything else is E0101). `vunit-yavs` sets `supports_batch_compile` and `supports_concurrent_compiles_into_library` and leaves `batch_file_list_arguments` empty, so the runner puts the names on the command line (limited to its 32000 characters, no encoding involved). A runner that writes the list as UTF-8 can switch to `("@{}",)` with no change in yavs.
- **A token server that cannot be reached is warning `W0118`, not error `E0128`** (decided by the maintainer on 2026-10-31, proposed in #878 on 2026-10-30; reverses the 2026-10-29 `E0128` rule for this case): nothing listening, no answer within 10 s, or a connection that breaks during the run leaves the run on one thread. `E0128` stays for a value that is not `<port>:<secret>` and for a secret the server refuses, which are mistakes in the setup. Why: tokens only speed a run up. `vunit-yavs` likewise warns and runs without a server when it cannot bind its socket.
- **Worker threads start with the first token, and a package default caps them at 4** (proposed in #879 on 2026-10-30; the cap was 8 and the maintainer set it to 4 on 2026-10-31 until `--threads=auto` exists, #901, which revisits it): `Config::lazy_pool` (set by `yavs run` when it has a token server) builds the rayon pool at the first `helpers()` above 0; a pool that cannot be built leaves the run on one thread. `vunit-yavs` passes `--threads=min(-p N, 4)` when `yavs.max_threads` and `--yavs-max-threads` are not set (rtl_fan: 2.4x at 4 threads, 3.3x at 8; more threads buy little and cost memory in every simulation). Why: at `-p 256` the old behaviour made 256 simulations of 255 threads.
- **When the runner has `--parallel-compile` or `--batch-compile`, it compiles; otherwise the package batches** (agent, #114): `compile_source_files` hands over to the runner when `batch` or `num_threads` above 1 is passed, and keeps its own one-call-per-consecutive-files default otherwise, which works with every runner release.

- **Python from VHDL is verified through a package of our own and, locally, the runner's own Python package testbenches** (agent, #120): `python/vunit-yavs/tests/project_foreign` builds a C library (with Python embedded where a shared libpython and its headers exist: Linux only) and registers `native_library_hooks`; Windows runs the plain native-library test when a C compiler is on `PATH`. The runner's own VHDL Python package testbenches (106 tests: both testbench files) pass on yavs with the library built by that package and `--load`; the one test with an accented string literal needs `--encoding=latin1` for analysis and run (yavs reads UTF-8 source as Latin-1 characters, user decision "Source encoding"; the run re-reading sources with its own `--encoding` is #869).

## Static analysis: `yavs lint` (#895, 2026-10-31)

- **Rules run on the HIR of a normal analysis, one front end** (maintainer, 2026-10-30): crate `yavs-lint`, rule ids `lint_NNN` in their own namespace, four certainty classes with the definite class on by default, `yavs-lint.yaml` and `yavs-lint-waivers.yaml`, no mapping of the front-end rules of the source project. `-Werror=CODE` takes a rule id (`Out::set_warn_with`).
- **What a lint run reads** (agent, 2026-10-31): the files of a mapped library in the order of the library, the others in the order given, through `Db::analyze_file`, so it needs no change in `yavs-sem` and writes nothing: the library's order is what makes a whole library or directory analyzable without a dependency sort. A loose directory in the wrong order fails analysis with an error naming the unit; `yavs analyze` first is the answer. The analysed-unit cache is read, never written.
- **A failed file stops only itself, exit status 2** (agent, 2026-10-31): the other files are still checked, so one bad file does not hide findings elsewhere; 2 as for `run`, where analysis errors are usage-class. Only errors of analysis are printed: `yavs analyze` already printed its warnings.
- **Evidence is what analysis folded** (agent, 2026-10-31): a rule judges a width, index or divisor only when `Expr::value` is known, which is wider than literals (a constant counts) and never covers a generic. Code under an `if`, `elsif` or `if generate` condition that folds to false is not walked, so a constant may turn off an index it would break. A `case` on a constant is walked: narrow it if a corpus shows a false finding.
- **lint_741 and lint_781 judge predefined operators only** (agent, 2026-10-31): an overloaded `=` may resize, an overloaded `/` defines its own error.
- **lint_782 reports nothing of its own** (agent, 2026-10-31): analysis rejects it first, as E1403. The id stays so that a configuration naming it keeps working; the run shows the analysis error with exit status 2. lint_751 is real: analysis accepts a binding to an architecture that is not there yet, and a lint run has the whole library. lint_780 overlaps W1404, a warning of `yavs analyze`, and stays a finding, as a warning there is not a failure here.
- **lint_771 treats a procedure call that ends a list as an ending** (agent, 2026-10-31): the procedure may stop the run; a project's own failure procedure is common, and a rule in the definite class does not guess.

In the short format the lines are joined into the one line of the diagnostic. The file is named relative to the working directory. `vunit-yavs` reads the configuration once (`yavs lint --list-rules`) before the per-library runs, so the error is told once.

A schema declares keys, value types and nesting; one reader (`yavs_diag::yaml`) checks it before any converter looks at the tree, so a key that is not declared cannot be read by accident and a new key is added in one place. The noisy form is not measured. Cycle count and console are unchanged.
- **The interpreter tier is opt-in for `--cpubench`** (maintainer, 2026-10-31): the defaults are `auto`, `auto-cold` and `auto@4`; `--with-interp` adds `interp`.
- **The POWER compiler comes from a pinned `ziglang` wheel in the harness's own virtual environment** (maintainer, 2026-10-31): `tools/realbench/requirements.txt` (version and hashes), installed into `<cache>/venv` the first time an image needs it (so `--prepare` makes it), nothing outside the cache; `YAVS_PPC_ZIG` and `YAVS_PPC_PREFIX` override it.
