The Microwatt window read instructions 1.028 and the generic L1i column on small designs moves up to 1.39 on tiny counts, so neither is a verdict. Whole runs decide.

## Cranelift: rare ways cold where they are made (yavs-clift `lower.rs`, wave 3 S1a, 2026-11-07)

Written by Claude. On branch `perf/w3-s1a`; whether it reaches `perf/iterative` or `main` is the maintainer's decision.

- **Decision:** the codes of a short `SigRead` after the plane-word tests (`sig_read_word`'s `codes_at`) and the native call of an in-place `ieee` op (`ieee_native`'s `fb`) are cold blocks; the end of a statement cuts the temporary length back with `umin` and one store, no branch. Only layout and one branch change; no operation's result does.
- **Why:** the large designs run more distinct taken branch sites than this host's branch target buffer holds. Cranelift (0.137) lays a function out in reverse postorder with the cold blocks last. Reverse postorder is a topological order, so where two ways meet again the join comes after both, and one of the two ways is a taken jump unless the other is cold. Writing a guard with the other polarity (`brif !c, slow, go`) therefore only turns the taken conditional into a taken `jmp` over the other way: measured on GRLIB, distinct taken sites of the window 10 372 to 10 407, always-taken conditionals of generated code 4 068 to 3 687, generated `jmp` 1 538 to 1 948. Rejected.
- **Measured** (exact single-stepped windows of a warm run, distinct taken sites per window without returns, LRU replay of a branch target buffer of 8 192 entries, misses per kernel cycle): GRLIB 10 378 to 9 674 sites (generated code 7 195 to 6 488), 55.8 to 48.2 misses; Microwatt 10 684 to 9 500 sites (generated code 7 506 to 6 338), 316.6 to 36.0 misses, each pair from runs with the same compile set (a second base run of Microwatt that compiled differently had 171 more runtime sites). By kind of IR instruction, GRLIB `SigRead` -374, `Stmt` -265, `CallNative` -62; Microwatt `SigRead` -580, `CallNative` -316, `Stmt` -238. Instructions per kernel cycle unchanged (26 268 to 26 274, 136 077 to 135 486). No class of site grew (sites joined to IR instructions through `YAVS_CLIFT_CODEDIR` and the IR dump).
- **Not done here:** branches whose two ways are both common at different sites (the address-space chain of a native frame's `host`, the drive compare's hit and miss, a signal read's codes or planes form) keep one taken way; only a profile (which way a site takes) can choose, the cold layout from a stored block list.

## Slices between process variables at auto: a full fact table (2026-11-02, #1059, branch `perf/iterative`)

- **Cause:** not the interpreter's address decode. The optimiser's table of memory facts holds 64 and stopped learning when full. Before frame objects a store through an unknown pointer dropped the facts about temporaries, so the table stayed empty. With frame objects that store is known to touch one variable, the facts stay, and the two descriptors of each slice (four facts each) fill it after eight statements. Every later slice in the block kept its `MakeDope`, `LayoutWord`, `Alloc`, `SubtypeCheck` and `DopeLen`.
- **Decision:** a full table forgets its oldest fact about memory a register points to (`Table::make_room`, `Key::is_temporary`). Facts about a known address, a variable, stay, and a table holding only those stops learning as before. No length test changes: fewer facts means more run-time tests, never fewer.
- **Rejected: forget the oldest of any fact.** It evicts variables a later statement reads. **Rejected: a larger table.** Every store and statement scans it, and the cliff only moves.
- **A sibling, whole copies between two variables (`r1 := r0`):** the direct copy has no frame to frame arm, so these went through the staging buffer. `Op::CopyFrames` calls `Machine::root_pair` out of the dispatch, and `lcopy_wide` tries it too. A copy that leaves its object or overlaps goes to the staged path, which reports or handles it. **Rejected: the same arm in `copy_pair`.** That is inlined in `run_ops`, and the larger function cost 3 to 4 percent more instructions on designs that make no such copy (m16 17 768 to 18 495 per clock, identical IR).
- **The form of #1059, 32 statements, instructions per clock, 2 000 to 12 000 clocks, all threads, Cranelift bench build, `--tier=auto`:** 42 335 to 19 321 (bar 21 462, 5 percent over 20 440), without frame objects 20 212. With 32 copies of one statement on two variables: 43 090 to 19 605.
- **Every form, simulation thread only, 50 000 to 250 000 clocks, before and after at auto:** slice 39 466 to 17 369, concatenation of slices 86 770 to 34 044, slice of a record field 40 020 to 17 370, whole 512-bit vector 34 805 to 18 214, wide slice 61 124 to 33 274, whole record 13 044 to 9 112. Forced compiled: slice 17 524 to 5 477, concatenation 39 943 to 9 046. The other forms tried (elements, fields, equality, gates, arithmetic, conversions, calls, signals) move under 0.5 percent.
- **Still dearer than without frame objects at auto:** whole record 1.18x, about 43 instructions per statement; most forms 1.01 to 1.04x, about 10 instructions per statement from the failed frame lookup in `slots_of`, which frame objects pay on most interpreter accesses. Testing the object flag first adds a branch for every other frame access in the dispatch: not tried. Forced compiled, every form but `wide_eq`, `sig_rec` and one that reads no object is cheaper with them.
- **Open:** one form that reads no composite variable and has identical ops pays 340 instructions per clock (8 523 to 8 863) with frame objects, in the kernel functions and not in `run_ops`. Not explained (#1062).
- **What it costs real designs: little.** Interpreter tier, where windows repeat exactly, instructions head to fix: GRLIB 0.999, Microwatt 0.997, `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` 0.993, `vai_window_gen_interlock`, `sc5_fifo_repack`, `sc5_timestamp` and `hdlm_lfsr` 1.000 (2 rounds on the small ones, 1 on the others). At auto, 2 rounds with an A/A in the same sitting: all nine between 0.956 and 1.003, the A/A between 0.959 and 1.006, so at auto this is noise and the bar of 0.5 percent is met. Start-up to T0 at the interpreter tier moves 0.9995 to 1.0007 on the three tests that read highest at auto. One earlier single round read GRLIB 1.009 and `sc5_timestamp` 1.012; neither repeated. `rec_pair` 123 996 to 123 798, m9 17 976 unchanged, m15 25 695 to 25 697, m16 17 768 unchanged, per clock on the simulation thread. The cliff is large on a block of many slices or copies between variables and rare in these nine.
- **Not measured:** cycles with a useful band (none decided: 2 rounds, `cyc` 0.955 to 1.036 against A/A 0.946 to 1.020).


## Compiling `Kind::Frame` in a first-level build: killed at its bars (yavs-clift, #1046, 2026-11-02, branch `perf/iterative`)

- **Question:** with the cold block layout on the branch, does `Tune::FIRST.frame = true` (the knob that lifts the refusal of `Kind::Frame` functions, 1c4778df) pay? No budget change, no size cap.
- **Bars, set first:** Microwatt whole-run instructions down at least 5 percent and cycles not up beyond the paired band; GRLIB instructions and cycles not up beyond their bands; no small test's cold CPU up over 1 percent; no other test's instructions up over 1 percent.
- **Decision: killed, reverted (af7d6f43).** One test fails the last bar in both harnesses: `uvvm_axistream_vvc`.
- **Cause, the one of "Cranelift tier, round 11" again:** with `frame=1` a trace of `uvvm_axistream_vvc` compiles `wait_until_given_time_after_rising_edge` (131 IR, `Kind::Frame`) and `fetch_command_and_prepare_executor` (248 IR) in frame mode. Frame-mode code moves every process that calls them into the interpreter's loop for compiled code. The cold block layout did not change that; it only made Microwatt's big bodies pay.

  | `uvvm_axistream_vvc`, on / off | instructions | cycles | CPU |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | `run.py` warm, medians | 1.024 | 1.049 | |
  | `run.py` cold | 1.026 | 1.042 | 1.029 |
  | all threads, fresh world each run, 9 rounds | 1.038 [1.012, 1.065] | 1.038 [1.017, 1.060] | 1.035 [1.015, 1.055] |
  | all threads, warm world, 9 rounds | 1.014 [1.006, 1.022] | 1.044 [1.031, 1.056] | 1.040 [1.025, 1.055] |

  A single traced cold run read 0.936 in instructions: the compile outcome of this test varies from run to run (#673), so read the rounds, not one run. Code bytes: 535 KB against 281 KB cold (different functions compile), 541 against 580 warm.
- **What did gain (warm worlds only):** Microwatt whole run, all threads, `window.py --full --inherit`, pristine world per variant, 2 warm-ups, 3 rounds, core 9: instructions 0.870 (0.870, 0.870, 0.871), cycles 0.936 [band +-1.3 percent], IPC 1.82 to 1.68, L1i per 1000 1.03 to 1.48, branch misses per 1000 3.96 to 4.47, wall 223.7 s to 210.2 s. The bar was met there (5 percent in instructions, cycles down beyond the band).
- **A first cold run gains nothing, as the 2 percent budget refuses the Frame processes:** Microwatt, fresh world, `YAVS_AUTO_TRACE=1`: no `Kind::Frame` function compiled with `frame=1` (`execute1_1`, `popcnt_a`, `decode1_1`, `rotator_0`, `multiply_0` refused 87 to 132 times each, "fits at" 48 to 57 s of a run that was seen for 20 to 26 s). Instructions 0.999, cycles 0.996, CPU 0.988 (one pair, other jobs on the host; read only the compile outcome). `rec_pair` at `auto` (2.6 s, 7 runs, core 11): 49.55 G instructions against 49.54 G, wall 2.66 s against 2.62 s: `comb` stays interpreted.
- **Other bars, all met:** GRLIB whole run, 4 rounds, all threads: cycles 1.009 [+-2.2], instructions 1.001; simulation thread: cycles 1.000 [+-4.1], instructions 0.997. Nine windows, 3 rounds, simulation thread: instructions 1.000 (GRLIB), 0.927 (Microwatt), between 0.973 and 1.008 on the other seven; cycle geomean 0.993 [+-2.0]. The seven small windows again with compile threads counted (4 rounds): instructions 0.988 to 1.009, `hdlm_lfsr` the highest; its A/A (the same variant twice, 10 rounds) reads 1.034 and on/off 1.002, so that test cannot resolve 1 percent (#673). Five small tests plus `sc5_timestamp` and `fletcher_bufferreader`, cold, fresh world, 9 rounds, CPU on/off: 0.987 to 1.012; the highest, `sc5_fifo_repack` 1.012 [0.998, 1.027], read 0.996 [0.987, 1.006] over 25 rounds. Peak RSS unchanged (geomean 1.000 warm, 1.002 cold over 41 tests). `run.py`, 41 tests without GRLIB, `--tier=auto` against itself with the knob off: geomeans warm instructions 0.989, cycles 0.989; cold instructions 0.998, CPU 0.990, cycles 0.999. Other tests that read above 1.01 in that sitting did not repeat in 9 paired rounds: `uvvm_util_rand` (1.031 warm; 1.002 cold, 0.998 warm), `vai_window_gen_interlock` (1.019 cold; 1.002), `poc_arith_addw` (1.016 warm; 0.999 cold, 0.947 warm with a wide band); `vunit_logging` reads 1.015 warm in both (a 0.02 s run).
- **Results cannot change:** difftest 613 of 613 on interpreter, Cranelift, `yavs-auto`, `yavs-auto-warm` and `yavs-auto` at `--tier-heat=0,0,0` (every function compiled at first sight, so the Frame bodies run), 1 and 4 threads, shuffled; external lists 995 and 455 pass; `cargo test --workspace` and the `clift` tests of `yavs`, `yavs-clift` and `yavs-llvm` green; CI run 41389772379 green on all platforms, Windows and arm included. All on the flip commit, before the revert.
- **What a budget change does (a measuring aid, not kept):** the hidden `--tier-heat=2000,40000,1000` (the default thresholds with budget 0). It is not a Frame-only knob: it drops the budget and the payback rule for every function, and `Tune::frame` has no effect under it (`rec_pair` 33.77 G with `frame=0`, 33.71 G with `frame=1`). `rec_pair`, 7 runs, core 11: instructions 33.71 G against 49.54 G (0.680), wall 1.97 s against 2.62 s (0.752), peak RSS 36 MB against 26. Microwatt cold, fresh world, 2 rounds, other jobs on the host, against the default with `frame=1`: instructions 0.898 [0.892, 0.904], CPU 0.962 [0.74, 1.25], undecidable; code 15.6 MB against 10.6. The cold gain on `rec_pair` and Microwatt is in the budget, not in `Tune::frame`, and has not been tested on the other 40 tests.
- **A follow-up that has not been tried:** compile `Kind::Frame` only for processes (the Microwatt gain is in `execute1_1`, `decode2_1` and the like), not for subprograms that processes call (`wait_until_given_time_after_rising_edge`), which is where `uvvm_axistream_vvc` loses. That is a size-free, kind-based rule; it needs the same bars and `uvvm_axistream_vvc` added to the guard list.
- **Not covered:** `neorv32_coremark` (no RISC-V compiler on this host), LLVM, thread counts other than 1 and 4 in difftest, `uvvm_axistream_vvc` with `Kind::Frame` limited as above.

## Lane C, cheap general items: array `case` dispatch kept, four items not (#1051, lane of #1046, 2026-11-02, branch `perf/iterative`)

Written by Claude. Step 7 of the iterative plan. Bar per item, fixed before coding, Cranelift `--tier=auto`, simulation thread, window instructions: at least 0.5 percent down on at least three of the nine tests, no test up more than 0.3 percent, generated bytes up at most 1 percent. An item under 0.5 percent in the count stops there. A is `383ac32e`, the base of the branch when the work began (it has since merged main; merge base now `2c523cd8`), so the numbers do not include other lanes.

- **One window cannot decide this bar.** The compile outcome of `auto` moved identical binaries by up to 2 percent in instructions (`vai_window_gen_interlock` 8 percent over eight worlds, `hdlm_lfsr` 7), more than the bar. Medians of three worlds per variant, and where a row stayed in doubt, eight worlds, plus the two deterministic cells: `--tier=interp` and forced compiled (`--tier-heat=1,0,0`). Cycles are not used: `window.py` read the first variant slow (#1055).
- **Count, dynamic ops at the window's end on the interpreter (percent of ops, `op-census` with throwaway counters), by rank:**

  | item | count | verdict |
  |---|---|---|
  | signal read CSE | repeated scalar reads in one activation 0.12 to 7.63, vector reads 0.00 to 1.57: an upper bound | built, killed at its bar |
  | `LEq` from array `case` chains | 1.05 GRLIB, 1.27 Microwatt, 1.31 `neorv32_single_cache`, 0 elsewhere | **kept** |
  | range facts | `Check` kinds 0.6 to 6.8, but what a wider analysis removes is 0.00 to 0.38 of ops on six of seven tests, 3.04 on `hdlm_lfsr` alone (GRLIB, Microwatt not counted) | stopped at the count |
  | scalar `case` dispatch | tests saved by halving against a chain, 0.77 on `fletcher_bufferreader`, at most 0.32 elsewhere, negative on four | built on top of the kept item, killed |
  | trigger forms (#647) | `SigAttr` 0.00 on all nine, `SigLastValue` at most 0.02: #1001 left nothing that runs | stopped at the count |

- **Kept: `Inst::LKey`, one key for a `case` on a logic vector.** Up to 63 elements and every choice a known constant: the value becomes a number when all its elements are '0' or '1', and -1 otherwise, and an ordinary `Inst::Case` dispatches on it. A choice holding another value (`"XXXX"`, `"UU01"`) stays a compare, reached from the default, so a value with a metavalue takes exactly what it took, and a repeated key keeps the chain. Sim1's idea of an exact integer map for short arrays, ours from the bit-planes. Instructions, three worlds: `grlib_leon3mp` 0.9947, `microwatt_coremark` 0.9875, `neorv32_single_cache` 0.9912 (0.9906 in a second sitting). Generated bytes, all compiled: GRLIB 0.986, Microwatt 0.990, NEORV32 0.959, none up. Design `case_vector`: 52837 ops to 37030, held in `perf.rs`.
- **Rows over the 0.3 ceiling, and why they do not count:** `vai_window_gen_interlock` read 1.015 and 1.010 at three worlds; eight worlds each read 0.977. It runs no array `case`: interpreter 215.15 and 215.08 G, forced compiled 59.08 and 59.08 G. `fletcher_bufferreader` 1.004 in one sitting and 1.000 in another, 12.60 and 12.60 G interpreted, 11.85 and 11.85 G forced compiled. `sc5_timestamp` 1.002, 0.996. `hdlm_lfsr` 0.999, 1.002, with 7 percent between worlds of one binary. These tests have no array `case`, so the differences are compile outcome.
- **Killed: signal read CSE.** Forward availability over the blocks, a suspension clears it, scalar reads only. It removes real reads (30 M of 2145 M ops on Microwatt, 4.9 M of 366 M on `sc5_fifo_repack`) but half stay as a `Move`. Interpreter instructions: `sc5_fifo_repack` 0.982, `neorv32_single_cache` 0.996, GRLIB 0.997, the rest level. At `auto`: GRLIB 0.998, Microwatt 0.996, `neorv32_single_cache` 0.998, `sc5_fifo_repack` 0.998, `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` 1.006. The larger falls on `vai_window_gen_interlock` and `hdlm_lfsr` are compile outcome: their ops did not move. No three tests reach 0.5, one is over the ceiling. Most repeated reads are not available at all: `hdlm_lfsr` repeats them across a loop with different elements between.
- **Killed: `Inst::Case` as a binary tree in Cranelift.** Against the kept item, three worlds: `neorv32_single_cache` 0.9994, others level within noise. Bytes down 0.0 to 0.2 percent. GRLIB and Microwatt were stopped unfinished, since two tests cannot meet a bar of three. Worth another look if case tables grow, since the kept item adds arms.
- **Correctness.** New corpus test `process/case_vector_values`: metavalues against choices of '0' and '1' and the reverse, 'L' and 'H', both directions, BIT_VECTOR, slices, named constants, 63 and 64 elements, a case with no others; both references agree. Difftest 614 of 614 at 1 and 4 threads, shuffled, on interpreter, Cranelift and Cranelift auto, on this commit. External lists sim1 995, sim2 455 pass (run with the tree on top; it touched only `Inst::Case` in Cranelift, since removed). Edge forms: no code of theirs changed; their corpus tests are in that difftest.
- **Not known:** the gain in cycles (#1055, and instructions only in this entry). LLVM has no fast path for `LKey`: it steps the interpreter there. The new test and the edge tests pass on it, the rest of difftest was not run on LLVM, no LLVM instruction counts. `wait until v(2) = '1'` (#647 item 2) is a level compare the `SigAttr` count does not see, so its share is not measured. Vector read CSE was not built: the temporary a read fills may be written later. Range facts were measured only by running the existing analysis on every function, its compile cost not measured; patch kept outside the repository, as are read CSE and the tree.

## Compiling `Kind::Frame` processes, not subprograms, in a first-level build: kept (yavs-clift, #1046, 2026-11-02, branch `perf/iterative`)

- **Question:** the follow-up of "Compiling `Kind::Frame` in a first-level build: killed at its bars". `Tune::FIRST.frame` is on for processes only; a `Kind::Frame` subprogram (a function or procedure that processes call) stays interpreted (new `Tune::frame_calls`, off for `FIRST`, on for the LLVM values; `YAVS_FIRST_TUNE=frame_calls=1` brings back the all-Frame behaviour of 1c4778df). `Worker::need` decides by the kind of the function's process (`base_of`). No budget change, no size cap.
- **Bars, set first:** Microwatt whole-run warm instructions at most 0.95 and cycles not above 1.0 (band); `uvvm_axistream_vvc` instructions and cycles within 0.5 percent or their band; GRLIB not up beyond its bands; no other test up over 1 percent in instructions, confirmed by paired rounds; small tests' cold CPU not up over 1 percent; `hdlm_lfsr` and `vai_window_gen_interlock` read against their A/A.
- **Decision: kept.** All met on 3a51c68e plus this change (the branch had moved to 2333f08d, a case-dispatch commit, before the push; the measurements are on 3a51c68e). Cranelift bench build, `--tier=auto`, all threads counted (compile threads included), one pinned core of 9 to 15 per sitting, pristine world per variant, `window.py` paired per-round ratios, the knob off being `YAVS_FIRST_TUNE=frame=0` of the same binary.
- **`uvvm_axistream_vvc`, the test that killed the all-Frame step:** with this change `wait_until_given_time_after_rising_edge` (131 IR) is not compiled (a cold trace compiles it only with `frame_calls=1`). Warm, 9 rounds: instructions 0.998, cycles 0.992 [+-1.0 percent]. Cold, fresh world each run, 9 rounds: instructions 0.994, cycles 0.997 [+-3.3 percent]. In the same sittings `frame_calls=1` read instructions 1.050 and 1.041, cycles 1.064 and 1.036, so the cause was the subprograms.
- **Microwatt whole run, warm** (`window.py --full --inherit`, 2 warm-ups, 3 rounds, core 11): instructions 0.870 (0.870, 0.870, 0.870), cycles 0.949 [+-0.9 percent] (0.945, 0.950, 0.951), IPC 1.84 to 1.68, L1i per 1000 1.26 to 1.67, branch misses per 1000 3.98 to 4.56, wall 222.1 s to 210.5 s. The same as the all-Frame step in instructions (0.870), so none of the Microwatt gain was in a subprogram.
- **GRLIB whole run, 5 rounds:** warm instructions 0.998, cycles 1.004 [+-2.8]; cold (fresh world each run) 1.000 and 1.003 [+-2.1].
- **Five small tests plus `sc5_timestamp` and `fletcher_bufferreader`, cold, 9 rounds, all threads:** instructions 0.997 to 1.002, cycles 0.996 to 1.012 with bands of +-0.8 to 2.1 (geomean 1.004 [+-0.4]); warm 0.987 to 1.009 in instructions (geomean 0.998). `sc5_fifo_repack` cold cycles read 1.012 in 9 rounds and 1.000 [+-0.8] in 25. `hdlm_lfsr` and `vai_window_gen_interlock`, 10 rounds with the knob on twice: instructions 0.972 to 1.002 for both copies of the knob, warm and cold (warm `hdlm_lfsr` reads 0.972 and 0.980 against off, so that test cannot resolve 1 percent, #673).
- **Breadth:** `run.py --compare`, 41 tests without GRLIB (`neorv32_coremark` needs a RISC-V compiler this host does not have, `uvvm_rand_perf` is excluded), `auto` and `auto-cold`, knob off against on, the guard's own counted instructions: geomeans warm 1.00, cold 1.00; wall 0.98 and 1.00; CPU 1.01 and 1.00; the tool lists no slowdown (instructions over 1.05, or wall over 1.10 and 0.05 s). Tests that read over 1.01 in a counted run (mostly runs of 0.1 s, 0.2 G instructions: `hdlm_unsigned_divider` 1.03, `hdlm_ring_buffer` 1.02, `olo_intf_i2c_master` 1.02, `vai_pe_array` 1.02, cold `sc5_fifo_repack` 1.03) were run again in paired rounds, warm 9 and cold 9 (13 tests) and 15 rounds with the knob on twice (5 tests): between 0.94 and 1.04 warm and 0.97 to 1.02 cold, and the two copies of the knob on differ from each other as much (`olo_fix_cordic_rot` warm 1.038 and 0.990, `hdlm_ring_buffer` 0.959 and 0.941), so those are the noise of the compile threads' counts on short runs, not this change.
- **Results cannot change:** difftest 613 of 613 on interpreter, Cranelift, `yavs-auto`, `yavs-auto-warm` and `yavs-auto` at `--tier-heat=0,0,0`, 1 and 4 threads shuffled; external lists 995 and 455 pass; `cargo test --workspace`, clippy with `-D warnings` and the `clift` tests of `yavs` and `yavs-clift` green.
- **What it does not do:** a first cold run still compiles none of the big Frame processes. The 2 percent compile budget refuses them (traced for Microwatt in that entry); `rec_pair` at `auto`, cold, 5 rounds, is 49.611 G with the knob on and off. The gain is in warm worlds (a repeated regression, the profile and cache of earlier runs). Not covered: `neorv32_coremark`, LLVM, thread counts other than 1 and 4 in difftest, Windows and arm by hand (CI).
- **Open, for the maintainer:** a Frame-only budget factor for the first cold run was measured separately and is not part of this change.

## A compile budget factor for `Kind::Frame` processes: kept (yavs-clift, #1046, 2026-11-02, branch `perf/iterative`)

- **Question:** the open item of the entry above. `Worker::factor` gives a `Kind::Frame` process (a large combinational one) `FRAME_BUDGET = 4` times the 2 percent compile budget (`Some(_) if self.kind(id) == Kind::Frame`, after the compute, rtl and native cases), so that the big ones may compile in a first cold run. A maintainer decision under rule 44: the change lowers runtime, so it is kept with its numbers. One commit, revertible alone.
- **Measured** as an environment knob in a binary otherwise equal to 0e32edd9, factor 4 against 1 (the value before this change); Cranelift bench build, `--tier=auto`, all threads counted, paired rounds, one pinned core of 9 to 15.
- **`rec_pair`, cold, 7 rounds:** instructions 0.916 [0.910, 0.922], cycles 0.929 [0.911, 0.948], CPU 0.934. Factors 4, 16 and 50 all read about 0.917; factor 2 does nothing (CPU 0.984, instructions 1.000). **Warm, 7 rounds:** instructions 0.691, cycles 0.763, CPU 0.765.
- **Microwatt, cold whole run, 3 rounds:** instructions 0.899, cycles 0.963 [+-1.8], wall 226 s to 219 s, L1i misses per 1000 instructions 1.04 to 1.38.
- **Five small tests, cold, 9 rounds:** instructions 1.000 to 1.003, cycles 0.993 to 1.012 (geomean 1.002 [+-0.5]): level. `run.py --compare`, 41 tests, cold: geomean instructions 1.00, CPU 1.00, wall 1.00; `uvvm_axistream_vvc`, `vai_window_gen_interlock`, `hdlm_ring_buffer` and `poc_arith_addw` read up once in a counted run and 0.99 to 1.00 in 9 paired rounds.
- **What got worse:** nothing found in cold. The warm `run.py` CPU geomean read 1.05 (runs of 0.01 to 0.2 s, CPU quantised); it was not repeated in paired rounds, so it is neither confirmed nor ruled out.
- **Why 4 and not more:** the payback rule (a Frame process needs 12 times its price seen) puts `rec_pair`'s `comb` at 1.25 s of a 2.5 s run whatever the factor, so the gain stays at 0.92; the budget only decides whether it may then compile (it needs 3.1 times the 2 percent at that moment). In Microwatt `execute1_1`, `loadstore1_1` and `loadstore1_2`, the biggest, are still refused at factors 4 and 16 by the "leave the compiled code" rule, a different gate.
- **Not re-measured here:** this entry applies the measured patch; the commit got a sanity run on `rec_pair` that the factor takes effect, and the correctness gates (difftest on all tiers, external lists, `cargo test --workspace`, clippy, CI on every platform) below.

## Shape as a compile-time fact (yavs-ir, yavs-clift, #1063, lane of #1046, 2026-11-02)

Written by Claude. All four commits are on `perf/iterative` (commits 1, 2 and 4 first; commit 3 with two interpreter fixes, maintainer, 2026-11-02). Each commit has its own numbers, measured on `perf/inv-shape` with all four; one more was built and dropped.

- **Census first.** Shape work (`FieldOf`, `SubtypeCheck`, `DopeLen`, `LayoutWord`, `Pos`, `SlicePos`, `Field`) is 9.5 percent of GRLIB's interpreted ops to 700 us and 3.6 percent of Microwatt's to 300 us. `LayoutOf` no longer runs on Microwatt (copies fold it); its share of bytes is code that runs rarely. The largest single source on GRLIB was the SDRAM model's `state_register` (16 percent of all ops, two instances), whose copy had no facts of its declarative part at all.
- **1. Nested subprograms' slot addresses (`decl.rs`).** A nested procedure that `Index`es an `AddrOf Up` address by a constant (a word of a variable's slot) made the whole slot an escape, so every word of it was poisoned before the declarative part ran, and its first branch on `2 ** col_bits` was unknown: no facts. Such a derived address is now followed like the address itself; its uses are classified, it escapes nothing. Sound for the same reason the rest of `nested_writes` is: every use of the derived register is seen. Test: `perf/spec_nested_mem.vhd` (copy equal to shared code, ops 52 425 to 51 221, bound 51 800).
- **2. Length of a gate result (`native_len`).** Ruling (maintainer, 2026-11-02): a `SubtypeCheck` folds only when the lengths are proven equal at compile time. A `std_logic_1164` or `numeric_std` gate, `not` or `to_x01` family on vectors has its operands' length only when both are known and equal; other lengths give no fact, so the native's report and the target's check stay. `ieee::parse` now ignores the `@n` a native with a fallback carries, which kept `native_len` from ever seeing `numeric_std` gates. `tests/gate_lengths.rs`: a shorter target, unequal operands (both packages), a longer `to_x01 (not a)` target and a generic that makes one instance 9 wide still fail at the statement with the same message on the interpreter, forced compiled and auto, and the #1005 tests (`record_lengths.rs`) stay green.
- **3. Gates as `LogicOp` (`Opt::gate_results`).** Such a gate whose result only the read of its data takes becomes a `LogicOp` into a block of its own (no call, no fat pair, no descriptor), computed straight in Cranelift and block by block in the interpreter. It lowers compiled instructions; it first raised the interpreter's, traced and reduced below.
- **4. Offset `LCopy` in 64 bits (`lcopy_inline`).** The run-time offset form of a process's `LCopy` of up to 64 elements shifts the low word right and the second block's word left by `64 - s` as two shifts (`1`, then `s ^ 63`), so offset 0 needs no branch; nothing in the generator uses `i128` any more. `clift_lcopy_shapes.rs` adds 1 to 64 elements at run-time offsets around block edges, onto another variable and onto itself.
- **Dropped: a constant offset for the fields before the first descriptor-sized field** (`Ty::static_field_offset`). Built, measured, made GRLIB worse (interpreter +0.35 percent, auto +1.0 percent instructions): the `Index` it makes replaces the interpreter's fused `LayoutOf` and `Field` op while the `LayoutOf` stays for other reads. **Not built: static-first field order**, which would change `Layout` and so waves, VHPI, DAP and foreign records and every cache key, with the prefix it would extend already shown to lower nothing; **and `LogicOp` written straight into the target**, which needs a merge form of `LogicOp` (an IR change) for about 15 to 20 of the 55 instructions left per 8-bit statement.
- **Numbers.** Simulation-thread instructions of the windows (GRLIB 300 to 700 us, Microwatt 300 to 800 us), Cranelift bench builds, untimed on CCD0, a fresh copy of one pristine warm world per binary; ratio to the commit before, cumulative in brackets.


  | commit | GRLIB clift | GRLIB interp | Microwatt clift | Microwatt interp |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 1. nested slot addresses | 0.9838 | 0.9885 | 0.9998 | 1.0002 |
  | 2. gate result lengths | 0.9984 (0.9823) | 0.9984 (0.9870) | 0.9973 (0.9971) | 0.9967 (0.9969) |
  | 3. gates as `LogicOp` | 0.9983 (0.9806) | 1.0014 (0.9883) | 0.9993 (0.9964) | 1.0008 (0.9977) |
  | 4. offset `LCopy` | 0.9918 (0.9725) | 1.0000 (0.9884) | 0.9752 (0.9717) | (0.9977) |

  Rows 3 and 4 were measured with commit 3 present; the set without it was measured separately, see below. Base: GRLIB 103.08 G forced compiled, 125.32 G interpreted; Microwatt 121.22 G and 169.87 G. Interpreted runs repeat to 0.01 percent. Bytes of machine code, forced compiled to 300 us: GRLIB 27.01 to 26.48 MB (0.980), Microwatt 16.05 to 15.81 MB (0.985), commits 3 and 4 nearly all of it.
- **`--tier=auto` decides nothing at one round.** The same binary read 108.32, 108.77 and 109.21 G on GRLIB in three fresh worlds and 107.86 to 110.42 G for commit 4, Microwatt 140.6 to 149.1 G: what the policy compiles moves the count by more than these changes do. Against one or two base runs the head reads 0.973 to 0.996 on GRLIB and 0.977 to 0.985 on Microwatt (commit 3 alone once 0.94); nothing better than "not worse" is claimed for auto. Cycles: see the timed rows on #1063.
- **Costs (cold and warm guards, `run.py --compare` of the base and the rebased head, 42 tests, one run each, cores 4 to 7 of CCD0 so wall is not valid):** whole-run instructions, compile threads included, warm 0.97 to 1.04 and cold 0.98 to 1.04 per test; GRLIB 1.00 warm and 0.99 cold, `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 1.00 and 1.03, `sc5_fifo_repack` 1.00 and 1.00. Over 1.02 in one run: `vai_window_gen_interlock` warm 1.04, `uvvm_util_rand` cold 1.04, `hdlm_axi_crossbar` warm 1.03, `uvvm_axistream_vvc` cold 1.03; not rerun in paired rounds, so not separated from the compile threads' noise on short runs. The optimiser runs one more analysis per function with a gate native, and `nested_writes` a small fixpoint. GRLIB peak RSS, whole run at auto, second and third run of a fresh world: 393 to 396 MB and 341 to 349 MB, under the 552 MB bound.
- **What got worse (commit 3, before the interpreter fix below).** On the interpreter: GRLIB +0.14 percent and Microwatt +0.08 percent instructions, though the statement itself falls (`v.c := v.a xor v.b` 684 to 588 interpreted, 267 to 55 compiled). Traced below.
- **Without commit 3 (commits 1, 2 and 4, first landed on `perf/iterative`).** Window instructions of the simulation thread, `--threads 1`, Cranelift bench builds, one round, core 2 (instructions only), base `1c67c47b`: forced compiled GRLIB 122.73 to 122.12 G (0.995), Microwatt 149.20 to 145.89 G (0.978); interpreted GRLIB 128.18 to 126.55 G (0.987), Microwatt 176.96 to 176.43 G (0.997). These are smaller than the cumulative column above because commit 3, which carried part of the compiled gain there, is not in this set, and the tier flags differ (`--tier=clift` here). `--tier=auto` was not measured for this set.
- **Commit 3, traced (2026-11-02).** The interpreter cost came from the new `logic_blocks`: on a GRLIB stretch (`tools/stepcount --ops`) `LogicGate` took 385 instructions per op against 169 for the native call it replaced, 261 of them in `logic_blocks` (address arithmetic, two operand lookups, a result lookup and an indirect call per 64-element block). Reading each operand once and writing once, a `match` for the gate and no address arithmetic in the first block brings the interpreter to +0.03 percent GRLIB and +0.02 percent Microwatt against the set without commit 3, and keeps the compiled gain (forced compiled GRLIB 122.12 to 121.98 G, Microwatt 145.89 to 145.52 G). Both fixes are taken with commit 3 onto `perf/iterative` (maintainer, 2026-11-02). `#[inline(never)]` of `op_lcopy` had also slipped onto `logic_blocks` in `3cd46ecd`; that was a defect; its own effect was not measured alone (with it fixed and a first rewrite of `logic_blocks`, GRLIB read 126.66 G against 126.72 G with commit 3 as written).
- **With commit 3 and the fix (all four, same method, base `1c67c47b`).** Forced compiled GRLIB 122.73 to 122.00 G (0.994), Microwatt 149.20 to 145.55 G (0.976); interpreted GRLIB 128.18 to 126.60 G (0.988), Microwatt 176.96 to 176.47 G (0.997). One round each; `--tier=auto` not measured.
- **Results cannot change:** difftest 614 of 614 on interpreter, Cranelift, `yavs-auto` and `yavs-auto-warm`, 1 and 4 threads shuffled; external lists 995 and 455; `cargo test --workspace`, fmt, clippy with `-D warnings` (also with `clift`). The #1005 length tests stay green. Waves, VHPI, DAP and foreign calls are untouched: no layout or field order changed. The compilation cache needs no new key: the facts come from the instance data and package digest a copy is already keyed by, and every stored entry's key mixes in the build (`yavs_cache::build_id`), so optimised code of an older build is never read.

## The callback rule counts a sensitivity list once (yavs-llvm `auto.rs`, #1046, 2026-11-02, branch `perf/inv-leave`)

- **Question:** in Microwatt `execute1_1`, `loadstore1_1` and `loadstore1_2` (14.3 percent of a cold run's sampled time, `execute1_1` alone 8.8) stay interpreted under `Tune::frame` and `FRAME_BUDGET` because `too_many_callbacks` refuses them: 295 of 2790, 204 of 1319 and 191 of 1807 instructions "leave". Of those 267, 191 and 174 are the `WaitOn`s of the sensitivity list, which compiled code never runs one by one: `yavs_rt_wait_same` skips the whole wait (forced compiled, `YAVS_COUNTERS=pc`: no `wait_same` refusal and no `WaitOn` callback in 377 k activations of `execute1_1`). What does leave is about 10 stepped `SigGather`/`SigScatter` per activation, as in the processes the rule lets through (`decode2_1` 6.9, `loadstore1_3` 8.7).
- **Change:** with a first-level generator (`Tune::wait_same`, on for `FIRST`, off for the LLVM values, `YAVS_FIRST_TUNE=wait_same=0|1`) a wait `yavs_interp::static_wait` finds counts once in `callbacks`. The rule stays one in ten. A maintainer decision under rule 44; one commit, revertible alone.
- **History:** the same idea was tried on 2026-10-24 for `counter_increment` of `neorv32_single_min` and dropped (38.9 G against 38.3 G). Now `neorv32_single_min` reads 0.998 in instructions warm, 9 paired rounds.
- **What it admits (cold, traced, 42 tests):** only GRLIB `p0` (2047 IR) and `neorv32_single_min` `request` (119 IR), plus Microwatt's three, which all compile in a first cold run with the knob on. `rtl_ram` (the case of #507) does not reach the rule any more.
- **Measured** (one Cranelift bench binary, knob off against on, `window.py`, pristine worlds, all threads, host load 25 to 70, so cycles are undecidable everywhere): Microwatt whole run warm instructions 0.956 (0.945, 0.946, 0.978), the same as forcing the three (0.956), cycles 0.929 [+-23.5]; GRLIB warm 0.997, cycles 1.074 [+-15.5]; `uvvm_axistream_vvc` warm 1.000, cycles 1.015 [+-4.0]; 41 tests head against candidate geomean instructions 0.99 warm, 1.00 cold; GRLIB cold 0.999. Cold `uvvm_axistream_vvc` read 1.01 over 9 runs head against candidate, where the rule changes nothing (A/A not run yet).
- **Results cannot change:** policy only. Difftest 614 of 614 on interpreter, Cranelift, `yavs-auto`, `yavs-auto-warm` and `yavs-auto` at `--tier-heat=0,0,0`, 1 and 4 threads shuffled; external lists 995 and 455 pass; `cargo test --workspace` and the `clift` tests of `yavs`, `yavs-clift`, `yavs-llvm` green; clippy with and without `clift`.
- **Not known:** cycles on a quiet host; Microwatt cold whole-run timing; LLVM.
## Record signal images and gathers into the variable (yavs-kernel `image.rs`, yavs-interp `gather.rs`, yavs-ir `opt.rs`, #1065, 2026-11-02, branch `perf/inv-mirror2`)

- **Question:** a whole record gather reads every leaf every time, though few change between gathers. Can the kernel keep the value in the layout the process code reads, written only where a leaf changed (an idea from sim2's signal values), and can `v := r` read the signal into `v` without its temporary (an idea from sim1's lowering, which yavs did not have either)?
- **Two commits.** First, `Opt::gather_into`: `Zero t; SigGather t; Copy v <- t` becomes `SigGather v` when only those read the frame temporary `t`. It stands alone. Second, record images: one image per signal set and leaf layout (`ImageSpec`), shared by every process that asks with the same spec; a process asks after 16 whole gathers, the kernel installs it serially before the next update, writes the leaves that changed after the update from the runs `Signal::changed` lists (and after the guards; `wake_sole` writes the images of the signal it takes out of `changed_sigs`), and a whole gather is one copy. Every 1024 copies a process compares the leaves written since with a quarter of the leaves its copies stood for and lets the image go when writing costs more; the last process to go stops the writes and unwatches the signal if only the image watched it. Overlapping leaves (two fields tied to one actual) get no image. Part gathers (an element of an array of records) read leaf by leaf as before.
- **Why after the update, not where `cur` is stored:** force, deposit, ports and conversions come through `changed` with no code of their own, and the parallel update never touches an image. Writing at each store of `cur` was suggested (round 2 expert); with exact runs (`fine`) and the lost sole-waiter wake removed, the pass left is `Images::push`, 0.8 percent of Microwatt's interpreter instructions, so it was not built.
- **State:** per kernel signal, not per process: the image (the value's size), the item list (24 bytes an item, twice), a `Vec` and a flag on `Signal`, a bit per signal. Microwatt at 800 us: 82 images, 109 KB; GRLIB: 109 images, 160 KB.
- **First version and what it taught:** forcing exact runs (`fine`) on every imaged signal cost `rec_pair` 6 percent (its record changes in many places every clock, so every waiter scan walks many runs), and keeping it watched after the image went cost 0.6 percent; `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` lost 8 percent before the give-up rule (9.8 leaves written per gather). All three are fixed in the final version.
- **At stake on the base (1c67c47b), window instructions / cycles, simulation thread:** Microwatt: gather 5.7 / 4.5 percent interpreted, 6.9 / 5.2 at `auto`, 7.1 / 5.2 all compiled; scatter 8.6 to 10.8 / 6.3 to 8.1; the same-value test of direct drives 9.8 to 12.5 / 5.3 to 7.2. GRLIB: gather 2.7 / 4.4 interpreted, 3.1 / 4.2 at `auto`; scatter 3.9 to 4.3 / 5.0 to 5.3; same-value test 5.9 to 6.0 / 3.3 to 3.4. Images touch the gather only; scatter and the same-value test are the larger part now.
- **Measured (Cranelift bench builds, base 1c67c47b against this branch):** Microwatt window instructions interpreted 0.952, `auto` 0.944, all compiled 0.948 (one world each; `sig_gather` 10.0 G to 1.8 G, `Images::push` +1.4 G of 168 G). `window.py`, nine tests, `auto`, 3 paired rounds, instructions (median): GRLIB 0.975, Microwatt 0.950, fletcher_bufferreader 0.984, fletcher_bufferwriter_512 0.988, vai_window_gen_interlock 0.989, hdlm_lfsr 0.968, sc5_fifo_repack 1.003, sc5_timestamp 1.008, neorv32_single_cache 1.015; the same binary with images off: 1.002, 0.965, 1.004, 1.004, 1.003, 0.953, 1.001, 0.999, 1.003. Microwatt and hdlm_lfsr at `auto` move between worlds by up to 8 percent (Microwatt 145 to 157 G in each variant), so their `auto` rows decide nothing; the interpreted and all-compiled rows do. The host load was 17 to 100 that day: cycle bands were up to +-128 percent, so no cycle verdict. `rec_pair` whole run, 5 rounds: `auto` 0.998, all compiled 0.997. Guards, `run.py --compare`, 8 tests, 3 runs, warm and cold: wall 0.99 and 0.99, instructions 0.99 and 0.99, fletcher_bufferreader 0.96 and 0.97; peak RSS level. The m_idiom probe of the round 2 study: 20000 clocks, interpreted, 1.204 G to 0.948 G instructions.
- **Whole runs, all threads, `auto`, warm, 3 paired rounds (load 10 to 15):** GRLIB instructions 0.965, cycles 0.910 [+-38 percent]; Microwatt instructions 0.942, cycles 0.984 [+-11.8 percent], wall 245.0 s to 241.1 s. Both cycle bands include 1.0: undecidable. Branch misses per 1000 instructions rose 3 and 4 percent.
- **Gather into the variable alone:** about 0.5 percent of Microwatt's interpreted instructions (0.956 with both, 0.961 with images alone) and 0.25 percent of `rec_pair` (interpreted, no cache); it saves less than its estimate since frame objects (step 1) came. It reads each whole record once instead of zeroing, reading and copying. `YAVS_NO_GATHER_INTO` acts when a function is optimised: code from a warm cache keeps the form it was stored with.
- **Correctness:** difftest 615 of 615 with `YAVS_IMAGE_AFTER=1 YAVS_IMAGE_CHECK=1` (every copy compared with the leaves, internal error on a difference) on interpreter, Cranelift, `yavs-auto` and `yavs-auto-warm`, 1 and 4 threads, shuffled; external lists 995 and 455 pass with the same knobs; new corpus test `composite/sigrec_image` (collapsed `in` ports of a record and of an element of an array of records, a port with a conversion, two fields tied to one actual, force and release of a leaf and of the whole record, integer, real, time, enumeration, string and null leaves, arrays of records whole, by element and by slice), `crates/yavs/tests/image.rs` (images on from the first gather and off: output and waves the same at 1 and 4 threads, shuffled).

## Cranelift: frame-mode addresses of unknown space found inline (yavs-clift, #1046, 2026-11-02)

Written by Claude. On branch `perf/iterative` (maintainer, 2026-11-02); whether it reaches `main` is the maintainer's decision. Study and numbers: the lowering redesign comment on #1046.

- **Decision:** frame-mode code probes the object table (`Mem::objs`, keyed by the address's own space) inline before `yavs_rt_host` for an address with no space fact, the call cold, as the LLVM lowering does since #527 (this replaces the plain call of #634 in Cranelift frame mode). A pointer loaded from a frame slot that every 8-byte `Store` fills with the address of one frame offset (`slot_targets`) is compared once with that address at its use and then read as the frame's own bytes. Both are guesses tested at the use: a miss takes the old lookup, so no result can change.
- **Why:** on GRLIB forced compiled the runtime lookup was about 107 instructions a lookup, 7 percent of an exact window and 30 percent of what generated code ran; 78 percent of lookups found an object already in the table, 18 percent were the descriptor of a variable sized by a generic in shared code (frame bytes reached through a pointer in another slot).
- **Measured (prototype 2ddfdce9 on 7dfdcc40):** exact window of 3 000 kernel cycles, instructions 0.953, lookups 89 649 to 6 025; `window.py` forced compiled GRLIB cycles 0.932 (+-6.3 percent), Microwatt 0.998, instructions 0.953 and 0.984; at `--tier=auto` level (geomean cycles 1.005 +-2.8 percent, instructions 1.002; Microwatt instructions 1.015, vai 1.027, not explained). Costs: bytes 1.106, compile and elaboration instructions 1.071.

## A fused byte drive in the interpreter (yavs-interp, #1046, 2026-11-02, branch `perf/inv-bytedrive`)

- **Question:** an integer, enumeration or real assignment ran as `StoreSlot` (time), `StoreSlot` (value) and `Drive` (or a `Zero`, a `StoreSlot` of the value and the `Drive`), the general `drive_at` path, while the scalar logic assignment is one op (`LSetDrive`). Per statement in the interpreter (`window.py`-style probe, 32 statements in a process, minus the empty process): unchanged integer 580 instructions, changed 1005.
- **Change:** `Op::ByteDrive`, found by the predecoder's `peephole` for a waveform in the frame (`opt/slots.rs`) that nothing else reads (`frame_wave_is_private`): the value `Store` and the one-element `Drive` become the op, the `Zero` and the time `Store` are not run. With no `Zero` (integer and real: two 8-byte stores cover the waveform) the time `Store` starts the match and the first `Drive` after it must be the waveform's. Zero delay on a lone byte signal calls `Ctx::assign_bytes_now`, which holds the direct-driver skip test (`Signal::direct_same_bytes`); a delay calls `Ctx::assign_bytes`; a reference of several parts or another kind of signal zeroes the waveform, stores the time and replays the IR from the value `Store` (`replay_lset_drive`, as `LSetDrive` does). Compiled code is not entered between the dropped head and the op (`Code::no_tier`) and does not use the op: it runs the IR and calls the host's `Drive`.
- **Out of line, on purpose:** the first version had the body in the dispatch loop. It lowered the integer probe more (same 278, changed 705) but raised the instructions of windows that do not use it by 0.7 to 0.9 percent in the interpreter (`vai_window_gen_interlock`, `sc5_fifo_repack`): a new arm moves the loop's code generation (as `ZeroReadVec` did, #668). Out of line the empty process costs 6725 instructions a clock against 6745 before, and the probe 334 and 759.
- **Measured** (one Cranelift bench binary per side, base 98a756cf, `window.py`, 3 rounds, paired medians of instructions; load 20 to 30, cycles undecidable). `--tier=interp`: `sc5_timestamp` 0.961, `fletcher_bufferwriter_512` 0.994, `vai_window_gen_interlock` 0.988, `grlib_leon3mp` 0.993, `microwatt_coremark` 0.990, `sc5_fifo_repack` 0.977, geomean 0.984. `--tier=auto`: timestamp 0.983, writer 0.983, vai 0.974, GRLIB 1.000, Microwatt 1.028 (rounds 0.989, 1.018, 1.079: what `auto` compiles moves it more than the op does), fifo 0.999, geomean 0.994. Per statement (instructions, minus the empty process, base against this branch): interpreter unchanged integer 580 to 334, changed 998 to 751, unchanged `std_ulogic` 276 to 272, changed 632 to 626; forced compiled 269 and 657 integer, 191 and 505 `std_ulogic`, identical: the compiled tier never runs the op.
- **What did not improve:** the changed integer drive in compiled code (657 on this base, 655 earlier, up from 606 when the direct byte skip test was added, which finds no match on a changing value) is the host's `Drive` step, not this op. A byte fast path in the host's `Drive` (`Host::step`, next to the logic one) is the candidate; not built.
- **Results cannot change:** difftest 615 of 615 on interpreter, Cranelift, `yavs-auto` and `yavs-auto-warm`, 1 and 4 threads shuffled; external lists 995 and 455; `cargo test --workspace`, fmt, clippy with `-D warnings` with and without `clift`. `crates/yavs/tests/slots.rs` `byte_drives_run_as_one_op_and_replay_what_the_fast_path_leaves` prints the same with the pass off and checks the op in the dump; removing the waveform head of the replay makes it fail.

## Facts of a process copy

**Decision.** A specialised copy of a process is made per instance data and per `yavs_ir::InstFacts`: the form the kernel keeps each instance signal in that the body names (codes, planes, bytes, element size, length). A process reaches its body through the function id it switches to, with no test per entry, and instances with equal facts share a body. Cranelift's frame-mode code of a copy reads a signal by that form without testing it; run addresses stay read through the view. Facts are made at the switch from the machine's table (`Machine::inst_facts`) and only for a tier that compiles copies. `--tier=clift` has no copies, so it has no facts: that needs copies under the eager tier first.

**Why it holds.** A signal's `cur` and `codes` are replaced only in `SimControl::settle`, before any process runs; force, release, deposit and resolved updates write those buffers in place (`crates/yavs-kernel/tests/signal_forms.rs`, and a debug assertion in `Host::view`). So every signal may have a form fact, forced and multi-source ones included.

**Rejected.** Code per instance with addresses as constants, chosen by a test at each entry: the test cost more than it saved and the extra bodies cost the front end (design study of the post-elaboration prototype).

## `--tier=auto`: a function the generator has no native-frame variant for gets frame-mode code once compiled code calls it

**Decision.** `native_set` is the static rule for which functions run on native frames. The Cranelift lowering refuses more: a layout read from a runtime descriptor (`LayoutOf`), an integer power (`BinRange Pow`), and every function that must call a refused one directly. A `Part::Native` compile that returns no code (`native` 0, no `run`) is therefore not a compile: `Worker::compile_part` remembers the refusal (`no_native`, per generator rank) and charges and lists nothing. `Worker::compile` then makes the function's frame-mode code instead, but only when a function that calls it already has compiled code (`entered_from_code`: frame-mode code, or published native-frame code). Otherwise the function stays interpreted and `declined`; `Worker::see` asks for it again once a caller is compiled. `native_ok` (native set and no refusal among the functions it reaches) replaces the bare `native_set` test where the part is chosen (`natural_part`, `tree`), so a caller of a refused function is a root with frame-mode code. `kind_of`, `factor` and `charge` keep the static test: a function's kind and price do not change because the generator refused it.

**Why.** Before, the refused function was picked and "compiled" as native-frame code again and again, charged each time, and never got frame-mode code, so every call to it from compiled code was an exit into the interpreter for the whole run. The refusal shows at lowering time, before code generation, so a warm run finds it without compiling and links the frame-mode code from the cache. The condition on a compiled caller is the one the first version lacked: frame-mode code of a function called by the interpreter alone is entered through a seam that costs about what the code saves (the reason `Tune::frame_calls` is off), and one with a loop of natives, called from interpreted callers, ran 1.4 times the instructions of the interpreter on a CPU benchmark. A call from compiled code is a step out of that code either way, and landing in code instead of an interpreter frame saves the body.

**The same refusal depends on the compile set.** A callee outside the set the policy is compiling together (`Generator::tree`) is called through `Mem::ntab`, so its caller gets a native variant that never reaches it (it is published only when its native callees exist, `ready`); a callee inside the set that is refused makes its caller refused. An eager compile of a caller alone and the auto compile of its tree can differ for that reason.

**Not done.** A native variant built earlier with an indirect call to a function found refused later stays unpublished (`ready`); its callers go through the interpreter as before. A short refused function (under `rt::SHORT`, no loop) is still left interpreted by the shortness rule, which no longer has the waiver for functions called natively.

## Shape facts in process copies (`opt/slots.rs`, `opt/decl.rs`, 2026-11-02)

**Decision.** Constant-size temporaries are frame bytes in a process with nested subprograms too: a nested subprogram reaches the frame through `AddrOf Up` below the lowered frame, so the bytes past it are as private as in any other process. And what the declarative part leaves in the frame counts as written by the body only when a block the body can reach writes it (`Opt::reached_from`), not by block number: the lowering splices the declarations of a process's signal copies in behind the first blocks of the body, and those stores kept the descriptors of the copies from being facts.

**Why.** A generic-sized vector drive in GRLIB's SDRAM model kept a wave object in temporary memory only because the model's process has nested procedures; the length checks of `iu3`'s signal copies stayed run-time checks only because of the block number of their declaration.

A formal array or record parameter of a locally static subtype reads its descriptor from the constant pool in the body, as an array variable does: every call passes the formal's own bounds (`param_dope`, LRM 4.2.2.3), so the pointer in the slot adds nothing. `ahb_slv_dec_cache` of GRLIB spent 11 percent of compiled code's instructions on a descriptor it could have known.
## Drive from compiled code: the byte one-pass path and the thin Cranelift call site (yavs-kernel, yavs-clift, #1046, 2026-11-03)

Written by Claude. On branch `perf/inv-cdrive-r2` off `perf/iterative` afbb0d12 (maintainer, 2026-11-02); whether it reaches `perf/iterative` is the maintainer's decision. Results: small and mixed, stated plainly below.

- **Decision 1 (`Ctx::assign_direct_bytes`):** an idle direct byte driver (integer, enumeration, real; `DriverInfo::bdirect`) takes a zero-delay one-element assignment in one pass, as `assign_direct_code` does for logic: the driver and element checks, the per-process quiet bit, the signal's element size, then the skip test or one `OutB` entry (`direct_bytes_entry`, shared with `assign_bytes_fast`). `direct_drive_now` tries it before `assign_bytes_now`. Same entries, skips and deltas.
- **Decision 2 (`yavs_rt_drive_f`, only where the copy has no facts for the target):** a `Drive` of one waveform element at a constant reference of 1 to 64 elements to a signal the function entry's table test covers, with the waveform in the frame (16 bytes at least inside it or its composite variable) or in the temporary area, passes the handle, the driver, the count, the inertial bit, the waveform's address and the bytes readable there. The callee finds the form in `TierSig` and reads the element after that (`direct_drive_wave`); a waveform not all in reach goes to the interpreter (`yavs_rt_signal`). A process copy whose facts name the target's form keeps its constant call of "Facts of a process copy". `sig_entry` skips the table test for a constant reference the entry's test covers, for every instruction that asks for an entry.
- **Measured, probe, forced compiled, instructions per statement:** shared code (base e2bb9aad): integer same value 269.1 to 227.7, changed 662.2 to 608.6; vector of 8 same 347.4 to 317.6, changed 971.5 to 942.6; generated code of one integer drive about 57 to 31. Process copy with facts (generic-parameterised probe, `YAVS_SPEC_AFTER=2`, base afbb0d12, decision 1 only): integer same 273.5 to 267.4, changed 688.6 to 644.0; vector of 8 same 355.0 to 359.0 (worse by 4, code layout). Batched scalar logic drives (a different path) unchanged.
- **Measured, whole design (GRLIB exact window, `--tier=auto`, 3 000 kernel cycles, base afbb0d12 / last commit; stepped windows of two runs overlapped on the host):** 37 561 to 38 054 instructions per kernel cycle (+1.3 percent): drive host category 5 304 to 5 131, generated code 4 530 to 4 406, but interpreter dispatch 7 365 to 8 129, which is what `auto` had compiled by the window (tier-up timing, not this change; the drive callbacks of the window were 20 005 and 18 799). On the older base e2bb9aad the same window read 37 994 to 37 525 (-1.2 percent) with the thin call (before facts). `window.py`, 3 paired rounds, `--tier=auto`: instructions geomean 0.996 (GRLIB 1.000, Microwatt 0.993, hdlm_lfsr 0.982, neorv32 1.007), cycles undecidable (geomean 0.981, band 3.5 percent). Microwatt stepped pieces on e2bb9aad: 190.9 M to 189.4 M and 193.2 M to 191.6 M instructions (-0.8 percent).
- **What it shows:** a skipped drive costs 150 to 260 host instructions (the drive callback 250 per call, `direct_drive_bits` 146 per entry) and 98 percent of GRLIB's zero-delay drives are skips; the call site was about 25 instructions of each, and with facts it was already constant. The lever left is the compare in compiled code (design in the local plan `cdrive.md`): not built, it needs per-driver state kept in step by every push path (maintainer's ruling, #634).
- **Correctness:** difftest 615 of 615 on interpreter, Cranelift, `yavs-auto` and `yavs-auto-warm`, 1 and 4 threads, shuffled; external lists 995 and 455 pass; `cargo test --workspace` and `-p yavs-clift -p yavs --features clift`, and clippy with and without `clift`, clean. `direct_paths.rs` (`random_bytes`, `forced_byte_drivers`) takes the one-pass path for its zero-delay assignments in the fast run and compares with the general path, forces, releases and deposits included.

## Logic rows read in place

A value has no plane offset, so the lowering reads a row of a logic array of arrays or a logic slice by copying it into a temporary (`Alloc`, `LCopy`), and `a(i).f(j)(k)` then takes one element of the copy. The optimiser now reads the source instead (`yavs-ir` `opt/place.rs`; no switch turns it off, the tests run the pass directly and the designs of `crates/yavs/tests/place.rs` check their own results). It is an optimiser pass and not a change of the lowering so that the read stays where it was, with a proof that nothing wrote between, and so that every tier gets it.

The temporary goes only when all of these hold: it is defined once and read by nothing but the copy and the forwarded readers; the copy starts at element 0 of it; every reader is after the copy in the same basic block; between them is nothing that can write what the source names (no call, `Stmt`, suspension or store, except into a block allocated after the copy) and no new value of the source or its offset; the reader provably stays inside the copied run, by constants or as `n - 1 - pos` with `pos` a position in the descriptor of `n` elements. A temporary reads as `U` past the run, the source as its neighbour, so an unproved reader keeps the copy. A copy out of the temporary (`LCopy d, do, t, to, m`) reads the source directly, since `LCopy` reads before it writes in every tier and so handles overlap (`a(0 to 3) := a(1 to 4)`); its run is inside by constants or by lengths equal or checked equal by a `SubtypeCheck` between the two. A value that crosses a wait, a statement end or a write, an argument and a wave object keep the copy. An impure index function that writes the prefix is a call between the two, so it reads what it read before. No check moves or goes, so errors and their order are unchanged and length checks stay at the assignment (#1005).


## Drive compare in compiled code (yavs-kernel, yavs-clift, perf/inv-inlcmp, 2026-11-03)

Written by Claude. Built as a prototype for the numbers of the maintainer's ruling on per-driver state kept in step by every push path; taken onto the perf branch by the maintainer's ruling (user, 2026-11-03), after CI.

- **Gate on copies (user, 2026-11-03).** `YAVS_SPEC_ALL` stays, the difftest candidate `yavs-clift-check` runs on the whole corpus in the `clift` job of CI (Linux, 1 and 4 threads shuffled), and the check counts only kept drives of the skip's kernel driver. Why: the other tiers reach hardly any process copy on the corpus, and copies also carry facts and shape facts. The check tests the skip, not the value: a value wrong before the drive (an optimiser bug on a copy) passes the check and shows only against `.expected`.

- **Decision.** A zero-delay drive at a constant reference in a process copy compares the value with the signal's current value in generated code and, when equal, makes no call. No copy of a value and no epoch: the compare reads `cur`, which changes only while no process runs. What the kernel's test asks besides `cur` is one word per process (`ProcState::gate`, bit per driver of the machine): the driver is direct on a signal that allows skipping (fixed), no direct entry of the kernel driver in this run (a bit goes at the push, and generated code zeroes the word before it keeps a drive whose bit is open or that has no bit; a closed bit means every bit of that kernel driver is closed), no waveform or phantom on any direct driver of the process since the start (shut for good), no force, release or deposit applied anywhere since the start (shut for good, in `update`: only these make `cur` of a direct element differ from its driving value). A hit is one store to `Mem::skipped`; `rt::enter_on` and `call_on` call `Ctx::gate_skipped` when the code is left, so the kernel's consumers (`phantoms`, `ACT_ASSIGNED`, `empty_delta`) are unchanged.
- **Why not the design of the earlier note** (cells per driver, per-process and global epochs, a flag the kernel consumes). The census of the exact windows found no case where comparing `cur` alone differs from the full test, and no hit on a process with a scheduled direct driver, so a monotone bit serves where an epoch and a cached pointer would need invalidating. The word errs on the closed side.
- **Correctness.** `YAVS_INLCMP=check` (always in debug builds) asks the kernel's full test (`Ctx::gate_check`) at every skip and aborts on a difference. `crates/yavs/tests/compiled_gate.rs`: delayed, transport, reject and two-element waveforms, force and release with the driver's value differing from the forced one, resolved signals, disjoint parts of a vector, several drivers on one kernel driver, more than 64 drivers, deltas of a run of skips, warm cache, 1 and 4 threads, against the interpreter. The tests also take: overlapping parts through two drivers of one kernel driver, the general path of `Ctx::assign` on byte arrays, a delay on the value held, values that differ in one plane or the last element, a drive in a procedure, a kept drive past the 64 bits, drives kept for other kernel drivers, a slice placed by a generic in a warm cache, a deposit from a plugin. Corpus group `held/` holds the same ground against the references. A copy exists only for a process with one suspension point that reads instance data, from its 1024th activation (`YAVS_SPEC_AFTER`), so short tests of the default tiers take no skip: difftest candidate `yavs-clift-check` (`YAVS_SPEC_ALL`, `YAVS_SPEC_AFTER=2`, check mode) is what reaches the compare on the corpus.
- **Not served.** Shared code (no facts), interpreted drives, record scatter, run-time references, `DriveSlot`, native frames.
- **Costs.** A changed drive pays the compare before its call, about 8 instructions for a scalar, about 30 for a vector; a kept scalar on a closed gate pays 3 more; each resumption pays a load and a store; each direct entry a bounds test and a store.

## Cranelift: compiled code found before the body is made (yavs-clift `cache.rs`, `lower.rs`, perf/iterative, 2026-11-03)

- **Decision.** As the LLVM tier's pre-key (#785): a warm run finds a function's code by a key made before the body is lowered, so a hit costs a look-up and a link, not the lowering, the inliner and Cranelift's hash of the body. The key over the body (`clif-<key>.img`) stays: a miss of the pre-key, after a change elsewhere in the program, still finds the code of an unchanged body.
- **The cut.** `Jit::build`, after the route of the function is known and before any `Context`. Lowering is `Jit::lower`; `Jit::link` is the hit.
- **Inputs, all traced from `build` and `gen_func`.** `yavs_cache::KeyBuilder`: format and build. `yavs_ir::opt::fingerprint`. The target: `cranelift_codegen::VERSION` (Cranelift's own `VersionMarker` hashes nothing, so its key does not hold the version) and `compute_cache_key` of an empty function (instruction set, triple, shared flags, the features of the host). The switches: `KEYED` by value, the mode of `YAVS_INLCMP`, debug or not. `Program::identity`, the stage-cache key: types, constants, tables, every other function, ids and all; none: no pre-key. The function's id, or for a process copy its process, or for a copy of a subprogram its `copy_tag` (`Program::code_key`): a copy's id depends on the order copies are made and is in no code it has (a copy of a subprogram names it through an id symbol, "Compiled code" under "Copies of subprograms by the descriptors of their arguments"). Native or frame mode. The function as handed out, serialised, with the calls of copies of subprograms named by what they are for (`Program::code_key_bytes`, the stored form's): a copy's folded data is in its code. A copy's facts (`Program::facts`), which are in nothing else. The route: per native callee (by `Program::code_key`), through the table or directly, and a direct callee's own pre-key, since its body may be inlined; a chain of keys, so a callee that changes changes its callers.
- **What generation decided is stored, not keyed.** The entry (`clifpre-<key>.img`, `Pre`) names the Cranelift key, the symbols of the body in the order of its references, and the kinds of instruction it steps (the `--tier=clift` census); or that the lowering refuses the function, so a refusal is not found again by lowering. The names are in terms of any run, since the module's ids follow the order of the compiles: a callback or a variant by symbol, module data by its bytes and alignment. A hit declares them in an empty `ir::Function` in that order and calls Cranelift's `try_finish_recompile`: code is stored once, the entry stays small.
- **Switches.** `NO_PRE` (`DUMP`, `CLIF`, `ASM`, `CODEDIR`: they want the code made or put source locations in it; `NATIVE_MAX`: what it gives depends on what was compiled before) turn pre-keys off. `every_switch_of_the_lowering_is_accounted_for` reads the sources of the lowering and of `rt.rs`, `regs.rs`, `native.rs`: a new variable fails until it is in a list.
- **A caller that misses over a linked callee.** The inliner needs the callee's body. `Jit::body_of` lowers it then, with the route the variant was made with (`NatInfo::nats`), so the caller comes out as a cold run makes it; asking `native_of` again would see a cycle differently. Not made otherwise.
- **The check.** `YAVS_CLIFT_PREKEY_CHECK`, always on in debug builds (as `YAVS_INLCMP=check`): a hit lowers anyway, an entry that differs from what was made is an internal error that aborts, naming the function and both sides; then it links by the entry, so the link is what runs under the check too. Key and names are compared: the Cranelift key does not hold the names, and a constant of another value is the same body. A debug build's difftest and tests check every warm function; CI runs `yavs-auto-warm` on the corpus with it (the `clift` job).
- **Mutation test.** `crates/yavs/tests/clift_prekey.rs`, debug builds: `YAVS_CLIFT_PREKEY_DROP` leaves named inputs out of the key; each is left out and changed (the facts, a switch, the flags, the route, an inlined callee's body, the fingerprint, a constant, the body, the id, native or not) and the check must stop the run, and with the whole key must not. A unit test moves every input of `pre_key`. A constant left out would be a wrong result with no error at all.
- **Format.** `yavs_cache::FORMAT` stays: it is the entry header's, which did not change, and `build_id` is in every key, so no other build reads a `clifpre` entry (yavs-cache AGENTS.md section 4). `a_bad_or_foreign_entry_is_a_miss` holds another format, a damaged payload, code that has gone, and another build to a miss that lowers, prints the same and writes the entry again.
- **The first runs.** A program has an identity from the first run of a closure (see "A closure's first run names its program"), so the second run is the first to link by pre-key. Until 2026-11-11 it had one from the second run, as for LLVM: the second wrote the entries and lowered again all that the first compiled (GRLIB 183 functions, 744 ms on the compile thread with the simulation held under `--tier-compile=wait`).
- **Not done.** The adapters `c<id>` still go through the body's key: a handful of Cranelift instructions each. `FIRST_HIT` (`auto.rs`, the policy's price of a link) is left as it is: 4 us an IR instruction, where a link now costs about 0.26 us by the work clock (see `docs/STATUS.md`).
- **The reference simulator (rule 22).** It elaborates and compiles in every run and keeps no machine code between runs, as far as its file listing and a search say; nothing was taken from it.

## A closure's first run names its program (yavs `cache.rs`, yavs-elab `sim.rs`, perf/b4-r1identity, 2026-11-11)

Written by Claude.

- **Decision.** The first run of a closure stores no lowered program (the image of a closure is made on its second analysis), but its program now has the identity the second run stores it under: the stage-entry key of the same analysis, extent and requests (`Stages::identity` no longer waits for the closure's entries; `lowering_key` is made in the first run too, and only read and stored once the closure keeps entries). So the first run writes the pre-keys of what it compiles and the second links them, where it lowered all of it again before.
- **Why the name holds.** The key names the analysis (options, every file of the closure with its hash), the `Db`'s extent and digest of files after elaboration, and every request of the lowering: the same requests on the same analysis give the same program, ids and all, which the stored lowering already relied on. New is only that the first run's analysis may be made otherwise than the second's: a unit whose entry was stale is analysed from source in the first and replayed in the second (`clift_prekey.rs` `a_unit_analysed_again_in_the_first_run_keeps_the_name`). An edit changes a file's hash, so the name (`an_edit_after_the_first_run_links_nothing_stale`).
- **Not named.** A program built on a library prefix's stages (`libstage`, `LibUse`): a cold lowering of the closure does not give the same ids. A program whose constant pool is too large to store (`LoweringKey::fits`): the second run would have no name for it either. Coverage, as before.
- **The policy's price is as before.** A function of the cache costs a link (`FIRST_LINK`) only when the stage cache holds the program (`Program::named_before`): in a suite, a closure's first run finds functions other testbenches compiled, under other names, and those are hits.
- **Check.** `YAVS_CLIFT_PREKEY_CHECK` in the second run holds every entry of the first to what the lowering makes now. The difftest candidate `yavs-auto-warm` runs twice in its dropped first pass, so CI's checked warm job links what a first run compiled, through a stored program, on the whole corpus. `clift_pre_unstored` (`YAVS_COUNTERS`) counts the pre-keys made for a program not stored yet.

## Record drive compare (yavs-interp, yavs-kernel, perf/land-reccmp, 2026-11-03)

Written by Claude. Item R1 of the kernel redesign study; taken towards the perf branch by the maintainer's ruling (user, 2026-11-03), without waiting for a quiet cycle check: its gain in cycles has not been measured.

- **Decision.** A whole zero-delay scatter (`Inst::SigScatter`, no part, no reject limit) compares the value with the record image of its signals (`image.rs`), which holds them in the layout of the value: as a whole, then run by run, adjacent leaves joined. What holds its value builds no planes and makes no kernel call; the run's delta stays (`Ctx::gate_skipped`). No new state in the kernel but a counter: the image exists for gathers and is shared with them. A plan asks after `IMAGE_AFTER` scatters that could compare (`YAVS_IMAGE_AFTER`).
- **When a skip is right.** Fixed, asked once (`Ctx::drive_skip_ok`): each leaf goes through a direct driver of this process that covers it, on a signal that allows skipping. Each scatter (`Ctx::drive_clean`): for each of the plan's kernel drivers, a calm waveform, no direct entry of this run, not `exact`, no force layer. An image holds `cur`; under those conditions `cur` of a direct element is its driving value. A force layer stays after its release and `exact` after a deposit, so such a signal goes on asking the kernel leaf by leaf for the rest of the run (its image is then let go by the review). Runs of one scatter are disjoint (`fits`), so an entry of an earlier run does not touch a later run's skip.
- **With the drive compare in compiled code.** They share no state but the idempotent note of a skip. A scatter leaves compiled code (`TierHost::step` then, the signal callback now, and not at all on a hit since "Record images in compiled code"), and `rt::batch_pure` does not list it, so kept drives are handed over first and show as direct entries; an entry a scatter makes closes the gate at its push. A hit of the inline compare makes no entry, so it does not disturb the scatter's test.
- **Review.** Every `IMAGE_REVIEW` scatters, the image's leaf writes since the last review, at `CMP_WRITE_COST` leaves each, against the leaves spared: if they cost more, this plan releases the image and never asks again (a record that changes in many leaves at every drive). A scatter that could not compare counts as sparing none. The cost is run-time counts per plan, no design name or threshold on size.
- **Images: asks before releases.** `Images::install` now takes the asks of a phase before its releases. A process could find the id of an image in the phase its last other user released it; depending on the order of the requests the image was gone, its bytes empty, and the next copy or compare an internal error. A gather could reach this before this change.
- **Shape.** The compare path is out of line (`scatter_compared`): inlined into `scatter_leaves`, its run loop changed the inlining of the common path, about 1 percent of the instructions of a record design that never compares.
- **Check.** `YAVS_IMAGE_CHECK` (always in debug builds) holds every run a compare would skip against the kernel's full test (`Ctx::gate_check`, per block or element where the test takes no more) before the scatter's first entry. Difftest candidate `yavs-clift-check` runs it from the first scatter (`YAVS_IMAGE_AFTER=1`), so the CI step of the `clift` job does. The check tests the skip, not the value: `.expected` and the off run do that.
- **Tests.** `crates/yavs/tests/record_compare.rs` (images off, on, on from the first scatter with the check: output and waves the same at 1 and 4 threads, shuffled, with a floor on `Stats::scatter_spared`; compiled copies with both checks), corpus `held/held_record` against the references (one leaf at a time under the held rest, force and release under held drives, entries and waveforms of the run, delays, delays alone, parts, two sources with a swap under a held value, a resolution function, a port, a procedure, the deltas of a run that only holds), `tests/direct_paths.rs` (`drive_clean`; asks before releases), `vhpi_run.rs` (a plugin turns the compare off), `perf.rs` `rec_cmp`, `rec_cmp_drop`. Reached by no test: a driving-value force or a deposit on a record held under the compare outside `direct_paths.rs` (a direct driver has no port, and a plugin turns `skip_ok` off).
- **Not served.** Parts of a record signal, drivers that are not direct, signals forced or deposited once, values of more than `IMAGE_MAX` bytes. A compare in generated code came later: "Record images in compiled code".
- **Reference.** The study found no reference that compares a whole record; sim1 compares per net before queueing, an idea of the existing skip. No code read for this.

## Record images in compiled code (yavs-clift, yavs-interp, yavs-kernel, perf/try-recinline, 2026-11-04)

Written by Claude. Item R1b of the kernel redesign study, tried at the maintainer's request; on a side branch, for the maintainer to rule on. The gathers go beyond the study's item: `YAVS_IMAGE_INLINE=noread` shows what is left without them. Its gain in cycles has not been measured.

- **Decision.** Frame-mode Cranelift code makes a whole `SigScatter` (no part, no reject limit, constant delay 0) that holds what the record image holds a compare and no call, and a whole `SigGather` a copy of the image and no call. Everything else, a miss above all, goes through `yavs_rt_signal` as before, which compares again. `YAVS_IMAGE_INLINE` turns either off.
- **The cell.** What generated code needs is per process, so it sits in the machine: `Machine::icells`, `TierFrame::cells`, `ImageCell`. A scatter's cell is found by its driver slot, a gather's by the low bits of its leaf table (`GATHER_CELLS`; a second table with the same bits stays with the host). Generated code tests: a table at all, an image, the leaf table, for a value type with a descriptor its address, uses left, for a scatter the plan's bit. The host writes the cell after a slow scatter or gather that started, used up or ended the plan's use of it; a plan that lets its image go clears it in the same step, before the image's last user can free the bytes in the serial phase.
- **A descriptor is only trusted where it is frozen.** `MPlan::at`, the address of a descriptor found equal, also takes instance data now, not only constants. A plan with a descriptor anywhere else gets no cell.
- **The plan gate.** The gate word of the inline drive compare could not serve: 42 to 49 percent of the held scatters lie past driver slot 64, and a kept drive zeroes the whole word. The second word of `ProcState::gate`, the plan gate, has one bit per plan (`Ctx::plan_gate`, at most 64 per process, the rest stay with the host). `gate_off` takes the bits of the entry's kernel driver at every push, `shut_gate` zeroes it for good at a waveform on a direct driver and at the first force, release or deposit applied, `resumption` puts it back from `gate_base`. A plan asks once compiled code has looked at the process, and only gets its bit open in this run when `Ctx::drive_clean` holds. So an open bit says all that `drive_clean` says: calm, no entry of this run, not `exact`, no force layer. It is not closed by keeping a drive in compiled code's batch, because a scatter is not `batch_pure`: the batch is handed over before it, and those drives then close the bit at their push.
- **What a hit does.** A scatter stores `Mem::skipped` as the inline drive compare does, so the kernel hears of the skip when the code is left.
