  pools then pays its trial on 5 ms instead of 25 (the trial of an 85 ms run cost 0.7 percent of its instructions).
- **Not done: a lower pool threshold under `auto`** (agent, measured): `POOL_WORK_NS` (20 us) keeps the compiled
  batches of `rtl_lfsr` (512 registers, about 15 us estimated) inline, so its first run under `--tier=auto` loses
  the threads after compiled code is in (1.10x against 1.57x at `--threads=4`, which keeps pooling on costs it
  timed while the processes were interpreted). A floor of 5 us under `auto` took it to 1.19x but made the trial of
  `lfsr64_xor` 9 percent slower in cycles; left for a change of the threshold itself, which also concerns
  `--threads=N`.
- **Decision: static estimate = fewer than 8 processes that may run in parallel** (not serial, not postponed): one
  thread, no trial, no cache lookup (agent). Why: no batch of fewer processes can pass the pool threshold unless its
  processes are very heavy; the processes' weights are not known before the run. `ponytail:` in the code.
- **Decision: the first trial starts 10 ms after the build; the CPU count is asked when a batch first wants the
  threads; the memory is looked up after the build only past the static estimate** (agent). Why: a tiny run paid 8
  percent of its CPU time (0.13 ms) for `available_parallelism` (cgroup files) and the cache lookup when both were
  done at the start, and 2 percent more instructions for the trial's sampling; measured on the three paths after the
  change: instructions within 0.07 percent of `--threads=1`, cycles within the spread of the runs (0.1 to 0.3
  percent).
- **Decision: at most 8 threads, never more than the CPUs the process may use** (agent). Why: the largest measured
  gains flatten by 8 (`docs/parallel.md`); more is unmeasured. `ponytail:` in `threads.rs`.
- **Decision: memory = gained or not, per command line (`run_id`), kind `thr` in the work library's store**
  (agent). A run after one that did not gain starts off with its first trial after 4 s; one after a run that gained
  starts on, with four strikes and 0.1 s pauses. Written only when it changes; not with `--no-cache`. Why: a regression
  runs the same command lines again; a stale entry only shifts the first trial, it cannot change a result.
- **Decision: the run id (`elab::run_digest`, used by this memory and the `--tier=auto` profile) is a digest of the
  arguments with response files read, where the argument that gives a `runner_cfg` generic counts without its `seed`
  and `output path` fields** (user, 2026-11-09). Every other generic and argument, the test cases, `tb path` and
  `run script path` of `runner_cfg` included, still tells runs apart. Why: VUnit draws a new seed in every invocation
  unless `--seed` is given, so a command line with `-grunner_cfg` was a first run every time; and the test runner
  package passes everything in a response file, so the old digest of the raw arguments saw only the file's name and
  kept one id for a test whose flags or generics changed. The `output_path` generic (a separate generic VUnit sets
  when a testbench declares it) still counts; ids made before this change are not found again (one cold run).
- **Decision: `--threads` keeps its default of 1** (agent, for the maintainer to confirm): `auto` could become the
  default once it is measured on more hosts and test suites; under a test runner's `-p N` without a token server the
  threads of all simulations would add up.
- **Decision: under the test runner's token server every simulation gets `--threads=auto`**, a connection's cap is
  `min(N, 8) - 1` (agent, 2026-11-07, for the maintainer to confirm). Replaces `--threads=min(N, 4)`
  (`DEFAULT_MAX_THREADS`, the maintainer's stopgap of 2026-10-31 on #879 "until `--threads=auto` exists"). Why: a
  simulation whose threads do not gain gives its tokens back after its trial and asks for none until the next one, so
  the cap no longer has to protect the processor tests; a gaining one can use up to 8. `yavs.max_threads` and
  `--yavs-max-threads` take a number or `auto`.

## Copies of subprograms by the descriptors of their arguments (`opt/subcopy.rs`, `copies.rs`, 2026-11-03; landed with the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-07)

**Decision.** The last step of a specialised copy's optimisation asks, per `Call`, which `'dope` arguments have bytes it knows (the constant pool, instance data outside the parameters of `for` generates, package data the copy has, what the declarative part left in the frame, a descriptor the copy itself was made for) and calls the copy of the callee for those bytes, in a reserved slot (`Program::sub_copy`). The copy has them as `Opt::wf` facts, so its layouts, lengths, positions and checks fold, and it asks the same of its own calls.

**Why.** A record or an array of composites passed to a subprogram costs a layout at each field, through a callback or a step, and keeps the subprogram off native frames, though the descriptor never changes in a run.

**Which descriptors.** Only those of a record or of an array of composites or several dimensions (`worth_keying`): compiled code makes the layout of a plain vector inline from its length, so such a copy would save little and split the code. Only those the lowered code of the callee reads and whose slot nothing writes or lets a pointer to (`reads`). Both are properties of the type and the code, no threshold.

**Stored form.** Copy ids differ per run, so a stored copy calls the subprogram itself and lists its calls of copies with what they are for (`CopyBlob::calls`); they are made again on load. A refused copy (no slot, `YAVS_SUB_PER`) leaves the call as a call of the subprogram, which handles any descriptor.

**Rewritten last.** Every pass before it reads a callee by id, and a copy's slot is empty, so inlining, the memo and the flags see the subprogram. `Program::memo_sig` goes by `base_of`. A debug build compares every descriptor an interpreted or stepped call passes with what its copy was made for (`Machine::check_sub_args`); compiled-to-compiled calls are not covered.

**Compiled code (maintainer, 2026-11-07).** A copy's id differs between runs that make copies in another order, so compiled code never holds it: its native frames (`yavs_rt_deopt`, `yavs_rt_xstep`) and its callers (the `Mem::ntab` index, the memo of pure calls) take it from an id symbol whose address is the copy's id in this run. Cranelift: an imported function `yavs.id.<tag>.<id>` (`Jit::slot`; a function reference, since Cranelift's inliner keeps those, and the module's lookup gives the id from the name), named `Name::Slot(tag)` in a pre-key entry and declared again under this run's id when the entry is linked. LLVM: an external global `yavs.id.<tag>` defined as an absolute symbol of the run's JIT before the object is linked (`lower::id_symbol`, `Jit::define_absolute`). The pre-keys of both tiers name a copy of a subprogram by its `copy_tag` and the copies a function calls by what they are for (`Program::code_key`, `code_key_bytes`); Cranelift names a copy's code `n<subprogram>_c<tag>` and its routes by `code_key`. So a warm run whose copies have other ids links all of their code. Code of a function with no copy is as before: the id symbols are only made for copies of subprograms.
- **Why.** Keyed by its own id (the first fix of the wrong link), a copy of a subprogram compiled again whenever its id moved.
- **Cost.** A load or a constant in place of an immediate, at the slow paths of a copy's frames and at its callers' table calls and memo; Cranelift loads the id through the module's GOT on x86-64.
- **Tests.** `sub_copies.rs` `warm_runs_with_other_copy_ids_link_the_same_code` (`YAVS_COPY_SKIP` leaves the first slots empty, so every copy has another id: all linked, none lowered, the same output, the pre-key check agreeing at one and four threads); `compiled_copies_of_subprograms_are_not_linked_under_another_id` (other copies in the third run, under the check). Counters `clift_sub_linked`, `clift_sub_lowered`, `clift_sub_compiled` (`YAVS_COUNTERS`).

**Tests.** `crates/yavs/tests/sub_copies.rs`; corpus `composite/subcopy_shapes` (matrices, arrays of unconstrained arrays, records with unconstrained fields and arrays of them from package, architecture and process objects; copies called from copies, recursion, `out` and `inout`), `subcopy_generics` (instances with the same and other generics, a generate, a subprogram of the architecture that reads a generic, a signal, an access value), `subcopy_bounds` (an index error inside a copy), `subcopy_edges` (null dimensions, arrays and fields, one data under three shapes through a pure function, recursion on record slices, a generate's parameter, a heap object of a new shape per call, one record as `in` and `inout`, a signal parameter, a partly constrained formal, two instances of a generic package, textio), `subcopy_nested` (a nested function on its parent's parameter, a heap object replaced by one of another shape, a failing whole-record assignment to an `inout` formal); `tools/difftest/reach.py --counters spec_subs` is above zero on them.

**Off.** `YAVS_NO_SUBCOPY=1` (fingerprint `subcopy`), `YAVS_SUB_ALL=1` keys on plain vectors too.

## Cold optimiser cost: exact fixes and a cheaper pass set for huge bodies (yavs-ir `opt`, yavs-lower, perf/w3-t3, maintainer ruling 2026-11-07)

The cold main thread of library testbenches had risen 6 to 28 percent over the pinned baseline of wave 3, mostly in
the IR optimiser and lowering. Decisions:

- **Exact fixes first** (the same IR, checked by `YAVS_DUMPIR` over the corpus): the set of entities named by
  `'path_name`/`'instance_name` found once per `Db` borrow, not per protected variable (`Cx::named_entities`, keyed
  by the `Db`'s address, expression count and version, dropped on `Lowerer::resume`); a vectorised search for a
  coverage directive (`covdir::mentions`); a table by register in `Func::sig_history_uses`; `proc_objects`
  answers `once_before` for every block of a process of 256 blocks or more in one linear pass (dominance of the
  body, cycles and the "reaches every block" terminators; debug builds compare it with the walks on every process);
  the fixed-point loops of the optimiser reuse their buffers.
- **Huge bodies get a cheaper pass set** (maintainer, 2026-11-07): from `HUGE_BODY` = 50 000 instructions after the
  first walk, no descriptor pass (`dopes`, with its `dead_defs` and `tidy`) and no short-circuit pass of processes.
  Such a body is a testbench sequencer that runs once (`uvvm_func_cov`'s `p_main`, 114 k): the passes cost more
  than they save there. The largest processes of GRLIB and Microwatt are under 20 k, so RTL keeps every pass. The
  size is in the optimiser fingerprint; `YAVS_HUGE_BODY=1` gives every body the cheaper set (difftest runs the
  corpus that way); `opt_huge` counts the bodies. Cost: the warm run of `uvvm_func_cov` reads 2.25 against 2.21 G.
- **Not done:** a worklist for `dead_defs` liveness (gains 13 M on the huge body, loses on small ones); the second
  round of `dopes` only after a `Copy` rewrite (no short proof that nothing else gives it work).

## Parallel kernel, step 3, and `--threads=auto` round 2 (yavs-kernel `run_batch`, `learn_pooled`, `kernel/auto.rs`, #884, 2026-11-07)

- **Decision: the kernel thread waits for the workers of a pooled batch spinning** (agent): after its own pieces it
  spins until every job it spawned has ended (`spin_until`), at most `JOIN_SPIN` (50 us), and only then enters the
  scope's blocking wait. Why: that wait sleeps on a condition variable, and the wake-up of the kernel thread was 3.2 to
  5.2 us of every pooled batch (timed per batch, interpreter, 2 to 8 threads, rtl_fan and rtl_lfsr), 0.65 to 0.9 us
  spinning; the bound keeps a worker preempted on a busy core from being waited for with the CPU. Measured against the
  build before, per round paired, 7 rounds, CPUs 4-7 and 20-23: wall 0.84 to 0.95 at 4 and 8 threads on rtl_fan,
  rtl_ff and rtl_lfsr, instructions 0.2 to 0.8 percent fewer.
- **Where the threads wait** (agent, measured per pooled batch with a local timing build, interpreter): of a pooled
  batch of rtl_lfsr at 4 threads (37 us against 94 us inline) about 2 us went to the start of the last worker, 4 to 5
  to the spread of the workers' ends, 3.6 to the kernel thread's wake-up (now 0.7) and the rest to the work, whose sum
  over the threads was 1.25 times the inline time (rtl_fan 1.4 times at 4 threads, both about 1.9 at 8, where two
  threads share a core). At 8 threads on a busy host the last worker often started 25 to 60 us late (rayon's workers
  yield, then sleep, between batches), and the scope waits for every spawned job to run even when the others took all
  pieces.
- **Not done** (agent, measured): workers that spin between pooled batches for twice the usual gap (up to 0.1 or 1 ms):
  no gain resolved on this host (rtl_lfsr 0.95 to 1.05 of the join spin alone); each thread first running its own
  pieces (by rayon's thread index): the fills of lines from other cores' caches (`ls_any_fills_from_sys.local_ccx`)
  did not drop and wall stayed within the noise; 8 pieces per thread instead of 4: a shorter tail but more busy time,
  no gain.
- **Decision: a pooled batch teaches `learn_pooled` when it ran on all the threads it may use** (`SimControl::cap`:
  under `--threads=auto` its `limit`), not only on all the pool's workers (agent). Why: on half the threads no batch was
  ever learnt from (`helpers == workers` never held), so the threshold stayed where the last window on all threads left
  it.
- **Decision: when the threads start (the run, or a trial of `--threads=auto`), the first `CALIBRATE` (2) batches of at
  least 8 processes run inline with every activation timed, and a process's first sample is its cost, not half of it**
  (agent). Why: a trial began with the costs of nothing (the threads were off) or of an earlier phase: the first
  windows estimated the batches at an eighth of their time (inline probes 8.9 times the estimate on rtl_ff), and once
  the batches pool only the probes (1 in 64 batches, a sixteenth of the processes each) refresh the costs, so the
  estimate took about 0.5 s to come right.
- **Decision: thread counts are compared by pooled time over the inline time of the window's probes, both against the
  same estimates, and all the threads are kept only when they are `FEWER_PERCENT` (5) faster than half** (agent). Why:
  compared by pooled time over the estimate, the later window always ran on better estimates and looked faster, so the
  first try kept half the threads on rtl_fan and rtl_ff, which run 10 to 18 percent faster on all 8; on a near tie fewer
  threads win because hardware threads of the same cores also slow the kernel thread between batches (compiled rtl_lfsr
  is 8 to 10 percent faster on 4 threads than on 8). Tried and dropped: comparing the windows by wall time per estimated
  work of all their batches; one window of a few dozen batches is too noisy for it (rtl_ff interpreted then kept half
  the threads, 83 percent of the best fixed speedup).
- **Decision: a pooled batch counts at most twice its estimate in `learn_pooled`'s average (was 8 times); under
  `--threads=auto` a window that won resets the threshold and the average, and so does a trial of a design that won
  before** (agent). Why: compiled rtl_lfsr gains 1.8x on 4 threads, but a few pooled batches at 3 times their estimate
  when its compiled code came in raised the threshold, its batches stopped wanting the threads, and the single batches
  pooled to test the raise found the workers asleep and could not bring it down: the run lost its threads (3151 of
  4677 batches pooled). A design that never gained keeps a raised threshold, so its trials stay short. `--threads=8`
  without `auto` still has this trap (compiled rtl_lfsr pooled 3369 to 3493 of 4920 batches in some runs).
- **Measured** (`docs/parallel.md` "Round 2"): best fixed speedups up to 2.89x (rtl_fan interpreted, 8 threads) and
  1.81x for compiled rtl_lfsr at 4 (was 1.53x); `auto` on the first run 90 to 95 percent of the best fixed speedup on
  five of the six gaining cells, 85 percent on compiled rtl_lfsr (default tier against fixed runs on fresh command
  lines), remembered 93 to 102 percent; the CNN accelerator
  bench 97 percent of 1.41x; the designs that do not gain within 0.3 percent of `--threads=1` in instructions, and
  within 0.8 percent under a token server. A first run under the default tier is also the compiled tier's first run of
  that command line (its profile is per command line): measured against fixed runs on fresh command lines the
  default-tier first runs reach 91, 94 and 85 percent, and `sc5_fifo_repack` compiled, which read 12 percent slower than
  a remembered `--threads=1`, is 0.96 of a fresh one.

## `--tier-compile`: the run waits while a function compiles (yavs, yavs-llvm `auto.rs`, yavs-kernel, yavs-interp, vunit-yavs, #1123, 2026-11-07)

- **Decision: `yavs run --tier-compile=wait|background`, default `wait`** (user, 2026-11-07: "Switch + low priority",
  then the same day: the background thread off by default). Why: a user ran simulations on all cores and the computer
  locked up. Under `--tier=auto` each run had one compile thread more than `--threads`, at the simulations' priority,
  so N runs on N cores kept up to 2N threads busy. The name follows `--tier`, `--tier-max-size` and `--tier-heat`
  (an option of the tier, not of the threads), and the values say what happens (the run waits, or the compile runs
  in the background) rather than on/off: `wait` still has a tier-up thread.
- **Decision: `wait` keeps the compile on the tier-up thread and stops the simulation while it compiles, instead of
  compiling on the simulation thread** (agent). The compile thread raises a gate (`yavs_kernel::hold_simulation`) and
  compiles once a simulation thread waits at a pause point (`pause_point`, one relaxed load: the start of every delta
  cycle; `watch_tick`, the interpreter's look every 128 jumps back or calls in a long activation, out of line and
  cold; the `RECHECK` look of the loop with the tier every 256 jumps; `Host::step`, where compiled code hands the
  interpreter an instruction; the `SPIN_CHECK` trim of a process that never suspends); the gate drops before a trial, which needs the run going. Why: the policy's clocks count the
  simulation threads only (the instructions they retire, or the process CPU less the sampler's and the compile
  thread's), so a parked simulation adds nothing and compiling there distorts nothing; on the simulation thread a
  compile would count as simulation work, and the generators (LLVM's static destructors, #625) would run on threads
  that `--threads` hands batches to. What is left of the old thread is a sleeping decision thread and the sampler.
  `Tier::hot`'s wait (eager `--tier-heat`, `YAVS_AUTO_SYNC`) is a pause point too, so those modes cannot deadlock, and
  `stop` releases a compile thread that waits for the gate. Compiled code in a loop that never leaves it reaches no
  pause point; a compile then waits for it (without the `RECHECK` and `Host::step` points, a compiled loop that
  calls an interpreted function held back that function's compile for the whole run: `clift_natfall.rs`).
- **Decision: in `wait` the compiles are paced: the model's compile time spent (`Worker::spent`) at most the
  simulation time seen (`Worker::total`)** (agent; not under `--tier-heat` budget 0 or `YAVS_AUTO_SYNC`, whose runs
  wait for the compile in `Tier::hot` and stop the sampler's clock). Why: the count rule compiles what it asks for
  without a budget, and a background thread could only ever make as much as the run lasted; a waiting run has no such
  limit. Unpaced, `osvvm_axi4_random` compiled all 107 functions the count asked for (1 to 4 before, the rest still
  queued when the run ended) and ran 2.9 times as long; paced it compiles 5. Both are functions of the looks and the
  model, as the rest of the policy (#670).
- **Decision: the background thread lowers itself to the lowest OS priority at its first compile**
  (`lowest_priority`: Linux `setpriority(PRIO_PROCESS, 0, 19)`, which sets the calling thread's nice value only;
  Windows `SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_LOWEST)`; nothing on other systems, which have no
  release build) (user, 2026-11-07). The priority is never raised again. Not in `wait`: the run waits on that thread,
  and a low priority would stall it on a loaded host. A tier that `set_compile` was never called on (the crates' own
  tests) compiles alongside at the usual priority, as before.
- The sampler sends no look without work, and none timed by the wall clock (where there is no CPU clock: not Linux),
  while the simulation is held, so batches end where they would with the compile on another core and the wall time
  of a compile is never seen as simulation time; the counters `tier_waited` and `tier_alongside` (`YAVS_COUNTERS`) count the compiles of
  each kind (`crates/yavs/tests/tier_compile.rs`).
- The test runner package passes the sim option `yavs.tier_compile` as `--tier-compile` (user, 2026-11-07).
- The policy's simulation clock never sees a compile: in both modes the compile runs on the tier-up thread, which the
  clock leaves out, and a held simulation thread sleeps.
- **Measured** (cold whole runs, 5 per cell, interleaved, Cranelift bench builds; "old" is the background thread at
  the usual priority before this change; wall, median): with a second free core `wait` costs what the compiles took,
  `background` is level with old: `grlib_leon3mp` 1.18 and 1.09 of old's 23.2 s, `neorv32_dual_full` 1.24 and 1.01
  of 2.16 s, `osvvm_axi4_random` 1.50 and 1.01 of 0.82 s, `hdlm_lfsr`, `uvvm_func_cov`, `vunit_logging` 0.96 to
  1.09. On one core shared by everything (the build before the last pause points) `wait` is level with old (GRLIB
  1.00, neorv32 0.83, the small ones 0.93 to 1.12), and `background` at nice 19 gets almost no CPU to compile
  (GRLIB 12 compiles for 155, neorv32 3 for 75), so a design that gains from compiled code runs interpreted (GRLIB
  1.22) and one that does not ends sooner (neorv32 0.71, osvvm 0.77). Peak RSS is the same in every mode (GRLIB 357 to 359 MB, neorv32 145 to 177 MB): memory was
  not the cause; a compile thread adds no memory a waiting run does not. Main-thread instructions with nothing
  compiled (`--tier-heat=2000000000,0,16000`, and `--tier=interp`) are within 0.03 percent of old.
- **Decision: in the first run of a program under `wait` (no profile of an earlier run), until the looks hold
  `WAIT_LONG` (1 s) of simulation work, a function the count rule asks for and the cache does not hold waits until
  the looks saw it interpreted for `WAIT_PAYBACK` (1) times its price; the runs after it compile as before** (user,
  2026-11-07: the gate in the first run only; `Worker::unpaid`, `stops`). Why: a waiting run pays every compile in
  full, and the count rule asks for processes the looks never saw (`neorv32_dual_full` compiled 75 functions in
  0.4 s, most of them seen 0, and ran slower than `--tier=interp`; `osvvm_axi4_random` stopped 0.3 s for three
  processes seen 3 to 5 ms). A function seen for its price (the model's 45 us an IR instruction, two to three times
  what Cranelift takes) has saved its compile if the rest of the run is like the part seen. A run past `WAIT_LONG`
  compiles as before: a long run repays what the count asks for, and GRLIB's large processes, seen for their price
  only after 4 to 16 s, ran later compiled and the run slower without the limit. In every run the gate held back
  what never repays within one run, so it was never cached, and warm neorv32 ran 1.18 times as long (its cached code
  gains: 1.65 s warm against 2.4 s interpreted); in the first run only, the second run compiles what the first
  skipped and the cache fills one run later. Links of cached code are not held back, `background` and the tests'
  tier are unchanged. A function of the looks, the profile and the program, as the rest (#670).
- **Tried and not kept** (cold, paired, the same host and lanes): the gate in every run (above); a payback by kind
  (the model's payback times 0.25: GRLIB later still, `uvvm_func_cov` 1.2 to 1.3 times the cycles with the next
  item); a function seen for twice its price passing the count gate (`hdlm_lfsr` compiled `main` at 0.14 s for
  0.49 s, but short suite tests compile what they do not get back); half and twice the factor (0.5: neorv32 back to
  0.95 to 0.98, 2: like 1); the asked function seen longest for its price first (level with oldest first); a looser
  pacing, twice the simulation time or none (no better anywhere).
- **Measured** (series of three whole runs in one world from a pristine one, against `wait` before the gate, paired
  and interleaved, Cranelift bench builds, timing cores 8 to 15 under the core locks, a loaded host; medians of 6 to 12
  pairs, GRLIB 4 with a free core and 8 on one; the A/A pair of the base read 0.92 to 1.08 in medians):
  first run with a second free core / on one core: `neorv32_dual_full` 0.85 / 0.87, `osvvm_axi4_random` 0.62 / 0.68,
  GRLIB 0.95 / 0.99, `hdlm_lfsr`, `uvvm_func_cov`, `vunit_logging` 0.98 to 1.04; second run: neorv32 1.00 / 0.95,
  osvvm 1.02 / 1.08 (it compiles what the first run skipped; A/A 0.95 / 1.00, spreads 0.74 to 1.17), GRLIB 0.92 /
  1.04 (A/A 0.95 / 0.95), the small ones 0.99 to 1.06; third run: neorv32 0.85 / 0.95, osvvm 0.69 / 0.88, GRLIB 0.94 /
  1.09 (A/A 0.92 / 1.08), the small ones 0.98 to 1.04. Outputs and exit codes equal in every run.

## `--tier=auto` under `--threads`: the simulation CPU is the kernel thread's (yavs-llvm `auto.rs`, #884, 2026-11-07)

- **Decision: the simulation CPU that `--tier=auto` judges by (the profile's `base` and its `better` verdict, the warm gate
  `YAVS_AUTO_WARM_GATE`, the trials' windows, the sampler where the counters are refused) is the CPU time of the kernel
  thread, the thread that makes the tier and runs the cycle, not the process's less the compile thread's** (agent). Why:
  the pool workers of `--threads` spin between batches, so the process's CPU time measured the thread count, not the
  work: a threaded `rtl_lfsr` stored 0.8 to 1.1 s at 0.15 s of simulate wall, `sc5_fifo_repack` 2.2 s at 0.8 s (now
  0.15 and 0.8 s, as at one thread), and a run whose threads were on for fewer windows than the run before looked 3
  percent better than it was. At one thread nothing changes but the sampler's own CPU, which is no longer counted. Ceiling: when a pooled
  batch outlasts the kernel thread's join spin the kernel thread sleeps and the rest of the batch is not counted.
- **Measured:** with the inflated `base` the warm runs of short threaded designs had passed the 400 ms warm gate that the
  same design at one thread never reaches, and linked their cached code at once; with the fix they wait for the count
  gate as at one thread, and threaded warm runs of `rtl_lfsr` read about 5 to 10 percent slower in simulate wall
  (host noise of the same size: an A/A pair read 1.08). At one thread a warm gate of 100 ms made the warm runs of
  `rtl_lfsr` 6 to 11 percent faster; the gate's value is the maintainer's to decide.

## `--threads=auto` round 3 (yavs-kernel `kernel/auto.rs`, #884, 2026-11-07)

- **Decision: under `--threads=auto` the kernel looks at the clock about once a millisecond (`TICK_GAP`): the tick mask
  starts at every 4 cycles and doubles or halves at each tick to keep that gap, at most every 65536 cycles** (agent).
  Why: a fixed 256 cycles were 20 ms of `rtl_ff` at one thread (6000 delta cycles in its whole run), so the first trial
  started at twice its `START` and the windows ended up to that late. Measured (bench builds, CPUs 8-15 and 24-31,
  first runs on fresh command lines, 7 to 10 rounds, paired ratios to the build before): the interpreter 0.94 to 0.96
  of the wall time on `rtl_fan`, `rtl_ff`, `rtl_lfsr`, the default tier 0.92 to 0.96 there and on `sc5_fifo_repack`
  (bands of a few percent on a loaded host), more batches pooled per run; the designs that never pool unchanged in
  instructions (0.999 to 1.000). The cost is a clock read per millisecond.
- **Decision: a batch whose `n - 1` processes could not pass the lowest pool threshold at the dearest cost known
  (`cost_hi`, the largest process cost) is not estimated, and is timed in one such batch in 16** (agent, #858). Why:
  the estimate (a pass over the batch) and the timed samples are what `--threads=N` costs a design that never pools.
  Measured (interpreter, `--threads=4` and `8`, 5 rounds): instructions over one thread on `rtl_ram` 1.012 to 1.004,
  unchanged within 0.001 elsewhere; `lfsr64` keeps its 2 percent, since its batch of 65 is estimated at just under
  the threshold and must be estimated. The bound only rises between the recounts every 65536 cycles, so one dear
  process keeps every batch estimated, as before.
- **Rulings (user, 2026-11-07):** keep the kernel-thread CPU fix and lower the warm gate, choosing the value or rule
  that loses nowhere beyond the A/A on one-thread and threaded warm runs of the small designs, short tests of the
  real-world suite and the processor designs; land the small-batch skip (#858) and the clock tick of about a
  millisecond.
- **Decision: the warm gate stays at 400 ms for what the cache lists, and a warm run whose last run was shorter links at
  once what the cache holds of the processes that run's profile named hot (`Worker::early`), and makes copies from the
  start (`named_hot`)** (agent, under the ruling). Why: a flat lower gate lost on the library suite whose tests share a
  cache list: OSVVM warm, instructions over all threads summed over its 314 runs, 1.013 and 1.028 at 200 ms and 1.065
  at 100 ms (two 400 ms passes 0.991 apart), as the earlier choice of 400 ms found. A short program's own hot processes
  are not what other tests compiled. Measured (bench builds, warm runs 1 to 3 of fresh worlds, 6 rounds, simulate
  wall, paired; A/A within 0.95 to 1.07): one thread `rtl_lfsr` 0.80 to 0.87, `lfsr64` 0.83 to 0.86, `rtl_ff`,
  `rtl_fan`, `rtl_chain`, `sc5_fifo_repack` within the A/A; `--threads=auto` `rtl_lfsr` 0.86 to 0.92, `lfsr64` 0.83,
  `rtl_ff` 0.95 to 0.97, the others within the A/A; OSVVM warm 0.990 (cold 1.000).
  Real-world suite, warm, 12 tests with `auto` and `auto@4` (one pass on a loaded host): instructions within 0.98 to
  1.04 of the base except `sc5_timestamp` 1.17 (its copies and links come earlier, wall 0.89 and 0.95, CPU 0.88);
  `grlib_leon3mp`, `neorv32_single_min` and `poc_arith_addw` ran over the gate before and decide as before
  (instructions 1.00 to 1.01; their walls moved 0.81 to 1.01 with the host's load).

## LLVM tier removed (yavs, yavs-llvm, tools, user, 2026-11-08)

- **Decision (user, 2026-11-08: "remove LLVM"; supersedes the earlier ruling to keep it until the
  Cranelift tier's leave-anywhere work, CG3(b), is decided).** The LLVM tier is gone: the `llvm` cargo
  feature of `yavs` and `yavs-llvm`, the LLVM generator, ORC JIT, object cache, code arena, lazy library
  load and `llvm-sys`. Cranelift (`yavs-clift`, feature `clift`) is the compiled tier, as in the release
  archives since 2026-10-28. Why: an LLVM build's `--tier=auto` took 1.2 to 1.5 times the cycles of
  the Cranelift build's on GRLIB and Microwatt (warm and cold, measured once before the removal), it needed a manual LLVM 21 install, and it had no
  CI job since 2026-10-30 (#898).
- **`--tier=llvm` and `--tier=auto3` are E0120** in every build, before any analysis, with a note that
  Cranelift is the compiled tier and a help line naming `--tier=auto`, `--tier=clift` and `interp`. The
  two values stay hidden in `TierArg` so the error is a diagnostic, not an unknown value. E0120 was
  widened ("a tier this yavs was built without, or one that was removed") rather than a new code.
  `--tier=auto` maps to the Cranelift policy (`clift-auto`) in every build with `clift`; without it,
  `auto` is E0120 as before.
- **E0127** (the LLVM library cannot be loaded) is retired with the tier and never reused.
- **Kept on purpose:** the crate `yavs-llvm` keeps its name and paths (a rename is a later step); its
  shared runtime (`rt.rs`, `auto.rs`, `native.rs`, `regs.rs`, `eloop.rs`, `generator.rs`, `census.rs`,
  `profile.rs`, `work.rs`, `hugezone.rs`, `perfmap.rs`) is what the Cranelift tier runs on. The policy's
  branches for a second, optimising generator (`Gens::main`, `OptLevel::Fast`/`FastRa`) stay until the
  policy work removes them. The leave-anywhere machinery stays (CG3(b) undecided).
- **Tests and tools.** Test cases and files that ran only `--tier=llvm`, `--tier=auto3` or LLVM's
  `--tier=auto` were deleted with the tier; the same cases under `--tier=clift` and `clift-auto` stay.
  The user ruled the same day that they are ported, and they were: `crates/yavs/tests/clift_parity.rs`
  (the designs of the deleted `compiled_*` and `auto_warm` tests, each against the interpreter on
  `clift`, `clift-auto` and four threads, with the host-call counters where the test is about a path
  compiled code takes alone), the `--tier=auto` cases of `cli.rs` and `vhpi_run.rs`, the Cranelift
  tiers added back to the lists of `edge_idioms`, `casetab`, `coverage`, `coverage_fec`, `sink`,
  `slots`, `lean_calls`, `rss` and `value_move`, and the policy tests of the sampled model that
  needed a generator (`crates/yavs-llvm/src/auto/policy_tests.rs`, on a stub first-level generator,
  with the prices of Cranelift). Not ported, because the mechanism is gone: the object cache of the
  LLVM tier, its measuring aids (`YAVS_LLVM_KINDS`, `YAVS_LLVM_ABLATE`), the mixed LLVM and Cranelift
  calls, `level_for` and the `FastRa` recompile of the optimising generator.
  difftest loses `yavs-llvm`, `yavs-auto3`, `yavs-auto3-eager`, `yavs-mixed`; realbench loses the
  tiers `llvm` and `auto3`, and its `codegen` phase now times `--tier=clift` (was `--tier=llvm`);
  waveq's third tier is `clift`; `tools/conformance/run.py --llvm` is `--compiled` (the auto and clift
  tiers). History (release notes, earlier decisions, `docs/STATUS.md`, conformance records) is not
  rewritten.
- **Dependencies:** LLVM 21 is no longer an approved manual dependency (root `AGENTS.md` rule 9,
  `docs/plan.md`).

## Crate `yavs-llvm` renamed `yavs-rt` (yavs-rt, yavs, yavs-clift, tools, user, 2026-11-10)

- **Decision (user, batch 3 housekeeping, 2026-11-10).** `crates/yavs-llvm` is `crates/yavs-rt` (package
  `yavs-rt`, library `yavs_rt`), the runtime of the compiled tier, with its history (`git mv`). The
  name was left from the LLVM tier removed on 2026-11-08, and the entry above kept it only until this
  step. Every reference in code, Cargo features (`yavs/clift`, `op-census`, `table-check`), tools and
  current documentation follows; dated entries and results below keep the old name as written.
- **No behaviour change.** The machine code of the difftest corpus (665 tests, 25 096 files from
  `YAVS_CLIFT_CODEDIR`, `--tier=clift --no-cache`) is byte for byte that of the build before the rename.
  The Rust symbols of the runtime change prefix (`yavs_rt::`), which `tools/realbench/replay.py` matches.
- **Pruned with it (no behaviour change).** With Cranelift the only generator these were dead:
  `Gens` and its `main` generator (`AutoTier::start_with` takes the one `Generator`), `OptLevel` (all
  levels, `Fast`/`FastRa` included, and `Generator::level_for` and the level argument of `compile` and
  of `Note`), the recompile of a function that ran at `Fast` (`Worker::fast`, `PAYBACK_RA`, `ra_cost`),
  the recompile at O2 of a function seen running compiled (`Heat::o2_threshold`, `Tune::o2_after`,
  `O2_AFTER`, the `see` upgrade parameter), `Tune::MAIN` with the LLVM price tables `HIT` and `HIT_GEN`
  and the clocked-process rule `rtl`, the generator ranks (`nat_by` and `no_native` are flags), and
  `YAVS_FIRST_ONLY`. What stays of the second compile (`o2` in the code) is the whole function again
  after code made with blocks listed as never run ran too much of them (`take_again`). The unit tests
  that read `Tune::MAIN` were dropped with it. The count-rule worker of the unit tests, which had no
  generator and so the old tuning and prices, now has the stub generator and the Cranelift tuning like
  every worker of a run; one test's long-run share (`next_asked`) is derived from the two prices.

## `--threads=auto` round 4 (yavs-kernel, #884, 2026-11-08)

- **Decision: the batch last estimated at or below the lowest pool threshold (`SimControl::stay`: its length, first
  and last process) is taken as `small` the next 15 times it comes: no estimate, timed in one batch in 16** (agent).
  Why: a batch near the threshold passes the bound of `small` (one dear process anywhere sets `cost_hi`), so it was
  estimated at every delta cycle and a sixteenth of its activations timed, though it stays inline. Two batches with
  the same key are taken to be the same: a wrong guess changes where a batch runs, never the output. Measured
  (interpreter, all-thread instructions, no batch pooled): over one thread `lfsr64` at `--threads=4` 1.021 to 1.002,
  `rtl_bus` at `--threads=8` 1.008 to 1.001; one thread unchanged.
- **Decision: the estimate of a batch stops once its splittable work passes `pool_ns` (`sum - max` only grows), except
  before a probe of `--threads=auto`; the pieces of the pooled batch add up their processes' costs and the whole
  estimate is put together after the join, so `learn_pooled` and the windows see what they saw before** (agent).
  Why: the pass over a batch of thousands of processes ran on the kernel thread before any worker started (about
  5 percent of the kernel thread's samples on `rtl_fan` at `--threads=4`). Measured (one PGO bench build with a
  switch, both cells and an A/A cell against the switch off, CPUs 12-15 and 28-31, 8 rounds, paired): all-thread
  instructions `rtl_fan` 0.93 to 0.97, `rtl_ff` 0.96 to 0.97, `rtl_lfsr` 0.97 to 0.99 (interpreter and default
  tier, 4 and 8 threads; the designs that never pool unchanged); wall `rtl_fan` 0.82 to 0.995 in all eight
  readings (two cells of one binary in four sittings) against 0.95 to 1.09 with the switch off, the others within
  the A/A (whose own band reached 0.90 to 1.07).
- **Decision: the trace line of `--tier=auto` that serves the calibration of `work::INSTR_PER_US` pairs the kernel
  thread's instructions with the kernel thread's CPU time** (agent). Why: since round 3 the CPU time is the kernel
  thread's; the instructions were the sum over the threads running at the last look, which counted the pool's
  workers and read 0 whenever none ran at that look (it did on `rtl_lfsr` at one and at four threads). Measured
  (`rtl_lfsr`, default tier, first run, loaded host): about 9 600 instructions per CPU microsecond at one thread and
  9 000 at four; `INSTR_PER_US` (16 000) is not changed here.

## Wake plan (yavs-kernel `finish_direct`, `wake_plan`, `Waiters::plan`, wave 3 item K1, 2026-11-08)

- **Decision: a signal of at most 64 elements whose alive waiters are all resident and have no edge trigger keeps a
  wake plan, and `wake_sole` wakes from it when the value is finished, so the signal never enters `changed_sigs`**
  (agent). Why: on the CPU designs nearly every changed signal with waiters that reached `cycle` was such a signal,
  left there by `wake_sole` because it had several waiters, which `cycle` then woke through `small_list` or a
  `take_woken` scan (counted on the base, per kernel cycle, of the signals with waiters that reached `cycle`:
  Microwatt 8.1 of 8.85, neorv32_single_cache 4.0 of 4.55, GRLIB 0.14 of 0.50; GRLIB's others come from the driver
  update paths, which this does not touch). The reference simulators wake the waiters of a value from a list at
  the write; this is that list, made once from what changes only when a waiter list changes.
- **The plan:** each alive waiter once (deduplicated by registration), as process, element mask and epoch, in
  registration order. Made at the first event after the lists changed; `Plan::Slow` when an alive waiter is plain (a
  plain one is gone at its first wake) or has an edge trigger (a trigger reads signals the update may not have
  finished), or the signal is wider. Dead waiters are left out: epochs and generations only grow. Forgotten by `add`
  (`Slow` for a plain waiter), by `drop_cache` (a process left a resident wait, the same point that drops the clock's
  wake list) and by a `take_woken` that removed waiters. A process in it whose epoch moved sends the signal to `cycle`
  (waking is idempotent). Not in a shuffled run (the wake order is its run order) or while a re-armed clock generator
  waits (`skip_n`).
- **Check:** `YAVS_WAKE_CHECK=1` (`Config::wake_check`) holds every wake `wake_sole` does, by the plan or by the one-waiter
  paths, against a scan of the waiter lists (`Waiters::hit_by`) and stops with an internal error naming the processes;
  difftest's `yavs-clift-check` candidate sets it. A mutant that never forgets the plan in `add` gives a wrong result on
  `delta/wake_plan` (a late waiter is not woken), and the check names it. Whole runs under the check: Microwatt, GRLIB and
  neorv32_single_cache pass with output, exit status and the counters `cycles`, `wakes`, `events`, `process_runs`
  equal to the base. `wakes` equal also says the clock batch (which wakes no process one by one) was taken in the same
  cycles, the worry recorded under "Kernel round 22" for a wake in `finish_direct`.
- **Measured** (bench builds of f8541916 and the change, warm whole runs from one master, `--tier=auto`, main-thread
  user instructions, median of 3, spread in brackets): Microwatt 118 906 to 115 699 per kernel cycle, **0.973**
  (0.10 %, 0.18 %); neorv32_single_cache at `--tier=clift` (its `auto` count moves with the compile race) 193 045 to
  191 534, **0.992** (0.03 %, 0.01 %); GRLIB 23 689 to 23 682, 1.000 (0.31 %, 0.51 %). Waiter-list scans per run:
  Microwatt 27.6 M to 0.52 M, neorv32_single_cache 0.60 M to 0.09 M, GRLIB 322 k to 31 k. Output and exit status equal
  in every run.

## Cranelift: code that never ran, lowered cheaply, as a lab switch (yavs-clift `lower.rs`, `blockcov.rs`, wave 3 CG3(a), 2026-11-08)

Written by Claude. A lab switch, off by default; landed with wave 3 batch 2 (maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-09).

- **Decision.** `YAVS_CLIFT_CHEAP=<cov tsv>` gives the blocks a `YAVS_CLIFT_BLOCKCOV` dump lists as never run the least code (`blockcov::cheap`, `gen_func`): in frame-mode code the instructions of such a block up to its jump or the next block start are one call of `yavs_rt_steps` (each instruction as `yavs_rt_signal` steps it, a frame it pushes as `yavs_rt_step` runs it; the first answer that is not `GO` leaves), the jump itself stays inline; a native-frame variant leaves at the start of such a block (`leave_at`, the interpreter goes on with the materialised frame), but never at its first block. The block is cold as well. Before the call the code stores the preloaded registers the block reads (`addr_value`, the constant and frame address an `AddrOf` or `Const` defined once makes): compiled code never stores them, and the interpreter does not set a parameter slot's address in every frame. Without a list, or with the switch unset, the code is byte for byte the code without the change (438 bodies of 33 corpus tests under `--tier=clift`). `all` and `alt` (every block, every second block) are the difftest candidates `yavs-clift-cheap` and `yavs-clift-cheapalt`, so correctness does not rest on a list; `cb_steps` counts the calls (debug and `op-census` builds; `perf.rs` holds it at 0 by default). In `NO_PRE`: a run with the switch makes its code again.
- **Why.** Block coverage (wave 3 CG1) found 25 to 59 percent of generated bytes in blocks that never run; every such byte is compile time, which `--tier-compile=wait` puts on the critical path.
- **Measured** (cold whole runs at `--tier=auto`, `wait`, one binary, an empty list against a list from a cold coverage run of the same binary; output and exit status equal in every run). `uvvm_axistream_vvc`: frame-mode bytes 0.62, native 0.44, compile thread 0.59 in instructions, compile CPU 0.53, main thread 1.007; cycles 0.796 +-1.9 % (12 pairs, one process per core), wall 0.83. GRLIB: frame-mode 0.86, native 0.60, compile thread 0.86, compile CPU 0.91, all threads 0.976; cycles 0.927 +-4.4 % (10 pairs). Microwatt: frame-mode 0.83, native 0.88, compile thread 0.88, compile CPU 0.82, all threads 0.995; cycles 0.982 +-1.0 % (4 pairs). `neorv32_dual_full`: level (a short cold run that compiles 240 KB). Under `--tier-compile=background` `uvvm_axistream_vvc` is level (1.008 +-1.6). Native frames kept full (`YAVS_CLIFT_CHEAP_NATIVE=0`): `uvvm_axistream_vvc` cycles 0.871, GRLIB 0.985 +-3.6 (most of GRLIB's compile is native variants).
- **The cost of a wrong list.** A block the list calls never-run that does run is stepped instruction by instruction, or, in a native frame, materialises the frame at every call: with the cold list, warm runs of `uvvm_axistream_vvc` ran 1.07 times the instructions (137 000 materialisations against 2 800), GRLIB 1.14, Microwatt 1.006 (1.1 million materialisations); with a list from a coverage run of a warm world 4.6 times (2.2 million materialisations), 1.09 with native frames kept full. The run after a run without a list compiles every listed body again (`uvvm_axistream_vvc` 1.55 times the instructions of that run without the list).
- **What it is not.** No ordinary run has a list: the switch reads a file. A list from one run applied to another compiles every listed body again (a different key), and blocks that never ran in the coverage run can run in the next one (code linked from the store runs from the start of the run, code compiled in a cold run only after the interpreter ran the beginning), which then steps instruction by instruction or, in a native frame, leaves; where the list comes from is open (CG2's stored list, the interpreter's coverage before the compile), as is CG3(b), a side exit per never-run block with a recompile rule, which keeps the leave-anywhere machinery in use.

## Cranelift: a stored list of the blocks that never ran (yavs-clift `blockcov.rs`, `lower.rs`, yavs-llvm `rt.rs`, `auto.rs`, wave 3 CG2, 2026-11-09)

Written by Claude. A lab switch, off by default; landed with wave 3 batch 2 (maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-09).

- **Decision.** `YAVS_CLIFT_LIST=write` makes a run a coverage run: its compiled code records the blocks it enters (the block tables of `YAVS_CLIFT_BLOCKCOV`), stores no code, route or compiled-function list, and at the end stores per function (`func_key`: id or copy tag; `body_hash`: the function's IR) the pcs that no table of its frame-mode code or variant saw run, one text entry per program (kind `never`, keyed by the optimiser fingerprint and `program_digest`, as routes are). `YAVS_CLIFT_LIST=on`: a function made under the policy gets its line when the hash matches (`listed`); the pcs go into its pre-key (`PreInputs::list`; with the function's id before them, since cheap blocks pass the id to the step counter as a constant and two process copies of one body otherwise shared a key, #1126, found by the debug-assertions difftest of `yavs-clift-listall`; a copy of a subprogram names its id slot instead), and a stored entry under the key without the list wins over compiling cheap code, so a world that holds full code keeps it. Frame-mode code steps the listed blocks (`yavs_rt_steps`, CG3(a)); native-frame variants lay them out cold (`YAVS_CLIFT_LIST_NATIVE=cheap`: they leave there, each leave counted as 64 steps).
- **The counter.** `yavs_rt_steps` gets the function's id and IR length and counts the instructions it steps (`rt::cheap_ran`): no code in the block itself, which already calls the host. Past `YAVS_CLIFT_AGAIN` (500) instructions per IR instruction (a stepped instruction costs about 45 ns, a frame-mode compile about 26 us per IR instruction, so the stepping has then cost what the compile will) the function is queued (`take_again`), the compile thread is woken (`auto::wake_again`) and compiles its frame-mode code again through the second-compile slot (`pending.later`, `done[k][1]`), which `Jit::define` builds in full under `<symbol>_full`. At the end of the run each line gets the run's steps added (`add_steps`) and a line at its limit is dropped: a block that runs a little in every run costs its function's compile once, not a step in every run.
- **Which run writes the list.** A run whose compiled code runs from each function's first entry: `--tier-heat=1,0,0` (every function compiled at its first entry) with `YAVS_AUTO_PROFILE=off`. A list from an ordinary cold run (or the count rule at 1) calls never-run what the interpreter ran before the compile; later runs link the code from the store and run it from the start. The coverage run is not automatic: who starts it, and when, is open.
- **Measured** (exact all-thread instructions, `--tier=auto`, `wait`, one bench binary, one world per series; every default series starts with an interpreted run so that its cold run, like the run after a coverage run, is not the program's first sighting, which alone moves run 2 by about 0.75; output and exit status equal in every run). Coverage run from first entry, then cold / run 2 / run 3 / warm against the default (one series each, so about 5 percent of noise between worlds): `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 0.980 / 0.974 / 1.006 / 0.984, with native variants leaving (`cheap`) 0.887 / 1.022 / 0.978 / 0.986, no function tripped; the cold run in a sitting on one binary (8 rounds rotated, two free cores): **0.951** instructions (8 of 8 below 1), 0.932 cycles, 0.942 wall with variants leaving, 0.981 instructions without, and on one core (4 rounds) 0.942 / 0.940 / 0.952; with `--tier-compile=background` cold 0.953, runs 2 to 4 level, no trip; GRLIB 0.996 / 1.050 / 1.017 (cold / run 2 / run 3; three trips in run 2: `TO_INTEGER` and two copies of `state_register`, 7 136 IR, 0.2 s each); Microwatt 0.996 / 1.001 / 0.999 (cold / run 2 / run 3); `neorv32_dual_full` 1.005 / 1.006 / 0.944 / 0.989; `hdlm_lfsr`, `hdlm_fifo_sync`, `vunit_logging`, `uvvm_func_cov` level (one run each). The coverage run costs a run of its own: 0.98 (axistream) to 1.26 (GRLIB) of a cold run on the big designs, 2.3 on `neorv32_dual_full`, 4 to 10 on the small tests (every function they enter is compiled).
- **A list from an ordinary cold run** (contrast, axistream): cold 0.90, then 1.15, 1.20, 1.18, and level from run 5 on, once the counter has dropped the functions whose blocks ran; GRLIB 0.999 / 1.044 / 1.008.
- **What it does not do.** Runs that link their code gain nothing (the code is already made); the list pays only in runs that compile, after a coverage run. A changed function has no list (its hash differs). Native variants are not compiled again during a run; inlined copies of a variant keep its cold layout. The compile price of the policy does not know cheap blocks (it prices a listed body as full).

## `--tier-compile=wait`: compiles priced as measured, a budget, the hottest per price first, and what the rest of the run repays (yavs-llvm `auto.rs`, wave 3 policy, 2026-11-08)

Written by Claude. Landed with wave 3 batch 2 (maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-09, accepting `neorv32_dual_full` run 5 at about 1.09 of the instructions).

- **What was wrong.** Under `wait` every compile is on the run's critical path, and the pacing that limits them compared two numbers that were each off: the model's price of a Cranelift compile (45 us an IR instruction for every part) against the looks' sampled function time. Traces of 455 cold compiles (GRLIB, `neorv32_dual_full`, the window generator, `osvvm_axi4_random`, `hdlm_lfsr`): frame-mode code costs 21 to 34 us an IR instruction (median 26, 38 past 3 000 IR), native-frame code 61 rising to 148 (it makes its callees with it); the charge over the real CPU per run was 0.9 to 2.1 (`neorv32_dual_full` run 2: 819 ms charged for 392 ms). The sampled total, in the work clock's units (16 000 instructions a microsecond; the simulation ran at 8 400 on neorv32) and without the time outside functions, was 0.35 to 0.77 of the kernel thread's CPU. The two errors together held the compiles to 0.14 to 0.5 of the simulation's CPU, by accident and differently per design.
- **Decision: pacing in measured units** (agent). Each look carries the kernel thread's CPU since the look before (`Look::cpu`, also a look with nothing running; a look not sent hands it to the next), summed in `Worker::sim_us`; each compile is charged `Worker::cpu_price` (`FIRST_FRAME_US` 28 an IR instruction, native-frame code `FIRST_NATIVE_US` 55 plus one per `FIRST_NATIVE_GROWTH` 16 instructions, a link as before) in `Worker::paid`. The thresholds keep `FIRST_US_PER_INSTR` and `spent`: the sampler's budget and the first run's `unpaid` gate are unchanged. Alone (the whole simulation CPU as the budget) it compiled everything the count asked for in run 2 (`neorv32_dual_full` 27.2 G against 22.3, `osvvm_axi4_random` 18.4 against 12.3; run 3 settled at 12.6 G): the accident above had been acting as a budget.
- **Decision: a budget** (T1, agent): a body the count asked for compiles only if `paid` plus its whole price (`body_price`) fits a quarter of `sim_us` (`WAIT_SHARE`), the whole of it once the looks hold `WAIT_LONG` of work (`WAIT_LONG_SHARE`: a long run repays more, and a quarter all through cost GRLIB's first run 5 to 11 percent); links fit always; when none fits the thread waits for more looks (`tier_over_budget`). Not carried across runs: the profile format is unchanged (the cache carries what was compiled; a carried spend was not needed for the gains below).
- **Decision: the hottest per price first** (T1, agent): of the bodies the count asked for, links first, then the most seen per `body_price` among those that fit, the oldest on a tie (`next_asked`). Alone it did little; with the budget it stops a one-shot sequencer from taking the budget (`uvvm_axistream_vvc` run 2 29.4 G oldest first against 25.0).
- **Decision: what the rest of the run repays** (T4, agent): in a run with a profile (written only where the kernel thread has a CPU clock, Linux: elsewhere T4 holds nothing), a function the cache does not hold waits while its share of the looks, times the rest of the run the profile predicts (its last run's simulation CPU less `sim_us`), times `WAIT_GAIN` (0.3: settled cached code saves 0.27 to 0.41 of the time on the measured designs) and `profile::EARLY_RUNS` (the cache serves the runs after, as `repays` counts), is below its `body_price` (`unrepaid`, `tier_unrepaid`). This is what stops `osvvm_axi4_random`'s runs from each compiling 0.2 to 0.4 s of bodies seen 0 to 3 ms (its `TransactionDispatcher`s). Half and double: 0.15 level with 0.3, 0.6 run 2 and 3 of `osvvm_axi4_random` 10 and 20 percent dearer. The first run has no prediction: its `unpaid` rule is unchanged (no prior was invented).
- **`background` is unchanged**: no budget, no order, no `unrepaid` (`stops` is false); a budget on a free core would give up wall for nothing, and on a busy core nice 19 starves the thread anyway.
- **Measured** (all-thread instructions, three runs in one world from a pristine one, paired with `main` f8541916, 4 rounds, timing cores under the locks; A/A within 1 percent): `osvvm_axi4_random` run 2 0.74, run 3 0.70; `neorv32_dual_full` run 2 0.91, run 3 0.94; `uvvm_axistream_vvc` run 1 0.97, run 2 0.94, run 3 1.00; GRLIB run 1 0.96, run 2 1.00; the window generator 1.00 to 1.005; `hdlm_lfsr`, `hdlm_fifo_sync`, `vunit_logging`, `uvvm_func_cov` level. Settled warm runs (series to run 6, GRLIB to run 4, 1 to 2 rounds, where the build before compiles almost nothing a run): `osvvm_axi4_random` 0.71 to 0.73, `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 1.00 to 1.01, GRLIB runs 3 and 4 1.004 and 1.008, `neorv32_dual_full` runs 5 and 6 1.03 to 1.08 in two rounds and 1.03 and 1.00 in a third: the rest rule never compiles about 30 bodies the build before compiles by run 4 (large processes seen 4 to 25 ms of a 0.6 s sampled run), so a settled neorv32 can stay up to about 5 percent dearer; doubling or quadrupling `WAIT_GAIN` did not resolve it (1.03 to 1.10 in one round). The OSVVM suite (314 runs, all-thread instructions summed): cold 1.002, warm 0.971. By piece (the knobs on one binary): budget alone `uvvm_axistream_vvc` run 2 1.34 and run 3 1.22 (it settles later), `osvvm_axi4_random` run 2 0.86; with the order run 3 1.36 and 0.95; only with `unrepaid` does every row reach the figures above. Wall: see the batch results (a host at load 20 to 57: A/A bands of 20 to 30 percent).
- **For the maintainer:** the settled `neorv32_dual_full` above (up to about 5 percent) against the early runs' gains; a carried heat per function across runs (a profile format change, not built) is the knob that would let those bodies compile once their summed time repays. A quarter all through (`YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_LONG_SHARE=0.25`) gives `uvvm_axistream_vvc`'s first run 0.78 instead of 0.97 and costs GRLIB's first run 1.05 to 1.11; the default keeps GRLIB's.
- **Decision: per-function heat carried across runs** (user, 2026-11-09: build it first; land the policy with batch 2 only if `neorv32_dual_full`'s runs 4 to 6 no longer lose beyond the A/A while the other gains hold). The run-to-run profile is format 4 (`yavs-auto-profile 4`; a profile of format 3 is no profile, never misread): `held <rank> <us> <runs>` lines name the processes (`Program::base_of`: a copy's id is new in every run) whose functions `unrepaid` held and that stayed uncompiled, with the interpreted time the runs saw them summed and the runs in a row they were held in (`Profile::held`, `Snapshot::held`, `Worker::carried`, at most `HELD_MAX` 1 024). `unrepaid` adds the earlier runs' time (in this run's CPU per look microsecond) to what the rest of the run would save, and a process held in `WAIT_HELD_RUNS` (1) runs in a row compiles anyway, outside the budget (`Worker::overdue`, `WAIT_HELD_FREE`). The carried time alone changed nothing measurable (the held bodies are seen 0 to 25 ms a run against prices of 50 to 120 ms); the overdue rule is what compiles them.
- **Measured against the ruling** (series to run 6, all-thread instructions against main, 2 to 3 rounds per sitting, five sittings; `base2` the A/A): `neorv32_dual_full` with the default, runs 4 / 5 / 6: 0.98 [0.93-1.02] / 1.09 [1.07-1.17] / 1.00 [0.94-1.00] against the A/A's 0.96 [0.94-1.00] / 0.97 [0.96-1.00] / 1.06 [0.94-1.07] in the same sitting; run 5 stays dearer in every variant tried (the bodies the earlier runs left compile there): without the overdue rule 1.02 to 1.12 at runs 5 and 6, overdue in the budget 1.11 to 1.15 at run 5, after two runs 1.04 to 1.15, holding only bodies dearer than a quarter or a sixteenth of the rest of the run (`YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_BIG`) 1.05 to 1.09 at run 5 and 1.00 to 1.05 at run 6. `osvvm_axi4_random` run 2 0.71 holds, its later runs 0.68 to 0.98 (A/A 0.68 to 1.13); `uvvm_axistream_vvc` runs 1 and 2 0.96 and 0.94, later level. **The ruling's bar is not met at run 5: the policy does not land with batch 2.**
- **Decision: no deadline for held bodies** (user, 2026-11-09: land it, then build a count-based carried heat): `WAIT_HELD_RUNS` unset (never), so a held process compiles only once the time the runs saw it in repays it (`unrepaid` with the carried time). Cause of the later-run loss with the deadline: the bodies the earlier runs held compile in the first run with room in the pacing, a run in which the build before compiles almost nothing (`neorv32_dual_full` run 5: 206 ms of compiles against 23 ms; with nothing overdue that run is 12.2 G against 13.4 G). Measured (PGO builds, series from pristine worlds, two locked free cores, 5 reps; all-thread instructions, then cycles, against main before batch 2 at d346127e; A/A two builds of 184e7eb2): `neorv32_dual_full` runs 1 to 8 0.99, 0.92, 0.97, 0.85, 0.94, 0.99, 1.02, 1.01 (cycles 0.85 to 1.02 from run 3) where the deadline reads 1.07 / 1.16 at run 5; `neorv32_single_cache` 0.98, 0.92, 0.91, 0.96, 1.01, 0.99, 0.99, 0.99 (cycles 1.00 to 1.04 at runs 4 to 7) where the deadline reads 1.05 and 1.07 at runs 4 and 5; `osvvm_axi4_random` run 2 0.72, runs 3 to 7 0.75 to 0.88, run 8 1.02, runs 9 to 12 1.04 to 1.08 (cycles 1.02 to 1.15) against a settled A/A of 0.999 to 1.009: the build before settles at 5.2 G with 105 bodies by run 8, this one at 5.4 to 5.7 G with 16 to 36 (the rest repay slowly: the gap is held callers, `TransactionDispatcher` and the read and write handlers, whose small hot callees such as `WaitForToggle` wait for a compiled caller; the sampler books a call's time to the callee, so the callers carry 2 to 4 ms a run of their own; a second sitting read 1.06 to 1.11 at runs 9 to 12 and 1.01 to 1.04 at runs 13 and 14 in instructions, cycles 1.06 to 1.18). The deadline itself (main) reads 1.05 to 1.33 on `osvvm_axi4_random` runs 7 to 11, still compiling there. The bar (every run within the A/A of the build before) is met on the two neorv32 designs and not on `osvvm_axi4_random` from run 9; the maintainer took that trade.
- **Tried, not landed: the held callers carry their held-back callees' time** (2026-11-09, lab branch `perf/policy-heat`): the carry credits a held process with the time of the subprograms that wait only for a compiled caller (split among their uncompiled callers) and with every copy of it that ran, and `next_asked` orders by the carried time. Against the same base (5 reps, cores locked): `osvvm_axi4_random` runs 8 to 14 1.12 to 1.24 in instructions (this entry's rule 1.01 to 1.11 in the same sittings), with `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_SHARE=1` 1.13 to 1.19; nd and ns 1 to 4 percent above this entry's rule from run 4. The bodies compile in more runs, each paying part of the bill the build before paid in runs 2 to 7.
- Tuning aids: `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_SHARE`, `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_LONG_SHARE`, `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_GAIN` (0: off), `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_ORDER`, `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_HELD_RUNS`, `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_HELD_FREE`, `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_BIG`. `YAVS_AUTO_TRACE` now says why a held function waits (`held f..: gate, uncalled subprogram, unpaid, unrepaid`) and when pacing turns on and off.

## Whole values driven from where they are (yavs-clift, yavs-interp, #1122, 2026-11-09)

- **Decision: a zero-delay assignment of a whole value that the interpreter fuses with its waveform in the frame
  (`Op::CopyDrive`, listed as `yavs_interp::FusedCopy` by `fused_drives`, kept by `batched_drives` when its time
  register is a constant 0) is driven in Cranelift code from the value's own bytes** (maintainer ruling 2026-11-08:
  no signal by reference, no caller-provided result storage; drive from the result as the interpreter's fused op
  does). The `Zero` of the waveform and the `Copy` of the value are not made; at the `Drive`, `Gen::drive_copy`
  calls `yavs_rt_drive_src(mem, driver, lo, len, data, n)`, which takes a logic target whose plane blocks are the
  `n` bytes (`direct_drive_now`, `direct_drive_wide`) and answers 0 for anything else. A constant reference of up
  to 64 logic elements in a process copy is compared first (`value_differs`, the skip of `cur_differs` with the
  delay known to be 0). A 0, a byte signal, or a value `host` cannot reach inline makes the waveform and drives as
  before; an address the interpreter must look at leaves at the `Copy`, where `Op::CopyDrive` makes the waveform
  itself (`wave_at`). The sites are the interpreter's or fewer, as for `ScalarDrive`.
  Why: every `q <= a + b;` and `l1 <= reduce(t);` zeroed its waveform (72 bytes for 112 elements) and copied the
  value into it before the kernel read it back. Measured (exact instructions, slope 20 k to 100 k cycles of the
  adder-tree testbench, 16 units, Cranelift bench builds): `--tier=clift` loop form 29.36 G to 27.78 G (0.946),
  function form 32.22 G to 31.31 G (0.972, about 236 instructions fewer per call with its element drives); default
  tier (fresh library, the same compiled set as the base, two warm pairs) loop 29.35 G to 27.76 to 27.80 G, function
  32.07 G to 31.13 to 31.30 G. Function over loop is 1.13 on both tiers now (1.10 before): the loop form gains more.
  A held-value design (vectors of 16 to 64 elements and an integer array assigned whole every cycle) 14.45 G to
  14.40 G on `--tier=clift`, level on the default tier. Cycles were not measured (the timing cores were taken).
- **Decision: the zeroing of the waveform is kept whole on the way that makes it** (agent). The idea of zeroing only
  its time word does not apply where the drive is fused (nothing is zeroed), and the other way must match the
  interpreter's `wave_at`.
- **Decision: a compile thread that died in a compile is joined when the run ends, so its panic is the run's
  internal error** (agent; `AutoTier::stop`). Why: a panic of the tier-up thread (the verifier's in debug builds)
  left the function interpreted and the run's result unchanged, so no test saw it: a lowering bug of this change
  (target registers loaded inside the skip's compare, in blocks the call does not always follow) only showed as
  copies that never ran compiled. `compiled_gate.rs` `whole_values_at_run_time_elements_of_copies` fails with that
  lowering bug put back.

## `--tier-compile=wait`: past a second, the first run still holds a process it hardly ran (yavs-llvm `auto.rs`, 2026-11-09, landed with the next entry)

- **Finding** (agent). `uvvm_axistream_vvc`'s first run under `wait` took 1.62 to 1.69 times the wall of the pinned
  baseline with a second free core (the cold cap is 1.20); `background` 1.08, `--tier=interp` level with the
  baseline. At `WAIT_LONG` (1 s of looks' work, 40 percent into the run) `unpaid` let everything the count had asked
  for compile: the test sequencer `p_main` (12 856 IR, seen 1.4 ms of a 579 ms price, compiled in 0.52 s), then
  the command executor (seen 2 percent of its price) and, now called from compiled code, the BFM procedures and
  some 100 callees seen 0: 1.85 s of compiles in a 2.3 s run, paid on the critical path; compiled code saved almost
  nothing in the rest of the run.
- **Change** (agent; landed by the user's ruling of 2026-11-09, with the later-run credit below). Past `WAIT_LONG` the first run holds a process (`unpaid`)
  while the looks saw it and its copies (`bseen` of its base) for less than `WAIT_LONG_FLOOR` (0.1) of its price;
  a subprogram is not held by it (it waits until compiled code calls it, as before). Holding by the function's own
  time instead held GRLIB's copies (seen 0, their time is the base's) and native callees of compiled processes, and
  its first run cost 3 percent more instructions; holding subprograms with the full payback past `WAIT_LONG` cost
  GRLIB the same. Counter `tier_unpaid_long`, knob `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_LONG_FLOOR`. The floor: GRLIB's first run is
  level from 0.05 to 0.2 and 1.6 percent dearer at 0.5; at 0.05 the command executor passed in one run of eight
  (88 bodies compiled, 1.6 times the baseline); 0.1 is the middle.
- **Measured** (cold, one process at a time on two free timing cores, cells in ABAB order, 8 to 10 pairs, plain
  bench builds; wall against the pinned baseline): `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 1.09 (main 1.62; 33.5 G instructions
  against 48.1, every run), on one core 1.13 (main 1.68); the other five cap tests unchanged against main
  (instructions 0.997 to 1.002). GRLIB runs 1 to 3 level (instructions 0.995 to 1.001), Microwatt cold level
  (0.1 percent), `neorv32_dual_full` and `osvvm_axi4_random` level in runs 1 to 3, the OSVVM suite (314 tests,
  cold then warm) 1.00 and 0.985.
- **Cost: the later runs of `uvvm_axistream_vvc`.** Once held bodies compile only when their own time repays them
  (no `overdue`), the bodies the first run skips never compile and the test settled at 1.34 times main's
  instructions. The next section adds the later-run credit that fixes this, and gives the combined numbers.

## `--tier-compile=wait`: a later run credits a held caller with the callees it unlocks (yavs-llvm `auto.rs`, 2026-11-09, user ruling: landed)

- **Finding** (agent). With the first-run floor above, `uvvm_axistream_vvc`'s later runs settled at 1.34 times
  main's instructions: the floor holds the sequencer `p_main` and the command executor in run 1, and the later-run
  rule (`unrepaid`) judges each body by its own time. The sampler books a call's time to the callee, so the executor
  (seen 0 to 2 percent of its price) never repays, and its callees (the BFM procedures, about a second of
  interpreted time a run) wait for a compiled caller for good.
- **Change** (agent; user ruling 2026-11-09: build subtree credit together with the floor). `unrepaid` holds a
  function only if neither its own time nor the time of what it unlocks repays: `Worker::unlocked` sums the time
  and `body_price` of the subprograms that wait only for it (not compiled, called by no compiled code, transitively;
  a callee's share split among its uncompiled callers that ran; a callee never seen adds no price). The credit never
  holds what the own-time rule lets go. `WAIT_SUBTREE`, knob `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_SUBTREE`, counter `tier_unlocked`. A
  first version that judged by the subtree alone held more than main on `osvvm_axi4_random` run 2 and walked the
  subtree on every look; the own rule first fixed both.
- **Measured** (PGO bench builds, two builds of main as the A/A, 5 reps per series from pristine worlds on two free
  timing cores; all-thread instructions against main): `uvvm_axistream_vvc` run 1 0.71 (A/A 0.99), run 2 1.22,
  run 3 1.07, runs 4 to 6 1.03 to 1.07 (A/A 0.99 to 1.01): settled about 3 percent above main, which compiles the
  sequencer in run 1; six-run sum 0.98 of main, wall sum level. `osvvm_axi4_random` to run 12, `neorv32_dual_full`
  and `neorv32_single_cache` to run 8 within the A/A (the credit fires there only once, in two of five `osvvm_axi4_random` second runs). Cold cap with a free core
  (plain bench builds, 10 pairs): `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 1.13 of the pinned baseline (main 1.72), the other five
  level with main; GRLIB's first run level.
- **Decided** (user, 2026-11-09, option (a)): land the floor and the credit together, accepting
  `uvvm_axistream_vvc` runs 2 to 6 above main (the ruling's own bar, every run within the A/A, fails there: main
  pays the dispatcher's subtree in run 1, over the cap, and compiling everything the count asks for in run 2
  measured 1.5 to 1.6 times main's run 2). `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_SUBTREE` and `tier_unlocked` stay. Reach: the corpus test
  `process/dispatch_subtree` (a dispatcher over two waiting procedures, the inner one large) has the second run of
  `yavs-auto-warm` compile the dispatcher and the outer procedure for what they unlock (`tier_unlocked` 2).

## Lean calls for array parameters (yavs-interp `pre.rs` `lean_params`, `ParamAddrs`, `exec.rs` `call_late`, agent, 2026-11-10; landing is the maintainer's call)

- **A function whose calls the lean rule refuses only because a parameter is not loaded by the prologue, or its slot is read
  after it, is looked at again at its 128th call through the full path (`Pre::late`, `LATE_AFTER`).** Its calls are lean from
  then on when the body reads a parameter's slot only as a whole 8-byte word or as the descriptor of a flat array parameter,
  or not at all. The string, logging and checking helpers of verification libraries are that shape: they read a string
  parameter's bounds through its descriptor in the frame after the prologue (the descriptor is selected as a result, stored
  in a fat pair for a native or passed to another call, which `opt/dopes.rs` cannot fold into registers), and leave
  parameters unread (an unused `'right`, a default argument). The rule every call checks (`Pre::lean`, #443, #730) is as
  before, decided when the function is first called.
- **Why late.** The analysis follows registers through the blocks; run for every function on its first call it cost
  `vunit_logging` 0.8 percent of a run's instructions (3.6 percent of a settled `--tier=auto` run), more than its few calls
  saved. A count on the full path (a relaxed load and store, no read-modify-write) bounds it to functions called often.
- **How.** `lean_params` follows the registers that hold a parameter slot's address (`ParamAddrs`: a forward data flow over
  the blocks; `Move`, `Select` and `Index` by a constant carry an address on, any other definition ends it). At or after the
  first op the call runs such a register may be loaded or stored as a whole 8-byte word (that parameter is kept), or used as
  a descriptor (`DopeLen`, `Pos`, `SlicePos`, `LayoutOf`, `TempRoot`, `SigGather`, `SigScatter`, a one-dimensional
  `SubtypeCheck`, `NewFill`/`NewFrame` of at most one descriptor, stored as a value, or an argument of a call or native)
  when it is exactly the descriptor of a flat array parameter (`Param::flat`: its three words are kept). Any other use keeps
  the full call. `call_late` (out of line) allocates the whole frame, writes the registers the prologue would load and the
  kept parameters' slots, and skips the parameters nothing reads; the existing lean calls keep their code.
- **Exact by construction.** A kept slot holds what `call_pre` writes there for the frame's whole life, and a skipped
  parameter is never read. The frame is allocated whole, so every collector root slot exists (an `in` parameter's root slot
  left empty is the existing lean rule: the caller keeps the object); `out`/`inout` parameters keep the `may_collect`
  exclusion of #730; the registers holding parameter slot addresses stay preloaded, so the tier contract (#566) is not
  touched. Folding the descriptor reads into registers was not taken: the optimiser shares registers, so a bound's register
  is written again later in these bodies (`add_msg_delimiter` writes its `'left` register again), and a fold would need a
  reaching-definition check where writing three slots is exact.
- **Measured.** Exact counts by step (a lab build with the rule switched per run, every new shape decided at the first call,
  `--tier=interp --threads 1`, whole runs, all-thread instructions): descriptor reads kept in the frame (a) `uvvm_sb_slv` 12.257
  to 12.203 G, `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 34.493 to 34.330 G; plus unread parameters skipped (b) 11.832 G and 33.426 G (-3.5 and -3.1
  percent in all). As built (late, plain bench builds, settled third run, `--tier=interp --threads 1`): `uvvm_sb_slv` 10.615 to
  10.276 G (-3.2 %), `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 32.223 to 31.269 G (-3.0 %), `uvvm_func_cov` -2.5 %, `osvvm_axi4_random` -0.5 %,
  `neorv32_dual_full` -0.8 %, `vunit_logging` -0.8 %, `uvvm_methods_log` level; outputs equal. Plain PGO bench builds, base
  built twice for the A/A, cores 8 to 11 in a Latin square, 12 pairs, cycles: cold `uvvm_sb_slv` 0.970 +-2.5 (A/A 0.995
  +-1.6), `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 0.979 +-3.0 against the second base build, `uvvm_func_cov` 0.976 +-2.0 against it; warm
  `uvvm_sb_slv` 0.981 +-1.0 (A/A 0.997 +-1.3); the other cells within the A/A. GRLIB and Microwatt instructions level, outputs
  equal.
- Tests: `pre::tests::lean_writes_read_descriptors_and_skips_unread_parameters` (a descriptor read and stored, an unread
  string, a copy that keeps the full call, decided once at the 128th call), corpus `process/lean_array_params` (descriptor
  reads, unread parameters, a returned parameter, a result descriptor selected between the parameter's and a new one, a
  descriptor passed on to a call, a report and a line, ascending, descending, null and heap strings, a callee that
  allocates and frees, a 2-D array, a protected method; arguments differ every round so the memo of pure calls does not
  answer them). Work counter `lean_late` (debug and `op-census` builds): the calls that took the new path; floor on the
  perf design `lean_late` (`crates/yavs/tests/perf.rs`).
- **A register defined once by the `AddrOf` of a parameter slot holds the address in every block (#1133, agent,
  2026-11-11).** The frame starts with it (`Pre::preloaded`), and the optimiser lets sibling blocks share one such
  definition, so a block the definition does not reach may still read the slot through it. `lean_params` first followed
  the address only from its definition, missed the descriptor read in the other branch and skipped those slots: the call
  read the bounds an earlier call left there (a check's message lost its context after the 128th call of the helper). The
  flow now starts at the entry with every such register. Corpus `process/lean_param_addr_join`.

## `--tier=auto`: the sampler names the caller after a resumed callee returns (yavs-interp `exec.rs`, 2026-11-10)

- **Finding** (agent). The watching loop names the top frame's function in the thread's sampling slot when an
  activation starts and again only every `WATCH` (128) calls and jumps back. A process that resumes inside the
  procedure it waits in had that procedure in the slot after it returned, so the samplers booked the caller's work
  to the procedure. On `osvvm_axi4_random`, a later run booked about a third of its sampled time to four small
  waiting procedures (`WaitForToggle`, `RequestTransaction` and two more); on `uvvm_axistream_vvc` the first run
  booked 284 ms to a 130-instruction wait procedure and almost nothing to the command executor; `--profile` named
  the wait procedure as the busiest subprogram of a design whose work was all in the process.
- **Change** (agent). The branch of `Op::Ret` that looks its caller up, which runs for frames the loop did not push
  (an activation that resumed inside a callee, more than eight levels, frames compiled code left), stores the caller
  in the slot and the pc slot (`book_return`, out of line; counter `booked_returns`, debug and `op-census` builds).
  The other returns and calls are unchanged. Filling the list of saved callers from the frame stack at the start of
  such an activation was not done: it makes the same two lookups earlier, and those returns would then take the
  branch that names nothing.
- **Measured** (agent; PGO bench builds, two builds of main as the A/A, 5 reps per series from pristine worlds on
  two free timing cores, `wait`; all-thread instructions / cycles against main). The interpreter loop is unchanged
  (`--tier=interp` counts equal); the watching loop with nothing compiled moved by register allocation alone, at most
  +0.1 percent of instructions (one instruction more in one op on a compute loop), with the new branch never taken
  there. `uvvm_axistream_vvc`: run 1 1.16 / 1.25 (A/A 0.99 / 1.01), run 2 0.76, run 3 0.81, runs 4 to 8 0.96 to 1.01;
  eight-run sum 0.95 / 0.97. With the executor's own time seen, the first run compiles it and the bus procedures
  under it, which main paid in run 2: the cold cap against the pinned baseline reads 1.44 (main 1.13).
  `osvvm_axi4_random` runs 1 to 14 0.95 to 1.11, sum 1.02 / 1.02 (A/A 1.00 / 0.98), runs 6, 9 and 11 above the A/A;
  `neorv32_dual_full` level but run 8 (1.04, A/A 1.00); `neorv32_single_cache` level; `background` level on all
  three. The other cold-cap tests, GRLIB's first run and Microwatt (untimed) level with main.
- **Decided** (user, 2026-11-10): land it, accepting the first-run loss on `uvvm_axistream_vvc` and up to 0.1
  percent more instructions in the watching loop; a first-run rule that prices the callee tree a process compile
  pulls in is to bring that test back under the cold cap.
- **Earlier readings that rest on the misbooking**: the subtree credit's finding that the executor was seen 0 to 2
  percent of its price, the first-run floor's hold of that executor, the gain of 0.95 for `WaitForToggle`, and the
