  forced compile of the waiting callees on `osvvm_axi4_random` (their booked time was the caller's).

## Cranelift: the stored never-run list is retired (yavs-clift, yavs-rt, user ruling, 2026-11-10)

Written by Claude. `YAVS_CLIFT_LIST` (with `write`, `on` and `all`), `YAVS_CLIFT_LIST_NATIVE` and `YAVS_CLIFT_AGAIN` are removed, with everything that served only them: the coverage run's write path, the per-program list in the store (kind `never`), the list in the pre-key (`PreInputs::list`) and the function's id that #1126 put before it, the trip and make-again path (`rt::cheap_ran`, `take_again`, `tripped`, the `<symbol>_full` rebuild, the compile thread's wake and its `YAVS_AUTO_SYNC` wait), the counters `clift_listed`, `clift_tripped` and `clift_again`, the difftest candidate `yavs-clift-listall` and the tests of the list. The entries above stay as the history of what it was.
- **Why.** No gain beyond the A/A on main: the one cell that gained was a cold run of `uvvm_axistream_vvc` (0.95 of the instructions with native variants leaving), and the other designs and later runs were level or worse (GRLIB's run 2 at 1.05 to 1.06). The coverage run that makes a good list costs 1 to 12 cold runs. `uvvm_func_cov` loses 3 to 8 percent. A list made from an ordinary run, the only kind that costs nothing, was lost: the blocks it calls never run are the ones the next runs run.
- **Kept.** `YAVS_CLIFT_CHEAP` (cheap lowering of the blocks of a `YAVS_CLIFT_BLOCKCOV` dump, and its `all` and `alt` test modes) with `YAVS_CLIFT_BLOCKCOV`, `YAVS_CLIFT_COLD` and `YAVS_CLIFT_CHEAP_NATIVE`, and `yavs_rt_steps`, now as it was before CG2: it steps the instructions of a cheap block and counts nothing. `YAVS_AUTO_SYNC` itself stays (`Tier::hot` waits for the compiles it asks for); only the wait for a tripped function's compile goes. With every switch off the generated code is byte-identical to the code before the removal (the `YAVS_CLIFT_CODEDIR` corpus check).

## `--tier-compile=wait`: the first run holds a process until the callee tree it pulls in repays (yavs-rt `auto.rs`, 2026-11-10, user ruling: landed)

- **Finding** (agent). With the sampler naming the caller after a resumed callee returns, the first run of
  `uvvm_axistream_vvc` sees its command executor's own time (44 ms, main saw 0), lets it past the first-run floor
  and compiles it, and with it the bus procedures that waited for a compiled caller: run 1 rose from 1.13 to 1.44 of
  the pinned baseline's cold wall (cap 1.20).
- **Change** (agent; user ruling 2026-11-10: price the callee tree a process compile pulls in). Past `WAIT_LONG`,
  `Worker::unpaid` also holds a process while it and the subprograms that wait only for it (`unlocked`) were seen for
  less than `WAIT_TREE` (2) times what compiling them all costs, times `wait_payback` (`Worker::tree_unpaid`). Knob
  `YAVS_AUTO_WAIT_TREE`, counter `tier_tree_held`.
- **Measured** (agent; PGO bench builds, two builds of main with the booking fix as the A/A, 5 reps from pristine
  worlds on two locked timing cores, `wait`; all-thread instructions / cycles against main): `uvvm_axistream_vvc`
  run 1 0.86 / 0.85 (A/A 1.00 / 0.97), run 2 1.33 / 1.16, run 3 1.06 / 1.01, run 4 1.04, runs 5 to 8 level; eight-run
  sum 1.03 / 0.98. On that test the factor acts as a switch: at 1.5 nothing changes, at 2 the whole tree waits for
  run 2. On `osvvm_axi4_random`, `neorv32_dual_full`, `neorv32_single_cache` and GRLIB the rule never fires
  (`tier_tree_held` 0 in every run); on Microwatt's first run it holds five processes for a while and compiles the
  same 227 bodies (instructions 1.002, untimed, one run); `background` is level. Cold cap of `uvvm_axistream_vvc` (free cores, 10 pairs,
  host load 7 to 11): 1.14 of the pinned baseline's wall with the rule (95 percent band 7 percent; cycles 1.12),
  1.40 without; the other five cap tests and GRLIB's first run level in instructions and cycles.
- **Bound** (agent). The rule moves the compile bill of the executor's tree (about half a second) from run 1 to run 2;
  it does not shrink it. With the booking fix run 2 is about 22.6 G instructions with an A/A band of 1 to 2 percent,
  while bringing run 1 under the cap takes about 5 G out of it, so no rule that only changes when the tree compiles
  can keep every run within the A/A.
- **Decided** (user, 2026-11-10, option (a)): land it, accepting `uvvm_axistream_vvc` run 2 at 1.33 for the cold cap.
  Reach: no corpus test lasts the second the rule waits for, so `tier_tree_held` is 0 on the corpus; its evidence is
  the realbench `uvvm_axistream_vvc` first run (`tier_tree_held` 55, the executor's copies), as for the floor above.

## `--tier-compile=wait`: the first run's tree rule leaves a margin over the end of the run (yavs-rt `auto.rs`, 2026-11-11, user ruling: landed)

- **Finding** (agent). The first run of `uvvm_axistream_vvc` came in two modes, 32 or 40 G instructions of all threads
  (on two free cores 1.09 or 1.36 of the pinned baseline's wall, cap 1.20). The kernel thread retires the same 27.5 G
  in both: the dear mode is about 50 more compiles, 0.7 s of compile CPU, after the tree rule (`Worker::tree_unpaid`)
  lets the command executor go at 94 to 97 percent of the run's looks, where nothing they compile can pay back.
  Whether the executor's tree was seen for `WAIT_TREE` (2) times its price before the run ends was left to the
  sampler's noise. Dear draws at 2: 25 and 30 of 50 in the night cap sitting of 2026-11-11 (cap 1.22 and 1.25), 2 of 8
  and 1 of 12 in untimed day series. Factor sweep (untimed, by day): 1.25 and 1.5 dear 10 of 10, 1.75 9 of 10 and 8 of
  8, 2 0 of 10 and 2 of 8, 2.5 0 of 10 and 0 of 8, 3.3 0 of 8: the edge lies near 2 and moves between sittings.
- **Change** (agent). `WAIT_TREE` 2.5, a quarter above that edge. The alternative 1 / `WAIT_GAIN` (3.3: a rest of the
  run as long as the part seen repays the tree at the later runs' gain) gives the same axistream series but makes
  Microwatt's first run 0.35 percent dearer in exact counts (median 927.4 G against 924.2, 8 runs each; 2.5 924.9).
- **Trade** (agent). Per mode nothing changes, only the draw. After a cheap first run the second pays the tree (31.9 G
  against 20.9 after a dear one) and the runs after it settle later: 19 functions the dear first run compiled
  (`check_value`, `matching_values`, `fetch`, ...) have about no sampled time and stay held by the later runs'
  `unrepaid` through run 6 or later. Eight-run sums 178.5 G against 171.0 (+4.4 percent), run 8 18.70 against 18.38.
  The ruling of 2026-11-10 (entry above) accepted run 2 at 1.33 on runs 5 to 8 being level; they are not quite.
- **Elsewhere** (agent). `tier_tree_held` is 0 at 2 and at 3.3 on `osvvm_axi4_random`, `uvvm_sb_slv`,
  `uvvm_func_cov`, `neorv32_dual_full`, GRLIB and the small cap tests, so their decisions do not change at 2.5;
  `background` never applies the rule (`unpaid` needs `stops`). Microwatt's first run holds five processes at every
  factor and is level at 2.5.
- **Cold cap** (agent; day sitting on two locked free cores with an A/A, 22 clean pairs a cell): 1.051 of the pinned
  baseline's wall with 2.5 (no dear draw; 3.3 the same), main 1.07 to 1.11 (light runs 1.05, dear runs 1.33).
- **Decided** (user, 2026-11-11): land 2.5; the cold cap keeps binding run 1 alone. The next night cap sitting
  confirms it; if 2.5 draws the dear mode even once there, the factor becomes 3.3 (1 / `WAIT_GAIN`).

## Auto tier: the second-compile slot is removed (yavs-rt `auto.rs`, 2026-11-10)

Written by Claude. `Worker::compile`, `compile_part` and `frame_instead` lose their `o2` parameter and `Worker::done` goes from `[bool; 2]` per function to one flag. The slot served the make-again path of the stored never-run list (`done[k][1]`, entry above), which is retired, so `o2` was always false. The entries above that name the slot stay as history. Generated code is byte-identical (the `YAVS_CLIFT_CODEDIR` corpus check).

## IR optimiser: passes linear in the size of a function (yavs-ir `opt`, perf/b3-optpass, 2026-11-10)

Written by Claude. Three passes cost a power of the function's size; each now computes exactly what it did (the same IR,
checked by `YAVS_DUMPIR` over the corpus and the measured designs, and the same machine code by `YAVS_CLIFT_CODEDIR`
over the corpus):

- `cfg::dead_defs` tested each `Alloc` by a scan to the next definition of its register (twice), quadratic in a
  block of many descriptors. Now one walk per block keeps the open allocation of each register; with none open it
  looks only for the next `Alloc`.
- The two forward analyses of promotion (`undefined_promoted`, the copies of `promote_cleanup`) ran a stack of
  blocks: a chain of `if`s walked its tail once per joining arm, cubic in the chain. Now sweeps in reverse postorder
  until nothing changes. The fixed point is the same in any order.
- The backward sweeps (liveness in `cfg::dead_defs`, `Opt::dead_defs`, `share`, `slots`, `memo`, `sink` and of the
  registers across suspensions, and the marker analysis `forward_hits`) go from the last block to the first; a chain numbered against the
  flow took 164 rounds. From the third round they go in postorder (`opt::postorder`, the unreached blocks last);
  most bodies are done in two rounds and never build it.
- **Not changed:** `Opt::kill` and `kill_all` scan a table capped at 64 facts (#1059): their share of the optimiser
  stays flat from 300 to 1200 statements, with as many escaping variables. The dense bit sets of the liveness
  analyses stay (blocks times registers / 64 per round) with their caps.

## IR optimiser, round 2: one optimised body per function, readers indexed once (yavs-ir `opt`, perf/b4-optpass2, 2026-11-10)

Written by Claude. A cold-run profile (frame pointers, all threads) put the optimiser at 37 to 57 percent of the
cycles of the small library testbenches, 14 to 19 percent of `osvvm_axi4_random`, 4 percent of `uvvm_axistream_vvc`,
3.6 percent of GRLIB (where Cranelift takes 13 percent on the compile threads) and 0.3 percent of Microwatt. Each
change below computes what the code did before (the same IR by `YAVS_DUMPIR` over the corpus, the same machine code by
`YAVS_CLIFT_CODEDIR` over the corpus in `--tier=clift` and in `auto` with every function compiled):

- **Kept bodies.** `opt::optimize_body` (a function optimised without inlining) is kept per program next to the
  forwarders (`FwdCache`) and handed out again: inlining asked for the same small callee at level 0, at level 1, for
  the wide variant and again when the callee itself was optimised, so a fifth to a third of the bodies of a small
  testbench were optimised two to four times. Counter `opt_bodies_kept`, design `body_once` in `perf.rs`. Not kept:
  copies (instance data, descriptors of a subprogram copy) and reserved copy slots. This relies on the rule stated at
  `optimize_func`: the result reads only what lowering produced, so it does not depend on when it is made.
- **Readers indexed once.** `gate_results` and `forward_frame_copies` searched the whole function for the readers of
  each candidate (37 and 12 percent of a function of 600 vector statements); each now indexes the readers at its first
  candidate and keeps the index right as it rewrites (a reader is checked against the code before use).
  `forward_frame_copies` also keeps, per block, whether it may change the source.
- **Smaller ones.** `inline::run_with` scanned the function for a string concatenation once per call site, now once;
  `undefined_promoted` tested each promoted register against every block, now one pass over the blocks;
  `promote_cleanup` used a SipHash set for its promoted registers (a flag per register now) and cleared the copies of
  a promoted register one by one at each definition (numbered by register now, a run of bits).
- **Tried, not kept:** liveness per register by walking back from its reads (`share::plan`) was slower on a chain of
  `if`s (0.85 to 1.05 G for 1200 statements): constants merged at the entry are live from there to their one use, so
  the walks sum to the square of the length where the bit sets divide it by 64. A sorted slot table for
  `in_descriptor` and `own_slot` and one successor list per function for `share`, `slots` and `memo` stay ideas: each
  is under half a percent of every profiled design.

## `--tier=auto`: copies made during a run are callers too (yavs-rt `auto.rs` `Worker::see_copies`, perf/b4-natcallee, 2026-11-10, user ruling: landed)

- **Finding** (agent). The count rule holds a subprogram until a caller has compiled code (`Worker::waits`,
  `entered_from_code`), and reads who calls whom from a map worked out once, at the first asked function. The
  copies of processes and of subprograms are made later, in slots that were empty then, so their calls were not in
  the map. A process copy was covered by `copy_compiled` (a compiled copy stands for its process), a copy of a
  subprogram (called only from copies) by nothing: on GRLIB the compiled LEON3 `iu.comb` copy called about 14
  subprogram copies (`op_mux`, `alu_op`, `rs1_gen`, ...) that stayed `uncalled subprogram` for the whole run, also when
  the cache held them, and each call left the compiled code through `TIER_UNWIND` (0.4 to 2.7 M trips a run). The
  ones that compiled came in through the sampler late, and `alu_op` (464 IR, `Kind::Big`, a sampled candidate only at
  585 ms seen) never did.
- **Change** (agent). Each batch of looks adds the calls of the copies made since to `callers` and `callees`
  (`see_copies`; slots filled in order, a slot whose copy this thread does not see yet is looked at again). Counter
  `tier_copy_calls` (the calls added). No new rule: the callees then compile under the rules a callee of a compiled
  caller always had (after `WAIT_LONG` in a first run, cached ones as links in a later run), and the subtree credit
  and the run-1 tree rule see the copies' callees.
- **Measured** (agent; exact counts, by the user's ruling of 2026-11-10 that a busy host is judged by counts: PGO
  bench builds, two builds of main as the A/A, 3 reps from pristine worlds, `wait`, no `YAVS_COUNTERS`; GRLIB runs 1
  to 4, all-thread instructions against main): 0.970, 0.964, 0.977, 0.980 (A/A 1.000, 1.005, 1.003, 1.002). Cycles and the cold cap
  are still to be timed on a quiet host. Trips into the
  interpreter from compiled code per run (lab counters, untimed): 2.68 M, 1.04 M, 0.58 M, 0.37 M before, 16 k, 2.7 k,
  0.9 k, 1.0 k after; `alu_op` compiles in run 1 once `comb` has code. Under `--tier-compile=background` GRLIB
  reads 0.958, 0.967, 0.969, 0.977 (A/A 0.993 to 1.005). Microwatt (40 to 70 calls added a run) is level: runs 1 and
  2 at 0.999 and 0.999 (A/A 1.003 and 1.001). `osvvm_axi4_random` reaches the path under `background` only
  (2 calls added in most runs), six-run sum 0.976 (A/A 0.958). On `uvvm_axistream_vvc`, `uvvm_sb_slv`,
  `uvvm_func_cov`, `neorv32_dual_full`, the small tests and `osvvm_axi4_random` under `wait` the counter is 0 (no copy
  made after the map has a call), so every decision is the same.
- **Not built.** Pricing a callee of a compiled caller by its trips from that caller, and linking cached callees at
  the moment their caller links: with the map right, the callees compile 0.14 to 0.45 s after `comb` in run 1 and
  link in later runs, so neither has a gap left to close.
- **Reach.** `tier_copy_calls` 119 on 27 corpus tests under `yavs-clift-count1` (0 under `yavs` and
  `yavs-clift-check`: no default-tier corpus test makes a copy after the first asked function). Unit test
  `a_copy_made_later_frees_what_it_calls` (fails without the change).
- **Decided** (user, 2026-11-10): land it on the exact counts; GRLIB cycles and its first-run cold cap are timed on a
  quiet host later. `copy_compiled` stays for now, though the map now holds the process copies' calls too.

## Cranelift first-run compile cost: settings kept, one hash per compiled body (yavs-clift `lower.rs` `cache.rs`, perf/b4-clcold, 2026-11-11)

Written by Claude. Profile of a cold GRLIB run (frame pointers, all threads, `--tier=auto`): the compile thread is 16
percent of the samples, Cranelift's `compile_stencil` 10.8 (register allocation 5.3, `optimize` 3.4 of which the egraph
pass 2.3), the lowering to Cranelift IR 3.0 (`gen_func`), the two Cranelift key hashes 0.65. Per function (local lab
log): 167 compiles in run 1, 62 process copies take 1.25 s of the 2.1 s of Cranelift time and 0.50 s of the 0.64 s of
lowering; the five largest functions take 29 percent.

- **Settings kept: `opt_level=speed`, backtracking register allocation.** Exact all-thread instructions, GRLIB,
  default tier, one world, runs 1 to 4 (`YAVS_CLIFT_OPT`, `YAVS_CLIFT_RA`): `opt_level=none` run 1 1.009 of the
  default, runs 3 and 4 1.049; single-pass allocation 1.059 and 1.120; both 1.089 and 1.194. The slower code costs more
  inside the first run than the cheaper compile saves, and every later run keeps the slower code (the key of the stored
  code includes the flags). Not a cold-only option either.
- **The `prog.layouts` lock is left as is.** Under `--tier-compile=wait` (the default) the simulation is held at a
  pause point for every compile, so the compile thread's and the main thread's optimisations do not overlap: a
  context-switch profile of the cold GRLIB run has no wait under `optimize_body_with`.
- **One hash per compiled body (landed).** A function with a pre-key that is not a copy hashed its Cranelift body for
  the pre-key entry (`clif_key`) and again in `compile_with_cache`. The entry now takes the key the compile looked up
  (`Kv::asked`, counter `clift_key_reused`); a copy still hashes first for `bodies`, a run under
  `YAVS_CLIFT_PREKEY_CHECK` hashes early as before, and the names and stepped kinds of the entry are read before the
  compile (which rewrites the body). Debug builds assert the key. Machine code and entries are unchanged. Exact
  main-thread instructions, forced `--tier=clift --threads=1`, to 2 us, run 2 (everything lowered again and linked):
  0.89 to 0.95 of before on seven designs, GRLIB 54.6 to 51.8 G; run 1 level (the first run of these worlds has no
  program identity, so no pre-key and nothing to save). Default tier, all threads: GRLIB run 2 0.997, runs 1, 3, 4 level;
  Microwatt level; the small testbenches compile nothing in their first runs and are level. Corpus machine code
  byte-equal (`YAVS_CLIFT_CODEDIR` with a cache, 12 602 functions under `--tier=clift`, 8 611 under `auto` with every
  function compiled); later runs under `YAVS_CLIFT_PREKEY_CHECK=1` agree with every entry written this way.
- **Tried, not kept:** one Cranelift `Context` and `FunctionBuilderContext` reused for every function (keeps the
  register allocator's buffers): forced GRLIB run 1 0.9991, the rest within 0.001.
- **Not done, measured:** the lowering resets per-register state at every block and host call (`known.clone_from`,
  `Gen::clear`, the `Heap` sweep over `known`): forced GRLIB run 1 1.1 and 0.7 percent of the instructions, cold
  default tier about 0.4 percent, mostly in process copies. Sparse resets need every write to `known` tracked
  (`track` in `yavs-rt` included).

## Compiled code: `is_x` and the reductions of a vector in place (yavs-clift `Gen::ieee_native`, perf/b4-stepops, 2026-11-11)

- **Finding** (agent). A re-count of what compiled code hands back to the host on main 5e652cb7 (`YAVS_COUNTERS=pc`)
  put the stepped instructions (`TierHost::step`) far below the other hand-backs: GRLIB about 1.06 M steps a run
  (machinery 0.15 percent of run 2's instructions), against 6.2 M native callbacks (`native_direct` 2.2 percent self)
  and 3.8 M steps of native frames (`native_step`). On Microwatt the native callbacks were 136 M a run: `is_x` of a
  vector 82 M, of a `std_ulogic` 25 M, the `or` reduction 18.5 M; `native_frame`, `yavs_rt_native` and `is_x_vec`
  were 3.1 percent of its instructions. `is_x` and the reductions had a one-word path in the interpreter
  (`lookup_fast`) but none in compiled code, and `is_x` of a `std_ulogic` was not among the code tables.
- **Change** (agent). `Op::IsX(true)` and `Op::Reduce` are in `ieee_layout` with one array operand read through
  `plane_operand` (1 to 64 elements, all four planes): `is_x` is any element whose plane 1 is clear or plane 3 set;
  a reduction is the native's fold on the plane words (`and`: a `0`/`L` decides, else `U` if any is `U`, else `X` if
  any other is not `0 1 L H`, else `1`; `or` the same with `1`/`H`; `xor` the parity of the `1`/`H` when no element is
  a metavalue; the negated gates swap `0` and `1` and keep `U` and `X`). A null or longer operand takes the native
  call of the same site. `is_x` of a `std_ulogic` is a code table (`code_table`), as `??` is. Rows `IsX vec` and
  `Reduce` are `IN_PLACE` in `ieee_paths.rs`; `IEEE_NATIVE_CALLS` bounds lowered. Counter `clift_scan_sites`.
- **Measured** (agent; exact counts, plain bench builds of 5e652cb7 and of the change, all-thread instructions,
  untimed on cores 0-7, no `YAVS_COUNTERS`, medians of 2 or 3 reps from pristine worlds, outputs and exit statuses
  equal in every run): default tier Microwatt runs 1 and 2 0.957 and 0.960, GRLIB runs 1 to 4 1.001, 0.976, 0.971,
  0.972 (run 1's compile set moves it by 1.5 percent either way; runs 2 to 4 repeat within 0.1 percent); forced
  `--tier=clift --no-cache --threads=1` Microwatt 0.967, `neorv32_single_cache` 0.992, `sc5_fifo_repack` 0.996,
  `hdlm_fifo_sync`, `vunit_logging`, `olo_axi_master_full`, `uvvm_axistream_vvc`, `uvvm_sb_slv`, `osvvm_axi4_random`
  within 0.05 percent. Cycles are still to be timed.
- **Test.** `clift_parity` `is_x_and_reductions_in_compiled_code_match_the_interpreter`: every code in vectors of 0
  to 66 elements, both directions, the three packages' reductions, in a function and in a process, and the scalar
  table; it fails with the decided `0` of `or` wrong, the parity wrong, `is_x`'s plane test wrong, the `U`/`X` choice
  wrong, the negation of a metavalue wrong, or the scalar table wrong.

## Compiled code: a byte concatenation of a native frame in one call (yavs-clift `Gen::cat_bytes`, yavs-rt `yavs_rt_cat`, perf/b4-stepops, 2026-11-11)

- **Finding** (agent). In a native-frame variant every `Cat` of bytes (strings, arrays of scalars) was a step of
  the host on a frame of its own (`TierHost::native_step`, `xstep_wide`): 1.4 M a run on `uvvm_axistream_vvc`
  (`add_msg_delimiter`, `check_value`), 0.6 M on `uvvm_sb_slv`; `native_step` and `yavs_rt_xstep` were 6.2 percent
  of `uvvm_axistream_vvc` run 3 (about 590 instructions a step of machinery).
- **Change** (agent). A native frame's `Cat` of bytes of at most 16 pieces (`native::cat_inline`; the front end
  writes a longer chain as copies and stores) stores its piece registers in a stack buffer and calls `yavs_rt_cat`:
  it finds the `n * m` bytes of the result and every piece (`Mem::find`, else the object table, as `yavs_rt_host`),
  tests each piece against the result before it writes any, then copies each array piece (`memmove`) and stores
  each scalar's low `w` bytes at its offset, in the interpreter's order. 0 (nothing written) takes the slow path,
  the step it had before. Frame-mode code keeps `yavs_rt_signal`. Counters `clift_cat_sites` (sites), `cb_cat`
  (calls, debug builds).
- **Tried, not kept** (agent, exact counts, forced `--tier=clift --no-cache --threads=1`): the pieces' lookups
  lowered inline (every `host` test in the code) grew the compiles of `hdlm_fifo_sync`, `vunit_logging`,
  `olo_axi_master_full`, `osvvm_axi4_random` and `uvvm_sb_slv` by 2.4 to 6.7 percent of their runs; the call in
  frame-mode code too cost them 0.1 to 0.4 percent more than in native frames only.
- **Measured** (agent; plain bench builds, all-thread instructions, untimed, against the `is_x` change before it):
  forced `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 0.973, `uvvm_sb_slv` 0.985, `osvvm_axi4_random`, `hdlm_fifo_sync`, `vunit_logging`,
  `olo_axi_master_full` 1.0007 to 1.0010 (the compile of the call and its slow path); Microwatt, GRLIB (default
  tier), `neorv32_single_cache` and `sc5_fifo_repack` make no such concatenation and are level. Default tier, 4
  runs from pristine worlds, 5 reps: `uvvm_axistream_vvc` runs 3 and 4 0.925 and 0.937 (4-run sum 0.960),
  `osvvm_axi4_random` sum 0.999, `uvvm_sb_slv` sum 1.017 (its compile sets are bimodal: main against itself gives
  sums of 36.9 to 38.2 G over three series), the small tests and GRLIB within 0.1 percent. Cycles are still to be
  timed.
- **Test.** `clift_parity` `byte_concatenations_in_compiled_code_match_the_interpreter`: strings with characters
  and null pieces, 16 pieces, a longer chain, arrays of integers, reals and booleans, in functions and a process,
  and a result that does not fit its target; it fails with a scalar stored short, a scalar's offset wrong, or an
  array piece one byte short. The refusal path (0) is not reached by any test: the front end gives no `Cat` whose
  pieces exceed the result.


## Held drives found before the kernel's look-ups, and the plan gate for `drive_clean` (yavs-kernel, yavs-rt, yavs-interp, perf/b4-mwdrive, 2026-11-11)

Written by Claude. The drive side of Microwatt, measured first with lab counters (whole default-tier warm run, 290 M `yavs_rt_drive_src` calls of up to 64 elements, about 45 a kernel cycle).

- **Where the calls went.** 223 M of them (77 percent) were dropped by the kernel as unchanged, at about 250 host instructions each. 210 M came from shared code, which has no facts and so no compare in compiled code (`drive_copy`); 113 M of those had the skip gate open and 49 M more had it closed only because compiled code zeroes the whole gate word before it keeps a scalar drive (a closed bit with no entry of the run). Whole record scatters handed to the host (`scatter_compared`, 27 M) each walked the plan's drivers for `drive_clean`, about 40 drivers and 480 instructions.
- **Decision 1: the plan gate bit stands for `drive_clean`.** An open bit of a plan (`Ctx::plan_open`) answers the question; the walk runs only on a closed bit. Exact: everything that makes `drive_clean` false takes the bit first (`gate_off` at every push, `shut_gate` for a waveform, a phantom, a force, release or deposit).
- **Decision 2: `yavs_rt_drive_src` asks the gate first (`Ctx::gate_same`).** The driver's bit in `gate_base`, no entry of the run through its kernel driver (`ProcState::gate_taken`, kept by `gate_off`, all bits when the run made entries before `gate_init`, cleared by `resumption`), the run's range, then `Signal::cur_holds`, the current value alone, as compiled code's compare reads it (under an open bit the driving value is the current one; asking `direct_same_planes`, which reads both, kept a third of the gain: Microwatt forced 0.980 against 0.968); a hit is `gate_skipped`. The live gate word cannot serve: compiled code zeroes it to keep a drive and the kernel sees the kept drives only when they are handed over, which happens before any call such as this one, so by then each is an entry (its bits taken) or a kernel skip. Debug builds hold every such skip against `gate_check` and abort on a difference; `DRIVE_SRC_HELD` counts them in builds that count (`drive_src_held`).
- **Not done (measured, for the maintainer).** (a) Reopening the gate word after a hand-over (`Ctx::gate_reopen` in `yavs_rt_drive_flush`), so compiled code's own compares in copies work again after a kept drive. (b) The compare in compiled code for shared code, the target's form tested at run time (`value_differs_at`, built and measured, not landed): it removes the call itself, which the runtime test cannot (the call, the entry and `direct()` are most of the 250 instructions), but it adds about 45 IR instructions to every fused drive site, so eager compiles grow.
- **Why not `direct_entries` for the entry test.** It scans the entry lists of a process with few drivers (no marks): Microwatt forced +0.7 percent against `gate_taken`, whose cost is one `or` at each push (`hdlm_lfsr` forced +0.1 percent).
- **Numbers.** `docs/STATUS.md`, "Held whole-value drives found before the kernel's look-ups".

## Compiled code: a native frame's layout from a run-time descriptor in one call (yavs-clift `Gen::layout_into`, yavs-rt `yavs_rt_layout_into`, perf/b4-layoutof, 2026-11-11)

- **Finding** (agent). A census on main bd29a1e7 (`YAVS_COUNTERS=pc`) put the steps of native frames of `LayoutOf`
  first among what compiled code still hands back to the host on GRLIB: 3.4 to 3.5 M a run (`icc_valid`, `op_find`,
  `cwp_gen`, `ic_ctrl`, `lock_gen`), each a `TierHost::native_step` on a frame of the host's. They are layouts of a
  record or array type whose words depend on the descriptor (no `static_layout`) and of which more than one word is
  read (one word is `fuse_layout`, a call of the memo already). Frame-mode code steps about 50 k a GRLIB run.
- **Change** (agent). In a native frame such a `LayoutOf` (`layout_shape` gives the word count, a descriptor of at
  most 4 KiB) finds the descriptor inline (`Gen::host`) and calls `yavs_rt_layout_into`: it takes the words from the
  interpreter's layout memo (`TierHost::layout_into`, `Machine::layout_into`: the memo's words when its descriptor
  bytes are the same or its array of scalars takes them from the bounds, else the memo made again, as
  `layout_word_of`) into new temporary memory it allocates itself (pad zeroed, as `Machine::temp_alloc`) and returns
  their address. 0 (nothing changed: the memo declined, the area must grow) takes the step it had before.
  Frame-mode code keeps its step. Counters `clift_layout_sites` (sites), `cb_layout_into` (calls, debug builds).
- **Tried, not kept** (agent, exact counts, forced `--tier=clift --no-cache --threads=1`): the allocation inline
  (`temp_alloc`, with or without its zeroing) and the call in frame-mode code too cost `osvvm_axi4_random` 0.9 to 1.0
  percent of its run in compiles (51 native and the frame-mode sites; frame mode alone was 0.6 percent of it, for
  about 50 k steps a GRLIB run); with the allocation inline in native frames only, 0.3 percent.
- **Measured** (agent; plain bench builds of bd29a1e7 and of the change with the next one (reals to integers), all
  thread instructions, untimed on cores 0-7, no `YAVS_COUNTERS`, medians from pristine worlds, outputs and exit
  statuses equal in every run): default tier GRLIB runs 2 to 4 0.988, 0.989, 0.988 (a copy of the base binary: 0.998
  to 1.0004; run 1 moves 1 to 5 percent with its compile set); forced GRLIB 0.989, `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 0.996,
  `osvvm_axi4_random` 1.0009, `hdlm_fifo_sync` 1.0004, `olo_axi_master_full` 1.0003, `uvvm_sb_slv`, `vunit_logging`,
  `neorv32_single_cache`, `sc5_fifo_repack` and Microwatt within 0.01 percent; default tier `uvvm_axistream_vvc`,
  `osvvm_axi4_random`, `uvvm_sb_slv` 4-run sums inside the spread of the base against a copy of itself (5 reps:
  101.0 to 105.0, 28.4 to 29.5, 35.1 G), the small tests and `neorv32_single_cache` within their run-to-run
  spread; Microwatt 2-run sums 1818.8 and 1819.4 G against 1812.8 to 1817.7 G for the base and its copy (run 1
  alone spans 0.5 percent): inside the spread, leaning 0.1 to 0.2 percent up, while forced it is level (
  1.0000). Cycles are still to be timed.
- **Test.** `clift_parity` `layouts_from_run_time_descriptors_in_compiled_code_match_the_interpreter`: records with
  unconstrained fields of several constraints read in functions, an array of them, a record of generic constraint
  in the process, at two generic values; `perf.rs` `layout_into` bounds `cb_xstep` at 0 and `cb_layout_into` at 400
  calls. The decline (0) is not reached by any test: no VHDL gives a layout the memo fails on that analysis lets
  through.

## Compiled code: reals rounded to integers in place (yavs-clift `Gen::f_to_i`, perf/b4-layoutof, 2026-11-11)

- **Finding** (agent). `FToI` and `FToIRange` (a real converted to an integer type) had no compiled form: each was a
  step, on a native frame a `TierHost::native_step` (78 k a run of `uvvm_axistream_vvc`, in `random`; 6.6 k on
  `osvvm_axi4_random`).
- **Change** (agent). Compiled code rounds as `arith::real_to_int` does: `trunc`, then away from zero when the
  dropped fraction (exact, `x - trunc(x)`) is at least one half (not the round-half-to-even of the machine's
  `nearest`); a result outside `-2^63 .. 2^63` or a NaN leaves at the instruction for the interpreter's error, and
  `FToIRange` tests the bounds as `Check` does. `inline_regs` lists both, so the policy no longer counts them as ways
  out. Counter `clift_real_int_sites`.
- **Measured** (agent; exact counts, forced `--tier=clift --no-cache --threads=1`, against the layout change before
  it): `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 0.9996, `vunit_logging` 0.9997, the others within 0.01 percent.
- **Test.** `clift_parity` `reals_to_integers_in_compiled_code_match_the_interpreter`: halves of both signs, the
  largest fraction under a half, both ends of `integer`, a subtype of a range, in a function and the process, and
  the four ways out of range; `perf.rs` `real_int` bounds `cb_xstep` at 0 and `cb_step` at 4.

## `--tier=auto`: who calls whom, without optimising the whole program (yavs-rt `auto.rs` `Worker::graph`, `prefetch`, `profile.rs` format 5, yavs-ir `Program::newly_optimised`, perf/b4-callersmap-2, 2026-11-11, agent; landing is the maintainer's)

- **Finding** (agent). The count rule's map of callers (`entered_from_code`, `unlocked`) was built at its first ask by
  reading `Program::func` of every function, and `func` optimises a function the first time it is asked for. So the
  first subprogram asked past the gate optimised the whole program, run or not: 210 to 1 380 functions a run on the
  measured designs, of which 5 to 160 ran later (`uvvm_func_cov`: 311 optimised, 87 ran; `neorv32_dual_full`: 1 334
  and 6; GRLIB 661 and 22). It ran on the compile thread beside the simulation, so it also optimised ahead the
  functions the simulation called later: taking it away alone (perf/b4-callersmap, held) cut all-thread instructions
  but added 2 to 5.5 percent on the simulation thread of `uvvm_func_cov`, `osvvm_axi4_random` and
  `uvvm_axistream_vvc`, which then optimised those functions itself. The map cannot come from the lowered code
  instead: inlining adds the callees of an inlined body and removes the inlined call, and copies of subprograms
  replace the callee, so lowered and optimised calls differ on every measured design (GRLIB: 71 edges only in the
  lowered code, 4 only in the optimised).
- **Change** (agent). `Program` lists each function it optimises (`optimised`, a mutex-guarded list and its length),
  before the optimised code can be handed out, so a thread that was given the code finds the function listed. The
  policy's `graph` takes in the calls of the functions listed since its last ask, in both directions, and replaces
  the build at the first ask and `see_copies`. Every caller the policy asks about has compiled code (made from the
  optimised code), was asked for by the count (`held`) or was seen running (`time`): each was optimised, so the
  answers are those of a map of the whole program. The run profile (format 5) lists the functions a run needed
  (ran or compiled; not copies, whose ids change), in the order they were optimised; the compile thread of the next
  run optimises them at its start, beside the simulation (`Worker::prefetch`), and nothing else. A run without that
  list (the first, or after a profile of format 4) optimises the whole program at the first question about callers,
  exactly as before (`force_all`). Counter `tier_copy_calls` now counts every call of a copy taken in.
- **Check** (agent). `YAVS_AUTO_CHECK_CALLS` (builds with debug assertions) compares every answer of `entered_from_code`
  and of `unlocked`'s caller count, and the callees of each function `unlocked` walks, with a walk over the code of
  every function, and stops at a caller the policy asks about that was never optimised.
- **Measured** (agent, exact counts, plain bench builds of fc7f12cf without and with the change, from pristine, runs 1
  to 4; median of 4 to 12 reps, a second copy of the base binary for the A/A). Main thread under `--tier-compile=wait`:
  `uvvm_func_cov` run 2 0.937, everything else level (`osvvm_axi4_random`, GRLIB 0.991 to 1.001; `neorv32_dual_full`
  0.998 to 1.014 with the ranges of the two overlapping; `uvvm_axistream_vvc` and `uvvm_sb_slv` by their bimodal modes,
  12 reps); under `background` 0.89 (`uvvm_func_cov`
  run 2) to level. All threads: `uvvm_func_cov` run 2 0.889, `osvvm_axi4_random` runs 2 and 3 0.985 and 0.840,
  `neorv32_dual_full` runs 2 to 4 0.97, GRLIB runs 1 and 2 0.994, the small tests +0.01 to +0.05 percent (the
  profile's longer text), Microwatt level. The first run decides and optimises as before by construction.
  Under `YAVS_AUTO_COUNT=1 YAVS_AUTO_GATE=0 YAVS_AUTO_SYNC=1` the compile decisions are identical on every design where
  that mode repeats itself (`hdlm_fifo_sync`, `vunit_logging`, `olo_axi_master_full`, `neorv32_dual_full`,
  `uvvm_axistream_vvc`, runs 1 to 3). The check above was clean over the difftest corpus and 13 realbench designs, runs
  1 to 4, with the run-2 prefetch in use.
- **Not changed here** (agent; for the maintainer). The stage cache stores a closure's lowering, and the optimised
  copies with it, only from its second run ("The image of a closure is made on its second analysis"), so run 2 optimises everything run 1 did again and
  run 3 is the first served: on `uvvm_func_cov` run 2 takes 5.13 G instructions, run 3 2.25 G (`osvvm_axi4_random`
  8.59 and 7.38, `neorv32_dual_full` 19.0 and 14.9). Storing in run 1 would be the larger lever for run 2, at the cost
  that decision avoids for a design that runs once.

## Compiled code: `ieee` ops and concatenations of 65 to 128 elements in place (yavs-clift `Gen::ieee_wide`, `Gen::cat_block`, perf/b4-wideieee, 2026-11-11)

- **Finding** (agent). After `is_x` and the reductions went in place, every native callback left on Microwatt
  (11.1 M a run) and every logic `Cat` it stepped through `yavs_rt_signal` (5.2 M) were either over the 64
  elements of the in-place arms or gates of vectors holding `U` (next entry): the 65 by 65 element products of
  `multiply` (`(m.is_signed and m.data1(63)) & m.data1`, a 130-element product), its 128-element sums and the
  `or`/`and` reductions of 65 elements, and `unsigned('0' & not inp) + 1` of `countbits` (65 elements).
- **Change** (agent). Where the bounds of every array operand of a light `numeric_std` or `std_logic_1164`
  native are constants of the code (registers a `Const` defines once), of at most 128 elements, and an operand
  or the result is over 64 (`Gen::wide_lens`), `Gen::ieee_wide` reads two plane blocks per operand and computes:
  `is_x` and the reductions (the native's fold over both blocks, `reduce_code`, `is_x_code`, shared with the
  one-block arms), the logical operators of equal lengths (`logic_block` per block, any element value), `+` and
  `-` of every form (two words with a carry; a negative `natural` takes the callback) and `*` of two vectors with
  a product of at most 192 elements (the product modulo 2 to the 192 of the operands extended to three words,
  from 64-bit products and `umulhi`), the arithmetic only without a metavalue, as the narrow arms; the result
  takes one to three blocks in the temporary area (`ieee_put`). Lengths known only at run time keep the one-block
  arms: making both forms at every site would grow every compile for designs that have none. `Gen::cat_block`
  takes a result of up to 128 elements with pieces of up to 128, a piece's block split over the two result
  blocks where it straddles them. Counter `clift_wide_sites` (sites).
- **Measured** (agent; exact counts, plain bench builds, all-thread instructions, untimed, no `YAVS_COUNTERS`):
  forced `--tier=clift --no-cache --threads=1` Microwatt 0.9928 against main 723863fa, every other design measured
  within 0.01 percent (GRLIB 1.0001); default tier against fc7f12cf Microwatt's 4-run sum 0.995 (a second copy of
  main's binary 1.002), GRLIB and the small designs within their spread. Output hashes and exit statuses equal to
  the base in every run. `temp_alloc` now zeroes a known size of up to 192 bytes by stores (was 128), for the
  three-block product.
- **Test.** `clift_parity` `wide_ieee_ops_and_concatenations_in_compiled_code_match_the_interpreter` and the
  corpus test `ieee/wide_ops` (sums, differences and products of 33 to 192 elements in every form, reductions,
  `is_x`, gates and concatenations of 65 to 128, with metavalues, `L` and `H`; in a function and a process); it
  fails with the product's carries, the sum's carry or borrow, the second block of a reduction or `is_x`, the
  straddling half of a concatenation, the sign extension or the clean-operand guard broken. `perf.rs` `wide_ieee`
  bounds the callbacks.

## Compiled code: the logical operators of vectors holding metavalues in place (yavs-clift `Gen::gate_planes`, perf/b4-wideieee, 2026-11-11)

- **Finding** (agent). The largest share of Microwatt's native callbacks after the entry above: twelve gates of
  `mmu_1` (`(r.pde(55 downto 12) and not finalmask) or ...`, 4 to 44 elements), 0.55 M each a run, 6.6 M of
  the 11.1 M. The in-place arm of the logical operators took operands of `0 1 L H` only, and the MMU's registers
  hold `U` in a run that never uses it.
- **Change** (agent). The logical operators of `std_logic_1164` and `numeric_std` of 1 to 64 elements read the
  four planes of both operands: when every element is `0 1 L H` the gate of the bits as before, else (out of
  line) the std_logic_1164 tables on the planes (`logic_block`, the `LogicOp` lowering's), which is what the
  native returns for equal lengths. Unequal lengths still take the native call.
- **Trade** (agent). The out-of-line tables are compiled at every gate site: forced `--tier=clift --no-cache`
  runs, which compile every function, cost `neorv32_single_cache` 0.09 percent, `hdlm_fifo_sync` 0.03 percent and
  GRLIB 0.02 percent more than the entry above alone (forced runs repeat within 0.01 percent); the default tier shows
  none of it beyond its spread. Microwatt forced 0.9895 against the entry above. A small runtime helper for the
  tables instead of the inline code would shrink the cost (not built).
- **Test.** The same `clift_parity` and corpus tests (gates of 1 to 128 elements on every element value); it
  fails with the out-of-line tables never taken. `perf.rs` `wide_ieee` holds gates of a vector of `U`.

## Compiled code: a native frame's deallocation in one call (yavs-clift `Gen::free`, yavs-rt `yavs_rt_free`, yavs-interp `TierHost::free`, perf/b4-callprice, 2026-11-12)

- **Finding** (agent). After the layout change above, `Free` (`deallocate`) was the only instruction
  `uvvm_axistream_vvc`'s native frames still handed to the host: 0.16 M a first run, 0.30 to 0.31 M a later one
  (`to_string`, `return_and_deallocate`, `get_string_len`), each a `TierHost::native_step` through `yavs_rt_xstep`
  (a frame of the host's pushed for the registers, the slot windows swapped in, the instruction dispatched by
  `Machine::step`, the view rebuilt and the object table forgotten): about 700 instructions more than the
  deallocation itself. Not a call between compiled functions: `Free` is an instruction, and `xstep_ok` sent every
  heap instruction there. GRLIB, Microwatt and `osvvm_axi4_random` run none; `uvvm_func_cov` about 900 a run.
- **Change** (agent). On a native frame compiled code reads the access value from its cell itself (`Gen::host`),
  does nothing for null, else calls `yavs_rt_free(env, mem, handle, cell)` and sets the cell to null. The host
  (`TierHost::free`) deallocates and brings the view's heap epochs up to date (`tier_heaps`); `Mem::forget_heap`
  then drops the freed object's entry, as `forget` does for the heap. It declines with nothing changed where the
  step would do more or fail: a collection or recycling due (`Machine::reclaim_work`, which also covers the cases
  `reclaim_pending` lets through), a stale value (the interpreter reports the double deallocation) and a cell
  inside the object it frees (the interpreter's null store after the free reports it, and the cell's memory is
  gone). A decline leaves the frame to the interpreter at the `Free` (`slow_path`), as the step's own decline did
  when a collection was due. Frame-mode code keeps its step. Counter `cb_free` (calls, debug builds).
- **Tried, not kept** (agent). The old step as the slow path (`slow_path_x`, so a decline steps instead of
  leaving): forced runs compile more per site (`uvvm_func_cov` +0.07 percent against -0.05 with the leave) for a
  decline that is rare.
- **Measured** (agent; plain bench builds of 39454ad5 and of the change, all-thread instructions, untimed on
  cores 0-7, no `YAVS_COUNTERS`, from pristine worlds, outputs and exit statuses equal in every run). Forced
  `--tier=clift --no-cache --threads=1`: `uvvm_axistream_vvc` 0.9950, `uvvm_sb_slv` 0.9951, `uvvm_func_cov`
  0.9995, `hdlm_fifo_sync` 0.9999, `olo_axi_master_full` 1.0001, `osvvm_axi4_random` 1.0002 (forced runs repeat
  within 0.01 percent; the compile of the sites). Default tier with the decisions fixed (`YAVS_AUTO_COUNT=1
  YAVS_AUTO_GATE=0 YAVS_AUTO_SYNC=1`, which repeats within 0.05 percent on these two designs): `uvvm_axistream_vvc`
  runs 2 to 4 0.985 to 0.987 (simulation thread 0.985), `uvvm_sb_slv` 0.970 to 0.975. Default tier as shipped:
  inside the spread of the base against a copy of itself on `uvvm_axistream_vvc` (all threads and the simulation
  thread, `wait` and `background`), `osvvm_axi4_random`, `uvvm_func_cov` and `uvvm_sb_slv`; GRLIB and Microwatt,
  which run no `Free`, level. Cycles and the cold cap are still to be timed.
- **Test.** `clift_parity` `deallocations_in_compiled_code_match_the_interpreter`: a local, a null value, a field
  of another heap object, a protected type's own variable (the shared heap), and the two errors (an object
  deallocated twice, a cell inside the object it frees); `perf.rs` `free_native` bounds `cb_free` at 400 calls.

## IR optimiser, round 3: whether a block is on a cycle, once per block and pass (yavs-ir `opt`, perf/b4-deadpass, 2026-11-12)

Written by Claude. On real testbenches the cold main-thread profile has no superlinear optimiser part left (no symbol
of the kind over 1 percent on `uvvm_func_cov`, `hdlm_fifo_sync`, `uvvm_axistream_vvc`, GRLIB or Microwatt to 2 us).
Long generated bodies still have some. In a function of 2400 mixed statements (vectors, slices, `if` chains,
string calls, loops, procedure calls) `Opt::in_cycle` took 31 percent of the run: `forward_frame_copies`,
`defaults_first` and `frame_objects` ask, per candidate (every local composite variable), whether its block is on a
cycle, and each question walks the function.

- **Change.** Those three passes keep the answer per block for the pass (`in_cycle_memo`): the candidates of a long
  function sit in a few blocks (the declarations). A pass changes no branch while it asks (they rewrite loads,
  allocations and copies, never a terminator), so the answer cannot go stale; debug builds walk again on each
  remembered answer and assert it is the same. Counter `opt_cycle_memo` (answers taken from the memo), perf design
  `cycle_memo` (`Min(1)`).
- **Measured** (main-thread `instructions:u`, `--tier=interp --threads 1`, `--no-cache`, optimiser = run minus
  `YAVS_NO_IROPT`): the optimiser on that function of 600 / 1200 / 2400 statements 0.40 / 1.09 / 3.28 G before,
  0.31 / 0.71 / 1.79 G after. Cold runs of the small testbenches, `uvvm_func_cov`, Microwatt and GRLIB to 2 us: level
  (inside the spread of two worlds of the same build). The same IR (`YAVS_DUMPIR` over the corpus and the generated
  functions), so the same machine code.
- **Held, not landed** (branch perf/b4-deadpass-held): the same per-access scans in processes, where the shape of
  2400 statements costs 4.56 G in the optimiser: the locals by slot for `frame_range`, `in_descriptor`, `own_slot`
  and `promote`, the frame objects by slot for the predecoder (`FrameObjects`), the candidates by slot in
  `proc_objects`, and the escaping ranges without repeats. Together 4.56 to 1.46 G on that process and 1.79 to 1.37 G
  on the function (with the escaping ranges also sorted for `kill`, 1.14 G on the process), but 0.05 to 0.2 percent
  more main-thread instructions on the small testbenches and Microwatt, more than two worlds of one build differ,
  though every lookup switches to the sorted form only past a size. A `Cell` in `Opt` (for a lazily built table)
  alone cost about 0.1 percent: `&Opt` is then not `Freeze`.

## Compiled code: an `LCopy` of a run-time count in a native frame in place (yavs-clift `Gen::lcopy_inline`, perf/b4-arrparam, 2026-11-12)

- **Finding** (agent). Since array parameters are cells ("Array parameters as cells"), what is left of the cost of a small function
  that returns a slice, such as a cache's `get_row(addr) return unsigned(addr(SET_SIZE_BITS - 1 downto
  ROW_OFF_BITS))`, is mostly not the parameter's bounds. Per call of that function compiled (`--tier=clift`,
  exact counts, a loop of calls less the loop alone), on 39454ad5: about 615 instructions with bounds from
  generics and an open parameter, 490 with a literal slice and an open parameter, 369 with everything literal,
  and 619 with a constrained parameter and the slice from generics: the parameter's own descriptor costs
  nothing once the slice's bounds come from instance data. The copy of the slice into the result block, of a
  count known only at run time, called `yavs_rt_lcopy`; in place it saves 20 to 30 instructions a call there
  (the runtime's copy, 100 to 190 instructions a loop iteration of the harness, is mostly the caller's
  frame-mode copy of the result into its variable, which keeps the call). In a forced
  compiled Microwatt run every native-frame body together is 1.2 percent of the instructions, `get_row`'s two
  bodies 0.1, `yavs_rt_lcopy` 0.45.
- **Change** (agent). In a native frame an `LCopy` whose count is known only at run time and whose destination
  offset is the constant 0 (a slice into a block of its own: the result of a function, a fresh temporary)
  copies up to 64 elements in place under one run-time test (`lcopy_inline` with one destination block: the
  bits above the run stay), and calls `yavs_rt_lcopy` above 64. The two-block destination form of a constant
  count writes its second blocks behind one branch instead of one per plane. Frame-mode code keeps the call:
  inlined there too, the forced compile of GRLIB grew 1.4 percent, more than its run gained. `clift_lcopy_count_sites`
  counts the sites.
- **Measured** (agent, plain bench builds, all-thread instructions, forced `--tier=clift --no-cache`, repeat
  within 0.01 percent): Microwatt 0.9994, GRLIB 0.9983; the small tests that are mostly compile under forced code
  grow by the compile (`hdlm_fifo_sync` and `olo_axi_master_full` 1.0009), the others within 0.01 percent. Default
  tier, runs 2 and 3 from pristine, 2 reps: GRLIB 0.9962 and 0.9963 outside the A/A range (main thread alone the
  same); Microwatt and the small tests inside their A/A.
- **Not done**, sized. The bounds of instance data in a shared function (the generics of `get_row`) fold only in
  a copy of the function per instance and per constant cell of the call (`opt/subcopy.rs` keys on `'dope`
  slots only, and its copies carry no instance facts): about 250 instructions a call on the harness above,
  at most the 1.2 percent of all native bodies on Microwatt. Holding an address parameter that a loop uses
  once (`rt::hold_addrs`) cut a 64-element `bit_reverse` by 8 to 13 percent but made forced GRLIB 0.23 percent
  dearer (the region asked at every entry): not kept.

## Memo of pure calls: priced at compiled call sites, and a leaner probe (yavs-ir `memo_fn.rs`, yavs-clift `Gen::native_call`, yavs-interp `pmemo.rs`, perf/b4-memoprice, 2026-11-12)

- **Finding** (agent, census on 4d94c5ef, forced `--tier=clift --no-cache --threads=1`, exact counts). A hit of the memo costs
  about 900 to 1000 instructions from compiled code (`yavs_rt_memo`, `TierHost::memo_probe`, the key, the lookup, the result
  copy), more than many whole compiled bodies, and every pure function with a loop, a call or 120 IR instructions was probed.
  Microwatt makes 32 M probes (28 M hits) in 36 functions, GRLIB 4.8 M in 27. Leaving one function's probe out at a time (a lab
  switch) gave its net worth: on Microwatt the memo pays 15 percent overall, but `andor`, `decode_a_const`, `decode_b_const`,
  `recode_primary_opcode`, the four `addr_hash_*`, `num_to_fxm`, `dawrx_match_enable` and a few smaller ones lose 250 to 2100
  instructions a call (about 9 G of 1048 G together); on GRLIB the memo costs 0.17 percent overall (`genmux`, `branch_true`,
  `ahbdrivedata`, `ahbreadword`, `rex_dpc` lose 550 to 1250 a call; `decode`, `TO_INTEGER`, `tz` win).
- **Change** (agent). `MemoSig::dear`: the function or one it calls has a cycle of blocks (a real one, not a jump to a lower
  block), calls itself, concatenates bytes or calls a native other than an `ieee` gate, conversion or comparison
  (`cheap_native`; arithmetic, shifts and resizing are calls on wide operands). A compiled call of a function that is not dear
  is made directly, without the probe (`clift_memo_unprobed_sites`); the interpreter keeps probing every memoised function, as
  an interpreted body is far dearer. The probe finds a function's memo once (`State::index`, keeping the last one found),
  builds the key without a per-cell check and copies an array result straight into temporary memory (`Machine::temp_bytes`):
  about 95 instructions less a hit.
- **Not taken.** The price is static, so it misses both ways: `decode` (GRLIB, a result of `2**n` elements) and `bcd_to_dpd`
  (Microwatt) are classed cheap but the memo paid for them; `decode_b_const` (a `resize`), `ahbdrivedata` and `ahbreadword` (a
  one-trip loop, a loop on a path that does not run) are classed dear but lose. A profile price (sampled body cost per miss, kept across runs) or an
  inline probe in compiled code (per-process table, arguments compared in place) would close more; neither was built.
- **Measured** (agent, plain bench builds, all-thread instructions, outputs and exit status equal to the base in every run).
  Forced `--tier=clift --no-cache --threads=1`, one run each (a byte copy of the base within 0.01 percent): Microwatt 0.9921
  (the leaner probe alone 0.9969), GRLIB 0.9989 (0.9988), `hdlm_fifo_sync` 0.9990, `vunit_logging`, `sc5_fifo_repack`,
  `hdlm_lfsr`, `neorv32_single_cache`, `olo_axi_master_full` 0.9994 to 0.9996.
  Default tier (`wait`), runs 1 to 3 from a pristine world, Microwatt and GRLIB 2 reps, small tests 3: Microwatt 0.9866,
  0.9881, 0.9881 (byte copy 0.9988, 0.9990, 0.9956), main thread alone 0.9868, 0.9916, 0.9899; GRLIB runs 2 and 3 0.9977
  and 0.9983 outside the copy's range (run 1 moves with the policy in both), main thread 0.998; the small tests and the
  cold-cap set (`uvvm_func_cov`, `osvvm_axi4_random`, `uvvm_axistream_vvc`, `neorv32_dual_full`, runs 1 and 2) inside
  the byte copy's spread or below it.
